sections.headingZh: 从月亮那里赢来的五天
sections.headingEn: Five days won from the Moon
sections.bodyZh: 普鲁塔克这样开头：瑞亚——埃及人叫她努特，是天空女神——和克洛诺斯（大地之神盖布）偷偷结合。太阳神发现了，便对她下了诅咒：她不得在任何一个月份、任何一年里生下孩子。爱慕瑞亚的赫尔墨斯——也就是埃及的托特——想出了一个办法。他去找月亮下棋，赢了月亮每一天光亮的七十分之一，把赢来的光拼成整整五天，加在一年的三百六十天之后。这五天不属于任何一个月份，于是诅咒落了空。埃及人至今把这五天叫做“加上去的日子”，当作众神的生日来庆祝。
sections.bodyEn: Plutarch begins with Rhea — the Egyptian sky goddess Nut — who lay secretly with Cronus, the earth god Geb. When the Sun found out, he cursed her: she should give birth in no month and no year. But Hermes, the Egyptian Thoth, who loved her, played draughts with the Moon and won from her a seventieth part of each day's light. From these winnings he composed five whole days and added them to the three hundred and sixty. Because the five days belong to no month, the curse could not touch them, and the Egyptians still keep them as the birthdays of the gods.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 普鲁塔克用希腊神名：瑞亚对应努特，克洛诺斯对应盖布，赫尔墨斯对应托特；对应关系是他的解释。

sections.bodyZh: 第一天，奥西里斯降生。据说他出生的那一刻，有一个声音宣告：“万物之主来到了光明之中。”也有人说，底比斯有个叫帕密勒斯的人在宙斯神庙打水时，听见一个声音命令他大声宣布：伟大而仁慈的国王奥西里斯诞生了。第二天出生的是阿鲁埃里斯，也叫大荷鲁斯。第三天出生的是提丰，他不按时也不走正路，而是撕破母亲的肋旁冲了出来。第四天，伊西斯在永远潮湿的地方出生。第五天出生的是奈芙蒂斯。普鲁塔克说，奥西里斯和阿鲁埃里斯是太阳的孩子，伊西斯是赫尔墨斯的孩子，提丰和奈芙蒂斯是克洛诺斯的孩子。奈芙蒂斯嫁给了提丰；而伊西斯和奥西里斯在出生之前就相爱，在母亲腹中的黑暗里已经结合。
sections.bodyEn: On the first day Osiris was born, and a voice proclaimed that the Lord of All had come into the light; some say a man named Pamyles, drawing water at the temple of Zeus in Thebes, heard a voice ordering him to announce that a great and beneficent king, Osiris, was born. On the second day came Arueris, the elder Horus; on the third Typhon, born neither in due time nor by the right way but bursting through his mother's side; on the fourth Isis, in the ever-moist marshes; on the fifth Nephthys. Nephthys married Typhon, while Isis and Osiris loved each other even in the womb.
sections.uncertaintyNote: “大荷鲁斯”（阿鲁埃里斯）与伊西斯之子荷鲁斯在普鲁塔克那里是两位；本站的荷鲁斯条目不把两者合并为单一判断。

sections.bodyZh: 奥西里斯做了埃及的国王。那时的埃及人还过着困苦而野蛮的生活，他教他们种植庄稼，为他们制定法律，教他们敬奉众神。后来他离开埃及，走遍了整个世界，把文明带到各地。他从来不用武器，而是靠说理劝服人们，用歌唱和各种音乐打动人心，所以希腊人认为他就是狄俄尼索斯。他不在的时候，提丰一直没敢作乱，因为伊西斯十分警觉，牢牢守着王权。
sections.bodyEn: Osiris, as king, freed the Egyptians from a destitute and brutish way of life: he showed them the fruits of cultivation, gave them laws and taught them to honour the gods. Then he travelled over the whole earth civilising it, with no need of weapons, winning people over by persuasion, song and every kind of music — which is why the Greeks identify him with Dionysus. While he was away Typhon attempted nothing, because Isis kept close watch.

sections.bodyZh: 奥西里斯回来以后，提丰设下了阴谋。他找来七十二个同谋，还有一位来自埃塞俄比亚、名叫阿索的女王帮忙。他偷偷量好了奥西里斯身体的尺寸，照着做了一只极其华美、装饰精巧的木箱，把它带到宴会上。客人们看见木箱都赞叹不已，提丰就半开玩笑地说：谁躺进去正好合身，就把箱子送给谁。客人们一个个进去试，没有一个合适。最后奥西里斯躺了进去。就在这一刻，同谋们一拥而上，猛地盖上箱盖，有的用钉子钉死，有的浇上熔化的铅，把箱子抬到河边，顺着尼罗河的塔尼斯河口送进了大海。普鲁塔克说，这件事发生在阿西尔月的第十七天，太阳正经过天蝎座，那是奥西里斯在位的第二十八年。
sections.bodyEn: When Osiris returned, Typhon plotted against him with seventy-two conspirators and a queen from Ethiopia named Aso. He secretly measured Osiris's body and had a beautiful, richly decorated chest made to that size, which he brought to a banquet. Everyone admired it, and Typhon promised in jest to give it to whoever fitted it exactly. One after another the guests tried; none fitted. Then Osiris lay down in it — and the conspirators slammed the lid, fastened it with nails and molten lead, carried it to the river and sent it to the sea by the Tanitic mouth. This happened, says Plutarch, on the seventeenth of Athyr, when the sun passes through the Scorpion, in the twenty-eighth year of Osiris's reign.
sections.uncertaintyNote: “第二十八年”也有人解释为奥西里斯的年龄；普鲁塔克两说并存。

sections.bodyZh: 最先知道这件事的，是住在凯姆米斯附近的潘神和萨提尔们，他们把消息传开——所以直到今天，人们把突如其来的恐慌叫做“潘神之惧”。伊西斯听到消息，在科普托斯剪下一绺头发，穿上了丧服。她四处游荡，心烦意乱，遇见谁都打听，连在路上玩耍的孩子也不放过。正是几个孩子告诉她，同谋们是从哪个河口把箱子送进大海的。普鲁塔克说，所以埃及人相信孩子有预言的能力，常常从孩子们在神庙里玩耍时随口说的话里寻找征兆。
sections.bodyEn: The first to learn of the deed were the Pans and Satyrs who lived near Chemmis, and they spread the news — which is why sudden alarms are still called panics. When Isis heard, she cut off a lock of her hair at Coptos and put on a garment of mourning. She wandered everywhere in distress, asking everyone she met, even children at play; and it was children who told her by which river mouth the conspirators had sent the chest out to sea. For this reason, Plutarch says, Egyptians think children have the power of prophecy and take omens from their chatter in temple courts.

sections.bodyZh: 在寻找的途中，伊西斯得知了一件事：奥西里斯曾在不知情的情况下与奈芙蒂斯同寝，把她当成了伊西斯。证据是他留在奈芙蒂斯身边的一只草木樨花环。奈芙蒂斯生下了一个孩子，因为害怕提丰，一出生就把他遗弃了。伊西斯在几只狗的引领下，费尽辛苦找到了这个孩子，把他抚养长大。这个孩子后来成了她的守卫和侍从，名叫阿努比斯；普鲁塔克说，人们相信他像狗守护人一样守护着众神。
sections.bodyEn: On her search Isis learned that Osiris, mistaking Nephthys for herself, had unwittingly lain with her; the proof was a garland of melilot he had left with her. Nephthys had borne a child and, for fear of Typhon, abandoned him at birth. Isis, guided by dogs, found the child with great difficulty and raised him, and he became her guard and attendant — Anubis, who is said to watch over the gods as dogs watch over men.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 阿努比斯的父母在埃及本土资料中有不同说法；这里只是普鲁塔克的版本。

sections.bodyZh: 后来伊西斯打听到，那只箱子被海浪冲到了腓尼基的比布鲁斯，搁浅在一丛石楠上。石楠在很短的时间里长成了一棵高大美丽的树，把箱子整个包进了树干里，从外面一点也看不出来。比布鲁斯的国王惊叹这棵树长得这样大，就把包着棺木的那段树干砍下来，做成了王宫屋顶的一根柱子。伊西斯知道后来到比布鲁斯，坐在一口泉水边，满面泪痕，一言不发，谁也不理，只有王后的侍女们来时，她才亲切地和她们说话，替她们编头发，并从自己身上把一股奇妙的香气传到她们身上。
sections.bodyEn: Isis then learned that the chest had been washed ashore at Byblos in Phoenicia, in the branches of a heather bush, which quickly grew into a large and beautiful tree, enclosing the chest entirely within its trunk. The king of Byblos, amazed at the tree's size, cut off the part that held the coffin and made it a pillar to support the roof of his house. Isis came to Byblos and sat by a spring, dejected and tearful, speaking to no one — except the queen's maidservants, whose hair she braided and whom she perfumed with the wonderful fragrance of her own body.

sections.bodyZh: 王后闻到侍女身上的香气，就派人把这位陌生女子请进宫里，让她做了小王子的保姆。伊西斯喂孩子时，不用乳房，而是把手指放进孩子嘴里让他吮吸。到了夜里，她把孩子身上凡人的部分放在火里烧去，自己则变成一只燕子，绕着那根柱子飞来飞去，哀哀地叫着。一天夜里，王后偷偷看见自己的孩子躺在火中，吓得尖叫起来，就这样夺走了孩子本可以得到的永生。伊西斯这才显露出女神的真身，请求把那根柱子给她。她轻而易举地把柱子从屋顶下取了出来，剖开树干，取出棺木，又用麻布把那段木头包好，浇上香油，交给国王夫妇——比布鲁斯人至今还在伊西斯神庙里供奉这段木头。
sections.bodyEn: The queen, smelling the fragrance on her maids, sent for the stranger and made her nurse to the baby prince. Isis nursed the child by giving him her finger to suck instead of her breast, and at night she burned away the mortal parts of his body, while she herself turned into a swallow and flew around the pillar lamenting. One night the queen saw her baby in the flames and shrieked, and so robbed him of immortality. Then the goddess revealed herself and asked for the pillar. She took it from under the roof with ease, cut away the wood, removed the coffin, wrapped the wood in linen, anointed it with perfume and gave it to the king and queen; it is still revered at Byblos in the temple of Isis.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 这一段与《荷马颂歌·致得墨忒耳》中得墨忒耳在厄琉息斯把婴儿放进火里的情节非常相似，学者常把两者对照。

sections.bodyZh: 伊西斯扑在棺木上放声痛哭，哭声大得把国王的小儿子活活吓死了。她带着棺木和国王的大儿子上了船，扬帆离开。清晨，菲德鲁斯河上吹来一阵大风，河水翻腾，她一怒之下把那条河弄干了。到了没有人的地方，她终于打开箱子，把脸贴在丈夫的脸上，抱着他痛哭。那个跟来的孩子悄悄走到她背后，看见了这一幕。伊西斯察觉了，转过身狠狠地看了他一眼，孩子承受不住那目光，当场吓死了。普鲁塔克也记下了别的说法：有人说他掉进海里淹死了，埃及人在宴会上唱的那首名叫“马涅罗斯”的歌，据说就是为他唱的。
sections.bodyEn: Isis threw herself on the coffin and wailed so loudly that the younger son of the king died of it. She took the elder son and the chest aboard a boat and set sail; when a rough wind rose from the river Phaedrus at dawn, she dried the river up in anger. In a solitary place she opened the chest, laid her face on her husband's face, embraced him and wept. The boy came quietly up behind her and saw; she turned and gave him a terrible look, and he died of fright. Plutarch adds other versions: some say he fell into the sea, and that the song Maneros, sung at Egyptian feasts, is in his honour.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 王子的结局普鲁塔克列出了几种说法，本站只按顺序转述，不判断哪一种更早。

sections.bodyZh: 伊西斯去布托看望在那里长大的儿子荷鲁斯，把装着丈夫遗体的箱子藏在偏僻的地方。可是提丰在月光下夜猎时偶然发现了它，认出了里面的尸体，就把它撕成十四块，撒到了各处。伊西斯得知后，乘着一只纸草做的小船穿过沼泽，一块一块地寻找。普鲁塔克说，所以乘纸草船的人不会被鳄鱼伤害——鳄鱼害怕女神，或者说是敬畏她。也因此埃及有许多“奥西里斯的坟墓”：每找到一块，伊西斯就在那里举行一次葬礼。也有人说，她做了许多遗体的像，分给各个城市，让大家都以为自己拥有真正的遗体，好让提丰找不到真正的坟墓。
sections.bodyEn: Isis went to her son Horus, who was being reared at Buto, and put the chest out of the way. But Typhon, hunting by night under the moon, came upon it, recognised the body and tore it into fourteen parts, which he scattered. Isis searched for them in a papyrus boat, sailing through the marshes — which is why crocodiles do not harm people who sail in papyrus boats, out of fear or reverence for the goddess. And that is why there are many tombs of Osiris in Egypt: she held a funeral wherever she found a part. Others say she made images of him and gave them to city after city, so that Typhon would never find the true tomb.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 普鲁塔克记下了“每处举行葬礼”和“分发假像”两种解释，本站两说并存。

sections.bodyZh: 后来，奥西里斯从冥界回到人间，亲自训练儿子荷鲁斯作战。他问荷鲁斯：你认为什么事最高尚？荷鲁斯回答：为受到伤害的父亲和母亲报仇。他又问：什么动物对作战最有用？荷鲁斯说：马。奥西里斯奇怪他为什么不说狮子，荷鲁斯说：狮子对需要救援的人有用，而马能截住并消灭逃跑的敌人。奥西里斯听了很高兴，知道儿子已经准备好了。许多人投奔到荷鲁斯一边，连提丰的妾图埃里斯也来了；一条追赶她的蛇被荷鲁斯的部下砍成了几段。战斗持续了许多天，最后荷鲁斯取得了胜利。
sections.bodyEn: Later Osiris came from the other world to Horus and trained him for battle. He asked what Horus thought most noble; Horus answered: to avenge one's father and mother for the wrongs done them. He asked which animal was most useful in war; Horus said the horse, for a lion helps one who needs rescue, but a horse cuts off and destroys a fleeing enemy. Osiris was pleased, knowing his son was ready. Many came over to Horus, even Typhon's concubine Thueris; a serpent pursuing her was cut to pieces by Horus's men. The battle lasted many days, and Horus prevailed.

sections.bodyZh: 被锁住的提丰交到了伊西斯手里，她却没有处死他，而是把他放了。荷鲁斯忍受不了，冲上去把母亲头上的王冠夺了下来；赫尔墨斯便给伊西斯戴上了一顶牛头形状的头盔。提丰又正式控告荷鲁斯不是合法的儿子，但在赫尔墨斯的帮助下，众神确认了荷鲁斯的合法身份。此后提丰又在两次战斗中被打败。伊西斯在奥西里斯死后为他生下了哈波克拉特斯，这孩子早产，下肢虚弱。普鲁塔克在第二十章说，这些就是故事里最重要的部分，他故意略去了其中最可憎的情节。他提醒读者，不要把这些故事当成字面上的事实，它们像彩虹一样，是真相映在别处的影子。他还说，在菲莱附近有一座无人能踏上的小岛，据说是奥西里斯的坟墓：鸟不在那里落脚，鱼不游近那里，祭司们每天在那里斟满三百六十只祭酒的碗。
sections.bodyEn: Typhon was handed over to Isis in chains, but she did not put him to death; she let him go. Horus could not bear it: he laid hands on his mother and tore the royal diadem from her head, and Hermes set on her a helmet shaped like a cow's head. Typhon then formally accused Horus of illegitimacy, but with Hermes' help the gods judged Horus legitimate, and Typhon was beaten in two further battles. After Osiris's death Isis bore Harpocrates, born untimely and weak in his lower limbs. In chapter 20 Plutarch says these are the chief points, leaving out the most monstrous; he warns that such stories are not literal facts but, like a rainbow, reflections of a truth. Near Philae, he adds, is an island no one may set foot on, the tomb of Osiris, where no bird alights and no fish comes near, and priests fill three hundred and sixty libation bowls each day.
sections.uncertaintyNote: 普鲁塔克明说自己略去了最可憎的情节，本站不从其他资料补写；菲莱附近“阿巴顿”岛的描述是他引述的传说。

events.titleZh: 从月亮那里赢来的五天
events.titleEn: Five days won from the Moon
events.summaryZh: 普鲁塔克这样开头：瑞亚——埃及人叫她努特，是天空女神——和克洛诺斯（大地之神盖布）偷偷结合。
events.summaryEn: Plutarch begins with Rhea — the Egyptian sky goddess Nut — who lay secretly with Cronus, the earth god Geb.
events.uncertaintyNote: 普鲁塔克用希腊神名：瑞亚对应努特，克洛诺斯对应盖布，赫尔墨斯对应托特；对应关系是他的解释。

events.summaryZh: 第一天，奥西里斯降生。
events.summaryEn: On the first day Osiris was born, and a voice proclaimed that the Lord of All had come into the light; some say a man named Pamyles, drawing water at the temple of Zeus in Thebes, heard a voice ordering him to announce that a great and beneficent king, Osiris, was born.
events.uncertaintyNote: “大荷鲁斯”（阿鲁埃里斯）与伊西斯之子荷鲁斯在普鲁塔克那里是两位；本站的荷鲁斯条目不把两者合并为单一判断。

events.summaryZh: 奥西里斯做了埃及的国王。
events.summaryEn: Osiris, as king, freed the Egyptians from a destitute and brutish way of life: he showed them the fruits of cultivation, gave them laws and taught them to honour the gods.

events.summaryZh: 奥西里斯回来以后，提丰设下了阴谋。
events.summaryEn: When Osiris returned, Typhon plotted against him with seventy-two conspirators and a queen from Ethiopia named Aso.
events.uncertaintyNote: “第二十八年”也有人解释为奥西里斯的年龄；普鲁塔克两说并存。

events.summaryZh: 最先知道这件事的，是住在凯姆米斯附近的潘神和萨提尔们，他们把消息传开——所以直到今天，人们把突如其来的恐慌叫做“潘神之惧”。
events.summaryEn: The first to learn of the deed were the Pans and Satyrs who lived near Chemmis, and they spread the news — which is why sudden alarms are still called panics.

events.summaryZh: 在寻找的途中，伊西斯得知了一件事：奥西里斯曾在不知情的情况下与奈芙蒂斯同寝，把她当成了伊西斯。
events.summaryEn: On her search Isis learned that Osiris, mistaking Nephthys for herself, had unwittingly lain with her; the proof was a garland of melilot he had left with her.
events.uncertaintyNote: 阿努比斯的父母在埃及本土资料中有不同说法；这里只是普鲁塔克的版本。

events.summaryZh: 后来伊西斯打听到，那只箱子被海浪冲到了腓尼基的比布鲁斯，搁浅在一丛石楠上。
events.summaryEn: Isis then learned that the chest had been washed ashore at Byblos in Phoenicia, in the branches of a heather bush, which quickly grew into a large and beautiful tree, enclosing the chest entirely within its trunk.

events.summaryZh: 王后闻到侍女身上的香气，就派人把这位陌生女子请进宫里，让她做了小王子的保姆。
events.summaryEn: The queen, smelling the fragrance on her maids, sent for the stranger and made her nurse to the baby prince.
events.uncertaintyNote: 这一段与《荷马颂歌·致得墨忒耳》中得墨忒耳在厄琉息斯把婴儿放进火里的情节非常相似，学者常把两者对照。

events.summaryZh: 伊西斯扑在棺木上放声痛哭，哭声大得把国王的小儿子活活吓死了。
events.summaryEn: Isis threw herself on the coffin and wailed so loudly that the younger son of the king died of it.
events.uncertaintyNote: 王子的结局普鲁塔克列出了几种说法，本站只按顺序转述，不判断哪一种更早。

events.summaryZh: 伊西斯去布托看望在那里长大的儿子荷鲁斯，把装着丈夫遗体的箱子藏在偏僻的地方。
events.summaryEn: Isis went to her son Horus, who was being reared at Buto, and put the chest out of the way.
events.uncertaintyNote: 普鲁塔克记下了“每处举行葬礼”和“分发假像”两种解释，本站两说并存。

events.summaryZh: 后来，奥西里斯从冥界回到人间，亲自训练儿子荷鲁斯作战。
events.summaryEn: Later Osiris came from the other world to Horus and trained him for battle.

events.summaryZh: 被锁住的提丰交到了伊西斯手里，她却没有处死他，而是把他放了。
events.summaryEn: Typhon was handed over to Isis in chains, but she did not put him to death; she let him go.
events.uncertaintyNote: 普鲁塔克明说自己略去了最可憎的情节，本站不从其他资料补写；菲莱附近“阿巴顿”岛的描述是他引述的传说。

claims.statement: In Plutarch's account Hermes (Thoth) wins a seventieth part of each day's light from the Moon at draughts and composes the five epagomenal days, on which Rhea (Nut) can give birth.
Plutarch lists the births on the five added days: Osiris, Arueris (the elder Horus), Typhon who bursts through his mother's side, Isis and Nephthys.
Plutarch says Osiris as king taught the Egyptians cultivation, laws and worship, then civilised the world by persuasion and music rather than weapons.
In Plutarch's account Typhon (Seth) and seventy-two conspirators trap Osiris in a chest made to his measure, seal it with nails and molten lead and send it to the sea by the Tanitic mouth.
Plutarch says that on hearing of the murder Isis cut a lock of her hair at Coptos, put on mourning and searched everywhere, learning the river mouth from children at play.
In Plutarch's account Isis, guided by dogs, finds and rears the child Nephthys abandoned for fear of Typhon; he becomes her guardian Anubis.
Plutarch tells that the chest lodged in a heather tree at Byblos, which grew around it; the king made the trunk a pillar of his palace, and Isis came to Byblos and sat weeping by a spring.
Plutarch says Isis, as nurse to the Byblian prince, burned away his mortality by night until the queen's cry broke the rite; then she revealed herself and took the coffin from the pillar.
Plutarch describes Isis opening the chest in a solitary place, laying her face on Osiris's face and weeping; the Byblian boy who sees her dies at her look.
In Plutarch's account Typhon (Seth), hunting by moonlight, finds the body of Osiris, tears it into fourteen parts and scatters them; Isis recovers them in a papyrus boat.
Plutarch says Osiris returned from the other world to train Horus, who answers that the noblest deed is to avenge one's parents, and who prevails over Typhon after many days of battle.

Plutarch says Isis released the captured Typhon, Horus tore the diadem from her head, the gods with Hermes' help judged Horus legitimate, and the tomb of Osiris is placed on an inaccessible island near Philae.

entities.canonicalName: Murder of Osiris and the conception of Horus
entities.nameZh: 奥西里斯遇害与荷鲁斯受孕

stories.canonicalTitle: The Rock-Cave Door and the Eight-Forked Serpent: the long story of Susanoo
stories.titleZh: 天之岩户与八岐大蛇：须佐之男的长篇故事
stories.summaryZh: 伊邪那岐把天上交给天照大神、夜之国交给月读、大海交给须佐之男。须佐之男却哭个不停，要去母亲所在的根之国，被父亲赶走。他上天向姐姐告别，两人在天安河边立誓生子；须佐之男自称得胜，在高天原胡作非为，害死了织女。天照大神躲进天之岩户，天地陷入长夜。八百万众神聚在河边商议，思金神出谋，造镜子与勾玉，天宇受卖命在岩户前狂舞，众神大笑，天照大神好奇开门，被天手力男神拉了出来。须佐之男被逐出天界，杀死大宜都比卖，五谷由此而生；他在出云救下栉名田比卖，用八坛烈酒灌醉八岐大蛇，斩杀它并从蛇尾得到草薙剑，最后在须贺建宫，唱出“八云立”之歌。
stories.summaryEn: Izanagi gives Heaven to Amaterasu, the night to Tsukuyomi and the sea to Susanoo, who weeps until the mountains wither and is banished. Going up to take leave of his sister, he swears an oath with her by the Tranquil River of Heaven; claiming victory, he runs riot and causes the death of a weaving maiden. Amaterasu hides in the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling and the world falls into night. The eight hundred myriad deities take counsel through Omoikane, make a mirror and jewels, and Ame-no-Uzume dances until they roar with laughter; Amaterasu peeps out and Tajikarao draws her forth. Expelled, Susanoo kills the food goddess, from whose body grain arises; in Izumo he saves Kushinadahime, makes the eight-forked serpent drunk, slays it, finds the Kusanagi sword in its tail and builds his palace at Suga.
stories.editorialNote: 依据张伯伦 1882 年英译本第十一至十九节（sacred-texts 页码 kj018–kj026）；张伯伦的神名直译是十九世纪的译法，本站用现代通行读法讲述，《日本书纪》的异说另行处理。

versions.labelZh: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十一至十九节（长篇讲述）
versions.labelEn: Kojiki, Chamberlain translation, Sections XI–XIX (long retelling)

source.title: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
source.rightsStatus: Public-domain translation; site transcription; locator and independent summary only
source.sourcePerspective: Nineteenth-century English translation of the Kojiki with the translator's notes
source.reuseRestrictions: Summarize by section; Chamberlain's renderings of divine names are period conventions, not modern standard readings.

versions.witnessScope: 神圣文本档案所收张伯伦 1882 年英译《古事记》
versions.narrativeScope: 三贵子分治、须佐之男啼哭、天安河誓约、须佐之男胡闹、天之岩户、放逐与大宜都比卖、八岐大蛇、须贺宫
versions.rightsNote: 张伯伦 1882 年译本属公共领域；本站发布按节顺序的独立讲述，神名采用现代通行读法。

sections.bodyZh: 伊邪那岐从黄泉回来，在河里洗去污秽。他洗左眼时，生出了天照大神；洗右眼时，生出了月读；洗鼻子时，生出了建速须佐之男。伊邪那岐非常欢喜，说：我生了许多孩子，最后得到了三个尊贵的孩子。他摘下颈上的玉串，摇得叮当作响，交给天照大神，命她统治高天原；又命月读统治夜之国；命须佐之男统治大海。三位神各自领受了父亲的命令，去治理分给自己的地方——只有一位没有去。
sections.bodyEn: Returning from Yomi, Izanagi washed away its pollution in a river. As he washed his left eye, Amaterasu was born; as he washed his right eye, Tsukuyomi; as he washed his nose, Takehaya-Susanoo. Rejoicing that at the end of his begetting he had gained three illustrious children, Izanagi took off his necklace of jewels, shook it so that it jingled, and gave it to Amaterasu, charging her to rule the Plain of High Heaven. He charged Tsukuyomi with the dominion of the night, and Susanoo with the plain of the sea. Each went to rule as charged — all but one.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十一节。

sections.headingEn: The god who wept the mountains dry
sections.bodyZh: 须佐之男不肯去治理大海。他一直哭，哭到胡子长了八拳那么长垂到胸前，还在哭。他哭得青山枯萎，河流和大海全都干涸。于是恶神的声音像五月的苍蝇一样到处嗡嗡作响，各种灾祸一齐发生。伊邪那岐问他：你为什么不治理我交给你的地方，却在这里哭个不停？须佐之男回答：我哭，是因为想去母亲所在的根之坚洲国。伊邪那岐大怒，说：既然如此，你就不许再住在这个国家！就把他赶走了。
sections.bodyEn: Susanoo would not rule the sea. He wept and howled until his beard, eight hands long, reached down over his breast. His weeping withered the green mountains and dried up all the rivers and seas, so that the voices of evil deities swarmed like summer flies and every kind of calamity arose. Izanagi asked why he wept instead of ruling the land entrusted to him. Susanoo answered that he wept because he wished to go to his mother's land, the Nether Distant Land. In great anger Izanagi said that he should not dwell in this land, and expelled him.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十二节。

sections.bodyZh: 须佐之男说：那么我先去向姐姐天照大神告别，然后再走。他向天上走去，山川都震动起来，大地都摇晃了。天照大神听到动静，大吃一惊，说：我弟弟上来，一定没安好心，他是想夺走我的国家。她立刻解开头发，绾成男子的发髻，在发髻上、发鬘上和左右手腕上都缠上长长的勾玉串，背上装着一千支箭的箭囊，胸前挂着装着五百支箭的箭囊，手臂上戴着护腕，挥舞着弓。她用力踏地，双腿陷到大腿那么深，把泥土像雪花一样踢散，威风凛凛地站着等他，大声问：你上来做什么？
sections.bodyEn: Susanoo said he would first take leave of his elder sister Amaterasu. As he went up to Heaven the mountains and rivers shook and every land quaked. Amaterasu, alarmed, said her brother could only be coming to take her land. She undid her hair and bound it up in the manner of a man, wound strings of curved jewels on her bunches of hair, her head-dress and both arms, slung on her back a quiver of a thousand arrows and at her side a quiver of five hundred, put on an elbow-pad and brandished her bow. She stamped till her legs sank into the hard earth to the thighs, kicked the soil about like rotten snow, and stood waiting to demand why he had come.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十三节。

sections.headingEn: The oath by the Tranquil River
sections.bodyZh: 须佐之男说：我没有坏心。父亲问我为什么哭，我说想去母亲的国家，父亲就把我赶走了。我只是来向你告别的。天照大神问：怎么证明你的心是清白的？须佐之男说：我们各自立誓生孩子吧。两人隔着天安河站定。天照大神先拿过须佐之男佩带的十拳剑，把它折成三段，在天之真名井里涮得叮当作响，放进嘴里嚼碎，吹出的气雾中生出了三位女神。接着须佐之男拿过天照大神缠在头发和手臂上的勾玉串，同样在井里涮洗、嚼碎、吹气，从雾气中生出了五位男神。
sections.bodyEn: Susanoo replied that he had no evil intent: his father had expelled him and he had only come to say farewell. Asked how he could prove the purity of his heart, he proposed that each should swear and produce children. Standing on either side of the Tranquil River of Heaven, Amaterasu first took his ten-grasp sabre, broke it into three, rinsed the pieces jingling in the True-Pool-Well of Heaven, crunched them and blew out a misty breath, from which three goddesses were born. Then Susanoo took the strings of curved jewels from her hair and arms, rinsed, crunched and blew in the same way, and five male deities were born.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十三节。

sections.bodyZh: 天照大神宣布：后来生的五位男神，是从我的东西里生出来的，所以是我的孩子；先生的三位女神，是从你的东西里生出来的，所以是你的孩子。须佐之男却说：因为我的心是清白的，所以我生出了温柔的女孩子。这样说来，当然是我赢了。他自以为得胜，得意忘形起来。（这五位男神中的长子，后来成了天皇家的祖先；三位女神则成为宗像大社供奉的神。）
sections.bodyEn: Amaterasu declared that the five male deities, born from her jewels, were her children, and the three goddesses, born from his sabre, were his. But Susanoo said that because his heart was pure he had begotten gentle maidens, and so of course he had won. Puffed up with his victory, he grew reckless. (The eldest of the five male deities becomes, later in the Kojiki, the ancestor of the imperial line; the three goddesses are those worshipped at Munakata.)
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十四节。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 括号里关于皇室祖先与宗像三女神的说明见于《古事记》的同一段落及后文，属于文本自身的谱系说明。

sections.headingEn: Riot in the Plain of High Heaven
sections.bodyZh: 仗着这场“胜利”，须佐之男在高天原胡作非为。他踏坏天照大神水田的田埂，填平灌溉的水沟，又在她品尝新谷的神殿里撒下粪便。天照大神却替他辩解：那像粪便的东西，是我弟弟喝醉了吐出来的；他填平水沟、踏坏田埂，是舍不得那些土地白白空着。可须佐之男的恶行不但没有停止，反而更加厉害。有一天，天照大神正坐在神圣的织殿里，让织女们为众神织造衣裳。须佐之男在织殿的屋顶上捅开一个洞，把一匹从尾巴倒着剥了皮的天之斑马扔了进去。织女吓得跳起来，被梭子刺中下身，就这样死了。
sections.bodyEn: On the strength of his victory Susanoo ran riot. He broke down the divisions of Amaterasu's rice fields, filled in the ditches, and strewed excrement in the palace where she tasted the first fruits. Amaterasu excused him: what looked like excrement was what her brother had vomited when drunk, and he had filled the ditches and broken the ridges only because he grudged the land lying idle. But his wickedness grew worse. While Amaterasu sat in her sacred weaving hall seeing to the weaving of the deities' garments, he broke a hole in the roof and flung down a heavenly piebald horse flayed backwards; a heavenly weaving maiden, startled, struck herself with her shuttle and died.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十五节。

sections.bodyZh: 天照大神看见这一切，感到害怕，就打开天之岩户——天上的岩石屋子的门——走了进去，把门牢牢关上，隐居起来。于是整个高天原一片黑暗，下面的苇原中国也一片黑暗，永远的黑夜笼罩了一切。在这片黑暗里，无数恶神的声音像五月的苍蝇一样到处嗡嗡作响，各种各样的灾祸接连发生。《古事记》对这场灾难只写了寥寥几句，却是神代故事的一个大转折：天照大神是照耀天地的女神，她一躲起来，天上和人间就没有了白天，众神的世界也失去了秩序。接下来的一整段，讲的都是众神如何同心协力，想办法把她请出来。
sections.bodyEn: Terrified at the sight, Amaterasu opened the door of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling, went in, made it fast and hid herself. Then the whole Plain of High Heaven was dark, and the Central Land of Reed-Plains below was dark too: eternal night prevailed. In that darkness the voices of the myriad deities swarmed like summer flies, and every kind of calamity arose.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

sections.bodyZh: 八百万位神聚集在天安河的河滩上开会商议，请高御产巢日神的儿子思金神想办法。依照他的计划，众神先把常世的长鸣鸟聚在一起，让它们一齐啼叫。又从天安河上游取来坚硬的岩石，从天上的金山取来铁，请来锻冶师天津麻罗，命伊斯许理度卖命造一面镜子，命玉祖命做一串长长的、有五百颗勾玉的玉串。他们又请天儿屋命和布刀玉命，从天香山上取来一头雄鹿完整的肩胛骨，用天香山上的桦树皮烧它，进行占卜。
sections.bodyEn: The eight hundred myriad deities assembled in a divine assembly in the bed of the Tranquil River of Heaven and bade Omoikane, child of Takami-musubi, think of a plan. They gathered the long-singing birds of eternal night and made them sing. They took hard rocks from the river-bed and iron from the Heavenly Metal-Mountains, called the smith Amatsumara, and charged Ishikoridome to make a mirror and Tamanoya to make a long string of five hundred curved jewels. They summoned Ame-no-Koyane and Futotama to pull out the whole shoulder-blade of a true stag of Mount Kagu and perform divination with cherry-bark from the same mountain.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

sections.headingEn: The sakaki tree hung with treasures
sections.bodyZh: 众神把天香山上一棵长满枝叶的真杨桐树连根拔起，在上面的枝条上挂起那串五百颗勾玉，在中间的枝条上挂起那面八咫镜，在下面的枝条上挂起白色和青色的布帛。布刀玉命双手捧着这棵树，作为隆重的供品；天儿屋命念诵庄严的祝词。天手力男神则悄悄藏在岩户门边，等待时机。这些东西在后世都有了特别的意义：镜子和勾玉与后来从大蛇尾中得到的草薙剑，被看作代代相传的三件神圣宝物；注连绳、杨桐枝和祝词，至今仍是神社祭祀中常见的东西。不过在这个故事里，它们只有一个用处——把躲起来的女神请出来。
sections.bodyEn: They uprooted a five-hundred-branched true sakaki tree from Mount Kagu of Heaven. On its upper branches they hung the long string of five hundred curved jewels; on its middle branches the large mirror; on its lower branches pendant offerings of white and blue cloth. Futotama held these as grand offerings, Ame-no-Koyane recited a solemn liturgy, and Ame-no-Tajikarao stood hidden beside the door.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

sections.bodyZh: 天宇受卖命用天香山的日影蔓束起衣袖，用真拆葛做成头饰，手里握着一束天香山的竹叶，在天之岩户前倒扣一只木桶，在上面用力踏脚，踏得咚咚作响。她跳着跳着，神灵附了体，露出了胸脯，把裙带一直推到了下身。整个高天原都震动起来，八百万位神一齐哈哈大笑。这是整个神话里最热闹、也最奇特的一幕：漆黑一片的天上，众神围着紧闭的岩户，看着一位女神在倒扣的木桶上又踏又跳，笑声震动了天地。后世把天宇受卖命尊为舞蹈与艺能之神，神乐的起源也常被追溯到这一段。
sections.bodyEn: Ame-no-Uzume bound up her sleeves with heavenly clubmoss from Mount Kagu, made a head-dress of spindle-tree, took in her hand a bundle of bamboo grass from Mount Kagu, and laid an upturned tub before the door of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling, stamping on it until it resounded. Becoming divinely possessed, she bared her breasts and pushed her skirt-string down to her private parts. The Plain of High Heaven shook, and the eight hundred myriad deities laughed together.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

sections.bodyZh: 天照大神觉得奇怪，把岩户的门稍稍打开一条缝，在里面问：我藏了起来，以为高天原会一片黑暗，苇原中国也会一片黑暗，为什么天宇受卖命还在跳舞，八百万位神都在大笑？天宇受卖命回答：因为这里来了一位比您更尊贵的神，所以我们高兴地跳舞欢笑。就在她说话的时候，天儿屋命和布刀玉命把镜子推到天照大神面前。天照大神看到镜中的光，越发惊奇，一点一点地走出门来想看个究竟。藏在门边的天手力男神一把握住她的手，把她拉了出来。布刀玉命立刻在她身后拉起一根注连绳，说：您不能再回到里面去了！天照大神一出来，高天原和苇原中国自然又恢复了光明。
sections.bodyEn: Amaterasu, wondering, opened the door a crack and asked why, when she had thought Heaven and the Central Land would be dark, Ame-no-Uzume danced and all the deities laughed. Uzume answered that they rejoiced because there was a deity more illustrious than she. While she spoke, Ame-no-Koyane and Futotama pushed the mirror forward to show it to Amaterasu, who, more and more astonished, came gradually out to gaze. Tajikarao, hidden beside the door, took her hand and drew her out, and Futotama stretched a bottom-tied rope behind her, saying she must not go back further in than this. As she came forth, Heaven and the Central Land were lit again.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

sections.headingEn: Expulsion and the origin of grain
sections.bodyZh: 八百万位神一起商议，罚须佐之男交出一千桌赎罪的供品，剪掉他的胡子，拔掉他手指和脚趾的指甲，把他赶出了高天原。在路上，须佐之男向大宜都比卖讨要食物。大宜都比卖从鼻子、嘴巴和臀部取出各种美味，做成佳肴献给他。须佐之男偷偷看见了，以为她拿污秽的东西给他吃，就把她杀了。从被杀的女神身上长出了各种东西：头上生出蚕，两只眼睛里生出稻种，两只耳朵里生出粟，鼻子里生出小豆，阴部生出麦，臀部生出大豆。神产巢日神让人把这些收起来，当作种子。
sections.bodyEn: The eight hundred myriad deities took counsel together, fined Susanoo a thousand tables of offerings, cut off his beard and pulled out his finger- and toe-nails, and drove him out with a divine expulsion. Then he asked food of Ōgetsuhime, who took dainties from her nose, mouth and hindquarters and offered them to him. Watching, he thought she was offering him filth, and killed her. From her body things were born: silkworms from her head, rice-seeds from her eyes, millet from her ears, small beans from her nose, barley from her genitals and soy beans from her hindquarters. Kami-musubi had them taken and used as seeds.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十七节。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 《日本书纪》里杀死食物女神的是月读，对象叫保食神；本篇只讲《古事记》的版本。

sections.bodyZh: 须佐之男被赶出天界，降落到出云国肥河上游一个叫鸟发的地方。这时他看见河上漂下来一双筷子，心想上游一定有人住，就沿着河往上走。果然遇见一位老人和一位老妇人，两人中间夹着一位少女，正在哭泣。老人说：我是这里的国神大山津见神的儿子，名叫足名椎，妻子叫手名椎，女儿叫栉名田比卖。我们原本有八个女儿，可是高志的八岐大蛇每年都来，吃掉一个。现在又到了它来的时候，所以我们在哭。须佐之男问那条蛇长什么样。老人说：它的眼睛像红色的酸浆果，一个身子上长着八个头、八条尾巴，身上长满了苔藓、桧树和杉树，身长横跨八道山谷、八座山峰，看它的肚子，总是血淋淋地溃烂着。
sections.bodyEn: Expelled, Susanoo descended to Torikami at the head of the river Hi in Izumo. Seeing chopsticks floating down, he knew people lived upstream and went up the river, where he found an old man and an old woman weeping with a maiden between them. The old man said he was Ashinazuchi, son of the great mountain deity, his wife was Tenazuchi and their daughter Kushinadahime. They had had eight daughters, but the eight-forked serpent of Koshi came every year and devoured one, and now it was time for it to come again. Its eyes, he said, were like red winter-cherries; it had one body with eight heads and eight tails; moss, cypress and cryptomeria grew on its body; its length spanned eight valleys and eight hills; and its belly was always bloody and inflamed.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十八节。

sections.headingEn: Eight vats of liquor and the Kusanagi sword
sections.bodyZh: 须佐之男说：我是天照大神的弟弟，刚从天上下来。你们愿意把女儿嫁给我吗？老夫妇恭恭敬敬地答应了。须佐之男把少女变成一把密齿的梳子，插在自己的发髻上，然后吩咐老夫妇：酿造八次反复酿成的烈酒，再围一道篱笆，篱笆上开八个门，每个门口搭一个台子，每个台子上放一只酒槽，槽里都盛满烈酒。一切准备好后，八岐大蛇果然来了，它把八个头分别伸进八只酒槽里，大口喝酒，喝醉了就趴下睡着了。须佐之男拔出佩带的十拳剑，把大蛇砍成碎块，肥河里流的全成了血。他砍到大蛇中间的那条尾巴时，剑刃崩了个缺口。他觉得奇怪，用剑尖剖开尾巴一看，里面有一把锋利的大刀。他认为这是不同寻常的宝物，就把它献给了天照大神——这就是草薙剑。
sections.bodyEn: Susanoo revealed that he was the elder brother of Amaterasu, just descended from Heaven, and asked for the maiden; the old couple respectfully agreed. He turned her into a close-toothed comb and stuck it in his hair. Then he told them to brew eightfold-refined liquor, build a fence with eight gates, and at each gate set a platform with a vat full of the liquor. The serpent came as foretold, dipped a head into each vat and drank, then lay down drunk and slept. Susanoo drew his ten-grasp sabre and cut the serpent to pieces, so that the river Hi ran with blood. When he cut its middle tail, the edge of his sabre broke; wondering, he split the tail open with its point and found a great sword. Thinking it a strange thing, he presented it to Amaterasu — the Herb-Quelling sword, Kusanagi.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十八节。
sections.uncertaintyNote: “草薙”这个名字在《古事记》的这一段只作注明；名称由来的故事（日本武尊割草）在后文另有讲述。

sections.headingZh: 须贺的宫殿与八云之歌
sections.headingEn: The palace of Suga and the song of eight clouds
sections.bodyZh: 之后，须佐之男在出云国寻找建造宫殿的地方。他来到须贺这个地方，说：我来到这里，心里清清爽爽的。就在那里建起了宫殿，所以那地方至今叫做须贺。他在那里建宫时，有云从地上升起，他便作了一首歌：八云立，出云八重垣，为了让妻子住进来，我筑起八重垣——啊，那八重垣！这被认为是日本最早的和歌。他把栉名田比卖的父亲足名椎叫来，任命他做宫殿的长官，并赐给他一个名字：稻田宫主须贺之八耳神。
sections.bodyEn: Then Susanoo looked for a place in Izumo to build a palace. Arriving at Suga he said that his heart was refreshed, and he built his palace there — which is why the place is still called Suga. As he built it, clouds rose up, and he made a song: Eight clouds arise. The eightfold fence of Izumo makes an eightfold fence for the spouses to retire within. Oh, that eightfold fence! He called Ashinazuchi and made him master of the palace, giving him the name Inada-no-Miyanushi-Suga-no-Yatsumimi.
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十九节。
sections.uncertaintyNote: “日本最早的和歌”是后世（如《古今和歌集》序）的说法，不是《古事记》本文的断言。

events.summaryZh: 伊邪那岐从黄泉回来，在河里洗去污秽。
events.summaryEn: Returning from Yomi, Izanagi washed away its pollution in a river.

events.titleEn: The god who wept the mountains dry
events.summaryZh: 须佐之男不肯去治理大海。
events.summaryEn: Susanoo would not rule the sea.

events.summaryZh: 须佐之男说：那么我先去向姐姐天照大神告别，然后再走。
events.summaryEn: Susanoo said he would first take leave of his elder sister Amaterasu.

events.titleEn: The oath by the Tranquil River
events.summaryZh: 须佐之男说：我没有坏心。
events.summaryEn: Susanoo replied that he had no evil intent: his father had expelled him and he had only come to say farewell.

events.summaryZh: 天照大神宣布：后来生的五位男神，是从我的东西里生出来的，所以是我的孩子；先生的三位女神，是从你的东西里生出来的，所以是你的孩子。
events.summaryEn: Amaterasu declared that the five male deities, born from her jewels, were her children, and the three goddesses, born from his sabre, were his.
events.uncertaintyNote: 括号里关于皇室祖先与宗像三女神的说明见于《古事记》的同一段落及后文，属于文本自身的谱系说明。

events.titleEn: Riot in the Plain of High Heaven
events.summaryZh: 仗着这场“胜利”，须佐之男在高天原胡作非为。
events.summaryEn: On the strength of his victory Susanoo ran riot.

events.summaryZh: 天照大神看见这一切，感到害怕，就打开天之岩户——天上的岩石屋子的门——走了进去，把门牢牢关上，隐居起来。
events.summaryEn: Terrified at the sight, Amaterasu opened the door of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling, went in, made it fast and hid herself.

events.titleZh: 须贺的宫殿与八云之歌
events.titleEn: The palace of Suga and the song of eight clouds

claims.statement: Izanagi gives Amaterasu his jewel necklace and the Plain of High Heaven, Tsukuyomi the dominion of night and Susanoo the plain of the sea.
Susanoo weeps until his beard grows long, the mountains wither and the seas dry, saying he wants to go to his mother's land; Izanagi expels him.
Fearing that Susanoo comes to seize her land, Amaterasu binds her hair like a man, arms herself with jewels, quivers and bow and stamps the earth as she waits for him.
Across the Tranquil River of Heaven Amaterasu crunches Susanoo's sabre and blows out three goddesses, and Susanoo crunches her jewels and blows out five male deities.
Amaterasu assigns the five male deities to herself and the three goddesses to Susanoo, who claims that his gentle daughters prove his pure heart and that he has won.
Susanoo breaks Amaterasu's rice-field ridges, defiles her hall and flings a backward-flayed piebald horse into her weaving hall, causing a weaving maiden's death.
Terrified, Amaterasu shuts herself in the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling, so that Heaven and the Central Land of Reed-Plains fall into continual night and calamities arise.

The eight hundred myriad deities assemble in the bed of the Tranquil River of Heaven and have Omoikane devise a plan: singing birds, a mirror, a string of jewels and divination by a stag's shoulder-blade.
The deities hang jewels, a mirror and cloth offerings on a sakaki tree from Mount Kagu; Futotama holds it, Ame-no-Koyane recites a liturgy and Tajikarao hides beside the door.
Ame-no-Uzume stamps on an upturned tub before the Rock-Dwelling, becomes divinely possessed and bares herself, so that the Plain of High Heaven shakes with the laughter of the deities.
When Amaterasu opens the door a crack and is shown the mirror, Ame-no-Tajikarao draws her out by the hand and Futotama stretches a rope behind her, and light returns.
Expelled from Heaven, Susanoo kills the food goddess Ōgetsuhime, and silkworms, rice, millet, beans and barley grow from her body; Kami-musubi takes them as seeds.

Ashinazuchi tells Susanoo that the eight-forked serpent of Koshi, with eight heads and eight tails, eyes like red winter-cherries and a body spanning eight valleys and hills, has devoured seven of his eight daughters.
Susanoo makes the eight-forked serpent drunk with eight vats of liquor, cuts it to pieces, finds a great sword in its middle tail and presents it to Amaterasu.
Susanoo builds his palace at Suga in Izumo, saying his heart is refreshed, sings the song of the eightfold fence as clouds rise, and makes Ashinazuchi master of the palace.

entities.canonicalName: Amaterasu hides in the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling

stories.canonicalTitle: The Rāmāyaṇa: the long story of Rāma and Sītā
stories.titleZh: 罗摩衍那：罗摩与悉多的长篇故事
stories.summaryZh: 阿逾陀的十车王求子，毗湿奴为了消灭不怕天神与恶魔的罗刹王罗波那，化身为王子罗摩降生。罗摩折断湿婆的大弓，娶了从犁沟里出生的悉多；却因继母吉迦伊的两个恩典被流放森林十四年，悉多和弟弟罗什曼那随行，弟弟婆罗多把罗摩的鞋子供在王座上代为摄政。在森林里，罗波那用金鹿引开罗摩，劫走悉多。罗摩与猴王须羯哩婆结盟，神猴哈奴曼一跃跨过大海，在无忧树林里找到悉多，火烧楞伽。猴军在海上架起石桥，罗摩在大战中射杀罗波那。悉多经过火的考验，众人乘飞车回到阿逾陀，罗摩加冕为王。
stories.summaryEn: King Daśaratha of Ayodhyā prays for sons, and Vishnu is born as Prince Rāma to destroy Rāvaṇa, the rākṣasa king whom no god or demon can kill. Rāma breaks Śiva's bow and marries Sītā, born from a furrow, but is exiled to the forest for fourteen years through his stepmother Kaikeyī's two boons, followed by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, while Bharata rules in the name of his sandals. Rāvaṇa lures Rāma away with a golden deer and carries Sītā off. Rāma allies with the vānara king Sugrīva; Hanumān leaps the sea, finds Sītā in the aśoka grove and burns Laṅkā. The army builds a bridge across the sea, Rāma kills Rāvaṇa, Sītā passes through fire and Rāma is crowned in Ayodhyā.
stories.editorialNote: 依据格里菲斯 1870–1874 年英译（通行本，不是巴罗达精校本）的第一至六卷；第七卷（后篇）里悉多第二次被放逐等情节不在本篇范围。图尔西达斯、甘班等后世与地方的《罗摩衍那》各有不同，本站不混入。

sections.headingEn: A cry of grief becomes a verse
sections.bodyZh: 史诗从诗人自己讲起。苦行者蚁垤问仙人那罗陀：如今世上，有没有一个既有德行又有勇气、懂得正法、知恩图报、言而有信的人？那罗陀说：有，他就是甘蔗王族的罗摩，接着把罗摩的一生简要讲了一遍。不久，蚁垤到多摩萨河边沐浴，看见一对麻鹬正在树上相亲相爱，一个猎人一箭射死了雄鸟，雌鸟围着倒在血泊里的伴侣哀哀悲鸣。蚁垤心中涌起悲悯，脱口说出一句诅咒猎人的话——话一出口，他自己也吃了一惊：这句话音节整齐，可以和着琴弦吟唱。他把这种由悲伤（śoka）而生的诗体叫做“输洛迦”（śloka）。这时梵天亲自来到他面前，对他说：就用这种诗体，把那罗陀讲给你的罗摩的故事完整地唱出来吧；你所写的一切都会是真实的，只要山川还在，这部诗就会在世间流传。
sections.bodyEn: The epic begins with its own poet. The ascetic Vālmīki asked the sage Nārada whether there was any man on earth who was virtuous, brave, grateful and true to his word; Nārada told him of Rāma of the Ikṣvāku line and sketched his life. Soon after, bathing by the river Tamasā, Vālmīki saw a hunter shoot one of a pair of mating curlews, and heard the hen cry over her fallen mate. Pity broke from him as a curse on the hunter — in measured syllables that could be sung to the lute. He called this metre, born of grief (śoka), the śloka. Then Brahmā came to him and told him to sing the whole story of Rāma in that metre: all he wrote would be true, and it would endure while mountains and rivers lasted.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·开篇（那罗陀、梵天来访）。

sections.headingEn: The golden bowl from the sacrificial fire
sections.bodyZh: 阿逾陀城的国王十车王富有、公正、受人爱戴，却没有儿子。他举行了马祭，又请仙人鹿角主持求子的祭祀。就在这时，天上的众神来到梵天面前诉苦：罗刹王罗波那靠苦行从梵天那里得到恩典，天神、乾闼婆、夜叉和罗刹都杀不死他——他看不起人类，根本没有把人算进去。他仗着这个恩典欺压三界，众神毫无办法。正说着，毗湿奴骑着金翅鸟来了。众神恳求他化身为人，降生为十车王的四个儿子，去除掉罗波那。毗湿奴答应了。于是从十车王的祭火中走出一位光芒四射的神灵，捧着一只盛满天界乳粥的金碗。国王把乳粥分给三位王后：憍萨厘雅生下了罗摩，吉迦伊生下了婆罗多，须弥多罗生下了一对双胞胎——罗什曼那和设睹卢祇那。
sections.bodyEn: Daśaratha, king of Ayodhyā, was rich, just and beloved, but had no son. He performed the horse sacrifice and a rite for sons with the sage Ṛṣyaśṛṅga. Meanwhile the gods complained to Brahmā: Rāvaṇa, king of the rākṣasas, had won by austerities a boon that no god, gandharva, yakṣa or rākṣasa could slay him — scorning men, he had not even named them — and he was oppressing the three worlds. Vishnu arrived on Garuḍa, and the gods begged him to be born as a man, as Daśaratha's four sons, to destroy Rāvaṇa. He agreed. From the sacrificial fire rose a radiant being bearing a golden bowl of heavenly rice-milk; the king shared it among his queens, and Kausalyā bore Rāma, Kaikeyī Bharata, and Sumitrā the twins Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·求子祭祀与众神的请求。

sections.headingEn: Into the forest with the sage
sections.bodyZh: 王子们长大了，个个精通经典和武艺，其中罗摩最受众人喜爱，罗什曼那则像影子一样跟着他。一天，大仙人众友来到王宫，请国王把还不满十六岁的罗摩借给他，去保护他的祭祀不受罗刹的骚扰。十车王舍不得，宁愿自己率军前往，但在家庭祭司婆私吒的劝说下终于答应了。众友带着罗摩和罗什曼那上路，教给他们能驱除饥渴和疲劳的咒语。在一片荒凉的森林里，女罗刹多吒迦向他们扑来，罗摩起初不愿杀害女子，只想把她打退，众友却催促他说，为了保护众生，这样做并不违背正法。罗摩便射杀了她。众友非常满意，把许多神兵的咒语传授给他。到了众友的净修林，祭祀开始的第六天，罗刹摩哩遮和苏跋呼带人从天上撒下血肉，罗摩一箭把摩哩遮射飞到一百由旬外的海里，又射死了苏跋呼。
sections.bodyEn: The princes grew up learned in scripture and arms; Rāma was loved by all, and Lakṣmaṇa followed him like his shadow. One day the great sage Viśvāmitra came and asked for Rāma, not yet sixteen, to guard his sacrifice from rākṣasas. Daśaratha begged to go himself with an army, but the family priest Vasiṣṭha persuaded him. On the road Viśvāmitra taught the brothers spells against hunger and weariness. In a desolate forest the rākṣasī Tāṭakā rushed at them; Rāma was loth to kill a woman, but the sage urged that protecting the world was no breach of dharma, and Rāma shot her. Pleased, Viśvāmitra gave him the spells of the divine weapons. On the sixth day of the sacrifice Mārīca and Subāhu rained blood from the sky; Rāma's arrow hurled Mārīca a hundred leagues into the sea and killed Subāhu.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·众友的祭祀与多吒迦。

sections.bodyZh: 众友又带着两位王子前往弥提罗国。弥提罗的国王遮那竭告诉他们：有一次他为祭祀耕地，犁头翻开的犁沟里出现了一个女婴，他给她取名悉多，当作亲生女儿养大。他立下誓言，谁能拉开祖先传下来的湿婆大弓，就把悉多嫁给谁。许多国王都来试过，却连举都举不起来。那张弓装在一辆八个轮子的铁车上，由五千个壮汉拉了出来。罗摩打开弓匣，像玩耍一样轻轻把弓举起，给它装上弦，然后用力一拉——大弓从中间断成了两截，发出像雷霆、像山崩一样的巨响，在场的人全都吓得跌倒在地，只有众友、遮那竭和两位王子还站着。遮那竭欢喜地把悉多许给了罗摩。十车王赶来，四兄弟在同一天成婚。回国路上，持斧罗摩拦路挑战，罗摩又拉开了他带来的毗湿奴大弓，持斧罗摩才心服离去。
sections.bodyEn: Viśvāmitra then led the princes to Mithilā. King Janaka told them that once, ploughing ground for a sacrifice, he had found a baby girl in the furrow; he named her Sītā and raised her as his daughter, vowing to give her to whoever could string the bow of Śiva that his ancestors had kept. Many kings had failed even to lift it. Five thousand men drew it out on an eight-wheeled iron cart. Rāma opened the case, raised the bow as if in play, strung it and drew it — and it broke in the middle with a crash like thunder or a falling mountain. Everyone fell to the ground except Viśvāmitra, Janaka and the two princes. Janaka gave Sītā to Rāma, and the four brothers were married on one day. On the road home Paraśurāma challenged Rāma, who strung the bow of Vishnu as well, and the challenger withdrew.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·第六十七章“断弓”。

sections.bodyZh: 许多年过去了，十车王年事已高，决定立罗摩为太子，满城百姓欢天喜地，挂起彩旗，准备第二天的灌顶典礼。可是王后吉迦伊身边的驼背侍女曼他罗，在宫墙上看到这番景象，急忙跑去对吉迦伊说：罗摩一旦登基，你的儿子婆罗多就只能做奴仆，甚至会被赶出国去。起初吉迦伊还为罗摩高兴，送给曼他罗一件首饰；但曼他罗一再挑拨，终于说动了她，还提醒她：当年你在与商钵罗的战争中救过国王的命，国王许给你两个恩典，你一直没有用。吉迦伊扯下首饰，躺在“愤怒之室”的地上。十车王来了，看见心爱的王后这样，就以罗摩的名义发誓答应她的任何要求。吉迦伊说：第一，立婆罗多为太子；第二，让罗摩穿上树皮衣，到弹宅迦林中流放十四年。国王听了昏倒在地，哀求了整整一夜，吉迦伊却毫不动摇。
sections.bodyEn: Years later the aged Daśaratha resolved to make Rāma heir, and the city hung out banners for the consecration. But Kaikeyī's hunchbacked maid Mantharā, seeing the rejoicing from the palace roof, ran to tell her mistress that once Rāma reigned, her son Bharata would be a servant or an exile. At first Kaikeyī was glad for Rāma and gave Mantharā a jewel, but Mantharā worked on her until she yielded, reminding her of the two boons the king had promised when she saved his life in the war against Śambara. Kaikeyī tore off her ornaments and lay on the floor of the chamber of wrath. When the king, finding her so, swore by Rāma to grant her wish, she asked that Bharata be made heir and that Rāma go in bark garments to the Daṇḍaka forest for fourteen years. The king fell senseless and pleaded all night in vain.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·曼他罗与吉迦伊的恩典。

sections.bodyZh: 第二天一早，罗摩被召进宫，吉迦伊把国王的决定告诉了他。罗摩的脸色一点也没有变，他平静地说：为了父亲的诺言，我今天就去森林。母亲憍萨厘雅悲痛欲绝；罗什曼那怒不可遏，要拿起武器夺回王位，罗摩却劝住他说：遵守父亲的话就是正法。罗摩去向悉多告别，劝她留在宫中。悉多却说：妻子的命运就是丈夫的命运，有你在的森林，胜过没有你的宫殿；你要是不带我去，我就去死。罗什曼那也坚持要一起走。三人脱下华服，穿上树皮衣。全城的人哭着跟在车后，一直送到城外。他们在恒河边得到猎人首领古诃的帮助渡过了河，从此走进了森林。
sections.bodyEn: Next morning Rāma was summoned and Kaikeyī told him the king's decision. His face did not change; he said calmly that for his father's word he would go to the forest that very day. His mother Kausalyā was overwhelmed with grief; Lakṣmaṇa raged and would have taken the throne by arms, but Rāma restrained him, saying that obeying their father was dharma. When Rāma bade Sītā stay behind, she answered that a wife's lot is her husband's lot, that the forest with him was better than a palace without him, and that if he left her she would die. Lakṣmaṇa too insisted on coming. The three put off their fine clothes and put on bark garments, the whole city followed their chariot weeping, and on the Ganges the hunter chief Guha ferried them across into the forest.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·罗摩出城流放。

sections.bodyZh: 车夫苏曼多罗独自赶着空车回来，十车王听说儿子真的走进了森林，悲痛得一病不起。夜里，他对憍萨厘雅讲起了年轻时犯下的一桩罪过：那时他自恃能“听声射箭”，在黑夜的河边听见像大象饮水的声音，一箭射去，射中的却是一个正在用水罐打水的年轻苦行者。少年临死前请他把水带给自己又老又瞎的父母。两位老人得知儿子的死讯，父亲诅咒国王：你将来也会像我一样，为了思念儿子而死。十车王说：这个诅咒如今应验了。他一遍遍呼唤着罗摩的名字，在午夜时分死去了。
sections.bodyEn: When the charioteer Sumantra came back alone, Daśaratha, hearing that his son had truly entered the forest, fell ill with grief. That night he told Kausalyā of a sin of his youth: proud of shooting at a sound, he had heard by a dark river what seemed an elephant drinking and loosed an arrow — but struck a young ascetic filling a water jar. The dying boy asked him to carry water to his old, blind parents. On hearing of their son's death the father cursed the king to die, like him, grieving for a son. That curse, Daśaratha said, was now fulfilled; and calling Rāma's name he died at midnight.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·十车王之死。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 那位少年苦行者在后世传统中常被叫做“室罗波那”（Śravaṇa），蚁垤本里没有给出这个名字。

sections.headingEn: A pair of sandals on the throne
sections.bodyZh: 婆罗多从舅父家回来，才知道父亲已死、兄长被流放，而这一切都是母亲为他谋来的。他痛斥吉迦伊，拒绝接受王位，为父亲办完葬礼后，带着母亲们和军队进入森林，去质多罗俱吒山找罗摩。兄弟相见，罗摩得知父亲去世，悲痛不已。婆罗多跪在他面前恳求他回去为王，众人也一齐劝说。罗摩却说：父亲的诺言必须遵守，十四年期满之前，我不会回去。婆罗多无可奈何，请罗摩把脚上那双饰金的鞋子给他。他把鞋子顶在头上带回去，供在王座上，自己穿上树皮衣，住在城外的南迪村，以“鞋子的仆人”的身份代为治理国家，并且发誓：十四年期满那天罗摩若不回来，他就投火而死。
sections.bodyEn: Bharata returned from his uncle's house to learn that his father was dead and his brother exiled, all for his sake. He rebuked Kaikeyī, refused the throne, performed his father's rites and went with the queens and the army to Mount Citrakūṭa to find Rāma. When the brothers met, Rāma mourned their father. Bharata knelt and begged him to return and reign, and all joined in; but Rāma answered that his father's word must be kept, and he would not return before the fourteen years were over. Then Bharata asked for Rāma's gold-adorned sandals. Carrying them on his head, he set them on the throne, put on bark garments, and ruled from the village of Nandigrāma as the sandals' servant, vowing to enter the fire if Rāma did not return on the appointed day.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·婆罗多寻兄与鞋子。

sections.bodyZh: 罗摩一行在弹宅迦林中住了许多年，保护林中的苦行者，仙人投山把毗湿奴的神弓和永不空竭的箭囊送给了他。后来他们在戈达瓦里河边的五树林住下，罗什曼那搭了一座草屋。一天，罗波那的妹妹、女罗刹首哩薄那迦看见了罗摩，爱上了他，要他做丈夫。罗摩开玩笑地说自己已有妻子，让她去找罗什曼那；罗什曼那也开玩笑地把她推回给罗摩。她恼羞成怒，以为是悉多挡了路，张牙舞爪地向悉多扑去。罗摩命令罗什曼那惩罚她，罗什曼那拔剑割下了她的鼻子和耳朵。首哩薄那迦哭着逃到哥哥伽罗那里。伽罗先派十四个罗刹去，被罗摩全部射死；接着伽罗和突舍那率领一万四千罗刹大军杀来，罗摩让罗什曼那带着悉多躲进山洞，自己一个人迎战，把整支大军消灭了。
sections.bodyEn: For years they lived in the Daṇḍaka forest protecting its hermits, and the sage Agastya gave Rāma the bow of Vishnu and inexhaustible quivers. Then they settled at Pañcavaṭī on the Godāvarī, where Lakṣmaṇa built a hut. There Rāvaṇa's sister, the rākṣasī Śūrpaṇakhā, saw Rāma and desired him. Rāma jestingly said he had a wife and sent her to Lakṣmaṇa, who in jest sent her back. Enraged and blaming Sītā, she rushed at her; at Rāma's command Lakṣmaṇa cut off her nose and ears. She fled to her brother Khara. Khara sent fourteen rākṣasas, whom Rāma shot down; then Khara and Dūṣaṇa came with fourteen thousand, and Rāma, sending Lakṣmaṇa with Sītā to a cave, destroyed the whole host alone.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·首哩薄那迦与伽罗之军。

sections.bodyZh: 首哩薄那迦逃到楞伽，当众责骂罗波那只顾享乐，连自己的国土都保不住，又极力夸赞悉多的美貌。罗波那动了心，乘着飞车去找当年被罗摩一箭射进海里的摩哩遮。摩哩遮吓得发抖，劝他千万别去招惹罗摩；罗波那却威胁说，不听命令就杀了他。摩哩遮叹道：反正都是死，死在罗摩手里还好些。他变成一只金色的鹿，身上点缀着银色的斑点，角尖像宝石，在草屋前来回走动。悉多一见就喜欢上了，求罗摩去捉。罗什曼那提醒说这一定是摩哩遮的幻术，罗摩还是嘱咐弟弟守护悉多，自己追了出去。金鹿时隐时现，把他引得越来越远，罗摩终于一箭射中。摩哩遮现出原形，临死前学着罗摩的声音大喊：“啊，悉多！啊，罗什曼那！”悉多听了惊慌失措，催罗什曼那去救。罗什曼那说没有人能伤害罗摩，悉多竟说出刺耳的话，指责他心怀不轨。罗什曼那受了委屈，只好离开草屋。
sections.bodyEn: Śūrpaṇakhā fled to Laṅkā, rebuked Rāvaṇa for his idleness and praised Sītā's beauty. Rāvaṇa flew in his chariot to Mārīca, whom Rāma's arrow had once hurled into the sea. Mārīca trembled and begged him not to provoke Rāma, but Rāvaṇa threatened to kill him, and he sighed that it was better to die by Rāma's hand. He became a golden deer dappled with silver, its horns tipped with gems, and grazed before the hut. Sītā longed for it. Lakṣmaṇa warned it was Mārīca's magic, but Rāma left him to guard Sītā and gave chase. The deer led him far away until his arrow struck it; dying, Mārīca cried out in Rāma's voice, ‘Ah Sītā! Ah Lakṣmaṇa!’ Sītā, frantic, urged Lakṣmaṇa to go; when he said none could harm Rāma, she accused him with cruel words of wanting her for himself, and, wounded, he went.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·摩哩遮与金鹿。

sections.headingEn: The ten-headed king and the vulture
sections.bodyZh: 罗什曼那刚走，罗波那就扮成一个云游的婆罗门苦行者来到草屋前。悉多按待客之礼请他进来，给他水和食物，并告诉他自己是谁。罗波那这才夸耀自己是楞伽之王，要她做他的王后。悉多轻蔑地回答：你就像一只想得到母狮的豺狗。罗波那现出了十个头的真身，一把抓住她，拖上飞车，向南飞去。悉多一路向树木、河流和山神呼喊，求它们告诉罗摩。年老的鹫王阇吒优私是十车王的朋友，他拦住罗波那，劝他放了悉多，随即与他搏斗，打碎了他的车子，杀死了驾车的驴子和车夫；可他终究年老力衰，被罗波那砍断了翅膀和双脚，跌落在地。飞过一座山时，悉多看见山顶上坐着五只猴子，就把自己的披巾和首饰包在一起扔了下去。罗波那把她带回楞伽，给她十二个月的期限，把她关在无忧树林里，由许多女罗刹看守。
sections.bodyEn: As soon as Lakṣmaṇa had gone, Rāvaṇa came to the hut disguised as a wandering brahmin ascetic. Sītā received him as a guest with water and food and told him who she was. Then he boasted that he was king of Laṅkā and asked her to be his queen; she answered scornfully that he was a jackal longing for a lioness. Rāvaṇa took his true ten-headed form, seized her and carried her off southward in his chariot while she called on the trees, rivers and mountain spirits to tell Rāma. The old vulture-king Jaṭāyu, friend of Daśaratha, barred his way, smashed his chariot and killed its asses and driver, but, old and spent, had his wings and feet cut off by Rāvaṇa. Passing a hill where five monkeys sat, Sītā dropped her scarf and ornaments. In Laṅkā Rāvaṇa gave her twelve months and set her in the aśoka grove under guard of rākṣasīs.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·悉多被劫与阇吒优私。

sections.bodyZh: 罗摩在回来的路上遇见了罗什曼那，心中顿生不祥之感。草屋果然空无一人。罗摩悲痛欲狂，向树木、河流和野兽一一询问悉多的下落，看到散落的花朵、折断的车子和血迹，以为她被罗刹吃掉了，怒气冲冲地要毁灭世界，罗什曼那苦苦劝他冷静。他们找到奄奄一息的阇吒优私，鹫王告诉他们是罗波那劫走了悉多、往南方去了，说完就断了气。罗摩像为父亲举行葬礼一样，亲手为他火化。兄弟俩继续向南，被一个没有头、胸前长着大嘴的怪物迦槃陀抓住，他们砍断了他的两只长臂。迦槃陀在火葬的火焰中恢复了天神的形貌，告诉他们：去般波湖边的哩舍牟迦山找猴王须羯哩婆，他会帮你们找到悉多。在般波湖边，年老的女苦行者舍波哩欢喜地迎接了罗摩，随后升入天界。
sections.bodyEn: On the way back Rāma met Lakṣmaṇa and felt dread; the hut was empty. Half mad with grief, Rāma asked the trees, rivers and beasts where Sītā was; seeing scattered flowers, a broken chariot and blood, he thought rākṣasas had eaten her and threatened to destroy the worlds until Lakṣmaṇa calmed him. They found the dying Jaṭāyu, who told them Rāvaṇa had taken Sītā south, and died. Rāma cremated him with the rites due to a father. Going on, they were seized by the headless monster Kabandha, whose mouth was in his chest, and cut off his long arms; restored to divine form in his funeral fire, he told them to seek the monkey-king Sugrīva on Mount Ṛśyamūka by Lake Pampā. There the aged ascetic woman Śabarī welcomed Rāma joyfully and then rose to heaven.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·罗摩的哀伤、阇吒优私、迦槃陀与舍波哩。

sections.bodyZh: 哈奴曼扮成苦行者来迎接他们，把他们带到须羯哩婆面前。罗摩和须羯哩婆围着火结为盟友。须羯哩婆拿出那包从天上落下的首饰，罗摩认出是悉多的，痛哭失声；罗什曼那说，耳环和手镯他认不出，只认得脚镯，因为他每天向悉多行礼时只看她的脚。须羯哩婆讲了自己的遭遇：哥哥波林夺走了他的妻子和王国，把他赶到这座山上。罗摩一箭射穿七棵娑罗树，让他相信自己的力量。须羯哩婆向波林挑战，罗摩藏在树后；第一次两兄弟长得太像，罗摩分不清；第二次须羯哩婆戴上花环，罗摩一箭射中了波林。垂死的波林责问罗摩为什么从暗处射他，罗摩回答：你夺了弟弟的妻子，作为国王的代表，我有责任惩罚你。须羯哩婆登上王位，雨季过后，他派出四路猴军寻找悉多，罗摩把刻着自己名字的戒指交给了往南去的哈奴曼。
sections.bodyEn: Hanumān, disguised as an ascetic, met them and brought them to Sugrīva, and Rāma and Sugrīva swore friendship around a fire. Sugrīva showed the bundle of ornaments that had fallen from the sky; Rāma knew them as Sītā's and wept, and Lakṣmaṇa said he knew only her anklets, for he had looked only at her feet when he bowed to her. Sugrīva told how his brother Vālin had taken his wife and kingdom. Rāma shot an arrow through seven sāl trees to prove his strength. When the brothers fought, Rāma stood hidden behind a tree; the first time he could not tell them apart, the second time Sugrīva wore a garland, and Rāma's arrow struck Vālin. The dying Vālin reproached him for shooting from hiding; Rāma answered that Vālin had taken his brother's wife and that he punished him on the king's behalf. Sugrīva was crowned, and after the rains sent search parties to the four quarters; Rāma gave his signet ring to Hanumān, who went south.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第四卷·与须羯哩婆结盟与波林之死。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 罗摩从暗处射杀波林是否合乎正法，在印度传统内部本身就有长久的争论；本站只讲蚁垤本里双方的说法。

sections.bodyZh: 南路的猴军由安伽陀和哈奴曼率领，找了一个多月仍无消息，来到南方大海边时都绝望了，打算绝食而死。这时，一只没有翅膀的老鹫出现了，他是阇吒优私的哥哥商波底。他告诉猴子们：悉多被关在大海对面一百由旬外的楞伽城。说完，他烧焦的翅膀竟重新长了出来。可是谁能跳过这么宽的海？老熊王阇婆梵提醒哈奴曼：你是风神的儿子，小时候曾一跃扑向太阳，你的力量连你自己都忘了。哈奴曼站上摩亨陀罗山，身体越变越大，用力一蹬，山都被踩得渗出水来，他像一支箭一样飞上了天。海中的弥那迦山从水里升起，请他歇脚，他只轻轻碰了一下就继续飞；蛇母须罗娑奉众神之命张开大嘴考验他，他先把身体变得巨大，又突然缩得像拇指一样小，从她嘴里钻进去又钻出来；女妖辛悉迦抓住他的影子把他往下拖，他钻进她的身体把她撕开。最后，他落在楞伽城外的三峰山上。
sections.bodyEn: The southern party under Aṅgada and Hanumān searched for over a month in vain and, reaching the southern sea, despaired and resolved to starve. Then a wingless old vulture appeared — Sampāti, Jaṭāyu's elder brother — who told them Sītā was held in Laṅkā, a hundred leagues across the sea; as he spoke his scorched wings grew again. But who could leap so far? The old bear-king Jāmbavān reminded Hanumān that he was the wind god's son, who as a child had sprung at the sun, and whose strength he had forgotten. Hanumān swelled to a great size on Mount Mahendra, pressed it until water oozed from its rocks, and flew like an arrow. The mountain Maināka rose from the sea to offer him rest; Surasā, mother of serpents, opened her jaws to test him, and he grew huge, then shrank to a thumb's size and darted in and out; Siṃhikā seized his shadow, and he tore her from within. At last he landed on Mount Trikūṭa outside Laṅkā.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第四至五卷·商波底与哈奴曼跨海。

sections.bodyZh: 哈奴曼把身体缩得像猫一样小，趁着夜色潜入楞伽。他看遍了金碧辉煌的宫殿和罗波那的后宫，一度把熟睡的王后曼度陀哩误认为悉多，随即醒悟：悉多绝不会在这里安睡。最后，他在无忧树林里找到了她：她消瘦苍白，穿着沾满尘土的衣服，被一群面目狰狞的女罗刹围着。罗波那来了，又是威胁又是引诱，说只剩两个月期限，到时她若不从，就把她剁了做早饭。悉多在两人之间放下一根草茎，隔着草茎回答他：你配不上我，罗摩的箭会来惩罚你。罗波那走后，哈奴曼躲在树上，轻声唱起罗摩的故事。悉多先是惊恐，以为又是罗波那的幻术，等哈奴曼把罗摩的戒指递给她，她才喜极而泣。哈奴曼要背她回去，悉多拒绝了：她不愿主动碰触罗摩以外的男子，而且应当由罗摩亲自来救她、雪洗耻辱。她把自己的髻珠交给哈奴曼作信物。
sections.bodyEn: Shrinking to the size of a cat, Hanumān slipped into Laṅkā by night. He searched the golden palaces and Rāvaṇa's women's quarters, once mistaking the sleeping queen Mandodarī for Sītā before realising Sītā would never sleep there. At last he found her in the aśoka grove, thin and pale, in soiled clothes, surrounded by fearsome rākṣasīs. Rāvaṇa came, threatening and coaxing: in two months, if she would not yield, he would have her cut up for his breakfast. Sītā laid a blade of grass between them and answered across it that he was unworthy of her and Rāma's arrows would punish him. When he left, Hanumān, hidden in a tree, softly sang Rāma's story. Sītā feared another illusion until he gave her Rāma's ring, and then wept for joy. He offered to carry her back; she refused, unwilling to touch any man but Rāma and wishing Rāma himself to rescue her and wipe out the insult, and gave him her crest-jewel as a token.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第五卷·无忧树林中的悉多。

sections.bodyZh: 哈奴曼想试一试罗刹的力量，就把无忧树林毁了个干净，打死了前来捉他的大批卫兵，连罗波那的儿子阿刹也死在他手里。罗波那的长子因陀罗耆用梵天的神兵把他捆住，哈奴曼明知自己挣得开，却甘愿被绑去见罗波那。他当面劝罗波那把悉多还给罗摩，罗波那大怒，下令处死他；罗波那的弟弟维毗沙那提醒说，使者不可杀。于是罗波那下令在他的尾巴上缠上浸油的布点火，牵着他游街示众。悉多听说后，向火神祈祷让火焰变得清凉，哈奴曼果然感到尾巴上的火一点也不烫。他挣脱绳索，跳上屋顶，从一座宫殿跳到另一座宫殿，把楞伽城烧成一片火海。烧完之后他才惊恐地想起悉多，赶紧回去，看见她安然无恙，这才放心。他跃回大海对岸，把髻珠交给罗摩，罗摩把它贴在胸前，泪流满面。
sections.bodyEn: To test the rākṣasas' strength Hanumān wrecked the aśoka grove and slew the guards sent against him, among them Rāvaṇa's son Akṣa. Rāvaṇa's eldest son Indrajit bound him with the weapon of Brahmā, and Hanumān, though he could break free, let himself be led before Rāvaṇa, whom he urged to return Sītā. Rāvaṇa ordered his death, but his brother Vibhīṣaṇa reminded him that envoys may not be slain; so Rāvaṇa had oiled rags wrapped round Hanumān's tail and set alight, and paraded him through the streets. Sītā prayed to the fire god to be cool to him, and Hanumān felt no heat. Breaking his bonds, he leapt from palace roof to palace roof until Laṅkā was a sea of flame — then, in sudden fear for Sītā, went back and found her unharmed. He leapt back across the sea and gave Rāma the crest-jewel, which Rāma pressed to his breast weeping.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第五卷·火烧楞伽。

sections.bodyZh: 猴军浩浩荡荡向南进发，来到大海边。楞伽城里，维毗沙那劝哥哥把悉多还回去，免得国破家亡，罗波那却骂他是叛徒。维毗沙那带着四个随从飞过大海来投奔罗摩。须羯哩婆怀疑他是奸细，罗摩说：凡是来向我求庇护的，我都要保护，哪怕是罗波那本人。他接纳了维毗沙那，当场为他举行了楞伽王的灌顶。罗摩向大海祈求让路，在海边躺了三天三夜，大海毫无回应。罗摩发怒，搭箭要把大海射干，海神这才从水中升起，告诉他：猴军中的那罗是工巧天的儿子，让他来造桥，我会托住桥身。猴子们拔来大树、搬来山石，扔进海里，五天之内，一座一百由旬长的石桥横跨了大海。猴军踏着石桥渡海，把楞伽城团团围住。
sections.bodyEn: The army marched south to the sea. In Laṅkā Vibhīṣaṇa urged his brother to return Sītā before ruin came, and Rāvaṇa called him a traitor; so Vibhīṣaṇa flew across the sea with four companions to Rāma. Sugrīva suspected a spy, but Rāma said he would protect anyone who sought his refuge, even Rāvaṇa himself, and consecrated Vibhīṣaṇa then and there as king of Laṅkā. Rāma lay three days by the shore begging the ocean to give way; when it did not answer, he angrily drew an arrow to dry it up, and the Ocean rose from the waters and told him that Nala, son of the divine architect Viśvakarman, could build a bridge that the sea would bear. The monkeys hurled trees and rocks into the sea, and in five days a bridge a hundred leagues long spanned it. The army crossed and laid siege to Laṅkā.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·维毗沙那投奔与那罗造桥。

sections.bodyZh: 大战开始了。罗波那的儿子因陀罗耆能隐身作战，他躲在云中放出蛇箭，把罗摩和罗什曼那捆得动弹不得，猴军以为两位王子已死。危急之时，金翅鸟从天而降，群蛇见了天敌纷纷逃散，兄弟俩才得以解脱。罗波那的弟弟鸠槃羯叻拿身躯如山，一睡就是几个月，罗刹们敲锣打鼓、赶着大象从他身上踩过才把他叫醒。他冲进战场大口吞吃猴子，连须羯哩婆也被他夹走。罗摩用箭射断了他的双臂和双腿，最后射下了他的头。因陀罗耆又用梵天的神兵射倒了几乎整支猴军，哈奴曼奉命飞到喜马拉雅山采药，认不出是哪几种草药，就把整座山峰连根拔起托了回来，药草的香气让倒下的猴子全都复活了。最后，罗什曼那与因陀罗耆展开激战，射下了他的头。
sections.bodyEn: The war began. Rāvaṇa's son Indrajit, who could fight unseen, shot serpent-arrows from the clouds that bound Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa so fast the monkeys thought them dead — until Garuḍa swooped down and the serpents fled from their enemy. Rāvaṇa's giant brother Kumbhakarṇa, who slept for months at a time, was woken with drums and with elephants driven over his body; he strode into battle devouring monkeys and carried off Sugrīva, until Rāma's arrows severed his arms and legs and at last his head. Indrajit then felled almost the whole army with the weapon of Brahmā; Hanumān flew to the Himalaya for healing herbs and, unable to tell which they were, tore up the whole peak and brought it back, and the herbs' fragrance revived the fallen. At last Lakṣmaṇa fought Indrajit and shot off his head.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·因陀罗耆、鸠槃羯叻拿与药山。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 哈奴曼取药山的情节在通行本里出现过两次（一次救全军，一次救罗什曼那），各本次序不尽相同；本节只概述其中一次。

sections.bodyZh: 儿子和兄弟都死了，罗波那终于亲自出战。他用一支神矛击中罗什曼那，哈奴曼再一次取来草药救活了他。因陀罗派自己的车夫摩多梨驾着天车来帮助罗摩。两人的决战持续了很久，天地为之震动。罗摩一箭射下罗波那的一个头，立刻又长出一个新的头来；他一连射下了一百个头，罗波那仍然不死。这时摩多梨提醒他：用梵天的神兵吧。罗摩搭上仙人投山传给他的那支梵天之箭，箭上燃着火焰，带着风的速度，一箭射穿了罗波那的心脏。十首魔王从车上倒下，众神从天上撒下花雨。维毗沙那为哥哥痛哭，犹豫要不要为这个恶人举行葬礼，罗摩对他说：仇恨到死亡为止，他现在也是我的兄弟，为他举行葬礼吧。随后，维毗沙那在楞伽登上了王位。
sections.bodyEn: With his sons and brother dead, Rāvaṇa came out to fight himself. He struck down Lakṣmaṇa with a dart, and Hanumān again brought herbs to revive him. Indra sent his charioteer Mātali with his celestial chariot to carry Rāma. Their duel lasted long and shook heaven and earth. Each time Rāma's arrow struck off one of Rāvaṇa's heads, another grew in its place, until a hundred had fallen and he still lived. Then Mātali reminded Rāma of the weapon of Brahmā. Rāma loosed the arrow Agastya had given him, flaming and swift as the wind, and it pierced Rāvaṇa's heart; the ten-headed king fell from his chariot, and the gods rained flowers. When Vibhīṣaṇa wept and hesitated to give his wicked brother funeral rites, Rāma told him that enmity ends with death: Rāvaṇa was his brother too, and the rites should be done. Vibhīṣaṇa was then crowned king of Laṅkā.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·罗波那之死。

sections.headingEn: The ordeal of fire and the return home
sections.bodyZh: 悉多沐浴更衣后被带到罗摩面前。当着众人的面，罗摩却说出冷酷的话：我打这一仗，是为了洗雪家族的耻辱，不是为了你；你在别人家里住了这么久，现在你想去哪里就去哪里吧。悉多泪流满面，却镇定而有尊严地回答：我的心从来只属于你，被抓走不是我的过错。她请罗什曼那堆起柴堆，向火神祈祷后走进了火焰。火神从火中升起，把毫发无损的悉多交还给罗摩，宣布她清白无瑕。梵天和众神也现身，告诉罗摩他就是那罗延（毗湿奴）本身，十车王也乘着天车出现，祝福儿子。罗摩说：我早知道悉多是清白的，只是要让天下人都看到。他们乘着飞车布湿波迦飞回阿逾陀。在南迪村，婆罗多捧着那双鞋子出城迎接，把王国交还给哥哥。罗摩加冕为王，史诗说，在他统治的年代里，没有寡妇哀哭，没有疾病和盗贼，人们长寿而安乐。
sections.bodyEn: Sītā, bathed and adorned, was brought before Rāma. Before everyone he spoke harshly: he had fought to wipe out the insult to his line, not for her; she had lived long in another's house and might now go where she pleased. Weeping, but with calm dignity, Sītā answered that her heart had always been his and her capture was not her fault. She asked Lakṣmaṇa to build a pyre, prayed to the fire god and entered the flames. Agni rose from the fire, gave her back to Rāma unharmed and declared her pure. Brahmā and the gods appeared and told Rāma he was Nārāyaṇa himself, and Daśaratha came in a celestial car to bless his son. Rāma said he had known Sītā was pure but the world had to see it. In the flying chariot Puṣpaka they returned to Ayodhyā; at Nandigrāma Bharata met them with the sandals and restored the kingdom. Rāma was crowned, and in his reign, says the epic, no widow wept, there was no sickness or theft, and people lived long and happily.
sections.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·悉多的火之考验、回国与加冕。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 火的考验是今天印度内外讨论最多的情节之一；第七卷（后篇）里还有悉多被第二次放逐的故事，不在本篇范围。

events.titleEn: A cry of grief becomes a verse
events.summaryZh: 史诗从诗人自己讲起。
events.summaryEn: The epic begins with its own poet.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.titleEn: The golden bowl from the sacrificial fire
events.summaryZh: 阿逾陀城的国王十车王富有、公正、受人爱戴，却没有儿子。
events.summaryEn: Daśaratha, king of Ayodhyā, was rich, just and beloved, but had no son.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.titleEn: Into the forest with the sage
events.summaryZh: 王子们长大了，个个精通经典和武艺，其中罗摩最受众人喜爱，罗什曼那则像影子一样跟着他。
events.summaryEn: The princes grew up learned in scripture and arms; Rāma was loved by all, and Lakṣmaṇa followed him like his shadow.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryZh: 众友又带着两位王子前往弥提罗国。
events.summaryEn: Viśvāmitra then led the princes to Mithilā.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryZh: 许多年过去了，十车王年事已高，决定立罗摩为太子，满城百姓欢天喜地，挂起彩旗，准备第二天的灌顶典礼。
events.summaryEn: Years later the aged Daśaratha resolved to make Rāma heir, and the city hung out banners for the consecration.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryZh: 第二天一早，罗摩被召进宫，吉迦伊把国王的决定告诉了他。
events.summaryEn: Next morning Rāma was summoned and Kaikeyī told him the king's decision.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryZh: 车夫苏曼多罗独自赶着空车回来，十车王听说儿子真的走进了森林，悲痛得一病不起。
events.summaryEn: When the charioteer Sumantra came back alone, Daśaratha, hearing that his son had truly entered the forest, fell ill with grief.
events.uncertaintyNote: 那位少年苦行者在后世传统中常被叫做“室罗波那”（Śravaṇa），蚁垤本里没有给出这个名字。

events.titleEn: A pair of sandals on the throne
events.summaryZh: 婆罗多从舅父家回来，才知道父亲已死、兄长被流放，而这一切都是母亲为他谋来的。
events.summaryEn: Bharata returned from his uncle's house to learn that his father was dead and his brother exiled, all for his sake.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryZh: 罗摩一行在弹宅迦林中住了许多年，保护林中的苦行者，仙人投山把毗湿奴的神弓和永不空竭的箭囊送给了他。
events.summaryEn: For years they lived in the Daṇḍaka forest protecting its hermits, and the sage Agastya gave Rāma the bow of Vishnu and inexhaustible quivers.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryZh: 首哩薄那迦逃到楞伽，当众责骂罗波那只顾享乐，连自己的国土都保不住，又极力夸赞悉多的美貌。
events.summaryEn: Śūrpaṇakhā fled to Laṅkā, rebuked Rāvaṇa for his idleness and praised Sītā's beauty.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.titleEn: The ten-headed king and the vulture
events.summaryZh: 罗什曼那刚走，罗波那就扮成一个云游的婆罗门苦行者来到草屋前。
events.summaryEn: As soon as Lakṣmaṇa had gone, Rāvaṇa came to the hut disguised as a wandering brahmin ascetic.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryZh: 罗摩在回来的路上遇见了罗什曼那，心中顿生不祥之感。
events.summaryEn: On the way back Rāma met Lakṣmaṇa and felt dread; the hut was empty.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryZh: 哈奴曼扮成苦行者来迎接他们，把他们带到须羯哩婆面前。
events.summaryEn: Hanumān, disguised as an ascetic, met them and brought them to Sugrīva, and Rāma and Sugrīva swore friendship around a fire.
events.uncertaintyNote: 罗摩从暗处射杀波林是否合乎正法，在印度传统内部本身就有长久的争论；本站只讲蚁垤本里双方的说法。

events.summaryZh: 南路的猴军由安伽陀和哈奴曼率领，找了一个多月仍无消息，来到南方大海边时都绝望了，打算绝食而死。
events.summaryEn: The southern party under Aṅgada and Hanumān searched for over a month in vain and, reaching the southern sea, despaired and resolved to starve.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryZh: 哈奴曼把身体缩得像猫一样小，趁着夜色潜入楞伽。
events.summaryEn: Shrinking to the size of a cat, Hanumān slipped into Laṅkā by night.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryZh: 哈奴曼想试一试罗刹的力量，就把无忧树林毁了个干净，打死了前来捉他的大批卫兵，连罗波那的儿子阿刹也死在他手里。
events.summaryEn: To test the rākṣasas' strength Hanumān wrecked the aśoka grove and slew the guards sent against him, among them Rāvaṇa's son Akṣa.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryZh: 猴军浩浩荡荡向南进发，来到大海边。
events.summaryEn: The army marched south to the sea.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryZh: 大战开始了。
events.summaryEn: The war began.
events.uncertaintyNote: 哈奴曼取药山的情节在通行本里出现过两次（一次救全军，一次救罗什曼那），各本次序不尽相同；本节只概述其中一次。

events.summaryZh: 儿子和兄弟都死了，罗波那终于亲自出战。
events.summaryEn: With his sons and brother dead, Rāvaṇa came out to fight himself.
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.titleEn: The ordeal of fire and the return home
events.summaryZh: 悉多沐浴更衣后被带到罗摩面前。
events.summaryEn: Sītā, bathed and adorned, was brought before Rāma.
events.uncertaintyNote: 火的考验是今天印度内外讨论最多的情节之一；第七卷（后篇）里还有悉多被第二次放逐的故事，不在本篇范围。

claims.statement: The opening cantos tell how Vālmīki's grief at a hunter killing a curlew became the first śloka and how Brahmā commanded him to sing the story of Rāma in that metre.

At the gods' plea against Rāvaṇa, whose boon protected him from gods and demons but not men, Vishnu agrees to be born as the four sons of Daśaratha, who receives the divine rice-milk from his sacrificial fire.
Lent to Viśvāmitra to guard his sacrifice, Rāma slays the rākṣasī Tāṭakā at the sage's urging, receives the divine weapons and drives off Mārīca and Subāhu.
At Mithilā Rāma lifts, strings and breaks the bow of Śiva that no king could lift, and Janaka gives him Sītā, the daughter found in a furrow.
Persuaded by her maid Mantharā, Kaikeyī claims Daśaratha's two old boons: Bharata's consecration and Rāma's exile to the forest for fourteen years.
When Rāma accepts exile without a change of face, Sītā insists that a wife shares her husband's lot and follows him into the forest with Lakṣmaṇa, all three in bark garments.
After Rāma leaves, Daśaratha tells Kausalyā how in youth he shot a young ascetic by mistake and was cursed by the boy's blind father to die grieving for a son, and dies at midnight.
Refusing the throne, Bharata seeks Rāma at Citrakūṭa; when Rāma will not break their father's word, Bharata takes his sandals, sets them on the throne and rules from Nandigrāma as their servant.
At Pañcavaṭī, when the rākṣasī Śūrpaṇakhā, rebuffed by both brothers, attacks Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa cuts off her nose and ears at Rāma's command, and Rāma then destroys the army of Khara and Dūṣaṇa alone.
Rāvaṇa forces Mārīca to take the form of a golden deer, which lures Rāma away; dying, Mārīca cries out in Rāma's voice so that Sītā sends Lakṣmaṇa after him.
Disguised as an ascetic, Rāvaṇa seizes Sītā and carries her to Laṅkā, cutting down the vulture-king Jaṭāyu who tries to stop him, while Sītā drops her ornaments to five monkeys.
Finding the hut empty, Rāma learns from the dying Jaṭāyu that Rāvaṇa took Sītā south, cremates the vulture as a father, and is directed by Kabandha to seek Sugrīva.
Rāma allies with Sugrīva through Hanumān, shoots Vālin from concealment and answers his reproach, makes Sugrīva king and gives his ring to Hanumān for the southern search.
Told by Sampāti that Sītā is in Laṅkā and reminded by Jāmbavān of his strength, Hanumān leaps the hundred-league sea from Mount Mahendra, passing Maināka, Surasā and Siṃhikā.
Hanumān finds Sītā in the aśoka grove after Rāvaṇa threatens her, gives her Rāma's ring, and receives her crest-jewel when she declines to be carried away by him.
Captured by Indrajit and sentenced by Rāvaṇa, Hanumān has his tail set alight, feels no heat through Sītā's prayer, and burns Laṅkā before leaping back with her crest-jewel.
Rāma grants refuge to Vibhīṣaṇa and, after the Ocean rises at his threatened arrow, has Nala build a bridge to Laṅkā in five days and lays siege to the city.
In the war before Laṅkā Garuḍa frees the brothers from Indrajit's serpent-arrows, Rāma slays Kumbhakarṇa, Hanumān brings the mountain of herbs, and Lakṣmaṇa slays Indrajit.
In single combat, with Indra's chariot driven by Mātali, Rāma strikes off Rāvaṇa's regrowing heads and finally kills him with the weapon of Brahmā, then tells Vibhīṣaṇa that enmity ends with death.
After Rāma's harsh public words Sītā enters a pyre and Agni returns her unharmed and declares her pure; the gods proclaim Rāma to be Nārāyaṇa, and Rāma returns to Ayodhyā to be crowned.

steps.storyTitleZh: 乳海搅拌：《摩诃婆罗多》精校本与《薄伽梵往世书》
steps.storyTitleEn: Churning of the Ocean — Mahābhārata critical edition and Bhāgavata Purāṇa witnesses
steps.rationaleZh: 比较毗湿奴化龟与湿婆饮毒。
steps.rationaleEn: Compare Viṣṇu's tortoise form and Śiva drinking the poison.
steps.transitionNote: 从文本见证转到物质见证。

steps.storyTitleZh: 吴哥寺乳海搅拌：浮雕物质见证
steps.storyTitleEn: Churning of the Sea of Milk as an Angkor Wat material witness
steps.versionLabelZh: APSARA 吴哥寺回廊浮雕层
steps.versionLabelEn: APSARA Angkor Wat gallery relief layer
steps.focusName: Angkor Wat Churning of the Sea of Milk relief
steps.rationaleZh: 最后看吴哥寺浮雕：同一主题的高棉物质见证，不由文本决定其版本。
steps.rationaleEn: End with the Angkor Wat relief: a Khmer material witness of the theme whose recension is not decided by the texts.

beats.textZh: Ifá 语料传统与奥伦米拉相关。
beats.textEn: Ifá divination tradition is associated with Orunmila.

deityStoryCards.name: Fuxi
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《系辞下》中的包牺氏（伏羲）：仰观天象、俯察地法，始作八卦，又结绳为网。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Baoxi (Fuxi) in Xi Ci II: the ancient ruler who observed heaven, earth and living things, first made the eight trigrams and knotted nets.

beats.textZh: 《系辞下》讲古代圣人的发明，第一位就是包牺氏——后世通常写作伏羲。书里说，远古的时候，是他在治理天下。
beats.textEn: Xi Ci II lists the inventions of the ancient sages, and the first is Baoxi — usually written Fuxi in later texts. In remote antiquity, it says, he ruled all under heaven.
beats.sourceTitle: Book of Changes, Xi Ci II (Great Commentary, part 2)
beats.uncertaintyNote: “包牺”即“伏羲”是传统注疏的读法。

beats.textZh: 他抬头观察天上的日月星辰，低头观察大地的形势；又细看鸟兽身上的花纹，看各地适合生长什么。近处，他从自己的身体取法；远处，他从万物取法。
beats.textEn: He looked up at the images in the sky and down at the patterns of the earth; he studied the markings of birds and beasts and what each land was suited for. Near at hand he drew on his own body, and far off on all things.
beats.sourceTitle: Book of Changes, Xi Ci II (Great Commentary, part 2)

beats.textZh: 于是他开始画出八卦——八个由三条线组成的符号，用来通达神明的德性，把万物的情状分门别类。
beats.textEn: Thereupon he first made the eight trigrams — eight figures of three lines each — to communicate with spirit-like virtue and to sort the dispositions of the myriad things.
beats.sourceTitle: Book of Changes, Xi Ci II (Great Commentary, part 2)
beats.evidenceNote: 《系辞下》第二章“于是始作八卦”。

beats.textZh: 他还把绳子打结，做成罗网，人们用它打猎、捕鱼。《系辞》接下来再讲神农等后来的圣人，这里只讲伏羲这一段。
beats.textEn: He also knotted cords into nets, which people used to hunt and fish. The Xi Ci then moves on to later sages such as Shennong; this retelling covers only Baoxi's part.
beats.sourceTitle: Book of Changes, Xi Ci II (Great Commentary, part 2)
beats.evidenceNote: 《系辞下》第二章“作结绳而为罔罟”。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 后续圣人的发明不在本故事范围内。

deityStoryCards.name: Gonggong
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Figure who contends with Zhuanxu and strikes Mount Buzhou in the Huainanzi Tian Wen and Liezi Tang Wen witnesses; whether deity, clan head or rival ruler is foregrounded varies by source and is not resolved here.

beats.textZh: 《淮南子·天文训》说，从前共工与颛顼争夺帝位。
beats.textEn: Huainanzi “Tian Wen” says that long ago Gonggong contended with Zhuanxu to become ruler.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Tian Wen Xun — passage opening 昔者共工
beats.uncertaintyNote: 颛顼在此作为传说中的君主登记，不作历史真实性判断。

beats.textZh: 共工发怒撞向不周山，支撑天的柱子折断，系住大地的绳索断绝。
beats.textEn: In anger Gonggong strikes Mount Buzhou; the pillar holding up heaven breaks and the cords binding the earth snap.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Tian Wen Xun — passage opening 昔者共工
beats.evidenceNote: 同段不周山、天柱与地维句组。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 不周山不映射为现代山名或坐标。

beats.textZh: 结果天向西北倾斜，日月星辰随之移动；地在东南不满，积水与尘埃都归向那里。这一段没有提到女娲，是《天文训》中独立的天地形势解释。
beats.textEn: As a result heaven tilts to the northwest and the sun, moon and stars shift with it; the earth falls short in the southeast, where waters and dust collect. The passage does not mention Nüwa and stands as an independent explanation of cosmic orientation in “Tian Wen”.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Tian Wen Xun — passage opening 昔者共工
beats.uncertaintyNote: 同书《览冥训》的女娲段与此段分属不同章节，不合成单一故事。

facts.textZh: 共工出现在“共工触不周山”之中。
facts.textEn: Gonggong is the actor who strikes Mount Buzhou in both registered witnesses.

beats.textZh: 《淮南子·览冥训》以远古为背景：支撑天地的四极崩坏，九州开裂，天不能全覆、地不能全载，大火与洪水都无法止息，猛兽鸷鸟危害百姓。本段只按这一见证的顺序概述，不补入其他文献给出的起因。
beats.textEn: Huainanzi “Lan Ming” sets the scene in remote antiquity: the four poles holding up the world have failed and the nine provinces have split; heaven no longer covers everything and earth no longer bears everything, fires and floods cannot be stopped, and wild beasts and birds of prey attack the people. This section follows only this witness and adds no cause taken from other texts.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Lan Ming Xun — passage opening 往古之時
beats.evidenceNote: 《淮南子·览冥训》“往古之时”段；Chinese Text Project 章节页。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 传世本用字存在异体；本站只发布独立概述，不复制整段原文。

beats.headingEn: Five-colored stones and the turtle's legs
beats.textZh: 于是女娲炼五色石来修补苍天，又截断巨鳌的足，用来重新立起四极。
beats.textEn: Nüwa then refines five-colored stones to patch the azure sky and cuts off the legs of a great turtle to set the four poles upright again.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Lan Ming Xun — passage opening 往古之時
beats.evidenceNote: 同段女娲补天与立四极的句组。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 炼字与鳌字在不同版本中有异体，不影响本段概述。

beats.headingEn: The black dragon and the reed ash
beats.textZh: 这一见证还写到女娲杀死黑龙以救济冀州，并堆积芦苇灰来堵住泛滥的洪水；随后天地重新安定，百姓得以存活。
beats.textEn: This witness adds that Nüwa kills a black dragon to relieve Jizhou and piles up reed ash to stop the flood waters; afterwards heaven and earth are set right and the people survive.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Lan Ming Xun — passage opening 往古之時
beats.evidenceNote: 同段黑龙、冀州与芦灰句组。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 冀州在此是文本中的九州之一，不映射为现代行政区或坐标；《列子·汤问》对应段落未陈述这两项。

beats.textZh: 《览冥训》的女娲段落没有把天地崩坏归因于共工。《淮南子》确实在《天文训》另记共工怒触不周山，但那是另一章中独立的天地倾斜起源，本站不把两章拼接成因果链。
beats.textEn: The Lan Ming Nüwa passage does not attribute the collapse to Gonggong. The Huainanzi does narrate Gonggong striking Mount Buzhou, but in a separate passage in the “Tian Wen” chapter that explains the tilt of heaven and earth; the site does not splice the two chapters into a causal chain.
beats.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Lan Ming Xun — passage opening 往古之時
beats.evidenceNote: 《览冥训》女娲段与《天文训》共工段分别定位。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 把共工触山写成女娲补天起因的说法见于较晚文献，已作为独立接受层排队。

facts.textZh: 女娲出现在“女娲补天”之中。
facts.textEn: Nüwa is the actor who repairs the sky in both registered witnesses.
facts.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Lan Ming Xun — Nüwa repair sentence group

facts.textZh: 女娲——情节：Piles up reed ash to stop the flood waters.
facts.textEn: In the Huainanzi Lan Ming witness Nüwa piles up reed ash to stop the flood waters.
facts.sourceLocation: Huainanzi, Lan Ming Xun — reed ash and flood waters

deityStoryCards.name: Pangu
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 徐整《三五历纪》佚文中的盘古：生于如鸡子的混沌之中，天地分开时日长一丈。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Pangu as quoted from Xu Zheng's lost Sanwu liji: born in an egg-like chaos, he grows a zhang a day as heaven and earth separate.

beats.textZh: 很久以前，天和地还没有分开，到处是一团混沌，样子像一个鸡蛋。盘古就生在这团混沌之中。
beats.textEn: Long ago heaven and earth were not yet apart; everything was one chaos shaped like a hen's egg, and Pangu was born inside it.
beats.evidenceNote: 《艺文类聚》卷一引《三五历纪》；《太平御览》卷一引文字句略异。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 原书已佚，只能依靠类书引文。

beats.textZh: 过了一万八千年，天地开辟：轻而清的阳气上升成为天，重而浊的阴气下沉成为地。盘古就在天地之间，一天之中变化九次，比天更神，比地更圣。
beats.textEn: After 18,000 years heaven and earth opened: the light, clear yang rose to become heaven, the heavy, murky yin sank to become earth. Pangu stood between them, changing nine times a day, more divine than heaven and wiser than earth.
beats.evidenceNote: 同一引文“阳清为天，阴浊为地”。

beats.textZh: 从此天每天升高一丈，地每天加厚一丈，盘古也每天长高一丈。这样又过了一万八千年，天高到了极点，地深到了极点，盘古也长到了极点。在这之后，才有了三皇。
beats.textEn: From then on heaven rose a zhang each day, earth grew a zhang thicker, and Pangu grew a zhang taller. After another 18,000 years heaven was as high as it could be, earth as deep, and Pangu as tall. Only after that came the Three Sovereigns.
beats.evidenceNote: 同一引文“天日高一丈……盘古日长一丈”。
beats.uncertaintyNote: “盘古垂死化身为日月山川”出自另一部书，本故事不合并。

deityStoryCards.name: Thunder Spirit of Leize
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《山海经·海内东经》的雷泽无名雷神；与后世雷公不自动合并。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Unnamed thunder spirit of Leize in the Classic of Mountains and Seas; not automatically merged with later Leigong.

beats.textZh: 《山海经·海内东经》的登记段落在雷泽描写一位无名雷神。
beats.textEn: The registered Hai Nei Dong Jing passage describes an unnamed thunder spirit in Leize.
beats.sourceTitle: Classic of Mountains and Seas, Hai Nei Dong Jing
beats.uncertaintyNote: “雷泽雷神”是数据库定位名，不是文本给出的专名。

beats.textZh: 该段把雷声与神灵击打腹部相连，系统把它保存为文本中的神话叙述。
beats.textEn: The passage connects thunder with the spirit striking its belly, and the system preserves this as a mythic statement in the text.
beats.sourceTitle: Classic of Mountains and Seas, Hai Nei Dong Jing
beats.uncertaintyNote: 不把神话陈述当作自然科学解释。

beats.textZh: 因为文本没有给出后世雷公的专名与完整形象，系统不按“雷神”这个共通标签自动合并。
beats.textEn: Because the passage does not give the later proper name and full image of Leigong, the system does not merge the figures under the generic label thunder god.
beats.sourceTitle: Classic of Mountains and Seas, Hai Nei Dong Jing
beats.uncertaintyNote: 后世接受史将在独立版本中处理。

deityStoryCards.name: Yellow Emperor
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《史记·五帝本纪》中少典之子轩辕，于涿鹿擒杀蚩尤并被尊为天子；本站不作历史真实性断言。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Xuanyuan, son of Shaodian, who in the Shiji fights Chiyou at Zhuolu and is honoured as Son of Heaven; no historical-reality claim is made.

beats.textZh: 黄帝是少典的儿子，姓公孙，名轩辕。他那个时代，神农氏的统治衰落了，诸侯互相攻打、欺压百姓，神农氏却无力征讨。轩辕于是操练军队，去讨伐不肯朝贡的诸侯。
beats.textEn: The Yellow Emperor was the son of Shaodian, surnamed Gongsun and named Xuanyuan. In his time the rule of Shennong had declined; the lords attacked one another and oppressed the people, and Shennong could not punish them. So Xuanyuan trained troops to subdue the lords who would not pay tribute.
beats.sourceTitle: Shiji, Annals of the Five Emperors
beats.uncertaintyNote: 此前轩辕与炎帝在阪泉的三次交战本故事未展开。

beats.textZh: 诸侯之中，蚩尤最为凶暴，没有人能制服他。蚩尤起来作乱，不听从帝王的命令。
beats.textEn: Among the lords Chiyou was the most violent, and no one could subdue him. Chiyou rose in rebellion and would not obey the ruler's command.
beats.sourceTitle: Shiji, Annals of the Five Emperors
beats.evidenceNote: 《五帝本纪》“蚩尤作乱，不用帝命”。

beats.textZh: 轩辕征召各路诸侯的军队，在涿鹿的原野上与蚩尤交战，终于把蚩尤擒住并杀死。
beats.textEn: Xuanyuan called up the armies of the lords and fought Chiyou in the wilds of Zhuolu, and at last captured and killed him.
beats.sourceTitle: Shiji, Annals of the Five Emperors
beats.uncertaintyNote: 涿鹿不在本站映射为现代坐标。

beats.textZh: 诸侯们都尊奉轩辕为天子，取代了神农氏，这就是黄帝。
