Kvasir, wisest of the gods, saw the shape of the net in the ashes, and they made one like it. Dragging the falls with Thor at one end, they drove Loki until he tried to leap over the net; Thor caught him in mid-air and held him by the tail, which is why the salmon tapers at the tail.

beats.textZh: 众神把洛基带进一个山洞，竖起三块扁石，在每块石头上钻一个洞。他们抓来洛基的两个儿子瓦利和纳尔维，把瓦利变成一匹狼，狼把他的兄弟撕成了碎片。众神用纳尔维的肠子把洛基捆在三块石头上：一块抵着肩膀，一块抵着腰，一块抵着膝盖窝，那些肠子随后变成了铁。斯卡蒂拿来一条毒蛇，挂在洛基的头上方，让蛇的毒液滴在他脸上。洛基的妻子西格恩站在他身旁，手里捧着一只碗接住毒液；碗满了，她就走开去倒掉，这时毒液就滴在洛基的脸上，他痛得猛烈挣扎，整个大地都随之颤抖——这就是人们所说的地震。洛基就这样被捆着，一直躺到诸神的黄昏来临。
beats.textEn: The gods took Loki into a cave, set up three slabs on edge and bored a hole in each. They took his sons Váli and Nari (or Narfi); Váli was turned into a wolf and tore his brother apart, and with Nari's entrails they bound Loki over the stones — one under his shoulders, one under his loins, one under the backs of his knees — and the bonds became iron. Skaði hung a venomous snake above him so that its poison dripped onto his face. His wife Sigyn stands by holding a bowl under the venom, and when the bowl is full she goes to empty it; then the venom drips on his face and he shudders so violently that the whole earth shakes — what men call earthquakes. There he lies bound until Ragnarök.

facts.textZh: 巴德尔是弗丽嘉的孩子。
facts.textEn: Gylfaginning presents Frigg as Baldr's mother in the account of his death.

facts.textZh: 弗丽嘉与奥丁是配偶。
facts.textEn: Frigg is Odin's wife and knows all fates, though she does not prophesy.

facts.textZh: 弗丽嘉出现在“巴德尔之死”之中。
facts.textEn: Frigg takes oaths from fire, water, metals, stones, plants and beasts not to harm Baldr, but not from the young mistletoe.

deityStoryCards.name: Freyr
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 尼奥尔德之子，掌管雨水、阳光与丰收；为娶葛德而交出宝剑（《欺骗古鲁菲》第24、37章）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Njörðr who rules rain, sunshine and the fruitfulness of the earth; gives away his sword to win Gerðr (Gylfaginning 24, 37).

beats.textZh: 尼奥尔德住在天上一个叫诺欧通的地方。他掌管风的运行，能平息海浪和火焰；出海航行和捕鱼的人都向他祈祷。他在华纳海姆长大，后来作为人质被送到阿萨神族。
beats.textEn: Njörðr lives in heaven at a place called Nóatún. He rules the motion of the wind and can calm sea and fire; those who sail or fish pray to him. He was raised in Vanaheim and later given to the Æsir as a hostage.

beats.textZh: 尼奥尔德有一儿一女。儿子弗雷掌管雨水、阳光和大地的收成，人们向他祈求丰年与富足。女儿芙蕾雅住在弗尔克范格，每当她骑马出战，就分得一半战死者，另一半归奥丁；她乘坐的车由两只猫拉着。
beats.textEn: Njörðr has a son and a daughter. Freyr rules rain, sunshine and the produce of the earth, and people pray to him for good seasons and wealth. Freyja lives at Fólkvangr; whenever she rides to battle she takes half the slain, Odin the other half, and her chariot is drawn by two cats.

beats.textZh: 后来，弗雷爱上了巨人之女葛德。为了娶到她，他把自己的宝剑交给了别人作为代价——这把剑从此不在他手中。
beats.textEn: Later Freyr falls in love with Gerðr, a giant's daughter. To win her he gives away his sword as the price, and the sword is no longer his.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 葛德尚未单独建立实体；诸神黄昏中的后果另行登记。

facts.textZh: 弗雷——职掌：rain, sunshine and the fruitfulness of the earth
facts.textEn: Freyr rules rain and sunshine and the produce of the earth, and is invoked for prosperity.

facts.textZh: 弗雷是尼奥尔德的孩子。
facts.textEn: Njörðr's son is Freyr.

facts.textZh: 弗雷与芙蕾雅是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Freyr and Freyja are the children of Njörðr.

deityStoryCards.name: Týr
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 众神中最勇敢的一位；束缚芬里尔时失去一只手（《欺骗古鲁菲》第25、34章）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: The boldest of the gods, who loses his hand when the wolf Fenrir is bound (Gylfaginning 25, 34).

beats.textZh: 斯诺里说，提尔是众神中最勇敢、最无畏的一位，打仗时人们向他祈求胜利。他只有一只手。
beats.textEn: Snorri says Týr is the boldest and most valiant of the gods, invoked for victory in battle — and he has only one hand.

beats.textZh: 众神想用一条魔法绳索捆住狼芬里尔。狼起了疑心，要求有人把手放进它嘴里，保证这不是诡计。众神面面相觑，只有提尔伸出了右手。
beats.textEn: The gods mean to bind the wolf Fenrir with a magic fetter. Suspicious, the wolf demands that someone put a hand in its mouth as a pledge of good faith. Only Týr holds out his right hand.

beats.textZh: 绳索越挣越紧，狼发现自己被骗了，便咬断了提尔的手。众神都笑了，只有提尔没有笑。
beats.textEn: The more the wolf struggles, the tighter the fetter grows. Realizing it has been tricked, Fenrir bites off Týr's hand — and all the gods laugh, except Týr.

deityStoryCards.name: Skaði
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Giantess counted among the goddesses; she fastens a venomous snake above the bound Loki (Gylfaginning 50).

beats.textZh: 奥丁的儿子巴德尔是众神中最好的一位，人人都称赞他。他容貌俊美、光彩照人，有一种最白的花就因为像他的睫毛那样白，被人们称作“巴德尔的睫毛”。他是阿萨神族中最聪明、最善于言辞、最仁慈的神，可是他的判决却从来不能实现。这一天，巴德尔做了几个可怕的梦，梦见自己的性命将要遭到危险。他把这些梦告诉了阿萨众神，众神聚在一起商议，最后决定：要为巴德尔求得一切东西的保护，使他免受任何伤害。
beats.textEn: Baldr, Odin's son, is the best of the gods and all praise him; so fair and bright that the whitest flower is called Baldr's brow. He is the wisest, most eloquent and most merciful of the Æsir, though none of his judgements can be fulfilled. Then Baldr dreamed great and perilous dreams threatening his life, and when he told the Æsir they took counsel together and resolved to ask protection for him from every kind of danger.

beats.textZh: 于是弗丽嘉出发，让世间万物都立下誓言，不伤害巴德尔：火与水、铁和各种金属、石头、泥土、树木、疾病、走兽、飞鸟、毒物和蛇，全都发了誓。这件事办成之后，众神都放下心来，并且以此为乐：巴德尔站在集会的场地中央，其他的神有的向他射箭，有的用刀剑砍他，有的向他扔石头，可是无论做什么都伤不了他。众神都认为这是一件了不起的荣耀。
beats.textEn: Frigg took oaths that they would not harm Baldr from fire and water, iron and every metal, stones, the earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds, poison and snakes. When this was done it became a sport of the Æsir: Baldr would stand in the assembly while some shot at him, some struck at him and some threw stones, and nothing harmed him. They all thought it a great honour.

beats.textZh: 劳菲之子洛基看见这一切，心里很不高兴，因为巴德尔毫发无伤。他变成一个女人，来到弗丽嘉住的芬萨利尔宫。弗丽嘉问这位女子：你知道阿萨众神在集会上做什么吗？女人说：他们都在朝巴德尔射箭、扔东西，可是什么也伤不了他。弗丽嘉说：不论是兵器还是木头，都伤不了巴德尔，因为我已经让万物都立了誓。女人问：真的万物都向你发誓不伤害巴德尔了吗？弗丽嘉答道：在瓦尔哈拉的西边，长着一棵小小的树苗，叫作槲寄生。我觉得它太年幼了，就没有让它发誓。那女人听了便走了。洛基找到槲寄生，把它拔下来，带到集会的地方去。
beats.textEn: Loki Laufeyjarson was displeased that Baldr took no harm. He went to Frigg at Fensalir in the likeness of a woman. Frigg told the stranger that neither weapons nor trees would harm Baldr, for she had taken oaths of all things. Had everything sworn? asked the woman. Frigg answered that a young shoot grew west of Valhöll called mistletoe, which seemed too young to ask for an oath. The woman went away; Loki took the mistletoe, pulled it up and went to the assembly.

beats.textZh: 霍德尔站在人圈的外面，因为他是瞎子。洛基走过去问他：你为什么不朝巴德尔扔东西？霍德尔说：因为我看不见巴德尔在哪里，而且我也没有武器。洛基说：你也该像别人一样向巴德尔表示敬意。我来给你指方向，你把这根树枝向他扔去吧。霍德尔接过槲寄生，照着洛基的指引朝巴德尔扔去。树枝穿透了巴德尔的身体，他倒在地上死了。斯诺里说：这是神和人所遭遇的最大不幸。
beats.textEn: Höðr stood at the edge of the ring, for he was blind. Loki asked why he did not shoot at Baldr. Because I cannot see where he is, said Höðr, and I have no weapon. Loki said he should honour Baldr like the others, and offered to show him where Baldr stood. Höðr took the mistletoe and threw it as Loki directed; it pierced Baldr and he fell dead to the earth. It was, says Snorri, the greatest misfortune ever to befall gods and men.

beats.textZh: 巴德尔倒下的时候，阿萨众神都说不出话来，双手也失去了力气，不能把他扶起。他们彼此相望，心里都知道是谁干了这件事，却不能在那里报仇，因为那是一处圣地。他们想说话的时候，涌出的只有泪水，没有一个神能把自己的悲痛告诉别人。在所有的神中，奥丁最承受不住这个打击，因为他最明白，巴德尔的死对阿萨众神意味着多大的损失与毁灭。
beats.textEn: When Baldr fell, the Æsir were struck dumb and their hands failed them to lift him. Each looked at the other, all of one mind about who had done the deed, but no vengeance could be taken there, for it was a place of great sanctuary. When they tried to speak, weeping came first, and none could tell the others his grief. Odin bore the loss worst of all, for he best understood how great a loss and ruin Baldr's death was for the Æsir.

beats.textZh: 众神稍稍平静之后，弗丽嘉开口问道：阿萨神族中有谁愿意赢得我全部的爱与恩宠，骑马走上通往冥界的路，去找赫尔，问她要多少赎金才肯让巴德尔回到阿斯加德？奥丁的儿子、勇敢的赫尔莫德说他愿意去。于是众神牵来奥丁的八足骏马斯莱布尼尔，交给赫尔莫德。他跃上马背，向冥界疾驰而去。这是众神在巨大的悲痛中想到的唯一办法：如果冥界的女王肯收下赎金，巴德尔也许还能回来。赫尔莫德的马蹄声远去了，而留在阿斯加德的众神，还要先为巴德尔送行。
beats.textEn: When the gods came to themselves, Frigg asked who among the Æsir would win all her love and favour by riding the road to Hel to find Baldr and offer Hel a ransom to let him come home to Ásgarðr. Hermóðr the Bold, Odin's son, undertook the journey. Odin's horse Sleipnir was led out, and Hermóðr mounted and galloped away.

beats.textZh: 阿萨众神抬起巴德尔的尸体，送到海边。巴德尔的船叫作“灵钟号”，是所有船中最大的一艘，众神想把它推下海，在船上为巴德尔举行火葬，可是船纹丝不动。他们只好派人到巨人之国去请一个名叫希罗金的女巨人来帮忙。她骑着一头狼来了，用毒蛇作缰绳。她跳下狼背，奥丁叫四个狂战士看住那头狼，他们只能把它摔倒才制服它。希罗金走到船头，只一推就把船推下了海，船底的滚木冒出火花，大地都颤抖起来。索尔大怒，握住锤子要打碎她的头，众神都为她求情，他才住手。巴德尔的遗体被抬上船，他的妻子南娜看见了，悲痛得心都碎了，当场死去，也被放上柴堆一起焚烧。索尔站在火堆前用妙尔尼尔为它祝圣，一个名叫利特的矮人从他脚前跑过，索尔一脚把他踢进了火里。奥丁把金环德罗普尼尔放在柴堆上，巴德尔的马也带着全套马具被送上火堆。
beats.textEn: The Æsir carried Baldr's body to the sea. His ship Hringhorni was the greatest of all ships, but they could not launch it, so they sent to Jötunheimr for the giantess Hyrrokkin, who came riding a wolf with vipers for reins. Four berserks could hold the wolf only by knocking it down. She pushed the ship off with one shove, so that fire flew from the rollers and the earth shook; Thor would have smashed her head had the gods not begged for her. When Baldr was laid on board, his wife Nanna's heart burst with grief, and she was laid on the pyre with him. Thor hallowed the pyre with Mjöllnir and kicked the dwarf Litr into the flames; Odin laid the ring Draupnir on the pyre, and Baldr's horse was burned with all its harness.

beats.textZh: 赫尔莫德骑着马走了九天九夜，穿过幽深黑暗的山谷，什么也看不见，直到来到冥河耶尔河边，骑上了铺着闪亮黄金的耶尔桥。守桥的少女名叫莫德古德，她问他的名字和家族，说：昨天有五队死人从这座桥上过去，可是桥被你一个人震得比他们全体还响；而且你的脸色不像死人。你为什么骑马走在通往冥界的路上？赫尔莫德说：我要去冥界找巴德尔。你有没有在路上见过他？莫德古德说：巴德尔已经骑马过了耶尔桥。通往冥界的路，就在下面，往北边去。
beats.textEn: For nine nights Hermóðr rode through dark, deep valleys where he could see nothing, until he came to the river Gjöll and rode onto the Gjallarbrú, roofed with gleaming gold. The maiden who guarded the bridge, Móðguðr, asked his name and lineage: the day before, five companies of dead men had ridden over, yet the bridge thundered more under him alone, and he did not have the colour of the dead. He said he was riding to Hel to seek Baldr; she told him Baldr had crossed the bridge, and that the road to Hel lay downward and to the north.

beats.textZh: 赫尔莫德一路骑到冥界的大门前，他跳下马，把马肚带勒紧，重新上马，用马刺一踢，骏马高高跃起，从大门上方越了过去，一点也没碰到。他骑到大殿前下了马，走进去，看见他的哥哥巴德尔坐在高座上。赫尔莫德在那里过了一夜。第二天早晨，他请求赫尔让巴德尔和他一起骑马回家，并告诉她阿萨众神为巴德尔哭得多么伤心。赫尔说：我要看看巴德尔是不是真的像人们说的那样受到爱戴。如果世上的一切东西，活的和死的，都为他哭泣，他就可以回到阿萨众神那里；可是只要有一样东西反对、不肯哭泣，他就得留在冥界。赫尔莫德起身告辞，巴德尔送他出殿，把金环德罗普尼尔交给他，让他带回去给奥丁作纪念；南娜也送给弗丽嘉一块亚麻头巾和其他礼物，还送给弗丽嘉的侍女富拉一枚金指环。
beats.textEn: At Hel's gate Hermóðr dismounted, tightened the girth, remounted and spurred Sleipnir, who leapt clean over the gate. In the hall he saw his brother Baldr in the seat of honour, and stayed the night. In the morning he asked Hel to let Baldr ride home, telling of the gods' grief. Hel said she would test whether Baldr was as beloved as they said: if all things in the world, alive and dead, wept for him, he would return to the Æsir; but if any refused to weep, he would stay with Hel. Baldr gave Hermóðr the ring Draupnir to take to Odin as a keepsake, and Nanna sent Frigg a linen kerchief and Fulla a gold ring.

beats.textZh: 赫尔莫德骑马回到阿斯加德，把他的所见所闻原原本本地告诉了众神。于是阿萨众神派出使者走遍全世界，请求万物为巴德尔哭泣，好让他从冥界回来。万物都哭了：人和动物、大地和石头、树木和各种金属都哭了——斯诺里说，就像你看见这些东西从严寒中被拿到温暖的地方时，身上会凝出水珠来一样。使者们走遍了天上和人间，所到之处，没有一样东西不在流泪。众神满怀希望，以为巴德尔就要回来了。可是，就在使者们办完差事、踏上归途的时候，他们经过了一个山洞——
beats.textEn: Hermóðr rode back and told all he had seen and heard. The Æsir sent messengers throughout the world asking that Baldr be wept out of Hel. All things did so — men and beasts, the earth and stones, trees and every metal — as you will have seen these things weep when they come out of frost into warmth.

beats.headingEn: The giantess who would not weep
beats.textZh: 使者们完成了使命，正在回家的路上，看见一个山洞里坐着一个女巨人，她自称叫作索克。他们请她也为巴德尔哭泣，让他从冥界回来。她回答说：索克要流干的眼泪，为巴德尔的火葬哭泣。不论他是活着还是死了，我从这老头的儿子身上什么好处也没得到。让赫尔留着她已经得到的吧！人们都认为，这个女巨人就是劳菲之子洛基变的，他给阿萨众神带来了最多的灾祸。巴德尔就这样留在了冥界。
beats.textEn: As the messengers were returning, having done their errand well, they found a giantess sitting in a cave who called herself Þökk. They asked her to weep Baldr out of Hel. She answered: Þökk will weep dry tears for Baldr's burning; alive or dead, the old man's son was no use to me — let Hel keep what she has. Men believe she was Loki Laufeyjarson, who had done the Æsir the most harm. And so Baldr remained in Hel.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 斯诺里说“人们认为”索克就是洛基，这是传统中的认定，不是故事中直接揭穿的情节。

beats.textZh: 众神对洛基怒不可遏，洛基逃到一座山上，盖了一间有四扇门的房子，好向四面八方都能看见。白天他常常变成一条鲑鱼，躲进法拉南格瀑布里。他坐在屋里想：阿萨众神会用什么办法来抓瀑布里的鲑鱼呢？他拿起亚麻线，像人们后来做网那样结了一张网。这时他看见众神已经来到不远处，奥丁从高座上望见了他的藏身之处。洛基赶快把网扔进火里烧掉，跳进河中。最聪明的神克瓦西尔第一个走进屋里，看见火中网的灰烬，明白这是捕鱼的工具，众神就照着灰烬的样子结了一张网。他们来到瀑布边撒网，索尔握住一头，其余的神握住另一头。洛基几次从网下、从网上逃脱，最后一次他想跳过网逃向大海，索尔在空中一把抓住了他，他滑溜溜地往外挣，索尔紧紧捏住他的尾巴——据说正因为这样，鲑鱼的尾巴才变得那么细。
beats.textEn: The gods were so angry that Loki fled and built a house with four doors on a mountain so he could watch every way, and by day he often hid as a salmon in the Fránangr falls. Wondering how the gods might catch him, he knotted linen into a net — the first net — and when he saw the gods coming, threw it in the fire and leapt into the river. Kvasir, wisest of the gods, saw the shape of the net in the ashes, and they made one like it. Dragging the falls with Thor at one end, they drove Loki until he tried to leap over the net; Thor caught him in mid-air and held him by the tail, which is why the salmon tapers at the tail.

beats.textZh: 众神把洛基带进一个山洞，竖起三块扁石，在每块石头上钻一个洞。他们抓来洛基的两个儿子瓦利和纳尔维，把瓦利变成一匹狼，狼把他的兄弟撕成了碎片。众神用纳尔维的肠子把洛基捆在三块石头上：一块抵着肩膀，一块抵着腰，一块抵着膝盖窝，那些肠子随后变成了铁。斯卡蒂拿来一条毒蛇，挂在洛基的头上方，让蛇的毒液滴在他脸上。洛基的妻子西格恩站在他身旁，手里捧着一只碗接住毒液；碗满了，她就走开去倒掉，这时毒液就滴在洛基的脸上，他痛得猛烈挣扎，整个大地都随之颤抖——这就是人们所说的地震。洛基就这样被捆着，一直躺到诸神的黄昏来临。
beats.textEn: The gods took Loki into a cave, set up three slabs on edge and bored a hole in each. They took his sons Váli and Nari (or Narfi); Váli was turned into a wolf and tore his brother apart, and with Nari's entrails they bound Loki over the stones — one under his shoulders, one under his loins, one under the backs of his knees — and the bonds became iron. Skaði hung a venomous snake above him so that its poison dripped onto his face. His wife Sigyn stands by holding a bowl under the venom, and when the bowl is full she goes to empty it; then the venom drips on his face and he shudders so violently that the whole earth shakes — what men call earthquakes. There he lies bound until Ragnarök.

deityStoryCards.name: Thrud
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 索尔与希芙之女；不是索尔的姐姐。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Daughter of Thor and Sif, not Thor’s sister.

beats.textZh: 希芙是斯露德的父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal identifies Thrud through Sif in its kinship terminology.

beats.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是斯露德的父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Thrud as a child of Thor.

deityStoryCards.name: Meili
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 古诺斯诗语与斯诺里材料称索尔为梅利之兄弟；资料仍极少。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Thor is called Meili’s brother in registered poetic and Snorrian witnesses; the dossier remains sparse.

beats.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔与梅利是兄弟姐妹。
beats.textEn: Old Norse poetic and Snorrian witness terminology calls Thor the brother of Meili.

beats.textZh: 诗语法提到梅利。
beats.textEn: Skáldskaparmál preserves Meili in Thor-kenning material.

deityStoryCards.name: Loki
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 古诺斯文本中的洛基；与索尔在多则叙事中互动，但兄弟关系只登记在现代改编层。古诺斯赫尔为洛基与安格尔波达之女。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Loki in Old Norse witnesses, interacting with Thor without an ancient sibling claim; Hel is Loki and Angrboda’s daughter in Snorri’s witness.

beats.textZh: 《索列姆之歌》把索尔置于寻找妙尔尼尔的中心位置。
beats.textEn: Thrymskvida places Thor at the center of the search for Mjolnir.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 当前版不扩写尚未逐节入库的情节。

beats.textZh: 洛基在诗中同行并提供建议；这项同伴关系不表示索尔与洛基是兄弟。
beats.textEn: Loki accompanies and advises him in the poem; this companionship does not make Thor and Loki brothers.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 保持亲属关系与故事同伴关系分离。

beats.textZh: 当前证据层确认两者共同处于妙尔尼尔寻回故事，但婚礼伪装与逐节行动尚未在本版本拆成独立Claims。
beats.textEn: The current evidence layer confirms both figures in the recovery story, while the wedding disguise and stanza-by-stanza actions have not yet been modeled as separate claims.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 详情将在后续逐节版本扩充。

facts.textZh: 洛基是赫尔的父母。
facts.textEn: Gylfaginning names Hel as a child of Loki and Angrboda.
facts.sourceTitle: Snorri Sturluson: Edda. Prologue and Gylfaginning

facts.textZh: 洛基——情节：learns of the unsworn mistletoe and pulls it up
facts.textEn: Disguised as a woman, Loki learns from Frigg that the young mistletoe west of Valhöll swore no oath, and pulls it up.

facts.textZh: 洛基——情节：as the giantess Þökk refuses to weep for Baldr
facts.textEn: A giantess named Þökk, believed to be Loki, alone refuses to weep for Baldr, so he remains in Hel.

facts.textZh: 洛基——情节：loses an eating contest to Logi
facts.textEn: Loki loses an eating contest to Logi, who devours the meat, the bones and the trough itself.

deityStoryCards.name: Lóðurr
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《女巫的预言》人类起源三神见证中的独立神祇；与 Loki 或 Vé 的同一说仅作待审研究问题。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Distinct deity in Völuspá; proposed identities with Loki or Vé remain unasserted research questions.

beats.textZh: 《女巫预言》17–18节在最初人类段落中分别命名阿斯克与恩布拉。
beats.textEn: Voluspa 17–18 names Ask and Embla in its first-human episode.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 当前中文概述不复制现代译文。

beats.textZh: 这段诗歌把奥丁、赫尼尔与洛杜尔放在同一创造人类场景中。
beats.textEn: The poetic passage places Odin, Hoenir, and Lodurr together in the human-creation scene.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 各神具体赐予项目将在逐词校勘后补充。

beats.textZh: 这里记录的是诗歌三神组合；《欺骗古鲁菲》的奥丁、维利、维组合不会覆盖它。
beats.textEn: This is the poetic triad; the Odin, Vili, and Ve grouping in Gylfaginning does not overwrite it.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 差异保持为版本并存，而非人物自动等同。

facts.textZh: 《女巫的预言》第17–18节见证提到洛杜尔。
facts.textEn: The passage names Lóðurr.

deityStoryCards.name: Heimdallr
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 住在彩虹桥边希敏约格的众神守望者，掌管加拉尔号角（《欺骗古鲁菲》第27章）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Watchman of the gods at Himinbjörg by Bifröst, keeper of Gjallarhorn (Gylfaginning 27).

beats.textZh: 海姆达尔是众神的守望者。他住在彩虹桥边一个叫希敏约格的地方，在天的尽头守着桥，防止山巨人闯进来。
beats.textEn: Heimdallr is the watchman of the gods. He lives at Himinbjörg by Bifröst, at the edge of heaven, guarding the bridge against the mountain-giants.

beats.textZh: 他需要的睡眠比鸟还少，无论白天黑夜都能看见一百里远；他还能听见草在地上生长、羊毛在羊身上生长的声音。
beats.textEn: He needs less sleep than a bird and sees a hundred leagues by day or night; he can hear grass growing in the ground and wool growing on sheep.

beats.headingZh: 加拉尔号角与九位母亲
beats.textZh: 海姆达尔有一支号角，叫加拉尔号角，吹响时所有世界都能听见。斯诺里还说，他是九位母亲的儿子，而这九位母亲是姐妹。
beats.textEn: Heimdallr has a horn called Gjallarhorn, whose blast is heard in all worlds. Snorri also says he is the son of nine mothers, who were sisters.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 九位母亲的名字见其他诗篇，本版不列出。

facts.textZh: 海姆达尔居于希敏约格。
facts.textEn: Heimdallr lives at Himinbjörg by Bifröst.

facts.textZh: 海姆达尔——来历：son of nine mothers, who were sisters
facts.textEn: Heimdallr is called the son of nine mothers, who were sisters.

deityStoryCards.name: Thor
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 索尔／Þórr：古诺斯文本中的锤持有者、巨人对手与家谱节点；本版补齐父母、配偶、子女、梅利与洛基文本关系。洛基并非古诺斯层兄弟。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Thor in registered Old Norse witnesses, now linked to source-specific parents, spouse, children, Meili and Loki episodes; Loki is not his Old Norse brother.

beats.headingEn: The goats raised from their bones
beats.textZh: 有一次，索尔驾着他的山羊车出门，洛基与他同行。傍晚他们来到一个农夫家里借宿。索尔把两只山羊宰了，剥了皮，放进大锅里煮，又邀请农夫一家和他们一起吃。他把羊皮铺在火塘边，吩咐农夫一家把骨头都丢在羊皮上。农夫的儿子夏尔菲却拿着一根羊腿骨，用刀把它劈开，去吸里面的骨髓。第二天天还没亮，索尔起身穿好衣服，拿起锤子妙尔尼尔举在羊皮上方祝圣，两只山羊就站了起来——可是其中一只的后腿瘸了。索尔发现后，说一定是有人不小心弄断了骨头。他皱起眉头，双手紧握锤柄，指节都发白了。农夫一家吓得魂不附体，哭着求饶，愿意拿出全部家产来赔偿。索尔看见他们这么害怕，怒气消了，便收下农夫的一儿一女——夏尔菲和罗斯克娃作为赔偿，从此他们一直做索尔的仆人。
beats.textEn: Thor once drove out in his goat chariot with Loki and lodged at a farmer's. He slaughtered his goats, boiled them, and invited the household to eat, telling them to throw the bones onto the goatskins spread by the fire. The farmer's son Þjálfi split a thigh bone for the marrow. Before dawn Thor raised his hammer Mjöllnir over the skins and blessed them, and the goats stood up — but one was lame in a hind leg. Thor frowned and gripped the hammer until his knuckles whitened; the terrified family offered all they had. His anger cooled, and he took the farmer's children, Þjálfi and Röskva, as his servants.

beats.textZh: 索尔把山羊留在农夫家，带着洛基、夏尔菲和罗斯克娃向东走，渡过深深的大海，来到巨人之国约顿海姆。天快黑时，他们走进一片大森林，找到一座很大的房子，门有房子那么宽，他们就在里面过夜。到了半夜，大地剧烈地震动，房子摇晃起来。索尔叫同伴们躲进房子侧面的一间小屋里，自己握着锤柄守在门口。天亮后索尔走出去，看见不远处躺着一个大汉正在睡觉，鼾声如雷——原来夜里的震动就是他的鼾声。这时大汉醒了，站起身来，个子高得索尔都不敢用锤子打他，只问他叫什么。大汉说：我叫斯克里米尔，我当然知道你是阿萨神族的索尔。你们把我的手套拿到哪里去了？他弯腰拾起手套——原来他们过夜的“房子”就是他的手套，那间小侧屋是手套的大拇指。
beats.textEn: Leaving the goats, Thor went east with Loki, Þjálfi and Röskva across the deep sea into Jötunheimr. At nightfall they sheltered in a great hall in a forest, its doorway as wide as the hall. At midnight the earth shook, and they crept into a side chamber while Thor guarded the door. In the morning Thor found a huge man asleep nearby, snoring — the cause of the quake. The giant woke and named himself Skrýmir, knew Thor at once, and asked where they had taken his glove. He picked it up: the hall they had slept in was his glove, and the side chamber its thumb.

beats.headingZh: 解不开的口袋，打不醒的巨人
beats.headingEn: A bag he could not open, a giant he could not wake
beats.textZh: 斯克里米尔提议和他们结伴同行，把干粮合在一起，装进他的一个口袋里背着。晚上他们在一棵大橡树下歇脚，斯克里米尔说自己要先睡，让索尔他们自己打开口袋吃晚饭，说完就倒头鼾声大作。索尔去解口袋，可是无论怎么用力，一个结也解不开，一根绳也拉不松。他大怒，抡起锤子朝斯克里米尔的头上砸去。巨人醒来问：是不是有片树叶掉在我头上了？你们吃过饭了吗？半夜他鼾声又起，索尔再次用尽全力，把锤子砸进他的头顶。巨人又醒来问：是不是有颗橡果掉在我头上了？天快亮时，索尔第三次挥锤，锤头一直没到柄。斯克里米尔坐起来摸摸脸说：树上是不是有鸟？我好像觉得有鸟粪落在脸上。临别时，他告诫他们：乌特加尔城里的人个子都比我高，到了那里不要太夸口，最好还是回头。说完他便背着口袋往北走了。
beats.textEn: Skrýmir proposed they travel together and put all the provisions in his bag. That evening under an oak he went to sleep, telling them to help themselves. Thor could not loosen a single knot. Furious, he struck the giant's head with his hammer; Skrýmir woke and asked whether a leaf had fallen on him. At midnight Thor struck again, driving the hammer deep; the giant asked whether an acorn had dropped. Near dawn Thor struck a third time, burying the hammer to the handle; Skrýmir sat up wondering if a bird had soiled his face. Parting, he warned them that the men of Útgarðr were bigger than he, and they had better turn back.

beats.textZh: 索尔一行继续前进，中午时分看见平原上矗立着一座城堡，高得他们要把头仰到脖子贴着后背才能看到顶。城门锁着，索尔打不开，他们便从栅栏的空隙里挤了进去。里面是一座大厅，门开着，长凳上坐着许多非常高大的人。他们来到国王乌特加尔洛基面前问候，国王慢条斯理地瞥了他们一眼，咧嘴一笑说：从远方来的消息总是迟到，莫非这个小家伙就是驾车的索尔？也许你比看上去要厉害些。你们有什么本事？在我们这里，若没有一样本领胜过别人，谁也不许留下。
beats.textEn: They went on and at noon saw a stronghold on a plain so tall that they had to bend their heads back to their spines to see over it. The gate was locked, so they squeezed between the bars. In the hall sat many huge men on benches. They greeted King Útgarða-Loki, who looked at them slowly and grinned: news travels slowly from far away, he said — could this little lad be Thor the charioteer? Perhaps he was greater than he looked. No one, he said, might stay there who was not master of some art.

beats.textZh: 站在最后面的洛基先开口说：我有一样本领，敢和人比赛——没有人能比我吃得更快。乌特加尔洛基说：若你做得到，那倒是一项本领，我们试试看。他叫一个坐在长凳尽头、名叫洛吉的人出来和洛基比赛。人们把一个大木槽抬进大厅，里面装满了肉。洛基坐在一头，洛吉坐在另一头，两人拼命地吃，在木槽中间碰了头。洛基把肉都吃光了，只剩下骨头；而洛吉把肉、骨头连同木槽一起都吃掉了。大家都说洛基输了。
beats.textEn: Loki, standing last, said he could eat faster than anyone. Útgarða-Loki called a man named Logi from the end of the bench. A trough full of meat was set on the floor; Loki sat at one end and Logi at the other, and each ate as fast as he could until they met in the middle. Loki had eaten all the meat off the bones, but Logi had eaten the meat, the bones and the trough as well. All agreed that Loki had lost.

beats.textZh: 乌特加尔洛基又问那个年轻人会什么。夏尔菲说，他愿意和任何人比赛跑步。国王说这是一项好本领，带大家来到一片适合赛跑的平地，叫来一个名叫胡吉的小个子年轻人和夏尔菲比赛。第一趟，胡吉跑到终点后回头，刚好迎面撞上夏尔菲；国王说：夏尔菲，你得再加把劲，不过从来还没有人比你跑得更快到过这里。第二趟，胡吉到达终点回头时，夏尔菲还差一箭之地。第三趟，夏尔菲跑得比前两次都快，可是胡吉已经到了终点回头，夏尔菲还没跑到一半。大家都说这场比赛已经分出了胜负。
beats.textEn: Asked what the young man could do, Þjálfi offered to race anyone. The king led them to a good running course and called a small young man named Hugi. In the first heat Hugi was so far ahead that he turned at the finish and met Þjálfi coming; in the second Þjálfi was a long bowshot behind; in the third, though Þjálfi ran faster than ever, Hugi had reached the end and turned back before Þjálfi was halfway. All agreed the contest was decided.

beats.headingEn: The horn that would not empty
beats.textZh: 国王问索尔愿意表演什么本领，人们都说他是个大英雄。索尔说他最愿意比喝酒。乌特加尔洛基叫侍从拿来他的部下饮罚酒用的角杯，说：谁若能一口气喝干这只角杯，就算是好酒量；有人要喝两口；但没有一个人差到三口还喝不干。索尔看那角杯并不很大，只是很长，他口渴得很，便把嘴凑上去大口猛喝，以为不必再弯第二次腰。可是等他喘不过气抬起头一看，杯里的酒几乎没有少。国王说：喝得不错，可也不算多，我真没想到阿萨神族的索尔只能喝这么一点。索尔又喝第二口，用尽全力，酒面下去得比上次还少，只是可以端着走而不洒出来。第三口他喝得更猛，酒面虽然明显下降，角杯却仍然远远没有喝干。索尔把角杯推开，再也不肯喝了。
beats.textEn: Asked for his feat, Thor chose drinking. A long horn was brought, from which the king's men drink as a penalty: a good drinker empties it in one draught, some in two, and none is so poor he cannot in three. It did not look large, and Thor, very thirsty, drank deeply, expecting not to need a second draught; but when he looked, the level had hardly changed. The king teased him. Thor drank a second time with all his strength, and the level fell even less — only enough that the horn could be carried without spilling. A third mighty draught lowered it noticeably, yet it was far from empty, and Thor gave up.

beats.textZh: 乌特加尔洛基说：现在很清楚，你的力气并不像我们想象的那么大。你愿不愿意试试别的游戏？索尔说：我愿意试试。不过在阿萨神族那里，这样的几口酒可不算少。你还有什么游戏？国王说：我们这里的年轻人有一种不值一提的小把戏，就是把我的猫从地上举起来。我原本不会对阿萨神族的索尔提这种事，要不是我看出你远没有我想的那么了不起。这时一只灰色的大猫跳到大厅的地板上。索尔走过去，一只手抱住猫的肚子往上举，可是他举得越高，猫就把背弓得越高；索尔把手伸到最高处，猫也只抬起了一只脚。国王说：果然不出我所料，这只猫很大，而索尔又矮又小，和我们这里的大个子比起来差得远呢。
beats.textEn: Útgarða-Loki remarked that Thor was clearly not as strong as they had thought, and offered a game the young men play, of little account: lifting his cat. A large grey cat leapt onto the floor. Thor put his hand under its belly and lifted, but the higher he raised his arm, the more the cat arched its back, and when he stretched up as far as he could, the cat lifted only one foot from the floor. Just as he expected, said the king: the cat is large, and Thor is short and small beside the great men here.

beats.textZh: 索尔大怒道：你们既然说我矮小，那就叫个人出来和我摔跤吧，我现在正发着火呢！乌特加尔洛基环顾长凳说：我看这里没有人不会觉得和你摔跤有失身份。不过，去把我的乳母埃利老婆婆叫来，索尔就和她摔吧，她曾经摔倒过不少看起来比索尔还强壮的人。不一会儿，一个年迈的老妇人走进大厅。两人扭在一起，索尔抓得越紧，老妇人站得越稳。她开始反扑，索尔脚下不稳，扭斗得非常激烈，没过多久，索尔就被摔得单膝跪地。乌特加尔洛基走过来叫他们停手，说索尔不必再和他的部下摔跤了。这时夜已经深了，国王给他们安排了座位，他们在那里受到款待，度过了一夜。
beats.textEn: Angry, Thor demanded someone to wrestle. The king said none of his men would stoop to it, but called his old nurse Elli, who had thrown men who seemed stronger than Thor. An aged woman came in. The harder Thor gripped, the firmer she stood; then she began to throw him, and before long Thor went down on one knee. Útgarða-Loki stopped the bout, saying Thor need not wrestle anyone else. Night had fallen, and they were given seats and good hospitality.

beats.textZh: 第二天清晨，索尔一行准备上路，乌特加尔洛基亲自送他们出城。分别时他问索尔对这趟旅程有什么想法，索尔说：我只能说自己受了奇耻大辱。国王说：既然你已经出了城，我就说实话吧——只要我活着，你就再也进不来了。你们一路上都被我的幻术骗了。那个斯克里米尔就是我，我用铁丝捆住了口袋，你当然解不开。你三次挥锤，第一下最轻，若真打中，我早就死了；我把一座石山挡在面前，你看那边山里三道方形的山谷，就是你锤子留下的。洛基比吃的对手洛吉，其实是野火，它把木槽也一起烧光了；和夏尔菲赛跑的胡吉，是我的思想，谁也跑不过思想。你喝的角杯，另一头连着大海，你喝下去的地方，从此就是海水的退潮。那只猫是盘绕世界、首尾相衔的世界之蛇，你把它举到几乎碰到天，我们都吓坏了。你摔跤的埃利是衰老，从来没有人——将来也不会有人——能不被衰老打倒。
beats.textEn: In the morning Útgarða-Loki escorted them out and, beyond the walls, told the truth: he had deceived them with illusions and would never let Thor in again. He himself had been Skrýmir, and had tied the bag with iron wire; the hammer blows would have killed him had he not set a mountain in the way — the three square valleys in it were the marks. Logi was wildfire, which burned the trough too; Hugi was his thought, which no one can outrun. The horn's end lay in the sea, and Thor's drinking caused the ebb tides. The cat was the Midgard Serpent, which Thor had lifted almost to the sky; and Elli was old age, which overthrows everyone.

beats.textZh: 乌特加尔洛基接着说：现在我们分手吧，你们最好别再来找我，我会用同样的幻术来保护我的城堡，让你们对我无可奈何。索尔听完，一把抓起锤子高高举起，想要砸下去——可是乌特加尔洛基已经不见了。他转身想回去捣毁城堡，只见眼前是一片辽阔美丽的平原，根本没有城堡的踪影。于是索尔掉头回去，一路走回了斯鲁德万。古鲁菲听到这里，问道：索尔后来有没有为这次受辱报仇？讲述的人回答：索尔心里早就打定主意，要找机会再去会一会世界之蛇。
beats.textEn: Útgarða-Loki bade them part and never return, for he would defend his stronghold with such tricks again. Thor seized his hammer and swung it up — but the giant was gone, and when he turned to destroy the stronghold he saw only wide, fair plains and no castle at all. So Thor went home to Þrúðvangar, resolved to meet the Midgard Serpent again.

beats.textZh: 没过多久，索尔装扮成一个年轻人，独自来到巨人希米尔家里借宿。第二天希米尔要出海钓鱼，索尔说要同去。希米尔叫他自己去找鱼饵，索尔就扭下希米尔牛群里最大的一头黑牛“天空撞击者”的牛头，带上了船。索尔划桨划得飞快，远远越过了希米尔平常钓比目鱼的地方，希米尔害怕地说再往前就有世界之蛇了。索尔在一根结实的钓线上挂了一个大钩，把牛头穿上去抛进海里。世界之蛇咬住了牛头，鱼钩扎进它的上颚，它猛地一挣，索尔的两只拳头都撞在了船舷上。索尔使出神力，双脚踩穿船底，抵住海床，把蛇一直拉到船边。索尔怒目瞪着它，世界之蛇也向他喷吐毒液。就在索尔举起锤子的那一刻，吓得脸色发白的希米尔拔刀割断了钓线，大蛇沉回海里。索尔把锤子朝它扔去，有人说锤子打掉了它的头；可是讲述的人说，真相是世界之蛇仍然活着，盘踞在环绕世界的海里。索尔一拳把希米尔打下了船，自己蹚水回到了岸上。
beats.textEn: Soon after, Thor, disguised as a young man, lodged with the giant Hymir and insisted on going fishing with him. For bait he tore the head off Hymir's largest ox, Himinhrjótr. He rowed far beyond Hymir's fishing grounds, out where the Midgard Serpent lies, baited a great hook with the ox head and cast it. The Serpent took it, and the hook caught in its jaw; it pulled so hard that Thor's fists struck the gunwale. Thor braced his feet through the bottom of the boat on the sea-bed and hauled the Serpent up, and they glared at each other as it spat poison. As Thor raised his hammer, the terrified Hymir cut the line, and the Serpent sank. Some say Thor's hammer struck off its head, but in truth it still lives in the encircling sea. Thor knocked Hymir overboard and waded ashore.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 斯诺里说“有人说”锤子打掉了蛇头，但他认为世界之蛇仍然活着；两种说法本站都保留。

deityStoryCards.name: Freyja
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 尼奥尔德之女；住在弗尔克范格，分得一半战死者，乘两只猫拉的车（《欺骗古鲁菲》第24章）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Daughter of Njörðr; lives at Fólkvangr, takes half the slain and drives a chariot drawn by two cats (Gylfaginning 24).

beats.textZh: 尼奥尔德住在天上一个叫诺欧通的地方。他掌管风的运行，能平息海浪和火焰；出海航行和捕鱼的人都向他祈祷。他在华纳海姆长大，后来作为人质被送到阿萨神族。
beats.textEn: Njörðr lives in heaven at a place called Nóatún. He rules the motion of the wind and can calm sea and fire; those who sail or fish pray to him. He was raised in Vanaheim and later given to the Æsir as a hostage.

beats.textZh: 尼奥尔德有一儿一女。儿子弗雷掌管雨水、阳光和大地的收成，人们向他祈求丰年与富足。女儿芙蕾雅住在弗尔克范格，每当她骑马出战，就分得一半战死者，另一半归奥丁；她乘坐的车由两只猫拉着。
beats.textEn: Njörðr has a son and a daughter. Freyr rules rain, sunshine and the produce of the earth, and people pray to him for good seasons and wealth. Freyja lives at Fólkvangr; whenever she rides to battle she takes half the slain, Odin the other half, and her chariot is drawn by two cats.

beats.textZh: 后来，弗雷爱上了巨人之女葛德。为了娶到她，他把自己的宝剑交给了别人作为代价——这把剑从此不在他手中。
beats.textEn: Later Freyr falls in love with Gerðr, a giant's daughter. To win her he gives away his sword as the price, and the sword is no longer his.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 葛德尚未单独建立实体；诸神黄昏中的后果另行登记。

facts.textZh: 芙蕾雅是尼奥尔德的孩子。
facts.textEn: Njörðr's daughter is Freyja.

facts.textZh: 弗雷与芙蕾雅是兄弟姐妹。
facts.textEn: Freyr and Freyja are the children of Njörðr.

facts.textZh: 芙蕾雅——使用：a chariot drawn by two cats
facts.textEn: Freyja drives a chariot drawn by two cats.

facts.textZh: 芙蕾雅居于弗尔克范格。
facts.textEn: Freyja's dwelling is Fólkvangr.

deityStoryCards.name: Modi
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 索尔之子；当前所用家谱见证没有明确登记其母亲。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Thor; the registered genealogy witness does not name his mother.

beats.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是莫迪的父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Modi as a child of Thor.

deityStoryCards.name: Sigyn
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Loki's wife, who holds a bowl to catch the serpent's venom over the bound Loki (Gylfaginning 50).

beats.textZh: 奥丁的儿子巴德尔是众神中最好的一位，人人都称赞他。他容貌俊美、光彩照人，有一种最白的花就因为像他的睫毛那样白，被人们称作“巴德尔的睫毛”。他是阿萨神族中最聪明、最善于言辞、最仁慈的神，可是他的判决却从来不能实现。这一天，巴德尔做了几个可怕的梦，梦见自己的性命将要遭到危险。他把这些梦告诉了阿萨众神，众神聚在一起商议，最后决定：要为巴德尔求得一切东西的保护，使他免受任何伤害。
beats.textEn: Baldr, Odin's son, is the best of the gods and all praise him; so fair and bright that the whitest flower is called Baldr's brow. He is the wisest, most eloquent and most merciful of the Æsir, though none of his judgements can be fulfilled. Then Baldr dreamed great and perilous dreams threatening his life, and when he told the Æsir they took counsel together and resolved to ask protection for him from every kind of danger.

beats.textZh: 于是弗丽嘉出发，让世间万物都立下誓言，不伤害巴德尔：火与水、铁和各种金属、石头、泥土、树木、疾病、走兽、飞鸟、毒物和蛇，全都发了誓。这件事办成之后，众神都放下心来，并且以此为乐：巴德尔站在集会的场地中央，其他的神有的向他射箭，有的用刀剑砍他，有的向他扔石头，可是无论做什么都伤不了他。众神都认为这是一件了不起的荣耀。
beats.textEn: Frigg took oaths that they would not harm Baldr from fire and water, iron and every metal, stones, the earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds, poison and snakes. When this was done it became a sport of the Æsir: Baldr would stand in the assembly while some shot at him, some struck at him and some threw stones, and nothing harmed him. They all thought it a great honour.

beats.textZh: 劳菲之子洛基看见这一切，心里很不高兴，因为巴德尔毫发无伤。他变成一个女人，来到弗丽嘉住的芬萨利尔宫。弗丽嘉问这位女子：你知道阿萨众神在集会上做什么吗？女人说：他们都在朝巴德尔射箭、扔东西，可是什么也伤不了他。弗丽嘉说：不论是兵器还是木头，都伤不了巴德尔，因为我已经让万物都立了誓。女人问：真的万物都向你发誓不伤害巴德尔了吗？弗丽嘉答道：在瓦尔哈拉的西边，长着一棵小小的树苗，叫作槲寄生。我觉得它太年幼了，就没有让它发誓。那女人听了便走了。洛基找到槲寄生，把它拔下来，带到集会的地方去。
beats.textEn: Loki Laufeyjarson was displeased that Baldr took no harm. He went to Frigg at Fensalir in the likeness of a woman. Frigg told the stranger that neither weapons nor trees would harm Baldr, for she had taken oaths of all things. Had everything sworn? asked the woman. Frigg answered that a young shoot grew west of Valhöll called mistletoe, which seemed too young to ask for an oath. The woman went away; Loki took the mistletoe, pulled it up and went to the assembly.

beats.textZh: 霍德尔站在人圈的外面，因为他是瞎子。洛基走过去问他：你为什么不朝巴德尔扔东西？霍德尔说：因为我看不见巴德尔在哪里，而且我也没有武器。洛基说：你也该像别人一样向巴德尔表示敬意。我来给你指方向，你把这根树枝向他扔去吧。霍德尔接过槲寄生，照着洛基的指引朝巴德尔扔去。树枝穿透了巴德尔的身体，他倒在地上死了。斯诺里说：这是神和人所遭遇的最大不幸。
beats.textEn: Höðr stood at the edge of the ring, for he was blind. Loki asked why he did not shoot at Baldr. Because I cannot see where he is, said Höðr, and I have no weapon. Loki said he should honour Baldr like the others, and offered to show him where Baldr stood. Höðr took the mistletoe and threw it as Loki directed; it pierced Baldr and he fell dead to the earth. It was, says Snorri, the greatest misfortune ever to befall gods and men.

beats.textZh: 巴德尔倒下的时候，阿萨众神都说不出话来，双手也失去了力气，不能把他扶起。他们彼此相望，心里都知道是谁干了这件事，却不能在那里报仇，因为那是一处圣地。他们想说话的时候，涌出的只有泪水，没有一个神能把自己的悲痛告诉别人。在所有的神中，奥丁最承受不住这个打击，因为他最明白，巴德尔的死对阿萨众神意味着多大的损失与毁灭。
beats.textEn: When Baldr fell, the Æsir were struck dumb and their hands failed them to lift him. Each looked at the other, all of one mind about who had done the deed, but no vengeance could be taken there, for it was a place of great sanctuary. When they tried to speak, weeping came first, and none could tell the others his grief. Odin bore the loss worst of all, for he best understood how great a loss and ruin Baldr's death was for the Æsir.

beats.textZh: 众神稍稍平静之后，弗丽嘉开口问道：阿萨神族中有谁愿意赢得我全部的爱与恩宠，骑马走上通往冥界的路，去找赫尔，问她要多少赎金才肯让巴德尔回到阿斯加德？奥丁的儿子、勇敢的赫尔莫德说他愿意去。于是众神牵来奥丁的八足骏马斯莱布尼尔，交给赫尔莫德。他跃上马背，向冥界疾驰而去。这是众神在巨大的悲痛中想到的唯一办法：如果冥界的女王肯收下赎金，巴德尔也许还能回来。赫尔莫德的马蹄声远去了，而留在阿斯加德的众神，还要先为巴德尔送行。
beats.textEn: When the gods came to themselves, Frigg asked who among the Æsir would win all her love and favour by riding the road to Hel to find Baldr and offer Hel a ransom to let him come home to Ásgarðr. Hermóðr the Bold, Odin's son, undertook the journey. Odin's horse Sleipnir was led out, and Hermóðr mounted and galloped away.

beats.textZh: 阿萨众神抬起巴德尔的尸体，送到海边。巴德尔的船叫作“灵钟号”，是所有船中最大的一艘，众神想把它推下海，在船上为巴德尔举行火葬，可是船纹丝不动。他们只好派人到巨人之国去请一个名叫希罗金的女巨人来帮忙。她骑着一头狼来了，用毒蛇作缰绳。她跳下狼背，奥丁叫四个狂战士看住那头狼，他们只能把它摔倒才制服它。希罗金走到船头，只一推就把船推下了海，船底的滚木冒出火花，大地都颤抖起来。索尔大怒，握住锤子要打碎她的头，众神都为她求情，他才住手。巴德尔的遗体被抬上船，他的妻子南娜看见了，悲痛得心都碎了，当场死去，也被放上柴堆一起焚烧。索尔站在火堆前用妙尔尼尔为它祝圣，一个名叫利特的矮人从他脚前跑过，索尔一脚把他踢进了火里。奥丁把金环德罗普尼尔放在柴堆上，巴德尔的马也带着全套马具被送上火堆。
beats.textEn: The Æsir carried Baldr's body to the sea. His ship Hringhorni was the greatest of all ships, but they could not launch it, so they sent to Jötunheimr for the giantess Hyrrokkin, who came riding a wolf with vipers for reins. Four berserks could hold the wolf only by knocking it down. She pushed the ship off with one shove, so that fire flew from the rollers and the earth shook; Thor would have smashed her head had the gods not begged for her. When Baldr was laid on board, his wife Nanna's heart burst with grief, and she was laid on the pyre with him. Thor hallowed the pyre with Mjöllnir and kicked the dwarf Litr into the flames; Odin laid the ring Draupnir on the pyre, and Baldr's horse was burned with all its harness.

beats.textZh: 赫尔莫德骑着马走了九天九夜，穿过幽深黑暗的山谷，什么也看不见，直到来到冥河耶尔河边，骑上了铺着闪亮黄金的耶尔桥。守桥的少女名叫莫德古德，她问他的名字和家族，说：昨天有五队死人从这座桥上过去，可是桥被你一个人震得比他们全体还响；而且你的脸色不像死人。你为什么骑马走在通往冥界的路上？赫尔莫德说：我要去冥界找巴德尔。你有没有在路上见过他？莫德古德说：巴德尔已经骑马过了耶尔桥。通往冥界的路，就在下面，往北边去。
beats.textEn: For nine nights Hermóðr rode through dark, deep valleys where he could see nothing, until he came to the river Gjöll and rode onto the Gjallarbrú, roofed with gleaming gold. The maiden who guarded the bridge, Móðguðr, asked his name and lineage: the day before, five companies of dead men had ridden over, yet the bridge thundered more under him alone, and he did not have the colour of the dead. He said he was riding to Hel to seek Baldr; she told him Baldr had crossed the bridge, and that the road to Hel lay downward and to the north.

beats.textZh: 赫尔莫德一路骑到冥界的大门前，他跳下马，把马肚带勒紧，重新上马，用马刺一踢，骏马高高跃起，从大门上方越了过去，一点也没碰到。他骑到大殿前下了马，走进去，看见他的哥哥巴德尔坐在高座上。赫尔莫德在那里过了一夜。第二天早晨，他请求赫尔让巴德尔和他一起骑马回家，并告诉她阿萨众神为巴德尔哭得多么伤心。赫尔说：我要看看巴德尔是不是真的像人们说的那样受到爱戴。如果世上的一切东西，活的和死的，都为他哭泣，他就可以回到阿萨众神那里；可是只要有一样东西反对、不肯哭泣，他就得留在冥界。赫尔莫德起身告辞，巴德尔送他出殿，把金环德罗普尼尔交给他，让他带回去给奥丁作纪念；南娜也送给弗丽嘉一块亚麻头巾和其他礼物，还送给弗丽嘉的侍女富拉一枚金指环。
beats.textEn: At Hel's gate Hermóðr dismounted, tightened the girth, remounted and spurred Sleipnir, who leapt clean over the gate. In the hall he saw his brother Baldr in the seat of honour, and stayed the night. In the morning he asked Hel to let Baldr ride home, telling of the gods' grief. Hel said she would test whether Baldr was as beloved as they said: if all things in the world, alive and dead, wept for him, he would return to the Æsir; but if any refused to weep, he would stay with Hel. Baldr gave Hermóðr the ring Draupnir to take to Odin as a keepsake, and Nanna sent Frigg a linen kerchief and Fulla a gold ring.

beats.textZh: 赫尔莫德骑马回到阿斯加德，把他的所见所闻原原本本地告诉了众神。于是阿萨众神派出使者走遍全世界，请求万物为巴德尔哭泣，好让他从冥界回来。万物都哭了：人和动物、大地和石头、树木和各种金属都哭了——斯诺里说，就像你看见这些东西从严寒中被拿到温暖的地方时，身上会凝出水珠来一样。使者们走遍了天上和人间，所到之处，没有一样东西不在流泪。众神满怀希望，以为巴德尔就要回来了。可是，就在使者们办完差事、踏上归途的时候，他们经过了一个山洞——
beats.textEn: Hermóðr rode back and told all he had seen and heard. The Æsir sent messengers throughout the world asking that Baldr be wept out of Hel. All things did so — men and beasts, the earth and stones, trees and every metal — as you will have seen these things weep when they come out of frost into warmth.

beats.headingEn: The giantess who would not weep
beats.textZh: 使者们完成了使命，正在回家的路上，看见一个山洞里坐着一个女巨人，她自称叫作索克。他们请她也为巴德尔哭泣，让他从冥界回来。她回答说：索克要流干的眼泪，为巴德尔的火葬哭泣。不论他是活着还是死了，我从这老头的儿子身上什么好处也没得到。让赫尔留着她已经得到的吧！人们都认为，这个女巨人就是劳菲之子洛基变的，他给阿萨众神带来了最多的灾祸。巴德尔就这样留在了冥界。
beats.textEn: As the messengers were returning, having done their errand well, they found a giantess sitting in a cave who called herself Þökk. They asked her to weep Baldr out of Hel. She answered: Þökk will weep dry tears for Baldr's burning; alive or dead, the old man's son was no use to me — let Hel keep what she has. Men believe she was Loki Laufeyjarson, who had done the Æsir the most harm. And so Baldr remained in Hel.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 斯诺里说“人们认为”索克就是洛基，这是传统中的认定，不是故事中直接揭穿的情节。

beats.textZh: 众神对洛基怒不可遏，洛基逃到一座山上，盖了一间有四扇门的房子，好向四面八方都能看见。白天他常常变成一条鲑鱼，躲进法拉南格瀑布里。他坐在屋里想：阿萨众神会用什么办法来抓瀑布里的鲑鱼呢？他拿起亚麻线，像人们后来做网那样结了一张网。这时他看见众神已经来到不远处，奥丁从高座上望见了他的藏身之处。洛基赶快把网扔进火里烧掉，跳进河中。最聪明的神克瓦西尔第一个走进屋里，看见火中网的灰烬，明白这是捕鱼的工具，众神就照着灰烬的样子结了一张网。他们来到瀑布边撒网，索尔握住一头，其余的神握住另一头。洛基几次从网下、从网上逃脱，最后一次他想跳过网逃向大海，索尔在空中一把抓住了他，他滑溜溜地往外挣，索尔紧紧捏住他的尾巴——据说正因为这样，鲑鱼的尾巴才变得那么细。
beats.textEn: The gods were so angry that Loki fled and built a house with four doors on a mountain so he could watch every way, and by day he often hid as a salmon in the Fránangr falls. Wondering how the gods might catch him, he knotted linen into a net — the first net — and when he saw the gods coming, threw it in the fire and leapt into the river. Kvasir, wisest of the gods, saw the shape of the net in the ashes, and they made one like it. Dragging the falls with Thor at one end, they drove Loki until he tried to leap over the net; Thor caught him in mid-air and held him by the tail, which is why the salmon tapers at the tail.

beats.textZh: 众神把洛基带进一个山洞，竖起三块扁石，在每块石头上钻一个洞。他们抓来洛基的两个儿子瓦利和纳尔维，把瓦利变成一匹狼，狼把他的兄弟撕成了碎片。众神用纳尔维的肠子把洛基捆在三块石头上：一块抵着肩膀，一块抵着腰，一块抵着膝盖窝，那些肠子随后变成了铁。斯卡蒂拿来一条毒蛇，挂在洛基的头上方，让蛇的毒液滴在他脸上。洛基的妻子西格恩站在他身旁，手里捧着一只碗接住毒液；碗满了，她就走开去倒掉，这时毒液就滴在洛基的脸上，他痛得猛烈挣扎，整个大地都随之颤抖——这就是人们所说的地震。洛基就这样被捆着，一直躺到诸神的黄昏来临。
beats.textEn: The gods took Loki into a cave, set up three slabs on edge and bored a hole in each. They took his sons Váli and Nari (or Narfi); Váli was turned into a wolf and tore his brother apart, and with Nari's entrails they bound Loki over the stones — one under his shoulders, one under his loins, one under the backs of his knees — and the bonds became iron. Skaði hung a venomous snake above him so that its poison dripped onto his face. His wife Sigyn stands by holding a bowl under the venom, and when the bowl is full she goes to empty it; then the venom drips on his face and he shudders so violently that the whole earth shakes — what men call earthquakes. There he lies bound until Ragnarök.

beats.textZh: 奥丁的儿子巴德尔是众神中最好的一位，人人都称赞他。他容貌俊美、光彩照人，有一种最白的花就因为像他的睫毛那样白，被人们称作“巴德尔的睫毛”。他是阿萨神族中最聪明、最善于言辞、最仁慈的神，可是他的判决却从来不能实现。这一天，巴德尔做了几个可怕的梦，梦见自己的性命将要遭到危险。他把这些梦告诉了阿萨众神，众神聚在一起商议，最后决定：要为巴德尔求得一切东西的保护，使他免受任何伤害。
beats.textEn: Baldr, Odin's son, is the best of the gods and all praise him; so fair and bright that the whitest flower is called Baldr's brow. He is the wisest, most eloquent and most merciful of the Æsir, though none of his judgements can be fulfilled. Then Baldr dreamed great and perilous dreams threatening his life, and when he told the Æsir they took counsel together and resolved to ask protection for him from every kind of danger.

beats.textZh: 于是弗丽嘉出发，让世间万物都立下誓言，不伤害巴德尔：火与水、铁和各种金属、石头、泥土、树木、疾病、走兽、飞鸟、毒物和蛇，全都发了誓。这件事办成之后，众神都放下心来，并且以此为乐：巴德尔站在集会的场地中央，其他的神有的向他射箭，有的用刀剑砍他，有的向他扔石头，可是无论做什么都伤不了他。众神都认为这是一件了不起的荣耀。
beats.textEn: Frigg took oaths that they would not harm Baldr from fire and water, iron and every metal, stones, the earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds, poison and snakes. When this was done it became a sport of the Æsir: Baldr would stand in the assembly while some shot at him, some struck at him and some threw stones, and nothing harmed him. They all thought it a great honour.

beats.textZh: 劳菲之子洛基看见这一切，心里很不高兴，因为巴德尔毫发无伤。他变成一个女人，来到弗丽嘉住的芬萨利尔宫。弗丽嘉问这位女子：你知道阿萨众神在集会上做什么吗？女人说：他们都在朝巴德尔射箭、扔东西，可是什么也伤不了他。弗丽嘉说：不论是兵器还是木头，都伤不了巴德尔，因为我已经让万物都立了誓。女人问：真的万物都向你发誓不伤害巴德尔了吗？弗丽嘉答道：在瓦尔哈拉的西边，长着一棵小小的树苗，叫作槲寄生。我觉得它太年幼了，就没有让它发誓。那女人听了便走了。洛基找到槲寄生，把它拔下来，带到集会的地方去。
beats.textEn: Loki Laufeyjarson was displeased that Baldr took no harm. He went to Frigg at Fensalir in the likeness of a woman. Frigg told the stranger that neither weapons nor trees would harm Baldr, for she had taken oaths of all things. Had everything sworn? asked the woman. Frigg answered that a young shoot grew west of Valhöll called mistletoe, which seemed too young to ask for an oath. The woman went away; Loki took the mistletoe, pulled it up and went to the assembly.

beats.textZh: 霍德尔站在人圈的外面，因为他是瞎子。洛基走过去问他：你为什么不朝巴德尔扔东西？霍德尔说：因为我看不见巴德尔在哪里，而且我也没有武器。洛基说：你也该像别人一样向巴德尔表示敬意。我来给你指方向，你把这根树枝向他扔去吧。霍德尔接过槲寄生，照着洛基的指引朝巴德尔扔去。树枝穿透了巴德尔的身体，他倒在地上死了。斯诺里说：这是神和人所遭遇的最大不幸。
beats.textEn: Höðr stood at the edge of the ring, for he was blind. Loki asked why he did not shoot at Baldr. Because I cannot see where he is, said Höðr, and I have no weapon. Loki said he should honour Baldr like the others, and offered to show him where Baldr stood. Höðr took the mistletoe and threw it as Loki directed; it pierced Baldr and he fell dead to the earth. It was, says Snorri, the greatest misfortune ever to befall gods and men.

beats.textZh: 巴德尔倒下的时候，阿萨众神都说不出话来，双手也失去了力气，不能把他扶起。他们彼此相望，心里都知道是谁干了这件事，却不能在那里报仇，因为那是一处圣地。他们想说话的时候，涌出的只有泪水，没有一个神能把自己的悲痛告诉别人。在所有的神中，奥丁最承受不住这个打击，因为他最明白，巴德尔的死对阿萨众神意味着多大的损失与毁灭。
beats.textEn: When Baldr fell, the Æsir were struck dumb and their hands failed them to lift him. Each looked at the other, all of one mind about who had done the deed, but no vengeance could be taken there, for it was a place of great sanctuary. When they tried to speak, weeping came first, and none could tell the others his grief. Odin bore the loss worst of all, for he best understood how great a loss and ruin Baldr's death was for the Æsir.

beats.textZh: 众神稍稍平静之后，弗丽嘉开口问道：阿萨神族中有谁愿意赢得我全部的爱与恩宠，骑马走上通往冥界的路，去找赫尔，问她要多少赎金才肯让巴德尔回到阿斯加德？奥丁的儿子、勇敢的赫尔莫德说他愿意去。于是众神牵来奥丁的八足骏马斯莱布尼尔，交给赫尔莫德。他跃上马背，向冥界疾驰而去。这是众神在巨大的悲痛中想到的唯一办法：如果冥界的女王肯收下赎金，巴德尔也许还能回来。赫尔莫德的马蹄声远去了，而留在阿斯加德的众神，还要先为巴德尔送行。

In the hall he saw his brother Baldr in the seat of honour, and stayed the night. In the morning he asked Hel to let Baldr ride home, telling of the gods' grief. Hel said she would test whether Baldr was as beloved as they said: if all things in the world, alive and dead, wept for him, he would return to the Æsir; but if any refused to weep, he would stay with Hel. Baldr gave Hermóðr the ring Draupnir to take to Odin as a keepsake, and Nanna sent Frigg a linen kerchief and Fulla a gold ring.

beats.textZh: 赫尔莫德骑马回到阿斯加德，把他的所见所闻原原本本地告诉了众神。于是阿萨众神派出使者走遍全世界，请求万物为巴德尔哭泣，好让他从冥界回来。万物都哭了：人和动物、大地和石头、树木和各种金属都哭了——斯诺里说，就像你看见这些东西从严寒中被拿到温暖的地方时，身上会凝出水珠来一样。使者们走遍了天上和人间，所到之处，没有一样东西不在流泪。众神满怀希望，以为巴德尔就要回来了。可是，就在使者们办完差事、踏上归途的时候，他们经过了一个山洞——
beats.textEn: Hermóðr rode back and told all he had seen and heard. The Æsir sent messengers throughout the world asking that Baldr be wept out of Hel. All things did so — men and beasts, the earth and stones, trees and every metal — as you will have seen these things weep when they come out of frost into warmth.

beats.headingEn: The giantess who would not weep
beats.textZh: 使者们完成了使命，正在回家的路上，看见一个山洞里坐着一个女巨人，她自称叫作索克。他们请她也为巴德尔哭泣，让他从冥界回来。她回答说：索克要流干的眼泪，为巴德尔的火葬哭泣。不论他是活着还是死了，我从这老头的儿子身上什么好处也没得到。让赫尔留着她已经得到的吧！人们都认为，这个女巨人就是劳菲之子洛基变的，他给阿萨众神带来了最多的灾祸。巴德尔就这样留在了冥界。
beats.textEn: As the messengers were returning, having done their errand well, they found a giantess sitting in a cave who called herself Þökk. They asked her to weep Baldr out of Hel. She answered: Þökk will weep dry tears for Baldr's burning; alive or dead, the old man's son was no use to me — let Hel keep what she has. Men believe she was Loki Laufeyjarson, who had done the Æsir the most harm. And so Baldr remained in Hel.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 斯诺里说“人们认为”索克就是洛基，这是传统中的认定，不是故事中直接揭穿的情节。

beats.textZh: 众神对洛基怒不可遏，洛基逃到一座山上，盖了一间有四扇门的房子，好向四面八方都能看见。白天他常常变成一条鲑鱼，躲进法拉南格瀑布里。他坐在屋里想：阿萨众神会用什么办法来抓瀑布里的鲑鱼呢？他拿起亚麻线，像人们后来做网那样结了一张网。这时他看见众神已经来到不远处，奥丁从高座上望见了他的藏身之处。洛基赶快把网扔进火里烧掉，跳进河中。最聪明的神克瓦西尔第一个走进屋里，看见火中网的灰烬，明白这是捕鱼的工具，众神就照着灰烬的样子结了一张网。他们来到瀑布边撒网，索尔握住一头，其余的神握住另一头。洛基几次从网下、从网上逃脱，最后一次他想跳过网逃向大海，索尔在空中一把抓住了他，他滑溜溜地往外挣，索尔紧紧捏住他的尾巴——据说正因为这样，鲑鱼的尾巴才变得那么细。
beats.textEn: The gods were so angry that Loki fled and built a house with four doors on a mountain so he could watch every way, and by day he often hid as a salmon in the Fránangr falls. Wondering how the gods might catch him, he knotted linen into a net — the first net — and when he saw the gods coming, threw it in the fire and leapt into the river. Kvasir, wisest of the gods, saw the shape of the net in the ashes, and they made one like it. Dragging the falls with Thor at one end, they drove Loki until he tried to leap over the net; Thor caught him in mid-air and held him by the tail, which is why the salmon tapers at the tail.

beats.textZh: 众神把洛基带进一个山洞，竖起三块扁石，在每块石头上钻一个洞。他们抓来洛基的两个儿子瓦利和纳尔维，把瓦利变成一匹狼，狼把他的兄弟撕成了碎片。众神用纳尔维的肠子把洛基捆在三块石头上：一块抵着肩膀，一块抵着腰，一块抵着膝盖窝，那些肠子随后变成了铁。斯卡蒂拿来一条毒蛇，挂在洛基的头上方，让蛇的毒液滴在他脸上。洛基的妻子西格恩站在他身旁，手里捧着一只碗接住毒液；碗满了，她就走开去倒掉，这时毒液就滴在洛基的脸上，他痛得猛烈挣扎，整个大地都随之颤抖——这就是人们所说的地震。洛基就这样被捆着，一直躺到诸神的黄昏来临。
beats.textEn: The gods took Loki into a cave, set up three slabs on edge and bored a hole in each. They took his sons Váli and Nari (or Narfi); Váli was turned into a wolf and tore his brother apart, and with Nari's entrails they bound Loki over the stones — one under his shoulders, one under his loins, one under the backs of his knees — and the bonds became iron. Skaði hung a venomous snake above him so that its poison dripped onto his face. His wife Sigyn stands by holding a bowl under the venom, and when the bowl is full she goes to empty it; then the venom drips on his face and he shudders so violently that the whole earth shakes — what men call earthquakes. There he lies bound until Ragnarök.

facts.textZh: 洛基是赫尔的父母。
facts.textEn: Gylfaginning names Hel as a child of Loki and Angrboda.
facts.sourceTitle: Snorri Sturluson: Edda. Prologue and Gylfaginning

deityStoryCards.name: Hermóðr
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Odin who rides Sleipnir nine nights to Hel to ransom Baldr (Gylfaginning 49).

beats.textZh: 奥丁的儿子巴德尔是众神中最好的一位，人人都称赞他。他容貌俊美、光彩照人，有一种最白的花就因为像他的睫毛那样白，被人们称作“巴德尔的睫毛”。他是阿萨神族中最聪明、最善于言辞、最仁慈的神，可是他的判决却从来不能实现。这一天，巴德尔做了几个可怕的梦，梦见自己的性命将要遭到危险。他把这些梦告诉了阿萨众神，众神聚在一起商议，最后决定：要为巴德尔求得一切东西的保护，使他免受任何伤害。
beats.textEn: Baldr, Odin's son, is the best of the gods and all praise him; so fair and bright that the whitest flower is called Baldr's brow. He is the wisest, most eloquent and most merciful of the Æsir, though none of his judgements can be fulfilled. Then Baldr dreamed great and perilous dreams threatening his life, and when he told the Æsir they took counsel together and resolved to ask protection for him from every kind of danger.

beats.textZh: 于是弗丽嘉出发，让世间万物都立下誓言，不伤害巴德尔：火与水、铁和各种金属、石头、泥土、树木、疾病、走兽、飞鸟、毒物和蛇，全都发了誓。这件事办成之后，众神都放下心来，并且以此为乐：巴德尔站在集会的场地中央，其他的神有的向他射箭，有的用刀剑砍他，有的向他扔石头，可是无论做什么都伤不了他。众神都认为这是一件了不起的荣耀。
beats.textEn: Frigg took oaths that they would not harm Baldr from fire and water, iron and every metal, stones, the earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds, poison and snakes. When this was done it became a sport of the Æsir: Baldr would stand in the assembly while some shot at him, some struck at him and some threw stones, and nothing harmed him. They all thought it a great honour.

beats.textZh: 劳菲之子洛基看见这一切，心里很不高兴，因为巴德尔毫发无伤。他变成一个女人，来到弗丽嘉住的芬萨利尔宫。弗丽嘉问这位女子：你知道阿萨众神在集会上做什么吗？女人说：他们都在朝巴德尔射箭、扔东西，可是什么也伤不了他。弗丽嘉说：不论是兵器还是木头，都伤不了巴德尔，因为我已经让万物都立了誓。女人问：真的万物都向你发誓不伤害巴德尔了吗？弗丽嘉答道：在瓦尔哈拉的西边，长着一棵小小的树苗，叫作槲寄生。我觉得它太年幼了，就没有让它发誓。那女人听了便走了。洛基找到槲寄生，把它拔下来，带到集会的地方去。
beats.textEn: Loki Laufeyjarson was displeased that Baldr took no harm. He went to Frigg at Fensalir in the likeness of a woman. Frigg told the stranger that neither weapons nor trees would harm Baldr, for she had taken oaths of all things. Had everything sworn? asked the woman. Frigg answered that a young shoot grew west of Valhöll called mistletoe, which seemed too young to ask for an oath. The woman went away; Loki took the mistletoe, pulled it up and went to the assembly.

beats.textZh: 霍德尔站在人圈的外面，因为他是瞎子。洛基走过去问他：你为什么不朝巴德尔扔东西？霍德尔说：因为我看不见巴德尔在哪里，而且我也没有武器。洛基说：你也该像别人一样向巴德尔表示敬意。我来给你指方向，你把这根树枝向他扔去吧。霍德尔接过槲寄生，照着洛基的指引朝巴德尔扔去。树枝穿透了巴德尔的身体，他倒在地上死了。斯诺里说：这是神和人所遭遇的最大不幸。
beats.textEn: Höðr stood at the edge of the ring, for he was blind. Loki asked why he did not shoot at Baldr. Because I cannot see where he is, said Höðr, and I have no weapon. Loki said he should honour Baldr like the others, and offered to show him where Baldr stood. Höðr took the mistletoe and threw it as Loki directed; it pierced Baldr and he fell dead to the earth. It was, says Snorri, the greatest misfortune ever to befall gods and men.

beats.textZh: 巴德尔倒下的时候，阿萨众神都说不出话来，双手也失去了力气，不能把他扶起。他们彼此相望，心里都知道是谁干了这件事，却不能在那里报仇，因为那是一处圣地。他们想说话的时候，涌出的只有泪水，没有一个神能把自己的悲痛告诉别人。在所有的神中，奥丁最承受不住这个打击，因为他最明白，巴德尔的死对阿萨众神意味着多大的损失与毁灭。
beats.textEn: When Baldr fell, the Æsir were struck dumb and their hands failed them to lift him. Each looked at the other, all of one mind about who had done the deed, but no vengeance could be taken there, for it was a place of great sanctuary. When they tried to speak, weeping came first, and none could tell the others his grief. Odin bore the loss worst of all, for he best understood how great a loss and ruin Baldr's death was for the Æsir.

beats.textZh: 众神稍稍平静之后，弗丽嘉开口问道：阿萨神族中有谁愿意赢得我全部的爱与恩宠，骑马走上通往冥界的路，去找赫尔，问她要多少赎金才肯让巴德尔回到阿斯加德？奥丁的儿子、勇敢的赫尔莫德说他愿意去。于是众神牵来奥丁的八足骏马斯莱布尼尔，交给赫尔莫德。他跃上马背，向冥界疾驰而去。这是众神在巨大的悲痛中想到的唯一办法：如果冥界的女王肯收下赎金，巴德尔也许还能回来。赫尔莫德的马蹄声远去了，而留在阿斯加德的众神，还要先为巴德尔送行。
beats.textEn: When the gods came to themselves, Frigg asked who among the Æsir would win all her love and favour by riding the road to Hel to find Baldr and offer Hel a ransom to let him come home to Ásgarðr. Hermóðr the Bold, Odin's son, undertook the journey. Odin's horse Sleipnir was led out, and Hermóðr mounted and galloped away.

beats.textZh: 阿萨众神抬起巴德尔的尸体，送到海边。巴德尔的船叫作“灵钟号”，是所有船中最大的一艘，众神想把它推下海，在船上为巴德尔举行火葬，可是船纹丝不动。他们只好派人到巨人之国去请一个名叫希罗金的女巨人来帮忙。她骑着一头狼来了，用毒蛇作缰绳。她跳下狼背，奥丁叫四个狂战士看住那头狼，他们只能把它摔倒才制服它。希罗金走到船头，只一推就把船推下了海，船底的滚木冒出火花，大地都颤抖起来。索尔大怒，握住锤子要打碎她的头，众神都为她求情，他才住手。巴德尔的遗体被抬上船，他的妻子南娜看见了，悲痛得心都碎了，当场死去，也被放上柴堆一起焚烧。索尔站在火堆前用妙尔尼尔为它祝圣，一个名叫利特的矮人从他脚前跑过，索尔一脚把他踢进了火里。奥丁把金环德罗普尼尔放在柴堆上，巴德尔的马也带着全套马具被送上火堆。
beats.textEn: The Æsir carried Baldr's body to the sea. His ship Hringhorni was the greatest of all ships, but they could not launch it, so they sent to Jötunheimr for the giantess Hyrrokkin, who came riding a wolf with vipers for reins. Four berserks could hold the wolf only by knocking it down. She pushed the ship off with one shove, so that fire flew from the rollers and the earth shook; Thor would have smashed her head had the gods not begged for her. When Baldr was laid on board, his wife Nanna's heart burst with grief, and she was laid on the pyre with him. Thor hallowed the pyre with Mjöllnir and kicked the dwarf Litr into the flames; Odin laid the ring Draupnir on the pyre, and Baldr's horse was burned with all its harness.

beats.textZh: 赫尔莫德骑着马走了九天九夜，穿过幽深黑暗的山谷，什么也看不见，直到来到冥河耶尔河边，骑上了铺着闪亮黄金的耶尔桥。守桥的少女名叫莫德古德，她问他的名字和家族，说：昨天有五队死人从这座桥上过去，可是桥被你一个人震得比他们全体还响；而且你的脸色不像死人。你为什么骑马走在通往冥界的路上？赫尔莫德说：我要去冥界找巴德尔。你有没有在路上见过他？莫德古德说：巴德尔已经骑马过了耶尔桥。通往冥界的路，就在下面，往北边去。
beats.textEn: For nine nights Hermóðr rode through dark, deep valleys where he could see nothing, until he came to the river Gjöll and rode onto the Gjallarbrú, roofed with gleaming gold. The maiden who guarded the bridge, Móðguðr, asked his name and lineage: the day before, five companies of dead men had ridden over, yet the bridge thundered more under him alone, and he did not have the colour of the dead. He said he was riding to Hel to seek Baldr; she told him Baldr had crossed the bridge, and that the road to Hel lay downward and to the north.

beats.textZh: 众神对洛基怒不可遏，洛基逃到一座山上，盖了一间有四扇门的房子，好向四面八方都能看见。白天他常常变成一条鲑鱼，躲进法拉南格瀑布里。他坐在屋里想：阿萨众神会用什么办法来抓瀑布里的鲑鱼呢？他拿起亚麻线，像人们后来做网那样结了一张网。这时他看见众神已经来到不远处，奥丁从高座上望见了他的藏身之处。洛基赶快把网扔进火里烧掉，跳进河中。最聪明的神克瓦西尔第一个走进屋里，看见火中网的灰烬，明白这是捕鱼的工具，众神就照着灰烬的样子结了一张网。他们来到瀑布边撒网，索尔握住一头，其余的神握住另一头。洛基几次从网下、从网上逃脱，最后一次他想跳过网逃向大海，索尔在空中一把抓住了他，他滑溜溜地往外挣，索尔紧紧捏住他的尾巴——据说正因为这样，鲑鱼的尾巴才变得那么细。
beats.textEn: The gods were so angry that Loki fled and built a house with four doors on a mountain so he could watch every way, and by day he often hid as a salmon in the Fránangr falls. Wondering how the gods might catch him, he knotted linen into a net — the first net — and when he saw the gods coming, threw it in the fire and leapt into the river. Kvasir, wisest of the gods, saw the shape of the net in the ashes, and they made one like it. Dragging the falls with Thor at one end, they drove Loki until he tried to leap over the net; Thor caught him in mid-air and held him by the tail, which is why the salmon tapers at the tail.

beats.textZh: 众神把洛基带进一个山洞，竖起三块扁石，在每块石头上钻一个洞。他们抓来洛基的两个儿子瓦利和纳尔维，把瓦利变成一匹狼，狼把他的兄弟撕成了碎片。众神用纳尔维的肠子把洛基捆在三块石头上：一块抵着肩膀，一块抵着腰，一块抵着膝盖窝，那些肠子随后变成了铁。斯卡蒂拿来一条毒蛇，挂在洛基的头上方，让蛇的毒液滴在他脸上。洛基的妻子西格恩站在他身旁，手里捧着一只碗接住毒液；碗满了，她就走开去倒掉，这时毒液就滴在洛基的脸上，他痛得猛烈挣扎，整个大地都随之颤抖——这就是人们所说的地震。洛基就这样被捆着，一直躺到诸神的黄昏来临。
beats.textEn: The gods took Loki into a cave, set up three slabs on edge and bored a hole in each. They took his sons Váli and Nari (or Narfi); Váli was turned into a wolf and tore his brother apart, and with Nari's entrails they bound Loki over the stones — one under his shoulders, one under his loins, one under the backs of his knees — and the bonds became iron. Skaði hung a venomous snake above him so that its poison dripped onto his face. His wife Sigyn stands by holding a bowl under the venom, and when the bowl is full she goes to empty it; then the venom drips on his face and he shudders so violently that the whole earth shakes — what men call earthquakes. There he lies bound until Ragnarök.

deityStoryCards.name: Hœnir
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《女巫的预言》人类起源三神见证中的独立神祇；不与 Vili 自动等同。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: A distinct deity in the Völuspá human-origin triad; not automatically identified with Vili.

beats.textZh: 《女巫预言》17–18节在最初人类段落中分别命名阿斯克与恩布拉。
beats.textEn: Voluspa 17–18 names Ask and Embla in its first-human episode.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 当前中文概述不复制现代译文。

beats.textZh: 这段诗歌把奥丁、赫尼尔与洛杜尔放在同一创造人类场景中。
beats.textEn: The poetic passage places Odin, Hoenir, and Lodurr together in the human-creation scene.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 各神具体赐予项目将在逐词校勘后补充。

beats.textZh: 这里记录的是诗歌三神组合；《欺骗古鲁菲》的奥丁、维利、维组合不会覆盖它。
beats.textEn: This is the poetic triad; the Odin, Vili, and Ve grouping in Gylfaginning does not overwrite it.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 差异保持为版本并存，而非人物自动等同。

facts.textZh: 《女巫的预言》第17–18节见证提到赫尼尔。
facts.textEn: The passage names Hœnir.

deityStoryCards.name: Höðr
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Blind god who, guided by Loki, throws the mistletoe that kills Baldr (Gylfaginning 49).

beats.textZh: 奥丁的儿子巴德尔是众神中最好的一位，人人都称赞他。他容貌俊美、光彩照人，有一种最白的花就因为像他的睫毛那样白，被人们称作“巴德尔的睫毛”。他是阿萨神族中最聪明、最善于言辞、最仁慈的神，可是他的判决却从来不能实现。这一天，巴德尔做了几个可怕的梦，梦见自己的性命将要遭到危险。他把这些梦告诉了阿萨众神，众神聚在一起商议，最后决定：要为巴德尔求得一切东西的保护，使他免受任何伤害。
beats.textEn: Baldr, Odin's son, is the best of the gods and all praise him; so fair and bright that the whitest flower is called Baldr's brow. He is the wisest, most eloquent and most merciful of the Æsir, though none of his judgements can be fulfilled. Then Baldr dreamed great and perilous dreams threatening his life, and when he told the Æsir they took counsel together and resolved to ask protection for him from every kind of danger.

beats.textZh: 于是弗丽嘉出发，让世间万物都立下誓言，不伤害巴德尔：火与水、铁和各种金属、石头、泥土、树木、疾病、走兽、飞鸟、毒物和蛇，全都发了誓。这件事办成之后，众神都放下心来，并且以此为乐：巴德尔站在集会的场地中央，其他的神有的向他射箭，有的用刀剑砍他，有的向他扔石头，可是无论做什么都伤不了他。众神都认为这是一件了不起的荣耀。
beats.textEn: Frigg took oaths that they would not harm Baldr from fire and water, iron and every metal, stones, the earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds, poison and snakes. When this was done it became a sport of the Æsir: Baldr would stand in the assembly while some shot at him, some struck at him and some threw stones, and nothing harmed him. They all thought it a great honour.

beats.textZh: 劳菲之子洛基看见这一切，心里很不高兴，因为巴德尔毫发无伤。他变成一个女人，来到弗丽嘉住的芬萨利尔宫。弗丽嘉问这位女子：你知道阿萨众神在集会上做什么吗？女人说：他们都在朝巴德尔射箭、扔东西，可是什么也伤不了他。弗丽嘉说：不论是兵器还是木头，都伤不了巴德尔，因为我已经让万物都立了誓。女人问：真的万物都向你发誓不伤害巴德尔了吗？弗丽嘉答道：在瓦尔哈拉的西边，长着一棵小小的树苗，叫作槲寄生。我觉得它太年幼了，就没有让它发誓。那女人听了便走了。洛基找到槲寄生，把它拔下来，带到集会的地方去。
beats.textEn: Loki Laufeyjarson was displeased that Baldr took no harm. He went to Frigg at Fensalir in the likeness of a woman. Frigg told the stranger that neither weapons nor trees would harm Baldr, for she had taken oaths of all things. Had everything sworn? asked the woman. Frigg answered that a young shoot grew west of Valhöll called mistletoe, which seemed too young to ask for an oath. The woman went away; Loki took the mistletoe, pulled it up and went to the assembly.

beats.textZh: 霍德尔站在人圈的外面，因为他是瞎子。洛基走过去问他：你为什么不朝巴德尔扔东西？霍德尔说：因为我看不见巴德尔在哪里，而且我也没有武器。洛基说：你也该像别人一样向巴德尔表示敬意。我来给你指方向，你把这根树枝向他扔去吧。霍德尔接过槲寄生，照着洛基的指引朝巴德尔扔去。树枝穿透了巴德尔的身体，他倒在地上死了。斯诺里说：这是神和人所遭遇的最大不幸。
beats.textEn: Höðr stood at the edge of the ring, for he was blind. Loki asked why he did not shoot at Baldr. Because I cannot see where he is, said Höðr, and I have no weapon. Loki said he should honour Baldr like the others, and offered to show him where Baldr stood. Höðr took the mistletoe and threw it as Loki directed; it pierced Baldr and he fell dead to the earth. It was, says Snorri, the greatest misfortune ever to befall gods and men.

beats.textZh: 巴德尔倒下的时候，阿萨众神都说不出话来，双手也失去了力气，不能把他扶起。他们彼此相望，心里都知道是谁干了这件事，却不能在那里报仇，因为那是一处圣地。他们想说话的时候，涌出的只有泪水，没有一个神能把自己的悲痛告诉别人。在所有的神中，奥丁最承受不住这个打击，因为他最明白，巴德尔的死对阿萨众神意味着多大的损失与毁灭。
beats.textEn: When Baldr fell, the Æsir were struck dumb and their hands failed them to lift him. Each looked at the other, all of one mind about who had done the deed, but no vengeance could be taken there, for it was a place of great sanctuary. When they tried to speak, weeping came first, and none could tell the others his grief. Odin bore the loss worst of all, for he best understood how great a loss and ruin Baldr's death was for the Æsir.

beats.textZh: 众神稍稍平静之后，弗丽嘉开口问道：阿萨神族中有谁愿意赢得我全部的爱与恩宠，骑马走上通往冥界的路，去找赫尔，问她要多少赎金才肯让巴德尔回到阿斯加德？奥丁的儿子、勇敢的赫尔莫德说他愿意去。于是众神牵来奥丁的八足骏马斯莱布尼尔，交给赫尔莫德。他跃上马背，向冥界疾驰而去。这是众神在巨大的悲痛中想到的唯一办法：如果冥界的女王肯收下赎金，巴德尔也许还能回来。赫尔莫德的马蹄声远去了，而留在阿斯加德的众神，还要先为巴德尔送行。
beats.textEn: When the gods came to themselves, Frigg asked who among the Æsir would win all her love and favour by riding the road to Hel to find Baldr and offer Hel a ransom to let him come home to Ásgarðr. Hermóðr the Bold, Odin's son, undertook the journey. Odin's horse Sleipnir was led out, and Hermóðr mounted and galloped away.

beats.textZh: 阿萨众神抬起巴德尔的尸体，送到海边。巴德尔的船叫作“灵钟号”，是所有船中最大的一艘，众神想把它推下海，在船上为巴德尔举行火葬，可是船纹丝不动。他们只好派人到巨人之国去请一个名叫希罗金的女巨人来帮忙。她骑着一头狼来了，用毒蛇作缰绳。她跳下狼背，奥丁叫四个狂战士看住那头狼，他们只能把它摔倒才制服它。希罗金走到船头，只一推就把船推下了海，船底的滚木冒出火花，大地都颤抖起来。索尔大怒，握住锤子要打碎她的头，众神都为她求情，他才住手。巴德尔的遗体被抬上船，他的妻子南娜看见了，悲痛得心都碎了，当场死去，也被放上柴堆一起焚烧。索尔站在火堆前用妙尔尼尔为它祝圣，一个名叫利特的矮人从他脚前跑过，索尔一脚把他踢进了火里。奥丁把金环德罗普尼尔放在柴堆上，巴德尔的马也带着全套马具被送上火堆。
beats.textEn: The Æsir carried Baldr's body to the sea. His ship Hringhorni was the greatest of all ships, but they could not launch it, so they sent to Jötunheimr for the giantess Hyrrokkin, who came riding a wolf with vipers for reins. Four berserks could hold the wolf only by knocking it down. She pushed the ship off with one shove, so that fire flew from the rollers and the earth shook; Thor would have smashed her head had the gods not begged for her. When Baldr was laid on board, his wife Nanna's heart burst with grief, and she was laid on the pyre with him. Thor hallowed the pyre with Mjöllnir and kicked the dwarf Litr into the flames; Odin laid the ring Draupnir on the pyre, and Baldr's horse was burned with all its harness.

beats.textZh: 赫尔莫德骑着马走了九天九夜，穿过幽深黑暗的山谷，什么也看不见，直到来到冥河耶尔河边，骑上了铺着闪亮黄金的耶尔桥。守桥的少女名叫莫德古德，她问他的名字和家族，说：昨天有五队死人从这座桥上过去，可是桥被你一个人震得比他们全体还响；而且你的脸色不像死人。你为什么骑马走在通往冥界的路上？赫尔莫德说：我要去冥界找巴德尔。你有没有在路上见过他？莫德古德说：巴德尔已经骑马过了耶尔桥。通往冥界的路，就在下面，往北边去。
beats.textEn: For nine nights Hermóðr rode through dark, deep valleys where he could see nothing, until he came to the river Gjöll and rode onto the Gjallarbrú, roofed with gleaming gold. The maiden who guarded the bridge, Móðguðr, asked his name and lineage: the day before, five companies of dead men had ridden over, yet the bridge thundered more under him alone, and he did not have the colour of the dead. He said he was riding to Hel to seek Baldr; she told him Baldr had crossed the bridge, and that the road to Hel lay downward and to the north.

beats.textZh: 赫尔莫德一路骑到冥界的大门前，他跳下马，把马肚带勒紧，重新上马，用马刺一踢，骏马高高跃起，从大门上方越了过去，一点也没碰到。他骑到大殿前下了马，走进去，看见他的哥哥巴德尔坐在高座上。赫尔莫德在那里过了一夜。第二天早晨，他请求赫尔让巴德尔和他一起骑马回家，并告诉她阿萨众神为巴德尔哭得多么伤心。赫尔说：我要看看巴德尔是不是真的像人们说的那样受到爱戴。如果世上的一切东西，活的和死的，都为他哭泣，他就可以回到阿萨众神那里；可是只要有一样东西反对、不肯哭泣，他就得留在冥界。赫尔莫德起身告辞，巴德尔送他出殿，把金环德罗普尼尔交给他，让他带回去给奥丁作纪念；南娜也送给弗丽嘉一块亚麻头巾和其他礼物，还送给弗丽嘉的侍女富拉一枚金指环。
beats.textEn: At Hel's gate Hermóðr dismounted, tightened the girth, remounted and spurred Sleipnir, who leapt clean over the gate. In the hall he saw his brother Baldr in the seat of honour, and stayed the night. In the morning he asked Hel to let Baldr ride home, telling of the gods' grief. Hel said she would test whether Baldr was as beloved as they said: if all things in the world, alive and dead, wept for him, he would return to the Æsir; but if any refused to weep, he would stay with Hel. Baldr gave Hermóðr the ring Draupnir to take to Odin as a keepsake, and Nanna sent Frigg a linen kerchief and Fulla a gold ring.

beats.textZh: 赫尔莫德骑马回到阿斯加德，把他的所见所闻原原本本地告诉了众神。于是阿萨众神派出使者走遍全世界，请求万物为巴德尔哭泣，好让他从冥界回来。万物都哭了：人和动物、大地和石头、树木和各种金属都哭了——斯诺里说，就像你看见这些东西从严寒中被拿到温暖的地方时，身上会凝出水珠来一样。使者们走遍了天上和人间，所到之处，没有一样东西不在流泪。众神满怀希望，以为巴德尔就要回来了。可是，就在使者们办完差事、踏上归途的时候，他们经过了一个山洞——
beats.textEn: Hermóðr rode back and told all he had seen and heard. The Æsir sent messengers throughout the world asking that Baldr be wept out of Hel. All things did so — men and beasts, the earth and stones, trees and every metal — as you will have seen these things weep when they come out of frost into warmth.

beats.headingEn: The giantess who would not weep
beats.textZh: 使者们完成了使命，正在回家的路上，看见一个山洞里坐着一个女巨人，她自称叫作索克。他们请她也为巴德尔哭泣，让他从冥界回来。她回答说：索克要流干的眼泪，为巴德尔的火葬哭泣。不论他是活着还是死了，我从这老头的儿子身上什么好处也没得到。让赫尔留着她已经得到的吧！人们都认为，这个女巨人就是劳菲之子洛基变的，他给阿萨众神带来了最多的灾祸。巴德尔就这样留在了冥界。
beats.textEn: As the messengers were returning, having done their errand well, they found a giantess sitting in a cave who called herself Þökk. They asked her to weep Baldr out of Hel. She answered: Þökk will weep dry tears for Baldr's burning; alive or dead, the old man's son was no use to me — let Hel keep what she has. Men believe she was Loki Laufeyjarson, who had done the Æsir the most harm. And so Baldr remained in Hel.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 斯诺里说“人们认为”索克就是洛基，这是传统中的认定，不是故事中直接揭穿的情节。

beats.textZh: 众神把洛基带进一个山洞，竖起三块扁石，在每块石头上钻一个洞。他们抓来洛基的两个儿子瓦利和纳尔维，把瓦利变成一匹狼，狼把他的兄弟撕成了碎片。众神用纳尔维的肠子把洛基捆在三块石头上：一块抵着肩膀，一块抵着腰，一块抵着膝盖窝，那些肠子随后变成了铁。斯卡蒂拿来一条毒蛇，挂在洛基的头上方，让蛇的毒液滴在他脸上。洛基的妻子西格恩站在他身旁，手里捧着一只碗接住毒液；碗满了，她就走开去倒掉，这时毒液就滴在洛基的脸上，他痛得猛烈挣扎，整个大地都随之颤抖——这就是人们所说的地震。洛基就这样被捆着，一直躺到诸神的黄昏来临。
beats.textEn: The gods took Loki into a cave, set up three slabs on edge and bored a hole in each. They took his sons Váli and Nari (or Narfi); Váli was turned into a wolf and tore his brother apart, and with Nari's entrails they bound Loki over the stones — one under his shoulders, one under his loins, one under the backs of his knees — and the bonds became iron. Skaði hung a venomous snake above him so that its poison dripped onto his face. His wife Sigyn stands by holding a bowl under the venom, and when the bowl is full she goes to empty it; then the venom drips on his face and he shudders so violently that the whole earth shakes — what men call earthquakes. There he lies bound until Ragnarök.

deityStoryCards.name: Magni
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 索尔之子；《诗语法》另称其母为雅恩莎撒。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Son of Thor; Skaldskaparmal also names Jarnsaxa as his mother.

beats.textZh: 雅恩莎撒是马格尼的父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal identifies Jarnsaxa as Magni’s mother.

beats.textZh: 索尔／雷神托尔是马格尼的父母。
beats.textEn: Skaldskaparmal names Magni as a child of Thor.

deityStoryCards.name: Kūrma
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Tortoise form assumed by Viṣṇu to support Mount Mandara in the Bhāgavata Purāṇa witness; kept separate from the Mahābhārata tortoise king Akūpāra.

beats.headingZh: 诸神与阿修罗暂时结盟
beats.headingEn: A truce between gods and asuras
beats.textZh: 《薄伽梵往世书》第八篇第5–6章中，诸神按毗湿奴的建议与阿修罗暂时结盟，合力拔起曼陀罗山并运往大海，毗湿奴亲自出手相助。
beats.textEn: In Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.5–8.6, on Viṣṇu's advice the gods make a temporary truce with the asuras; together they uproot Mount Mandara and carry it toward the ocean, with Viṣṇu himself stepping in to help.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 运山过程的细节只作概述，待逐颂校对。

beats.headingEn: Viṣṇu takes the form of a tortoise
beats.textZh: 以婆苏吉为绳开始搅拌后，曼陀罗山沉入水中；毗湿奴化作巨龟潜到山下，用背托起大山。
beats.textEn: Once the churning begins with Vāsuki as the rope, Mount Mandara sinks into the water; Viṣṇu assumes the form of a giant tortoise, dives beneath it and raises the mountain on his back.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 与精校本的龟王阿库帕拉构成显式见证差异，不做身份等同。

beats.textZh: 搅拌最先产生可怕的毒药，向各方蔓延；众生求助于湿婆，湿婆把毒药饮下。
beats.textEn: The churning first produces a terrible poison that spreads in every direction; beings turn to Śiva, who drinks it.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 后续图像传统与虔信解释未在本批次逐句建模。

beats.textZh: 其后又涌现多种宝物与存在，最后檀文陀利捧着盛满甘露的水罐出现。
beats.textEn: A series of treasures and beings then emerges, and finally Dhanvantari appears holding a vessel filled with the amṛta.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 此前出现之物的逐项清单尚未建模，不与精校本合并。

beats.textZh: 阿修罗抢走甘露后，毗湿奴化身为摩希尼迷惑他们，并把甘露分给诸神。罗睺假扮天神混入其中饮下甘露，被日月指认后，毗湿奴以神盘斩下其头。
beats.textEn: When the asuras snatch the amṛta, Viṣṇu becomes Mohinī, captivates them and distributes the amṛta to the gods. Rāhu, disguised as a god, slips in and drinks; when the Sun and Moon point him out, Viṣṇu severs his head with the discus.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 罗睺后来的天体身份不在本批次建模。

facts.textZh: 俱利摩（龟形化身）是毗湿奴的一种形态。
facts.textEn: The Bhāgavata Purāṇa witness presents the supporting tortoise as a form assumed by Viṣṇu.

deityStoryCards.name: Hanumān
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Vānara son of the wind god and minister of Sugrīva, who leaps the sea to Laṅkā, finds Sītā and burns the city; worshipped widely as a deity of devotion and strength.

beats.headingEn: A cry of grief becomes a verse
beats.textZh: 史诗从诗人自己讲起。苦行者蚁垤问仙人那罗陀：如今世上，有没有一个既有德行又有勇气、懂得正法、知恩图报、言而有信的人？那罗陀说：有，他就是甘蔗王族的罗摩，接着把罗摩的一生简要讲了一遍。不久，蚁垤到多摩萨河边沐浴，看见一对麻鹬正在树上相亲相爱，一个猎人一箭射死了雄鸟，雌鸟围着倒在血泊里的伴侣哀哀悲鸣。蚁垤心中涌起悲悯，脱口说出一句诅咒猎人的话——话一出口，他自己也吃了一惊：这句话音节整齐，可以和着琴弦吟唱。他把这种由悲伤（śoka）而生的诗体叫做“输洛迦”（śloka）。这时梵天亲自来到他面前，对他说：就用这种诗体，把那罗陀讲给你的罗摩的故事完整地唱出来吧；你所写的一切都会是真实的，只要山川还在，这部诗就会在世间流传。
beats.textEn: The epic begins with its own poet. The ascetic Vālmīki asked the sage Nārada whether there was any man on earth who was virtuous, brave, grateful and true to his word; Nārada told him of Rāma of the Ikṣvāku line and sketched his life. Soon after, bathing by the river Tamasā, Vālmīki saw a hunter shoot one of a pair of mating curlews, and heard the hen cry over her fallen mate. Pity broke from him as a curse on the hunter — in measured syllables that could be sung to the lute. He called this metre, born of grief (śoka), the śloka. Then Brahmā came to him and told him to sing the whole story of Rāma in that metre: all he wrote would be true, and it would endure while mountains and rivers lasted.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·开篇（那罗陀、梵天来访）。

beats.headingEn: The golden bowl from the sacrificial fire
beats.textZh: 阿逾陀城的国王十车王富有、公正、受人爱戴，却没有儿子。他举行了马祭，又请仙人鹿角主持求子的祭祀。就在这时，天上的众神来到梵天面前诉苦：罗刹王罗波那靠苦行从梵天那里得到恩典，天神、乾闼婆、夜叉和罗刹都杀不死他——他看不起人类，根本没有把人算进去。他仗着这个恩典欺压三界，众神毫无办法。正说着，毗湿奴骑着金翅鸟来了。众神恳求他化身为人，降生为十车王的四个儿子，去除掉罗波那。毗湿奴答应了。于是从十车王的祭火中走出一位光芒四射的神灵，捧着一只盛满天界乳粥的金碗。国王把乳粥分给三位王后：憍萨厘雅生下了罗摩，吉迦伊生下了婆罗多，须弥多罗生下了一对双胞胎——罗什曼那和设睹卢祇那。
beats.textEn: Daśaratha, king of Ayodhyā, was rich, just and beloved, but had no son. He performed the horse sacrifice and a rite for sons with the sage Ṛṣyaśṛṅga. Meanwhile the gods complained to Brahmā: Rāvaṇa, king of the rākṣasas, had won by austerities a boon that no god, gandharva, yakṣa or rākṣasa could slay him — scorning men, he had not even named them — and he was oppressing the three worlds. Vishnu arrived on Garuḍa, and the gods begged him to be born as a man, as Daśaratha's four sons, to destroy Rāvaṇa. He agreed. From the sacrificial fire rose a radiant being bearing a golden bowl of heavenly rice-milk; the king shared it among his queens, and Kausalyā bore Rāma, Kaikeyī Bharata, and Sumitrā the twins Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·求子祭祀与众神的请求。

beats.headingEn: Into the forest with the sage
beats.textZh: 王子们长大了，个个精通经典和武艺，其中罗摩最受众人喜爱，罗什曼那则像影子一样跟着他。一天，大仙人众友来到王宫，请国王把还不满十六岁的罗摩借给他，去保护他的祭祀不受罗刹的骚扰。十车王舍不得，宁愿自己率军前往，但在家庭祭司婆私吒的劝说下终于答应了。众友带着罗摩和罗什曼那上路，教给他们能驱除饥渴和疲劳的咒语。在一片荒凉的森林里，女罗刹多吒迦向他们扑来，罗摩起初不愿杀害女子，只想把她打退，众友却催促他说，为了保护众生，这样做并不违背正法。罗摩便射杀了她。众友非常满意，把许多神兵的咒语传授给他。到了众友的净修林，祭祀开始的第六天，罗刹摩哩遮和苏跋呼带人从天上撒下血肉，罗摩一箭把摩哩遮射飞到一百由旬外的海里，又射死了苏跋呼。
beats.textEn: The princes grew up learned in scripture and arms; Rāma was loved by all, and Lakṣmaṇa followed him like his shadow. One day the great sage Viśvāmitra came and asked for Rāma, not yet sixteen, to guard his sacrifice from rākṣasas. Daśaratha begged to go himself with an army, but the family priest Vasiṣṭha persuaded him. On the road Viśvāmitra taught the brothers spells against hunger and weariness. In a desolate forest the rākṣasī Tāṭakā rushed at them; Rāma was loth to kill a woman, but the sage urged that protecting the world was no breach of dharma, and Rāma shot her. Pleased, Viśvāmitra gave him the spells of the divine weapons. On the sixth day of the sacrifice Mārīca and Subāhu rained blood from the sky; Rāma's arrow hurled Mārīca a hundred leagues into the sea and killed Subāhu.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·众友的祭祀与多吒迦。

beats.textZh: 众友又带着两位王子前往弥提罗国。弥提罗的国王遮那竭告诉他们：有一次他为祭祀耕地，犁头翻开的犁沟里出现了一个女婴，他给她取名悉多，当作亲生女儿养大。他立下誓言，谁能拉开祖先传下来的湿婆大弓，就把悉多嫁给谁。许多国王都来试过，却连举都举不起来。那张弓装在一辆八个轮子的铁车上，由五千个壮汉拉了出来。罗摩打开弓匣，像玩耍一样轻轻把弓举起，给它装上弦，然后用力一拉——大弓从中间断成了两截，发出像雷霆、像山崩一样的巨响，在场的人全都吓得跌倒在地，只有众友、遮那竭和两位王子还站着。遮那竭欢喜地把悉多许给了罗摩。十车王赶来，四兄弟在同一天成婚。回国路上，持斧罗摩拦路挑战，罗摩又拉开了他带来的毗湿奴大弓，持斧罗摩才心服离去。
beats.textEn: Viśvāmitra then led the princes to Mithilā. King Janaka told them that once, ploughing ground for a sacrifice, he had found a baby girl in the furrow; he named her Sītā and raised her as his daughter, vowing to give her to whoever could string the bow of Śiva that his ancestors had kept. Many kings had failed even to lift it. Five thousand men drew it out on an eight-wheeled iron cart. Rāma opened the case, raised the bow as if in play, strung it and drew it — and it broke in the middle with a crash like thunder or a falling mountain. Everyone fell to the ground except Viśvāmitra, Janaka and the two princes. Janaka gave Sītā to Rāma, and the four brothers were married on one day. On the road home Paraśurāma challenged Rāma, who strung the bow of Vishnu as well, and the challenger withdrew.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·第六十七章“断弓”。

beats.textZh: 许多年过去了，十车王年事已高，决定立罗摩为太子，满城百姓欢天喜地，挂起彩旗，准备第二天的灌顶典礼。可是王后吉迦伊身边的驼背侍女曼他罗，在宫墙上看到这番景象，急忙跑去对吉迦伊说：罗摩一旦登基，你的儿子婆罗多就只能做奴仆，甚至会被赶出国去。起初吉迦伊还为罗摩高兴，送给曼他罗一件首饰；但曼他罗一再挑拨，终于说动了她，还提醒她：当年你在与商钵罗的战争中救过国王的命，国王许给你两个恩典，你一直没有用。吉迦伊扯下首饰，躺在“愤怒之室”的地上。十车王来了，看见心爱的王后这样，就以罗摩的名义发誓答应她的任何要求。吉迦伊说：第一，立婆罗多为太子；第二，让罗摩穿上树皮衣，到弹宅迦林中流放十四年。国王听了昏倒在地，哀求了整整一夜，吉迦伊却毫不动摇。
beats.textEn: Years later the aged Daśaratha resolved to make Rāma heir, and the city hung out banners for the consecration. But Kaikeyī's hunchbacked maid Mantharā, seeing the rejoicing from the palace roof, ran to tell her mistress that once Rāma reigned, her son Bharata would be a servant or an exile. At first Kaikeyī was glad for Rāma and gave Mantharā a jewel, but Mantharā worked on her until she yielded, reminding her of the two boons the king had promised when she saved his life in the war against Śambara. Kaikeyī tore off her ornaments and lay on the floor of the chamber of wrath. When the king, finding her so, swore by Rāma to grant her wish, she asked that Bharata be made heir and that Rāma go in bark garments to the Daṇḍaka forest for fourteen years. The king fell senseless and pleaded all night in vain.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·曼他罗与吉迦伊的恩典。

beats.textZh: 第二天一早，罗摩被召进宫，吉迦伊把国王的决定告诉了他。罗摩的脸色一点也没有变，他平静地说：为了父亲的诺言，我今天就去森林。母亲憍萨厘雅悲痛欲绝；罗什曼那怒不可遏，要拿起武器夺回王位，罗摩却劝住他说：遵守父亲的话就是正法。罗摩去向悉多告别，劝她留在宫中。悉多却说：妻子的命运就是丈夫的命运，有你在的森林，胜过没有你的宫殿；你要是不带我去，我就去死。罗什曼那也坚持要一起走。三人脱下华服，穿上树皮衣。全城的人哭着跟在车后，一直送到城外。他们在恒河边得到猎人首领古诃的帮助渡过了河，从此走进了森林。
beats.textEn: Next morning Rāma was summoned and Kaikeyī told him the king's decision. His face did not change; he said calmly that for his father's word he would go to the forest that very day. His mother Kausalyā was overwhelmed with grief; Lakṣmaṇa raged and would have taken the throne by arms, but Rāma restrained him, saying that obeying their father was dharma. When Rāma bade Sītā stay behind, she answered that a wife's lot is her husband's lot, that the forest with him was better than a palace without him, and that if he left her she would die. Lakṣmaṇa too insisted on coming. The three put off their fine clothes and put on bark garments, the whole city followed their chariot weeping, and on the Ganges the hunter chief Guha ferried them across into the forest.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·罗摩出城流放。

beats.textZh: 车夫苏曼多罗独自赶着空车回来，十车王听说儿子真的走进了森林，悲痛得一病不起。夜里，他对憍萨厘雅讲起了年轻时犯下的一桩罪过：那时他自恃能“听声射箭”，在黑夜的河边听见像大象饮水的声音，一箭射去，射中的却是一个正在用水罐打水的年轻苦行者。少年临死前请他把水带给自己又老又瞎的父母。两位老人得知儿子的死讯，父亲诅咒国王：你将来也会像我一样，为了思念儿子而死。十车王说：这个诅咒如今应验了。他一遍遍呼唤着罗摩的名字，在午夜时分死去了。
beats.textEn: When the charioteer Sumantra came back alone, Daśaratha, hearing that his son had truly entered the forest, fell ill with grief. That night he told Kausalyā of a sin of his youth: proud of shooting at a sound, he had heard by a dark river what seemed an elephant drinking and loosed an arrow — but struck a young ascetic filling a water jar. The dying boy asked him to carry water to his old, blind parents. On hearing of their son's death the father cursed the king to die, like him, grieving for a son. That curse, Daśaratha said, was now fulfilled; and calling Rāma's name he died at midnight.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·十车王之死。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 那位少年苦行者在后世传统中常被叫做“室罗波那”（Śravaṇa），蚁垤本里没有给出这个名字。

beats.headingEn: A pair of sandals on the throne
beats.textZh: 婆罗多从舅父家回来，才知道父亲已死、兄长被流放，而这一切都是母亲为他谋来的。他痛斥吉迦伊，拒绝接受王位，为父亲办完葬礼后，带着母亲们和军队进入森林，去质多罗俱吒山找罗摩。兄弟相见，罗摩得知父亲去世，悲痛不已。婆罗多跪在他面前恳求他回去为王，众人也一齐劝说。罗摩却说：父亲的诺言必须遵守，十四年期满之前，我不会回去。婆罗多无可奈何，请罗摩把脚上那双饰金的鞋子给他。他把鞋子顶在头上带回去，供在王座上，自己穿上树皮衣，住在城外的南迪村，以“鞋子的仆人”的身份代为治理国家，并且发誓：十四年期满那天罗摩若不回来，他就投火而死。
beats.textEn: Bharata returned from his uncle's house to learn that his father was dead and his brother exiled, all for his sake. He rebuked Kaikeyī, refused the throne, performed his father's rites and went with the queens and the army to Mount Citrakūṭa to find Rāma. When the brothers met, Rāma mourned their father. Bharata knelt and begged him to return and reign, and all joined in; but Rāma answered that his father's word must be kept, and he would not return before the fourteen years were over. Then Bharata asked for Rāma's gold-adorned sandals. Carrying them on his head, he set them on the throne, put on bark garments, and ruled from the village of Nandigrāma as the sandals' servant, vowing to enter the fire if Rāma did not return on the appointed day.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·婆罗多寻兄与鞋子。

beats.textZh: 罗摩一行在弹宅迦林中住了许多年，保护林中的苦行者，仙人投山把毗湿奴的神弓和永不空竭的箭囊送给了他。后来他们在戈达瓦里河边的五树林住下，罗什曼那搭了一座草屋。一天，罗波那的妹妹、女罗刹首哩薄那迦看见了罗摩，爱上了他，要他做丈夫。罗摩开玩笑地说自己已有妻子，让她去找罗什曼那；罗什曼那也开玩笑地把她推回给罗摩。她恼羞成怒，以为是悉多挡了路，张牙舞爪地向悉多扑去。罗摩命令罗什曼那惩罚她，罗什曼那拔剑割下了她的鼻子和耳朵。首哩薄那迦哭着逃到哥哥伽罗那里。伽罗先派十四个罗刹去，被罗摩全部射死；接着伽罗和突舍那率领一万四千罗刹大军杀来，罗摩让罗什曼那带着悉多躲进山洞，自己一个人迎战，把整支大军消灭了。
beats.textEn: For years they lived in the Daṇḍaka forest protecting its hermits, and the sage Agastya gave Rāma the bow of Vishnu and inexhaustible quivers. Then they settled at Pañcavaṭī on the Godāvarī, where Lakṣmaṇa built a hut. There Rāvaṇa's sister, the rākṣasī Śūrpaṇakhā, saw Rāma and desired him. Rāma jestingly said he had a wife and sent her to Lakṣmaṇa, who in jest sent her back. Enraged and blaming Sītā, she rushed at her; at Rāma's command Lakṣmaṇa cut off her nose and ears. She fled to her brother Khara. Khara sent fourteen rākṣasas, whom Rāma shot down; then Khara and Dūṣaṇa came with fourteen thousand, and Rāma, sending Lakṣmaṇa with Sītā to a cave, destroyed the whole host alone.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·首哩薄那迦与伽罗之军。

beats.textZh: 首哩薄那迦逃到楞伽，当众责骂罗波那只顾享乐，连自己的国土都保不住，又极力夸赞悉多的美貌。罗波那动了心，乘着飞车去找当年被罗摩一箭射进海里的摩哩遮。摩哩遮吓得发抖，劝他千万别去招惹罗摩；罗波那却威胁说，不听命令就杀了他。摩哩遮叹道：反正都是死，死在罗摩手里还好些。他变成一只金色的鹿，身上点缀着银色的斑点，角尖像宝石，在草屋前来回走动。悉多一见就喜欢上了，求罗摩去捉。罗什曼那提醒说这一定是摩哩遮的幻术，罗摩还是嘱咐弟弟守护悉多，自己追了出去。金鹿时隐时现，把他引得越来越远，罗摩终于一箭射中。摩哩遮现出原形，临死前学着罗摩的声音大喊：“啊，悉多！啊，罗什曼那！”悉多听了惊慌失措，催罗什曼那去救。罗什曼那说没有人能伤害罗摩，悉多竟说出刺耳的话，指责他心怀不轨。罗什曼那受了委屈，只好离开草屋。
beats.textEn: Śūrpaṇakhā fled to Laṅkā, rebuked Rāvaṇa for his idleness and praised Sītā's beauty. Rāvaṇa flew in his chariot to Mārīca, whom Rāma's arrow had once hurled into the sea.
