Mārīca trembled and begged him not to provoke Rāma, but Rāvaṇa threatened to kill him, and he sighed that it was better to die by Rāma's hand. He became a golden deer dappled with silver, its horns tipped with gems, and grazed before the hut. Sītā longed for it. Lakṣmaṇa warned it was Mārīca's magic, but Rāma left him to guard Sītā and gave chase. The deer led him far away until his arrow struck it; dying, Mārīca cried out in Rāma's voice, ‘Ah Sītā! Ah Lakṣmaṇa!’ Sītā, frantic, urged Lakṣmaṇa to go; when he said none could harm Rāma, she accused him with cruel words of wanting her for himself, and, wounded, he went.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·摩哩遮与金鹿。

beats.headingEn: The ten-headed king and the vulture
beats.textZh: 罗什曼那刚走，罗波那就扮成一个云游的婆罗门苦行者来到草屋前。悉多按待客之礼请他进来，给他水和食物，并告诉他自己是谁。罗波那这才夸耀自己是楞伽之王，要她做他的王后。悉多轻蔑地回答：你就像一只想得到母狮的豺狗。罗波那现出了十个头的真身，一把抓住她，拖上飞车，向南飞去。悉多一路向树木、河流和山神呼喊，求它们告诉罗摩。年老的鹫王阇吒优私是十车王的朋友，他拦住罗波那，劝他放了悉多，随即与他搏斗，打碎了他的车子，杀死了驾车的驴子和车夫；可他终究年老力衰，被罗波那砍断了翅膀和双脚，跌落在地。飞过一座山时，悉多看见山顶上坐着五只猴子，就把自己的披巾和首饰包在一起扔了下去。罗波那把她带回楞伽，给她十二个月的期限，把她关在无忧树林里，由许多女罗刹看守。
beats.textEn: As soon as Lakṣmaṇa had gone, Rāvaṇa came to the hut disguised as a wandering brahmin ascetic. Sītā received him as a guest with water and food and told him who she was. Then he boasted that he was king of Laṅkā and asked her to be his queen; she answered scornfully that he was a jackal longing for a lioness. Rāvaṇa took his true ten-headed form, seized her and carried her off southward in his chariot while she called on the trees, rivers and mountain spirits to tell Rāma. The old vulture-king Jaṭāyu, friend of Daśaratha, barred his way, smashed his chariot and killed its asses and driver, but, old and spent, had his wings and feet cut off by Rāvaṇa. Passing a hill where five monkeys sat, Sītā dropped her scarf and ornaments. In Laṅkā Rāvaṇa gave her twelve months and set her in the aśoka grove under guard of rākṣasīs.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·悉多被劫与阇吒优私。

beats.textZh: 罗摩在回来的路上遇见了罗什曼那，心中顿生不祥之感。草屋果然空无一人。罗摩悲痛欲狂，向树木、河流和野兽一一询问悉多的下落，看到散落的花朵、折断的车子和血迹，以为她被罗刹吃掉了，怒气冲冲地要毁灭世界，罗什曼那苦苦劝他冷静。他们找到奄奄一息的阇吒优私，鹫王告诉他们是罗波那劫走了悉多、往南方去了，说完就断了气。罗摩像为父亲举行葬礼一样，亲手为他火化。兄弟俩继续向南，被一个没有头、胸前长着大嘴的怪物迦槃陀抓住，他们砍断了他的两只长臂。迦槃陀在火葬的火焰中恢复了天神的形貌，告诉他们：去般波湖边的哩舍牟迦山找猴王须羯哩婆，他会帮你们找到悉多。在般波湖边，年老的女苦行者舍波哩欢喜地迎接了罗摩，随后升入天界。
beats.textEn: On the way back Rāma met Lakṣmaṇa and felt dread; the hut was empty. Half mad with grief, Rāma asked the trees, rivers and beasts where Sītā was; seeing scattered flowers, a broken chariot and blood, he thought rākṣasas had eaten her and threatened to destroy the worlds until Lakṣmaṇa calmed him. They found the dying Jaṭāyu, who told them Rāvaṇa had taken Sītā south, and died. Rāma cremated him with the rites due to a father. Going on, they were seized by the headless monster Kabandha, whose mouth was in his chest, and cut off his long arms; restored to divine form in his funeral fire, he told them to seek the monkey-king Sugrīva on Mount Ṛśyamūka by Lake Pampā. There the aged ascetic woman Śabarī welcomed Rāma joyfully and then rose to heaven.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·罗摩的哀伤、阇吒优私、迦槃陀与舍波哩。

beats.textZh: 哈奴曼扮成苦行者来迎接他们，把他们带到须羯哩婆面前。罗摩和须羯哩婆围着火结为盟友。须羯哩婆拿出那包从天上落下的首饰，罗摩认出是悉多的，痛哭失声；罗什曼那说，耳环和手镯他认不出，只认得脚镯，因为他每天向悉多行礼时只看她的脚。须羯哩婆讲了自己的遭遇：哥哥波林夺走了他的妻子和王国，把他赶到这座山上。罗摩一箭射穿七棵娑罗树，让他相信自己的力量。须羯哩婆向波林挑战，罗摩藏在树后；第一次两兄弟长得太像，罗摩分不清；第二次须羯哩婆戴上花环，罗摩一箭射中了波林。垂死的波林责问罗摩为什么从暗处射他，罗摩回答：你夺了弟弟的妻子，作为国王的代表，我有责任惩罚你。须羯哩婆登上王位，雨季过后，他派出四路猴军寻找悉多，罗摩把刻着自己名字的戒指交给了往南去的哈奴曼。
beats.textEn: Hanumān, disguised as an ascetic, met them and brought them to Sugrīva, and Rāma and Sugrīva swore friendship around a fire. Sugrīva showed the bundle of ornaments that had fallen from the sky; Rāma knew them as Sītā's and wept, and Lakṣmaṇa said he knew only her anklets, for he had looked only at her feet when he bowed to her. Sugrīva told how his brother Vālin had taken his wife and kingdom. Rāma shot an arrow through seven sāl trees to prove his strength. When the brothers fought, Rāma stood hidden behind a tree; the first time he could not tell them apart, the second time Sugrīva wore a garland, and Rāma's arrow struck Vālin. The dying Vālin reproached him for shooting from hiding; Rāma answered that Vālin had taken his brother's wife and that he punished him on the king's behalf. Sugrīva was crowned, and after the rains sent search parties to the four quarters; Rāma gave his signet ring to Hanumān, who went south.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第四卷·与须羯哩婆结盟与波林之死。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 罗摩从暗处射杀波林是否合乎正法，在印度传统内部本身就有长久的争论；本站只讲蚁垤本里双方的说法。

beats.textZh: 南路的猴军由安伽陀和哈奴曼率领，找了一个多月仍无消息，来到南方大海边时都绝望了，打算绝食而死。这时，一只没有翅膀的老鹫出现了，他是阇吒优私的哥哥商波底。他告诉猴子们：悉多被关在大海对面一百由旬外的楞伽城。说完，他烧焦的翅膀竟重新长了出来。可是谁能跳过这么宽的海？老熊王阇婆梵提醒哈奴曼：你是风神的儿子，小时候曾一跃扑向太阳，你的力量连你自己都忘了。哈奴曼站上摩亨陀罗山，身体越变越大，用力一蹬，山都被踩得渗出水来，他像一支箭一样飞上了天。海中的弥那迦山从水里升起，请他歇脚，他只轻轻碰了一下就继续飞；蛇母须罗娑奉众神之命张开大嘴考验他，他先把身体变得巨大，又突然缩得像拇指一样小，从她嘴里钻进去又钻出来；女妖辛悉迦抓住他的影子把他往下拖，他钻进她的身体把她撕开。最后，他落在楞伽城外的三峰山上。
beats.textEn: The southern party under Aṅgada and Hanumān searched for over a month in vain and, reaching the southern sea, despaired and resolved to starve. Then a wingless old vulture appeared — Sampāti, Jaṭāyu's elder brother — who told them Sītā was held in Laṅkā, a hundred leagues across the sea; as he spoke his scorched wings grew again. But who could leap so far? The old bear-king Jāmbavān reminded Hanumān that he was the wind god's son, who as a child had sprung at the sun, and whose strength he had forgotten. Hanumān swelled to a great size on Mount Mahendra, pressed it until water oozed from its rocks, and flew like an arrow. The mountain Maināka rose from the sea to offer him rest; Surasā, mother of serpents, opened her jaws to test him, and he grew huge, then shrank to a thumb's size and darted in and out; Siṃhikā seized his shadow, and he tore her from within. At last he landed on Mount Trikūṭa outside Laṅkā.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第四至五卷·商波底与哈奴曼跨海。

beats.textZh: 哈奴曼把身体缩得像猫一样小，趁着夜色潜入楞伽。他看遍了金碧辉煌的宫殿和罗波那的后宫，一度把熟睡的王后曼度陀哩误认为悉多，随即醒悟：悉多绝不会在这里安睡。最后，他在无忧树林里找到了她：她消瘦苍白，穿着沾满尘土的衣服，被一群面目狰狞的女罗刹围着。罗波那来了，又是威胁又是引诱，说只剩两个月期限，到时她若不从，就把她剁了做早饭。悉多在两人之间放下一根草茎，隔着草茎回答他：你配不上我，罗摩的箭会来惩罚你。罗波那走后，哈奴曼躲在树上，轻声唱起罗摩的故事。悉多先是惊恐，以为又是罗波那的幻术，等哈奴曼把罗摩的戒指递给她，她才喜极而泣。哈奴曼要背她回去，悉多拒绝了：她不愿主动碰触罗摩以外的男子，而且应当由罗摩亲自来救她、雪洗耻辱。她把自己的髻珠交给哈奴曼作信物。
beats.textEn: Shrinking to the size of a cat, Hanumān slipped into Laṅkā by night. He searched the golden palaces and Rāvaṇa's women's quarters, once mistaking the sleeping queen Mandodarī for Sītā before realising Sītā would never sleep there. At last he found her in the aśoka grove, thin and pale, in soiled clothes, surrounded by fearsome rākṣasīs. Rāvaṇa came, threatening and coaxing: in two months, if she would not yield, he would have her cut up for his breakfast. Sītā laid a blade of grass between them and answered across it that he was unworthy of her and Rāma's arrows would punish him. When he left, Hanumān, hidden in a tree, softly sang Rāma's story. Sītā feared another illusion until he gave her Rāma's ring, and then wept for joy. He offered to carry her back; she refused, unwilling to touch any man but Rāma and wishing Rāma himself to rescue her and wipe out the insult, and gave him her crest-jewel as a token.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第五卷·无忧树林中的悉多。

beats.textZh: 哈奴曼想试一试罗刹的力量，就把无忧树林毁了个干净，打死了前来捉他的大批卫兵，连罗波那的儿子阿刹也死在他手里。罗波那的长子因陀罗耆用梵天的神兵把他捆住，哈奴曼明知自己挣得开，却甘愿被绑去见罗波那。他当面劝罗波那把悉多还给罗摩，罗波那大怒，下令处死他；罗波那的弟弟维毗沙那提醒说，使者不可杀。于是罗波那下令在他的尾巴上缠上浸油的布点火，牵着他游街示众。悉多听说后，向火神祈祷让火焰变得清凉，哈奴曼果然感到尾巴上的火一点也不烫。他挣脱绳索，跳上屋顶，从一座宫殿跳到另一座宫殿，把楞伽城烧成一片火海。烧完之后他才惊恐地想起悉多，赶紧回去，看见她安然无恙，这才放心。他跃回大海对岸，把髻珠交给罗摩，罗摩把它贴在胸前，泪流满面。
beats.textEn: To test the rākṣasas' strength Hanumān wrecked the aśoka grove and slew the guards sent against him, among them Rāvaṇa's son Akṣa. Rāvaṇa's eldest son Indrajit bound him with the weapon of Brahmā, and Hanumān, though he could break free, let himself be led before Rāvaṇa, whom he urged to return Sītā. Rāvaṇa ordered his death, but his brother Vibhīṣaṇa reminded him that envoys may not be slain; so Rāvaṇa had oiled rags wrapped round Hanumān's tail and set alight, and paraded him through the streets. Sītā prayed to the fire god to be cool to him, and Hanumān felt no heat. Breaking his bonds, he leapt from palace roof to palace roof until Laṅkā was a sea of flame — then, in sudden fear for Sītā, went back and found her unharmed. He leapt back across the sea and gave Rāma the crest-jewel, which Rāma pressed to his breast weeping.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第五卷·火烧楞伽。

beats.textZh: 猴军浩浩荡荡向南进发，来到大海边。楞伽城里，维毗沙那劝哥哥把悉多还回去，免得国破家亡，罗波那却骂他是叛徒。维毗沙那带着四个随从飞过大海来投奔罗摩。须羯哩婆怀疑他是奸细，罗摩说：凡是来向我求庇护的，我都要保护，哪怕是罗波那本人。他接纳了维毗沙那，当场为他举行了楞伽王的灌顶。罗摩向大海祈求让路，在海边躺了三天三夜，大海毫无回应。罗摩发怒，搭箭要把大海射干，海神这才从水中升起，告诉他：猴军中的那罗是工巧天的儿子，让他来造桥，我会托住桥身。猴子们拔来大树、搬来山石，扔进海里，五天之内，一座一百由旬长的石桥横跨了大海。猴军踏着石桥渡海，把楞伽城团团围住。
beats.textEn: The army marched south to the sea. In Laṅkā Vibhīṣaṇa urged his brother to return Sītā before ruin came, and Rāvaṇa called him a traitor; so Vibhīṣaṇa flew across the sea with four companions to Rāma. Sugrīva suspected a spy, but Rāma said he would protect anyone who sought his refuge, even Rāvaṇa himself, and consecrated Vibhīṣaṇa then and there as king of Laṅkā. Rāma lay three days by the shore begging the ocean to give way; when it did not answer, he angrily drew an arrow to dry it up, and the Ocean rose from the waters and told him that Nala, son of the divine architect Viśvakarman, could build a bridge that the sea would bear. The monkeys hurled trees and rocks into the sea, and in five days a bridge a hundred leagues long spanned it. The army crossed and laid siege to Laṅkā.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·维毗沙那投奔与那罗造桥。

beats.textZh: 大战开始了。罗波那的儿子因陀罗耆能隐身作战，他躲在云中放出蛇箭，把罗摩和罗什曼那捆得动弹不得，猴军以为两位王子已死。危急之时，金翅鸟从天而降，群蛇见了天敌纷纷逃散，兄弟俩才得以解脱。罗波那的弟弟鸠槃羯叻拿身躯如山，一睡就是几个月，罗刹们敲锣打鼓、赶着大象从他身上踩过才把他叫醒。他冲进战场大口吞吃猴子，连须羯哩婆也被他夹走。罗摩用箭射断了他的双臂和双腿，最后射下了他的头。因陀罗耆又用梵天的神兵射倒了几乎整支猴军，哈奴曼奉命飞到喜马拉雅山采药，认不出是哪几种草药，就把整座山峰连根拔起托了回来，药草的香气让倒下的猴子全都复活了。最后，罗什曼那与因陀罗耆展开激战，射下了他的头。
beats.textEn: The war began. Rāvaṇa's son Indrajit, who could fight unseen, shot serpent-arrows from the clouds that bound Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa so fast the monkeys thought them dead — until Garuḍa swooped down and the serpents fled from their enemy. Rāvaṇa's giant brother Kumbhakarṇa, who slept for months at a time, was woken with drums and with elephants driven over his body; he strode into battle devouring monkeys and carried off Sugrīva, until Rāma's arrows severed his arms and legs and at last his head. Indrajit then felled almost the whole army with the weapon of Brahmā; Hanumān flew to the Himalaya for healing herbs and, unable to tell which they were, tore up the whole peak and brought it back, and the herbs' fragrance revived the fallen. At last Lakṣmaṇa fought Indrajit and shot off his head.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·因陀罗耆、鸠槃羯叻拿与药山。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 哈奴曼取药山的情节在通行本里出现过两次（一次救全军，一次救罗什曼那），各本次序不尽相同；本节只概述其中一次。

beats.textZh: 儿子和兄弟都死了，罗波那终于亲自出战。他用一支神矛击中罗什曼那，哈奴曼再一次取来草药救活了他。因陀罗派自己的车夫摩多梨驾着天车来帮助罗摩。两人的决战持续了很久，天地为之震动。罗摩一箭射下罗波那的一个头，立刻又长出一个新的头来；他一连射下了一百个头，罗波那仍然不死。这时摩多梨提醒他：用梵天的神兵吧。罗摩搭上仙人投山传给他的那支梵天之箭，箭上燃着火焰，带着风的速度，一箭射穿了罗波那的心脏。十首魔王从车上倒下，众神从天上撒下花雨。维毗沙那为哥哥痛哭，犹豫要不要为这个恶人举行葬礼，罗摩对他说：仇恨到死亡为止，他现在也是我的兄弟，为他举行葬礼吧。随后，维毗沙那在楞伽登上了王位。
beats.textEn: With his sons and brother dead, Rāvaṇa came out to fight himself. He struck down Lakṣmaṇa with a dart, and Hanumān again brought herbs to revive him. Indra sent his charioteer Mātali with his celestial chariot to carry Rāma. Their duel lasted long and shook heaven and earth. Each time Rāma's arrow struck off one of Rāvaṇa's heads, another grew in its place, until a hundred had fallen and he still lived. Then Mātali reminded Rāma of the weapon of Brahmā. Rāma loosed the arrow Agastya had given him, flaming and swift as the wind, and it pierced Rāvaṇa's heart; the ten-headed king fell from his chariot, and the gods rained flowers. When Vibhīṣaṇa wept and hesitated to give his wicked brother funeral rites, Rāma told him that enmity ends with death: Rāvaṇa was his brother too, and the rites should be done. Vibhīṣaṇa was then crowned king of Laṅkā.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·罗波那之死。

beats.headingEn: The ordeal of fire and the return home
beats.textZh: 悉多沐浴更衣后被带到罗摩面前。当着众人的面，罗摩却说出冷酷的话：我打这一仗，是为了洗雪家族的耻辱，不是为了你；你在别人家里住了这么久，现在你想去哪里就去哪里吧。悉多泪流满面，却镇定而有尊严地回答：我的心从来只属于你，被抓走不是我的过错。她请罗什曼那堆起柴堆，向火神祈祷后走进了火焰。火神从火中升起，把毫发无损的悉多交还给罗摩，宣布她清白无瑕。梵天和众神也现身，告诉罗摩他就是那罗延（毗湿奴）本身，十车王也乘着天车出现，祝福儿子。罗摩说：我早知道悉多是清白的，只是要让天下人都看到。他们乘着飞车布湿波迦飞回阿逾陀。在南迪村，婆罗多捧着那双鞋子出城迎接，把王国交还给哥哥。罗摩加冕为王，史诗说，在他统治的年代里，没有寡妇哀哭，没有疾病和盗贼，人们长寿而安乐。
beats.textEn: Sītā, bathed and adorned, was brought before Rāma. Before everyone he spoke harshly: he had fought to wipe out the insult to his line, not for her; she had lived long in another's house and might now go where she pleased. Weeping, but with calm dignity, Sītā answered that her heart had always been his and her capture was not her fault. She asked Lakṣmaṇa to build a pyre, prayed to the fire god and entered the flames. Agni rose from the fire, gave her back to Rāma unharmed and declared her pure. Brahmā and the gods appeared and told Rāma he was Nārāyaṇa himself, and Daśaratha came in a celestial car to bless his son. Rāma said he had known Sītā was pure but the world had to see it. In the flying chariot Puṣpaka they returned to Ayodhyā; at Nandigrāma Bharata met them with the sandals and restored the kingdom. Rāma was crowned, and in his reign, says the epic, no widow wept, there was no sickness or theft, and people lived long and happily.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·悉多的火之考验、回国与加冕。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 火的考验是今天印度内外讨论最多的情节之一；第七卷（后篇）里还有悉多被第二次放逐的故事，不在本篇范围。

deityStoryCards.name: Sītā
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Daughter of King Janaka, found in a ploughed furrow, wife of Rāma; revered in Hindu tradition as a form of Lakṣmī.

beats.headingEn: A cry of grief becomes a verse
beats.textZh: 史诗从诗人自己讲起。苦行者蚁垤问仙人那罗陀：如今世上，有没有一个既有德行又有勇气、懂得正法、知恩图报、言而有信的人？那罗陀说：有，他就是甘蔗王族的罗摩，接着把罗摩的一生简要讲了一遍。不久，蚁垤到多摩萨河边沐浴，看见一对麻鹬正在树上相亲相爱，一个猎人一箭射死了雄鸟，雌鸟围着倒在血泊里的伴侣哀哀悲鸣。蚁垤心中涌起悲悯，脱口说出一句诅咒猎人的话——话一出口，他自己也吃了一惊：这句话音节整齐，可以和着琴弦吟唱。他把这种由悲伤（śoka）而生的诗体叫做“输洛迦”（śloka）。这时梵天亲自来到他面前，对他说：就用这种诗体，把那罗陀讲给你的罗摩的故事完整地唱出来吧；你所写的一切都会是真实的，只要山川还在，这部诗就会在世间流传。
beats.textEn: The epic begins with its own poet. The ascetic Vālmīki asked the sage Nārada whether there was any man on earth who was virtuous, brave, grateful and true to his word; Nārada told him of Rāma of the Ikṣvāku line and sketched his life. Soon after, bathing by the river Tamasā, Vālmīki saw a hunter shoot one of a pair of mating curlews, and heard the hen cry over her fallen mate. Pity broke from him as a curse on the hunter — in measured syllables that could be sung to the lute. He called this metre, born of grief (śoka), the śloka. Then Brahmā came to him and told him to sing the whole story of Rāma in that metre: all he wrote would be true, and it would endure while mountains and rivers lasted.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·开篇（那罗陀、梵天来访）。

beats.headingEn: The golden bowl from the sacrificial fire
beats.textZh: 阿逾陀城的国王十车王富有、公正、受人爱戴，却没有儿子。他举行了马祭，又请仙人鹿角主持求子的祭祀。就在这时，天上的众神来到梵天面前诉苦：罗刹王罗波那靠苦行从梵天那里得到恩典，天神、乾闼婆、夜叉和罗刹都杀不死他——他看不起人类，根本没有把人算进去。他仗着这个恩典欺压三界，众神毫无办法。正说着，毗湿奴骑着金翅鸟来了。众神恳求他化身为人，降生为十车王的四个儿子，去除掉罗波那。毗湿奴答应了。于是从十车王的祭火中走出一位光芒四射的神灵，捧着一只盛满天界乳粥的金碗。国王把乳粥分给三位王后：憍萨厘雅生下了罗摩，吉迦伊生下了婆罗多，须弥多罗生下了一对双胞胎——罗什曼那和设睹卢祇那。
beats.textEn: Daśaratha, king of Ayodhyā, was rich, just and beloved, but had no son. He performed the horse sacrifice and a rite for sons with the sage Ṛṣyaśṛṅga. Meanwhile the gods complained to Brahmā: Rāvaṇa, king of the rākṣasas, had won by austerities a boon that no god, gandharva, yakṣa or rākṣasa could slay him — scorning men, he had not even named them — and he was oppressing the three worlds. Vishnu arrived on Garuḍa, and the gods begged him to be born as a man, as Daśaratha's four sons, to destroy Rāvaṇa. He agreed. From the sacrificial fire rose a radiant being bearing a golden bowl of heavenly rice-milk; the king shared it among his queens, and Kausalyā bore Rāma, Kaikeyī Bharata, and Sumitrā the twins Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·求子祭祀与众神的请求。

beats.headingEn: Into the forest with the sage
beats.textZh: 王子们长大了，个个精通经典和武艺，其中罗摩最受众人喜爱，罗什曼那则像影子一样跟着他。一天，大仙人众友来到王宫，请国王把还不满十六岁的罗摩借给他，去保护他的祭祀不受罗刹的骚扰。十车王舍不得，宁愿自己率军前往，但在家庭祭司婆私吒的劝说下终于答应了。众友带着罗摩和罗什曼那上路，教给他们能驱除饥渴和疲劳的咒语。在一片荒凉的森林里，女罗刹多吒迦向他们扑来，罗摩起初不愿杀害女子，只想把她打退，众友却催促他说，为了保护众生，这样做并不违背正法。罗摩便射杀了她。众友非常满意，把许多神兵的咒语传授给他。到了众友的净修林，祭祀开始的第六天，罗刹摩哩遮和苏跋呼带人从天上撒下血肉，罗摩一箭把摩哩遮射飞到一百由旬外的海里，又射死了苏跋呼。
beats.textEn: The princes grew up learned in scripture and arms; Rāma was loved by all, and Lakṣmaṇa followed him like his shadow. One day the great sage Viśvāmitra came and asked for Rāma, not yet sixteen, to guard his sacrifice from rākṣasas. Daśaratha begged to go himself with an army, but the family priest Vasiṣṭha persuaded him. On the road Viśvāmitra taught the brothers spells against hunger and weariness. In a desolate forest the rākṣasī Tāṭakā rushed at them; Rāma was loth to kill a woman, but the sage urged that protecting the world was no breach of dharma, and Rāma shot her. Pleased, Viśvāmitra gave him the spells of the divine weapons. On the sixth day of the sacrifice Mārīca and Subāhu rained blood from the sky; Rāma's arrow hurled Mārīca a hundred leagues into the sea and killed Subāhu.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·众友的祭祀与多吒迦。

beats.textZh: 众友又带着两位王子前往弥提罗国。弥提罗的国王遮那竭告诉他们：有一次他为祭祀耕地，犁头翻开的犁沟里出现了一个女婴，他给她取名悉多，当作亲生女儿养大。他立下誓言，谁能拉开祖先传下来的湿婆大弓，就把悉多嫁给谁。许多国王都来试过，却连举都举不起来。那张弓装在一辆八个轮子的铁车上，由五千个壮汉拉了出来。罗摩打开弓匣，像玩耍一样轻轻把弓举起，给它装上弦，然后用力一拉——大弓从中间断成了两截，发出像雷霆、像山崩一样的巨响，在场的人全都吓得跌倒在地，只有众友、遮那竭和两位王子还站着。遮那竭欢喜地把悉多许给了罗摩。十车王赶来，四兄弟在同一天成婚。回国路上，持斧罗摩拦路挑战，罗摩又拉开了他带来的毗湿奴大弓，持斧罗摩才心服离去。
beats.textEn: Viśvāmitra then led the princes to Mithilā. King Janaka told them that once, ploughing ground for a sacrifice, he had found a baby girl in the furrow; he named her Sītā and raised her as his daughter, vowing to give her to whoever could string the bow of Śiva that his ancestors had kept. Many kings had failed even to lift it. Five thousand men drew it out on an eight-wheeled iron cart. Rāma opened the case, raised the bow as if in play, strung it and drew it — and it broke in the middle with a crash like thunder or a falling mountain. Everyone fell to the ground except Viśvāmitra, Janaka and the two princes. Janaka gave Sītā to Rāma, and the four brothers were married on one day. On the road home Paraśurāma challenged Rāma, who strung the bow of Vishnu as well, and the challenger withdrew.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·第六十七章“断弓”。

beats.textZh: 许多年过去了，十车王年事已高，决定立罗摩为太子，满城百姓欢天喜地，挂起彩旗，准备第二天的灌顶典礼。可是王后吉迦伊身边的驼背侍女曼他罗，在宫墙上看到这番景象，急忙跑去对吉迦伊说：罗摩一旦登基，你的儿子婆罗多就只能做奴仆，甚至会被赶出国去。起初吉迦伊还为罗摩高兴，送给曼他罗一件首饰；但曼他罗一再挑拨，终于说动了她，还提醒她：当年你在与商钵罗的战争中救过国王的命，国王许给你两个恩典，你一直没有用。吉迦伊扯下首饰，躺在“愤怒之室”的地上。十车王来了，看见心爱的王后这样，就以罗摩的名义发誓答应她的任何要求。吉迦伊说：第一，立婆罗多为太子；第二，让罗摩穿上树皮衣，到弹宅迦林中流放十四年。国王听了昏倒在地，哀求了整整一夜，吉迦伊却毫不动摇。
beats.textEn: Years later the aged Daśaratha resolved to make Rāma heir, and the city hung out banners for the consecration. But Kaikeyī's hunchbacked maid Mantharā, seeing the rejoicing from the palace roof, ran to tell her mistress that once Rāma reigned, her son Bharata would be a servant or an exile. At first Kaikeyī was glad for Rāma and gave Mantharā a jewel, but Mantharā worked on her until she yielded, reminding her of the two boons the king had promised when she saved his life in the war against Śambara. Kaikeyī tore off her ornaments and lay on the floor of the chamber of wrath. When the king, finding her so, swore by Rāma to grant her wish, she asked that Bharata be made heir and that Rāma go in bark garments to the Daṇḍaka forest for fourteen years. The king fell senseless and pleaded all night in vain.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·曼他罗与吉迦伊的恩典。

beats.textZh: 第二天一早，罗摩被召进宫，吉迦伊把国王的决定告诉了他。罗摩的脸色一点也没有变，他平静地说：为了父亲的诺言，我今天就去森林。母亲憍萨厘雅悲痛欲绝；罗什曼那怒不可遏，要拿起武器夺回王位，罗摩却劝住他说：遵守父亲的话就是正法。罗摩去向悉多告别，劝她留在宫中。悉多却说：妻子的命运就是丈夫的命运，有你在的森林，胜过没有你的宫殿；你要是不带我去，我就去死。罗什曼那也坚持要一起走。三人脱下华服，穿上树皮衣。全城的人哭着跟在车后，一直送到城外。他们在恒河边得到猎人首领古诃的帮助渡过了河，从此走进了森林。
beats.textEn: Next morning Rāma was summoned and Kaikeyī told him the king's decision. His face did not change; he said calmly that for his father's word he would go to the forest that very day. His mother Kausalyā was overwhelmed with grief; Lakṣmaṇa raged and would have taken the throne by arms, but Rāma restrained him, saying that obeying their father was dharma. When Rāma bade Sītā stay behind, she answered that a wife's lot is her husband's lot, that the forest with him was better than a palace without him, and that if he left her she would die. Lakṣmaṇa too insisted on coming. The three put off their fine clothes and put on bark garments, the whole city followed their chariot weeping, and on the Ganges the hunter chief Guha ferried them across into the forest.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·罗摩出城流放。

beats.textZh: 车夫苏曼多罗独自赶着空车回来，十车王听说儿子真的走进了森林，悲痛得一病不起。夜里，他对憍萨厘雅讲起了年轻时犯下的一桩罪过：那时他自恃能“听声射箭”，在黑夜的河边听见像大象饮水的声音，一箭射去，射中的却是一个正在用水罐打水的年轻苦行者。少年临死前请他把水带给自己又老又瞎的父母。两位老人得知儿子的死讯，父亲诅咒国王：你将来也会像我一样，为了思念儿子而死。十车王说：这个诅咒如今应验了。他一遍遍呼唤着罗摩的名字，在午夜时分死去了。
beats.textEn: When the charioteer Sumantra came back alone, Daśaratha, hearing that his son had truly entered the forest, fell ill with grief. That night he told Kausalyā of a sin of his youth: proud of shooting at a sound, he had heard by a dark river what seemed an elephant drinking and loosed an arrow — but struck a young ascetic filling a water jar. The dying boy asked him to carry water to his old, blind parents. On hearing of their son's death the father cursed the king to die, like him, grieving for a son. That curse, Daśaratha said, was now fulfilled; and calling Rāma's name he died at midnight.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·十车王之死。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 那位少年苦行者在后世传统中常被叫做“室罗波那”（Śravaṇa），蚁垤本里没有给出这个名字。

beats.headingEn: A pair of sandals on the throne
beats.textZh: 婆罗多从舅父家回来，才知道父亲已死、兄长被流放，而这一切都是母亲为他谋来的。他痛斥吉迦伊，拒绝接受王位，为父亲办完葬礼后，带着母亲们和军队进入森林，去质多罗俱吒山找罗摩。兄弟相见，罗摩得知父亲去世，悲痛不已。婆罗多跪在他面前恳求他回去为王，众人也一齐劝说。罗摩却说：父亲的诺言必须遵守，十四年期满之前，我不会回去。婆罗多无可奈何，请罗摩把脚上那双饰金的鞋子给他。他把鞋子顶在头上带回去，供在王座上，自己穿上树皮衣，住在城外的南迪村，以“鞋子的仆人”的身份代为治理国家，并且发誓：十四年期满那天罗摩若不回来，他就投火而死。
beats.textEn: Bharata returned from his uncle's house to learn that his father was dead and his brother exiled, all for his sake. He rebuked Kaikeyī, refused the throne, performed his father's rites and went with the queens and the army to Mount Citrakūṭa to find Rāma. When the brothers met, Rāma mourned their father. Bharata knelt and begged him to return and reign, and all joined in; but Rāma answered that his father's word must be kept, and he would not return before the fourteen years were over. Then Bharata asked for Rāma's gold-adorned sandals. Carrying them on his head, he set them on the throne, put on bark garments, and ruled from the village of Nandigrāma as the sandals' servant, vowing to enter the fire if Rāma did not return on the appointed day.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·婆罗多寻兄与鞋子。

beats.textZh: 罗摩一行在弹宅迦林中住了许多年，保护林中的苦行者，仙人投山把毗湿奴的神弓和永不空竭的箭囊送给了他。后来他们在戈达瓦里河边的五树林住下，罗什曼那搭了一座草屋。一天，罗波那的妹妹、女罗刹首哩薄那迦看见了罗摩，爱上了他，要他做丈夫。罗摩开玩笑地说自己已有妻子，让她去找罗什曼那；罗什曼那也开玩笑地把她推回给罗摩。她恼羞成怒，以为是悉多挡了路，张牙舞爪地向悉多扑去。罗摩命令罗什曼那惩罚她，罗什曼那拔剑割下了她的鼻子和耳朵。首哩薄那迦哭着逃到哥哥伽罗那里。伽罗先派十四个罗刹去，被罗摩全部射死；接着伽罗和突舍那率领一万四千罗刹大军杀来，罗摩让罗什曼那带着悉多躲进山洞，自己一个人迎战，把整支大军消灭了。
beats.textEn: For years they lived in the Daṇḍaka forest protecting its hermits, and the sage Agastya gave Rāma the bow of Vishnu and inexhaustible quivers. Then they settled at Pañcavaṭī on the Godāvarī, where Lakṣmaṇa built a hut. There Rāvaṇa's sister, the rākṣasī Śūrpaṇakhā, saw Rāma and desired him. Rāma jestingly said he had a wife and sent her to Lakṣmaṇa, who in jest sent her back. Enraged and blaming Sītā, she rushed at her; at Rāma's command Lakṣmaṇa cut off her nose and ears. She fled to her brother Khara. Khara sent fourteen rākṣasas, whom Rāma shot down; then Khara and Dūṣaṇa came with fourteen thousand, and Rāma, sending Lakṣmaṇa with Sītā to a cave, destroyed the whole host alone.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·首哩薄那迦与伽罗之军。

beats.textZh: 首哩薄那迦逃到楞伽，当众责骂罗波那只顾享乐，连自己的国土都保不住，又极力夸赞悉多的美貌。罗波那动了心，乘着飞车去找当年被罗摩一箭射进海里的摩哩遮。摩哩遮吓得发抖，劝他千万别去招惹罗摩；罗波那却威胁说，不听命令就杀了他。摩哩遮叹道：反正都是死，死在罗摩手里还好些。他变成一只金色的鹿，身上点缀着银色的斑点，角尖像宝石，在草屋前来回走动。悉多一见就喜欢上了，求罗摩去捉。罗什曼那提醒说这一定是摩哩遮的幻术，罗摩还是嘱咐弟弟守护悉多，自己追了出去。金鹿时隐时现，把他引得越来越远，罗摩终于一箭射中。摩哩遮现出原形，临死前学着罗摩的声音大喊：“啊，悉多！啊，罗什曼那！”悉多听了惊慌失措，催罗什曼那去救。罗什曼那说没有人能伤害罗摩，悉多竟说出刺耳的话，指责他心怀不轨。罗什曼那受了委屈，只好离开草屋。
beats.textEn: Śūrpaṇakhā fled to Laṅkā, rebuked Rāvaṇa for his idleness and praised Sītā's beauty. Rāvaṇa flew in his chariot to Mārīca, whom Rāma's arrow had once hurled into the sea. Mārīca trembled and begged him not to provoke Rāma, but Rāvaṇa threatened to kill him, and he sighed that it was better to die by Rāma's hand. He became a golden deer dappled with silver, its horns tipped with gems, and grazed before the hut. Sītā longed for it. Lakṣmaṇa warned it was Mārīca's magic, but Rāma left him to guard Sītā and gave chase. The deer led him far away until his arrow struck it; dying, Mārīca cried out in Rāma's voice, ‘Ah Sītā! Ah Lakṣmaṇa!’ Sītā, frantic, urged Lakṣmaṇa to go; when he said none could harm Rāma, she accused him with cruel words of wanting her for himself, and, wounded, he went.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·摩哩遮与金鹿。

beats.headingEn: The ten-headed king and the vulture
beats.textZh: 罗什曼那刚走，罗波那就扮成一个云游的婆罗门苦行者来到草屋前。悉多按待客之礼请他进来，给他水和食物，并告诉他自己是谁。罗波那这才夸耀自己是楞伽之王，要她做他的王后。悉多轻蔑地回答：你就像一只想得到母狮的豺狗。罗波那现出了十个头的真身，一把抓住她，拖上飞车，向南飞去。悉多一路向树木、河流和山神呼喊，求它们告诉罗摩。年老的鹫王阇吒优私是十车王的朋友，他拦住罗波那，劝他放了悉多，随即与他搏斗，打碎了他的车子，杀死了驾车的驴子和车夫；可他终究年老力衰，被罗波那砍断了翅膀和双脚，跌落在地。飞过一座山时，悉多看见山顶上坐着五只猴子，就把自己的披巾和首饰包在一起扔了下去。罗波那把她带回楞伽，给她十二个月的期限，把她关在无忧树林里，由许多女罗刹看守。
beats.textEn: As soon as Lakṣmaṇa had gone, Rāvaṇa came to the hut disguised as a wandering brahmin ascetic. Sītā received him as a guest with water and food and told him who she was. Then he boasted that he was king of Laṅkā and asked her to be his queen; she answered scornfully that he was a jackal longing for a lioness. Rāvaṇa took his true ten-headed form, seized her and carried her off southward in his chariot while she called on the trees, rivers and mountain spirits to tell Rāma. The old vulture-king Jaṭāyu, friend of Daśaratha, barred his way, smashed his chariot and killed its asses and driver, but, old and spent, had his wings and feet cut off by Rāvaṇa. Passing a hill where five monkeys sat, Sītā dropped her scarf and ornaments. In Laṅkā Rāvaṇa gave her twelve months and set her in the aśoka grove under guard of rākṣasīs.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·悉多被劫与阇吒优私。

beats.textZh: 罗摩在回来的路上遇见了罗什曼那，心中顿生不祥之感。草屋果然空无一人。罗摩悲痛欲狂，向树木、河流和野兽一一询问悉多的下落，看到散落的花朵、折断的车子和血迹，以为她被罗刹吃掉了，怒气冲冲地要毁灭世界，罗什曼那苦苦劝他冷静。他们找到奄奄一息的阇吒优私，鹫王告诉他们是罗波那劫走了悉多、往南方去了，说完就断了气。罗摩像为父亲举行葬礼一样，亲手为他火化。兄弟俩继续向南，被一个没有头、胸前长着大嘴的怪物迦槃陀抓住，他们砍断了他的两只长臂。迦槃陀在火葬的火焰中恢复了天神的形貌，告诉他们：去般波湖边的哩舍牟迦山找猴王须羯哩婆，他会帮你们找到悉多。在般波湖边，年老的女苦行者舍波哩欢喜地迎接了罗摩，随后升入天界。
beats.textEn: On the way back Rāma met Lakṣmaṇa and felt dread; the hut was empty. Half mad with grief, Rāma asked the trees, rivers and beasts where Sītā was; seeing scattered flowers, a broken chariot and blood, he thought rākṣasas had eaten her and threatened to destroy the worlds until Lakṣmaṇa calmed him. They found the dying Jaṭāyu, who told them Rāvaṇa had taken Sītā south, and died. Rāma cremated him with the rites due to a father. Going on, they were seized by the headless monster Kabandha, whose mouth was in his chest, and cut off his long arms; restored to divine form in his funeral fire, he told them to seek the monkey-king Sugrīva on Mount Ṛśyamūka by Lake Pampā. There the aged ascetic woman Śabarī welcomed Rāma joyfully and then rose to heaven.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·罗摩的哀伤、阇吒优私、迦槃陀与舍波哩。

beats.textZh: 哈奴曼扮成苦行者来迎接他们，把他们带到须羯哩婆面前。罗摩和须羯哩婆围着火结为盟友。须羯哩婆拿出那包从天上落下的首饰，罗摩认出是悉多的，痛哭失声；罗什曼那说，耳环和手镯他认不出，只认得脚镯，因为他每天向悉多行礼时只看她的脚。须羯哩婆讲了自己的遭遇：哥哥波林夺走了他的妻子和王国，把他赶到这座山上。罗摩一箭射穿七棵娑罗树，让他相信自己的力量。须羯哩婆向波林挑战，罗摩藏在树后；第一次两兄弟长得太像，罗摩分不清；第二次须羯哩婆戴上花环，罗摩一箭射中了波林。垂死的波林责问罗摩为什么从暗处射他，罗摩回答：你夺了弟弟的妻子，作为国王的代表，我有责任惩罚你。须羯哩婆登上王位，雨季过后，他派出四路猴军寻找悉多，罗摩把刻着自己名字的戒指交给了往南去的哈奴曼。
beats.textEn: Hanumān, disguised as an ascetic, met them and brought them to Sugrīva, and Rāma and Sugrīva swore friendship around a fire. Sugrīva showed the bundle of ornaments that had fallen from the sky; Rāma knew them as Sītā's and wept, and Lakṣmaṇa said he knew only her anklets, for he had looked only at her feet when he bowed to her. Sugrīva told how his brother Vālin had taken his wife and kingdom. Rāma shot an arrow through seven sāl trees to prove his strength. When the brothers fought, Rāma stood hidden behind a tree; the first time he could not tell them apart, the second time Sugrīva wore a garland, and Rāma's arrow struck Vālin. The dying Vālin reproached him for shooting from hiding; Rāma answered that Vālin had taken his brother's wife and that he punished him on the king's behalf. Sugrīva was crowned, and after the rains sent search parties to the four quarters; Rāma gave his signet ring to Hanumān, who went south.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第四卷·与须羯哩婆结盟与波林之死。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 罗摩从暗处射杀波林是否合乎正法，在印度传统内部本身就有长久的争论；本站只讲蚁垤本里双方的说法。

beats.textZh: 南路的猴军由安伽陀和哈奴曼率领，找了一个多月仍无消息，来到南方大海边时都绝望了，打算绝食而死。这时，一只没有翅膀的老鹫出现了，他是阇吒优私的哥哥商波底。他告诉猴子们：悉多被关在大海对面一百由旬外的楞伽城。说完，他烧焦的翅膀竟重新长了出来。可是谁能跳过这么宽的海？老熊王阇婆梵提醒哈奴曼：你是风神的儿子，小时候曾一跃扑向太阳，你的力量连你自己都忘了。哈奴曼站上摩亨陀罗山，身体越变越大，用力一蹬，山都被踩得渗出水来，他像一支箭一样飞上了天。海中的弥那迦山从水里升起，请他歇脚，他只轻轻碰了一下就继续飞；蛇母须罗娑奉众神之命张开大嘴考验他，他先把身体变得巨大，又突然缩得像拇指一样小，从她嘴里钻进去又钻出来；女妖辛悉迦抓住他的影子把他往下拖，他钻进她的身体把她撕开。最后，他落在楞伽城外的三峰山上。
beats.textEn: The southern party under Aṅgada and Hanumān searched for over a month in vain and, reaching the southern sea, despaired and resolved to starve. Then a wingless old vulture appeared — Sampāti, Jaṭāyu's elder brother — who told them Sītā was held in Laṅkā, a hundred leagues across the sea; as he spoke his scorched wings grew again. But who could leap so far? The old bear-king Jāmbavān reminded Hanumān that he was the wind god's son, who as a child had sprung at the sun, and whose strength he had forgotten. Hanumān swelled to a great size on Mount Mahendra, pressed it until water oozed from its rocks, and flew like an arrow. The mountain Maināka rose from the sea to offer him rest; Surasā, mother of serpents, opened her jaws to test him, and he grew huge, then shrank to a thumb's size and darted in and out; Siṃhikā seized his shadow, and he tore her from within. At last he landed on Mount Trikūṭa outside Laṅkā.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第四至五卷·商波底与哈奴曼跨海。

beats.textZh: 哈奴曼把身体缩得像猫一样小，趁着夜色潜入楞伽。他看遍了金碧辉煌的宫殿和罗波那的后宫，一度把熟睡的王后曼度陀哩误认为悉多，随即醒悟：悉多绝不会在这里安睡。最后，他在无忧树林里找到了她：她消瘦苍白，穿着沾满尘土的衣服，被一群面目狰狞的女罗刹围着。罗波那来了，又是威胁又是引诱，说只剩两个月期限，到时她若不从，就把她剁了做早饭。悉多在两人之间放下一根草茎，隔着草茎回答他：你配不上我，罗摩的箭会来惩罚你。罗波那走后，哈奴曼躲在树上，轻声唱起罗摩的故事。悉多先是惊恐，以为又是罗波那的幻术，等哈奴曼把罗摩的戒指递给她，她才喜极而泣。哈奴曼要背她回去，悉多拒绝了：她不愿主动碰触罗摩以外的男子，而且应当由罗摩亲自来救她、雪洗耻辱。她把自己的髻珠交给哈奴曼作信物。
beats.textEn: Shrinking to the size of a cat, Hanumān slipped into Laṅkā by night. He searched the golden palaces and Rāvaṇa's women's quarters, once mistaking the sleeping queen Mandodarī for Sītā before realising Sītā would never sleep there. At last he found her in the aśoka grove, thin and pale, in soiled clothes, surrounded by fearsome rākṣasīs. Rāvaṇa came, threatening and coaxing: in two months, if she would not yield, he would have her cut up for his breakfast. Sītā laid a blade of grass between them and answered across it that he was unworthy of her and Rāma's arrows would punish him. When he left, Hanumān, hidden in a tree, softly sang Rāma's story. Sītā feared another illusion until he gave her Rāma's ring, and then wept for joy. He offered to carry her back; she refused, unwilling to touch any man but Rāma and wishing Rāma himself to rescue her and wipe out the insult, and gave him her crest-jewel as a token.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第五卷·无忧树林中的悉多。

beats.textZh: 哈奴曼想试一试罗刹的力量，就把无忧树林毁了个干净，打死了前来捉他的大批卫兵，连罗波那的儿子阿刹也死在他手里。罗波那的长子因陀罗耆用梵天的神兵把他捆住，哈奴曼明知自己挣得开，却甘愿被绑去见罗波那。他当面劝罗波那把悉多还给罗摩，罗波那大怒，下令处死他；罗波那的弟弟维毗沙那提醒说，使者不可杀。于是罗波那下令在他的尾巴上缠上浸油的布点火，牵着他游街示众。悉多听说后，向火神祈祷让火焰变得清凉，哈奴曼果然感到尾巴上的火一点也不烫。他挣脱绳索，跳上屋顶，从一座宫殿跳到另一座宫殿，把楞伽城烧成一片火海。烧完之后他才惊恐地想起悉多，赶紧回去，看见她安然无恙，这才放心。他跃回大海对岸，把髻珠交给罗摩，罗摩把它贴在胸前，泪流满面。
beats.textEn: To test the rākṣasas' strength Hanumān wrecked the aśoka grove and slew the guards sent against him, among them Rāvaṇa's son Akṣa. Rāvaṇa's eldest son Indrajit bound him with the weapon of Brahmā, and Hanumān, though he could break free, let himself be led before Rāvaṇa, whom he urged to return Sītā. Rāvaṇa ordered his death, but his brother Vibhīṣaṇa reminded him that envoys may not be slain; so Rāvaṇa had oiled rags wrapped round Hanumān's tail and set alight, and paraded him through the streets. Sītā prayed to the fire god to be cool to him, and Hanumān felt no heat. Breaking his bonds, he leapt from palace roof to palace roof until Laṅkā was a sea of flame — then, in sudden fear for Sītā, went back and found her unharmed. He leapt back across the sea and gave Rāma the crest-jewel, which Rāma pressed to his breast weeping.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第五卷·火烧楞伽。

beats.textZh: 猴军浩浩荡荡向南进发，来到大海边。楞伽城里，维毗沙那劝哥哥把悉多还回去，免得国破家亡，罗波那却骂他是叛徒。维毗沙那带着四个随从飞过大海来投奔罗摩。须羯哩婆怀疑他是奸细，罗摩说：凡是来向我求庇护的，我都要保护，哪怕是罗波那本人。他接纳了维毗沙那，当场为他举行了楞伽王的灌顶。罗摩向大海祈求让路，在海边躺了三天三夜，大海毫无回应。罗摩发怒，搭箭要把大海射干，海神这才从水中升起，告诉他：猴军中的那罗是工巧天的儿子，让他来造桥，我会托住桥身。猴子们拔来大树、搬来山石，扔进海里，五天之内，一座一百由旬长的石桥横跨了大海。猴军踏着石桥渡海，把楞伽城团团围住。
beats.textEn: The army marched south to the sea. In Laṅkā Vibhīṣaṇa urged his brother to return Sītā before ruin came, and Rāvaṇa called him a traitor; so Vibhīṣaṇa flew across the sea with four companions to Rāma. Sugrīva suspected a spy, but Rāma said he would protect anyone who sought his refuge, even Rāvaṇa himself, and consecrated Vibhīṣaṇa then and there as king of Laṅkā. Rāma lay three days by the shore begging the ocean to give way; when it did not answer, he angrily drew an arrow to dry it up, and the Ocean rose from the waters and told him that Nala, son of the divine architect Viśvakarman, could build a bridge that the sea would bear. The monkeys hurled trees and rocks into the sea, and in five days a bridge a hundred leagues long spanned it. The army crossed and laid siege to Laṅkā.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·维毗沙那投奔与那罗造桥。

beats.textZh: 大战开始了。罗波那的儿子因陀罗耆能隐身作战，他躲在云中放出蛇箭，把罗摩和罗什曼那捆得动弹不得，猴军以为两位王子已死。危急之时，金翅鸟从天而降，群蛇见了天敌纷纷逃散，兄弟俩才得以解脱。罗波那的弟弟鸠槃羯叻拿身躯如山，一睡就是几个月，罗刹们敲锣打鼓、赶着大象从他身上踩过才把他叫醒。他冲进战场大口吞吃猴子，连须羯哩婆也被他夹走。罗摩用箭射断了他的双臂和双腿，最后射下了他的头。因陀罗耆又用梵天的神兵射倒了几乎整支猴军，哈奴曼奉命飞到喜马拉雅山采药，认不出是哪几种草药，就把整座山峰连根拔起托了回来，药草的香气让倒下的猴子全都复活了。最后，罗什曼那与因陀罗耆展开激战，射下了他的头。
beats.textEn: The war began. Rāvaṇa's son Indrajit, who could fight unseen, shot serpent-arrows from the clouds that bound Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa so fast the monkeys thought them dead — until Garuḍa swooped down and the serpents fled from their enemy. Rāvaṇa's giant brother Kumbhakarṇa, who slept for months at a time, was woken with drums and with elephants driven over his body; he strode into battle devouring monkeys and carried off Sugrīva, until Rāma's arrows severed his arms and legs and at last his head. Indrajit then felled almost the whole army with the weapon of Brahmā; Hanumān flew to the Himalaya for healing herbs and, unable to tell which they were, tore up the whole peak and brought it back, and the herbs' fragrance revived the fallen. At last Lakṣmaṇa fought Indrajit and shot off his head.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·因陀罗耆、鸠槃羯叻拿与药山。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 哈奴曼取药山的情节在通行本里出现过两次（一次救全军，一次救罗什曼那），各本次序不尽相同；本节只概述其中一次。

beats.textZh: 儿子和兄弟都死了，罗波那终于亲自出战。他用一支神矛击中罗什曼那，哈奴曼再一次取来草药救活了他。因陀罗派自己的车夫摩多梨驾着天车来帮助罗摩。两人的决战持续了很久，天地为之震动。罗摩一箭射下罗波那的一个头，立刻又长出一个新的头来；他一连射下了一百个头，罗波那仍然不死。这时摩多梨提醒他：用梵天的神兵吧。罗摩搭上仙人投山传给他的那支梵天之箭，箭上燃着火焰，带着风的速度，一箭射穿了罗波那的心脏。十首魔王从车上倒下，众神从天上撒下花雨。维毗沙那为哥哥痛哭，犹豫要不要为这个恶人举行葬礼，罗摩对他说：仇恨到死亡为止，他现在也是我的兄弟，为他举行葬礼吧。随后，维毗沙那在楞伽登上了王位。
beats.textEn: With his sons and brother dead, Rāvaṇa came out to fight himself. He struck down Lakṣmaṇa with a dart, and Hanumān again brought herbs to revive him. Indra sent his charioteer Mātali with his celestial chariot to carry Rāma. Their duel lasted long and shook heaven and earth. Each time Rāma's arrow struck off one of Rāvaṇa's heads, another grew in its place, until a hundred had fallen and he still lived. Then Mātali reminded Rāma of the weapon of Brahmā. Rāma loosed the arrow Agastya had given him, flaming and swift as the wind, and it pierced Rāvaṇa's heart; the ten-headed king fell from his chariot, and the gods rained flowers. When Vibhīṣaṇa wept and hesitated to give his wicked brother funeral rites, Rāma told him that enmity ends with death: Rāvaṇa was his brother too, and the rites should be done. Vibhīṣaṇa was then crowned king of Laṅkā.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·罗波那之死。

beats.headingEn: The ordeal of fire and the return home
beats.textZh: 悉多沐浴更衣后被带到罗摩面前。当着众人的面，罗摩却说出冷酷的话：我打这一仗，是为了洗雪家族的耻辱，不是为了你；你在别人家里住了这么久，现在你想去哪里就去哪里吧。悉多泪流满面，却镇定而有尊严地回答：我的心从来只属于你，被抓走不是我的过错。她请罗什曼那堆起柴堆，向火神祈祷后走进了火焰。火神从火中升起，把毫发无损的悉多交还给罗摩，宣布她清白无瑕。梵天和众神也现身，告诉罗摩他就是那罗延（毗湿奴）本身，十车王也乘着天车出现，祝福儿子。罗摩说：我早知道悉多是清白的，只是要让天下人都看到。他们乘着飞车布湿波迦飞回阿逾陀。在南迪村，婆罗多捧着那双鞋子出城迎接，把王国交还给哥哥。罗摩加冕为王，史诗说，在他统治的年代里，没有寡妇哀哭，没有疾病和盗贼，人们长寿而安乐。
beats.textEn: Sītā, bathed and adorned, was brought before Rāma. Before everyone he spoke harshly: he had fought to wipe out the insult to his line, not for her; she had lived long in another's house and might now go where she pleased. Weeping, but with calm dignity, Sītā answered that her heart had always been his and her capture was not her fault. She asked Lakṣmaṇa to build a pyre, prayed to the fire god and entered the flames. Agni rose from the fire, gave her back to Rāma unharmed and declared her pure. Brahmā and the gods appeared and told Rāma he was Nārāyaṇa himself, and Daśaratha came in a celestial car to bless his son. Rāma said he had known Sītā was pure but the world had to see it. In the flying chariot Puṣpaka they returned to Ayodhyā; at Nandigrāma Bharata met them with the sandals and restored the kingdom. Rāma was crowned, and in his reign, says the epic, no widow wept, there was no sickness or theft, and people lived long and happily.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·悉多的火之考验、回国与加冕。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 火的考验是今天印度内外讨论最多的情节之一；第七卷（后篇）里还有悉多被第二次放逐的故事，不在本篇范围。

deityStoryCards.name: Mohinī
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Enchanting female form of Viṣṇu who distributes the amṛta in the Bhāgavata Purāṇa witness; the Mahābhārata witness is linked only through its own description of a deluding female form.

beats.headingZh: 诸神与阿修罗暂时结盟
beats.headingEn: A truce between gods and asuras
beats.textZh: 《薄伽梵往世书》第八篇第5–6章中，诸神按毗湿奴的建议与阿修罗暂时结盟，合力拔起曼陀罗山并运往大海，毗湿奴亲自出手相助。
beats.textEn: In Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.5–8.6, on Viṣṇu's advice the gods make a temporary truce with the asuras; together they uproot Mount Mandara and carry it toward the ocean, with Viṣṇu himself stepping in to help.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 运山过程的细节只作概述，待逐颂校对。

beats.headingEn: Viṣṇu takes the form of a tortoise
beats.textZh: 以婆苏吉为绳开始搅拌后，曼陀罗山沉入水中；毗湿奴化作巨龟潜到山下，用背托起大山。
beats.textEn: Once the churning begins with Vāsuki as the rope, Mount Mandara sinks into the water; Viṣṇu assumes the form of a giant tortoise, dives beneath it and raises the mountain on his back.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 与精校本的龟王阿库帕拉构成显式见证差异，不做身份等同。

beats.textZh: 搅拌最先产生可怕的毒药，向各方蔓延；众生求助于湿婆，湿婆把毒药饮下。
beats.textEn: The churning first produces a terrible poison that spreads in every direction; beings turn to Śiva, who drinks it.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 后续图像传统与虔信解释未在本批次逐句建模。

beats.textZh: 其后又涌现多种宝物与存在，最后檀文陀利捧着盛满甘露的水罐出现。
beats.textEn: A series of treasures and beings then emerges, and finally Dhanvantari appears holding a vessel filled with the amṛta.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 此前出现之物的逐项清单尚未建模，不与精校本合并。

beats.textZh: 阿修罗抢走甘露后，毗湿奴化身为摩希尼迷惑他们，并把甘露分给诸神。罗睺假扮天神混入其中饮下甘露，被日月指认后，毗湿奴以神盘斩下其头。
beats.textEn: When the asuras snatch the amṛta, Viṣṇu becomes Mohinī, captivates them and distributes the amṛta to the gods. Rāhu, disguised as a god, slips in and drinks; when the Sun and Moon point him out, Viṣṇu severs his head with the discus.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 罗睺后来的天体身份不在本批次建模。

facts.textZh: 摩希尼是毗湿奴的一种形态。
facts.textEn: The Bhāgavata Purāṇa witness presents Mohinī as a form assumed by Viṣṇu.

deityStoryCards.name: Brahma
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《薄伽梵往世书》8.5 中，梵天带领受困的众神去见毗湿奴，随后才有乳海搅拌。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: In Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.5 Brahmā leads the distressed gods to Viṣṇu before the churning of the ocean.

beats.headingEn: A cry of grief becomes a verse
beats.textZh: 史诗从诗人自己讲起。苦行者蚁垤问仙人那罗陀：如今世上，有没有一个既有德行又有勇气、懂得正法、知恩图报、言而有信的人？那罗陀说：有，他就是甘蔗王族的罗摩，接着把罗摩的一生简要讲了一遍。不久，蚁垤到多摩萨河边沐浴，看见一对麻鹬正在树上相亲相爱，一个猎人一箭射死了雄鸟，雌鸟围着倒在血泊里的伴侣哀哀悲鸣。蚁垤心中涌起悲悯，脱口说出一句诅咒猎人的话——话一出口，他自己也吃了一惊：这句话音节整齐，可以和着琴弦吟唱。他把这种由悲伤（śoka）而生的诗体叫做“输洛迦”（śloka）。这时梵天亲自来到他面前，对他说：就用这种诗体，把那罗陀讲给你的罗摩的故事完整地唱出来吧；你所写的一切都会是真实的，只要山川还在，这部诗就会在世间流传。
beats.textEn: The epic begins with its own poet. The ascetic Vālmīki asked the sage Nārada whether there was any man on earth who was virtuous, brave, grateful and true to his word; Nārada told him of Rāma of the Ikṣvāku line and sketched his life. Soon after, bathing by the river Tamasā, Vālmīki saw a hunter shoot one of a pair of mating curlews, and heard the hen cry over her fallen mate. Pity broke from him as a curse on the hunter — in measured syllables that could be sung to the lute. He called this metre, born of grief (śoka), the śloka. Then Brahmā came to him and told him to sing the whole story of Rāma in that metre: all he wrote would be true, and it would endure while mountains and rivers lasted.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·开篇（那罗陀、梵天来访）。

beats.headingEn: The golden bowl from the sacrificial fire
beats.textZh: 阿逾陀城的国王十车王富有、公正、受人爱戴，却没有儿子。他举行了马祭，又请仙人鹿角主持求子的祭祀。就在这时，天上的众神来到梵天面前诉苦：罗刹王罗波那靠苦行从梵天那里得到恩典，天神、乾闼婆、夜叉和罗刹都杀不死他——他看不起人类，根本没有把人算进去。他仗着这个恩典欺压三界，众神毫无办法。正说着，毗湿奴骑着金翅鸟来了。众神恳求他化身为人，降生为十车王的四个儿子，去除掉罗波那。毗湿奴答应了。于是从十车王的祭火中走出一位光芒四射的神灵，捧着一只盛满天界乳粥的金碗。国王把乳粥分给三位王后：憍萨厘雅生下了罗摩，吉迦伊生下了婆罗多，须弥多罗生下了一对双胞胎——罗什曼那和设睹卢祇那。
beats.textEn: Daśaratha, king of Ayodhyā, was rich, just and beloved, but had no son. He performed the horse sacrifice and a rite for sons with the sage Ṛṣyaśṛṅga. Meanwhile the gods complained to Brahmā: Rāvaṇa, king of the rākṣasas, had won by austerities a boon that no god, gandharva, yakṣa or rākṣasa could slay him — scorning men, he had not even named them — and he was oppressing the three worlds. Vishnu arrived on Garuḍa, and the gods begged him to be born as a man, as Daśaratha's four sons, to destroy Rāvaṇa. He agreed. From the sacrificial fire rose a radiant being bearing a golden bowl of heavenly rice-milk; the king shared it among his queens, and Kausalyā bore Rāma, Kaikeyī Bharata, and Sumitrā the twins Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·求子祭祀与众神的请求。

beats.headingEn: Into the forest with the sage
beats.textZh: 王子们长大了，个个精通经典和武艺，其中罗摩最受众人喜爱，罗什曼那则像影子一样跟着他。一天，大仙人众友来到王宫，请国王把还不满十六岁的罗摩借给他，去保护他的祭祀不受罗刹的骚扰。十车王舍不得，宁愿自己率军前往，但在家庭祭司婆私吒的劝说下终于答应了。众友带着罗摩和罗什曼那上路，教给他们能驱除饥渴和疲劳的咒语。在一片荒凉的森林里，女罗刹多吒迦向他们扑来，罗摩起初不愿杀害女子，只想把她打退，众友却催促他说，为了保护众生，这样做并不违背正法。罗摩便射杀了她。众友非常满意，把许多神兵的咒语传授给他。到了众友的净修林，祭祀开始的第六天，罗刹摩哩遮和苏跋呼带人从天上撒下血肉，罗摩一箭把摩哩遮射飞到一百由旬外的海里，又射死了苏跋呼。
beats.textEn: The princes grew up learned in scripture and arms; Rāma was loved by all, and Lakṣmaṇa followed him like his shadow. One day the great sage Viśvāmitra came and asked for Rāma, not yet sixteen, to guard his sacrifice from rākṣasas. Daśaratha begged to go himself with an army, but the family priest Vasiṣṭha persuaded him. On the road Viśvāmitra taught the brothers spells against hunger and weariness. In a desolate forest the rākṣasī Tāṭakā rushed at them; Rāma was loth to kill a woman, but the sage urged that protecting the world was no breach of dharma, and Rāma shot her. Pleased, Viśvāmitra gave him the spells of the divine weapons. On the sixth day of the sacrifice Mārīca and Subāhu rained blood from the sky; Rāma's arrow hurled Mārīca a hundred leagues into the sea and killed Subāhu.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·众友的祭祀与多吒迦。

beats.textZh: 众友又带着两位王子前往弥提罗国。弥提罗的国王遮那竭告诉他们：有一次他为祭祀耕地，犁头翻开的犁沟里出现了一个女婴，他给她取名悉多，当作亲生女儿养大。他立下誓言，谁能拉开祖先传下来的湿婆大弓，就把悉多嫁给谁。许多国王都来试过，却连举都举不起来。那张弓装在一辆八个轮子的铁车上，由五千个壮汉拉了出来。罗摩打开弓匣，像玩耍一样轻轻把弓举起，给它装上弦，然后用力一拉——大弓从中间断成了两截，发出像雷霆、像山崩一样的巨响，在场的人全都吓得跌倒在地，只有众友、遮那竭和两位王子还站着。遮那竭欢喜地把悉多许给了罗摩。十车王赶来，四兄弟在同一天成婚。回国路上，持斧罗摩拦路挑战，罗摩又拉开了他带来的毗湿奴大弓，持斧罗摩才心服离去。
beats.textEn: Viśvāmitra then led the princes to Mithilā. King Janaka told them that once, ploughing ground for a sacrifice, he had found a baby girl in the furrow; he named her Sītā and raised her as his daughter, vowing to give her to whoever could string the bow of Śiva that his ancestors had kept. Many kings had failed even to lift it. Five thousand men drew it out on an eight-wheeled iron cart. Rāma opened the case, raised the bow as if in play, strung it and drew it — and it broke in the middle with a crash like thunder or a falling mountain. Everyone fell to the ground except Viśvāmitra, Janaka and the two princes. Janaka gave Sītā to Rāma, and the four brothers were married on one day. On the road home Paraśurāma challenged Rāma, who strung the bow of Vishnu as well, and the challenger withdrew.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第一卷·第六十七章“断弓”。

beats.textZh: 许多年过去了，十车王年事已高，决定立罗摩为太子，满城百姓欢天喜地，挂起彩旗，准备第二天的灌顶典礼。可是王后吉迦伊身边的驼背侍女曼他罗，在宫墙上看到这番景象，急忙跑去对吉迦伊说：罗摩一旦登基，你的儿子婆罗多就只能做奴仆，甚至会被赶出国去。起初吉迦伊还为罗摩高兴，送给曼他罗一件首饰；但曼他罗一再挑拨，终于说动了她，还提醒她：当年你在与商钵罗的战争中救过国王的命，国王许给你两个恩典，你一直没有用。吉迦伊扯下首饰，躺在“愤怒之室”的地上。十车王来了，看见心爱的王后这样，就以罗摩的名义发誓答应她的任何要求。吉迦伊说：第一，立婆罗多为太子；第二，让罗摩穿上树皮衣，到弹宅迦林中流放十四年。国王听了昏倒在地，哀求了整整一夜，吉迦伊却毫不动摇。
beats.textEn: Years later the aged Daśaratha resolved to make Rāma heir, and the city hung out banners for the consecration. But Kaikeyī's hunchbacked maid Mantharā, seeing the rejoicing from the palace roof, ran to tell her mistress that once Rāma reigned, her son Bharata would be a servant or an exile. At first Kaikeyī was glad for Rāma and gave Mantharā a jewel, but Mantharā worked on her until she yielded, reminding her of the two boons the king had promised when she saved his life in the war against Śambara. Kaikeyī tore off her ornaments and lay on the floor of the chamber of wrath. When the king, finding her so, swore by Rāma to grant her wish, she asked that Bharata be made heir and that Rāma go in bark garments to the Daṇḍaka forest for fourteen years. The king fell senseless and pleaded all night in vain.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·曼他罗与吉迦伊的恩典。

beats.textZh: 第二天一早，罗摩被召进宫，吉迦伊把国王的决定告诉了他。罗摩的脸色一点也没有变，他平静地说：为了父亲的诺言，我今天就去森林。母亲憍萨厘雅悲痛欲绝；罗什曼那怒不可遏，要拿起武器夺回王位，罗摩却劝住他说：遵守父亲的话就是正法。罗摩去向悉多告别，劝她留在宫中。悉多却说：妻子的命运就是丈夫的命运，有你在的森林，胜过没有你的宫殿；你要是不带我去，我就去死。罗什曼那也坚持要一起走。三人脱下华服，穿上树皮衣。全城的人哭着跟在车后，一直送到城外。他们在恒河边得到猎人首领古诃的帮助渡过了河，从此走进了森林。
beats.textEn: Next morning Rāma was summoned and Kaikeyī told him the king's decision. His face did not change; he said calmly that for his father's word he would go to the forest that very day. His mother Kausalyā was overwhelmed with grief; Lakṣmaṇa raged and would have taken the throne by arms, but Rāma restrained him, saying that obeying their father was dharma. When Rāma bade Sītā stay behind, she answered that a wife's lot is her husband's lot, that the forest with him was better than a palace without him, and that if he left her she would die. Lakṣmaṇa too insisted on coming. The three put off their fine clothes and put on bark garments, the whole city followed their chariot weeping, and on the Ganges the hunter chief Guha ferried them across into the forest.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·罗摩出城流放。

beats.textZh: 车夫苏曼多罗独自赶着空车回来，十车王听说儿子真的走进了森林，悲痛得一病不起。夜里，他对憍萨厘雅讲起了年轻时犯下的一桩罪过：那时他自恃能“听声射箭”，在黑夜的河边听见像大象饮水的声音，一箭射去，射中的却是一个正在用水罐打水的年轻苦行者。少年临死前请他把水带给自己又老又瞎的父母。两位老人得知儿子的死讯，父亲诅咒国王：你将来也会像我一样，为了思念儿子而死。十车王说：这个诅咒如今应验了。他一遍遍呼唤着罗摩的名字，在午夜时分死去了。
beats.textEn: When the charioteer Sumantra came back alone, Daśaratha, hearing that his son had truly entered the forest, fell ill with grief. That night he told Kausalyā of a sin of his youth: proud of shooting at a sound, he had heard by a dark river what seemed an elephant drinking and loosed an arrow — but struck a young ascetic filling a water jar. The dying boy asked him to carry water to his old, blind parents. On hearing of their son's death the father cursed the king to die, like him, grieving for a son. That curse, Daśaratha said, was now fulfilled; and calling Rāma's name he died at midnight.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·十车王之死。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 那位少年苦行者在后世传统中常被叫做“室罗波那”（Śravaṇa），蚁垤本里没有给出这个名字。

beats.headingEn: A pair of sandals on the throne
beats.textZh: 婆罗多从舅父家回来，才知道父亲已死、兄长被流放，而这一切都是母亲为他谋来的。他痛斥吉迦伊，拒绝接受王位，为父亲办完葬礼后，带着母亲们和军队进入森林，去质多罗俱吒山找罗摩。兄弟相见，罗摩得知父亲去世，悲痛不已。婆罗多跪在他面前恳求他回去为王，众人也一齐劝说。罗摩却说：父亲的诺言必须遵守，十四年期满之前，我不会回去。婆罗多无可奈何，请罗摩把脚上那双饰金的鞋子给他。他把鞋子顶在头上带回去，供在王座上，自己穿上树皮衣，住在城外的南迪村，以“鞋子的仆人”的身份代为治理国家，并且发誓：十四年期满那天罗摩若不回来，他就投火而死。
beats.textEn: Bharata returned from his uncle's house to learn that his father was dead and his brother exiled, all for his sake. He rebuked Kaikeyī, refused the throne, performed his father's rites and went with the queens and the army to Mount Citrakūṭa to find Rāma. When the brothers met, Rāma mourned their father. Bharata knelt and begged him to return and reign, and all joined in; but Rāma answered that his father's word must be kept, and he would not return before the fourteen years were over. Then Bharata asked for Rāma's gold-adorned sandals. Carrying them on his head, he set them on the throne, put on bark garments, and ruled from the village of Nandigrāma as the sandals' servant, vowing to enter the fire if Rāma did not return on the appointed day.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第二卷·婆罗多寻兄与鞋子。

beats.textZh: 罗摩一行在弹宅迦林中住了许多年，保护林中的苦行者，仙人投山把毗湿奴的神弓和永不空竭的箭囊送给了他。后来他们在戈达瓦里河边的五树林住下，罗什曼那搭了一座草屋。一天，罗波那的妹妹、女罗刹首哩薄那迦看见了罗摩，爱上了他，要他做丈夫。罗摩开玩笑地说自己已有妻子，让她去找罗什曼那；罗什曼那也开玩笑地把她推回给罗摩。她恼羞成怒，以为是悉多挡了路，张牙舞爪地向悉多扑去。罗摩命令罗什曼那惩罚她，罗什曼那拔剑割下了她的鼻子和耳朵。首哩薄那迦哭着逃到哥哥伽罗那里。伽罗先派十四个罗刹去，被罗摩全部射死；接着伽罗和突舍那率领一万四千罗刹大军杀来，罗摩让罗什曼那带着悉多躲进山洞，自己一个人迎战，把整支大军消灭了。
beats.textEn: For years they lived in the Daṇḍaka forest protecting its hermits, and the sage Agastya gave Rāma the bow of Vishnu and inexhaustible quivers. Then they settled at Pañcavaṭī on the Godāvarī, where Lakṣmaṇa built a hut. There Rāvaṇa's sister, the rākṣasī Śūrpaṇakhā, saw Rāma and desired him. Rāma jestingly said he had a wife and sent her to Lakṣmaṇa, who in jest sent her back. Enraged and blaming Sītā, she rushed at her; at Rāma's command Lakṣmaṇa cut off her nose and ears. She fled to her brother Khara. Khara sent fourteen rākṣasas, whom Rāma shot down; then Khara and Dūṣaṇa came with fourteen thousand, and Rāma, sending Lakṣmaṇa with Sītā to a cave, destroyed the whole host alone.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·首哩薄那迦与伽罗之军。

beats.textZh: 首哩薄那迦逃到楞伽，当众责骂罗波那只顾享乐，连自己的国土都保不住，又极力夸赞悉多的美貌。罗波那动了心，乘着飞车去找当年被罗摩一箭射进海里的摩哩遮。摩哩遮吓得发抖，劝他千万别去招惹罗摩；罗波那却威胁说，不听命令就杀了他。摩哩遮叹道：反正都是死，死在罗摩手里还好些。他变成一只金色的鹿，身上点缀着银色的斑点，角尖像宝石，在草屋前来回走动。悉多一见就喜欢上了，求罗摩去捉。罗什曼那提醒说这一定是摩哩遮的幻术，罗摩还是嘱咐弟弟守护悉多，自己追了出去。金鹿时隐时现，把他引得越来越远，罗摩终于一箭射中。摩哩遮现出原形，临死前学着罗摩的声音大喊：“啊，悉多！啊，罗什曼那！”悉多听了惊慌失措，催罗什曼那去救。罗什曼那说没有人能伤害罗摩，悉多竟说出刺耳的话，指责他心怀不轨。罗什曼那受了委屈，只好离开草屋。
beats.textEn: Śūrpaṇakhā fled to Laṅkā, rebuked Rāvaṇa for his idleness and praised Sītā's beauty. Rāvaṇa flew in his chariot to Mārīca, whom Rāma's arrow had once hurled into the sea. Mārīca trembled and begged him not to provoke Rāma, but Rāvaṇa threatened to kill him, and he sighed that it was better to die by Rāma's hand. He became a golden deer dappled with silver, its horns tipped with gems, and grazed before the hut. Sītā longed for it. Lakṣmaṇa warned it was Mārīca's magic, but Rāma left him to guard Sītā and gave chase. The deer led him far away until his arrow struck it; dying, Mārīca cried out in Rāma's voice, ‘Ah Sītā! Ah Lakṣmaṇa!’ Sītā, frantic, urged Lakṣmaṇa to go; when he said none could harm Rāma, she accused him with cruel words of wanting her for himself, and, wounded, he went.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·摩哩遮与金鹿。

beats.headingEn: The ten-headed king and the vulture
beats.textZh: 罗什曼那刚走，罗波那就扮成一个云游的婆罗门苦行者来到草屋前。悉多按待客之礼请他进来，给他水和食物，并告诉他自己是谁。罗波那这才夸耀自己是楞伽之王，要她做他的王后。悉多轻蔑地回答：你就像一只想得到母狮的豺狗。罗波那现出了十个头的真身，一把抓住她，拖上飞车，向南飞去。悉多一路向树木、河流和山神呼喊，求它们告诉罗摩。年老的鹫王阇吒优私是十车王的朋友，他拦住罗波那，劝他放了悉多，随即与他搏斗，打碎了他的车子，杀死了驾车的驴子和车夫；可他终究年老力衰，被罗波那砍断了翅膀和双脚，跌落在地。飞过一座山时，悉多看见山顶上坐着五只猴子，就把自己的披巾和首饰包在一起扔了下去。罗波那把她带回楞伽，给她十二个月的期限，把她关在无忧树林里，由许多女罗刹看守。
beats.textEn: As soon as Lakṣmaṇa had gone, Rāvaṇa came to the hut disguised as a wandering brahmin ascetic. Sītā received him as a guest with water and food and told him who she was. Then he boasted that he was king of Laṅkā and asked her to be his queen; she answered scornfully that he was a jackal longing for a lioness. Rāvaṇa took his true ten-headed form, seized her and carried her off southward in his chariot while she called on the trees, rivers and mountain spirits to tell Rāma. The old vulture-king Jaṭāyu, friend of Daśaratha, barred his way, smashed his chariot and killed its asses and driver, but, old and spent, had his wings and feet cut off by Rāvaṇa. Passing a hill where five monkeys sat, Sītā dropped her scarf and ornaments. In Laṅkā Rāvaṇa gave her twelve months and set her in the aśoka grove under guard of rākṣasīs.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·悉多被劫与阇吒优私。

beats.textZh: 罗摩在回来的路上遇见了罗什曼那，心中顿生不祥之感。草屋果然空无一人。罗摩悲痛欲狂，向树木、河流和野兽一一询问悉多的下落，看到散落的花朵、折断的车子和血迹，以为她被罗刹吃掉了，怒气冲冲地要毁灭世界，罗什曼那苦苦劝他冷静。他们找到奄奄一息的阇吒优私，鹫王告诉他们是罗波那劫走了悉多、往南方去了，说完就断了气。罗摩像为父亲举行葬礼一样，亲手为他火化。兄弟俩继续向南，被一个没有头、胸前长着大嘴的怪物迦槃陀抓住，他们砍断了他的两只长臂。迦槃陀在火葬的火焰中恢复了天神的形貌，告诉他们：去般波湖边的哩舍牟迦山找猴王须羯哩婆，他会帮你们找到悉多。在般波湖边，年老的女苦行者舍波哩欢喜地迎接了罗摩，随后升入天界。
beats.textEn: On the way back Rāma met Lakṣmaṇa and felt dread; the hut was empty. Half mad with grief, Rāma asked the trees, rivers and beasts where Sītā was; seeing scattered flowers, a broken chariot and blood, he thought rākṣasas had eaten her and threatened to destroy the worlds until Lakṣmaṇa calmed him. They found the dying Jaṭāyu, who told them Rāvaṇa had taken Sītā south, and died. Rāma cremated him with the rites due to a father. Going on, they were seized by the headless monster Kabandha, whose mouth was in his chest, and cut off his long arms; restored to divine form in his funeral fire, he told them to seek the monkey-king Sugrīva on Mount Ṛśyamūka by Lake Pampā. There the aged ascetic woman Śabarī welcomed Rāma joyfully and then rose to heaven.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第三卷·罗摩的哀伤、阇吒优私、迦槃陀与舍波哩。

beats.textZh: 哈奴曼扮成苦行者来迎接他们，把他们带到须羯哩婆面前。罗摩和须羯哩婆围着火结为盟友。须羯哩婆拿出那包从天上落下的首饰，罗摩认出是悉多的，痛哭失声；罗什曼那说，耳环和手镯他认不出，只认得脚镯，因为他每天向悉多行礼时只看她的脚。须羯哩婆讲了自己的遭遇：哥哥波林夺走了他的妻子和王国，把他赶到这座山上。罗摩一箭射穿七棵娑罗树，让他相信自己的力量。须羯哩婆向波林挑战，罗摩藏在树后；第一次两兄弟长得太像，罗摩分不清；第二次须羯哩婆戴上花环，罗摩一箭射中了波林。垂死的波林责问罗摩为什么从暗处射他，罗摩回答：你夺了弟弟的妻子，作为国王的代表，我有责任惩罚你。须羯哩婆登上王位，雨季过后，他派出四路猴军寻找悉多，罗摩把刻着自己名字的戒指交给了往南去的哈奴曼。
beats.textEn: Hanumān, disguised as an ascetic, met them and brought them to Sugrīva, and Rāma and Sugrīva swore friendship around a fire. Sugrīva showed the bundle of ornaments that had fallen from the sky; Rāma knew them as Sītā's and wept, and Lakṣmaṇa said he knew only her anklets, for he had looked only at her feet when he bowed to her. Sugrīva told how his brother Vālin had taken his wife and kingdom. Rāma shot an arrow through seven sāl trees to prove his strength. When the brothers fought, Rāma stood hidden behind a tree; the first time he could not tell them apart, the second time Sugrīva wore a garland, and Rāma's arrow struck Vālin. The dying Vālin reproached him for shooting from hiding; Rāma answered that Vālin had taken his brother's wife and that he punished him on the king's behalf. Sugrīva was crowned, and after the rains sent search parties to the four quarters; Rāma gave his signet ring to Hanumān, who went south.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第四卷·与须羯哩婆结盟与波林之死。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 罗摩从暗处射杀波林是否合乎正法，在印度传统内部本身就有长久的争论；本站只讲蚁垤本里双方的说法。

beats.textZh: 南路的猴军由安伽陀和哈奴曼率领，找了一个多月仍无消息，来到南方大海边时都绝望了，打算绝食而死。这时，一只没有翅膀的老鹫出现了，他是阇吒优私的哥哥商波底。他告诉猴子们：悉多被关在大海对面一百由旬外的楞伽城。说完，他烧焦的翅膀竟重新长了出来。可是谁能跳过这么宽的海？老熊王阇婆梵提醒哈奴曼：你是风神的儿子，小时候曾一跃扑向太阳，你的力量连你自己都忘了。哈奴曼站上摩亨陀罗山，身体越变越大，用力一蹬，山都被踩得渗出水来，他像一支箭一样飞上了天。海中的弥那迦山从水里升起，请他歇脚，他只轻轻碰了一下就继续飞；蛇母须罗娑奉众神之命张开大嘴考验他，他先把身体变得巨大，又突然缩得像拇指一样小，从她嘴里钻进去又钻出来；女妖辛悉迦抓住他的影子把他往下拖，他钻进她的身体把她撕开。最后，他落在楞伽城外的三峰山上。
beats.textEn: The southern party under Aṅgada and Hanumān searched for over a month in vain and, reaching the southern sea, despaired and resolved to starve. Then a wingless old vulture appeared — Sampāti, Jaṭāyu's elder brother — who told them Sītā was held in Laṅkā, a hundred leagues across the sea; as he spoke his scorched wings grew again. But who could leap so far? The old bear-king Jāmbavān reminded Hanumān that he was the wind god's son, who as a child had sprung at the sun, and whose strength he had forgotten. Hanumān swelled to a great size on Mount Mahendra, pressed it until water oozed from its rocks, and flew like an arrow. The mountain Maināka rose from the sea to offer him rest; Surasā, mother of serpents, opened her jaws to test him, and he grew huge, then shrank to a thumb's size and darted in and out; Siṃhikā seized his shadow, and he tore her from within. At last he landed on Mount Trikūṭa outside Laṅkā.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第四至五卷·商波底与哈奴曼跨海。

beats.textZh: 哈奴曼把身体缩得像猫一样小，趁着夜色潜入楞伽。他看遍了金碧辉煌的宫殿和罗波那的后宫，一度把熟睡的王后曼度陀哩误认为悉多，随即醒悟：悉多绝不会在这里安睡。最后，他在无忧树林里找到了她：她消瘦苍白，穿着沾满尘土的衣服，被一群面目狰狞的女罗刹围着。罗波那来了，又是威胁又是引诱，说只剩两个月期限，到时她若不从，就把她剁了做早饭。悉多在两人之间放下一根草茎，隔着草茎回答他：你配不上我，罗摩的箭会来惩罚你。罗波那走后，哈奴曼躲在树上，轻声唱起罗摩的故事。悉多先是惊恐，以为又是罗波那的幻术，等哈奴曼把罗摩的戒指递给她，她才喜极而泣。哈奴曼要背她回去，悉多拒绝了：她不愿主动碰触罗摩以外的男子，而且应当由罗摩亲自来救她、雪洗耻辱。她把自己的髻珠交给哈奴曼作信物。
beats.textEn: Shrinking to the size of a cat, Hanumān slipped into Laṅkā by night. He searched the golden palaces and Rāvaṇa's women's quarters, once mistaking the sleeping queen Mandodarī for Sītā before realising Sītā would never sleep there. At last he found her in the aśoka grove, thin and pale, in soiled clothes, surrounded by fearsome rākṣasīs. Rāvaṇa came, threatening and coaxing: in two months, if she would not yield, he would have her cut up for his breakfast. Sītā laid a blade of grass between them and answered across it that he was unworthy of her and Rāma's arrows would punish him. When he left, Hanumān, hidden in a tree, softly sang Rāma's story. Sītā feared another illusion until he gave her Rāma's ring, and then wept for joy. He offered to carry her back; she refused, unwilling to touch any man but Rāma and wishing Rāma himself to rescue her and wipe out the insult, and gave him her crest-jewel as a token.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第五卷·无忧树林中的悉多。

beats.textZh: 哈奴曼想试一试罗刹的力量，就把无忧树林毁了个干净，打死了前来捉他的大批卫兵，连罗波那的儿子阿刹也死在他手里。罗波那的长子因陀罗耆用梵天的神兵把他捆住，哈奴曼明知自己挣得开，却甘愿被绑去见罗波那。他当面劝罗波那把悉多还给罗摩，罗波那大怒，下令处死他；罗波那的弟弟维毗沙那提醒说，使者不可杀。于是罗波那下令在他的尾巴上缠上浸油的布点火，牵着他游街示众。悉多听说后，向火神祈祷让火焰变得清凉，哈奴曼果然感到尾巴上的火一点也不烫。他挣脱绳索，跳上屋顶，从一座宫殿跳到另一座宫殿，把楞伽城烧成一片火海。烧完之后他才惊恐地想起悉多，赶紧回去，看见她安然无恙，这才放心。他跃回大海对岸，把髻珠交给罗摩，罗摩把它贴在胸前，泪流满面。
beats.textEn: To test the rākṣasas' strength Hanumān wrecked the aśoka grove and slew the guards sent against him, among them Rāvaṇa's son Akṣa. Rāvaṇa's eldest son Indrajit bound him with the weapon of Brahmā, and Hanumān, though he could break free, let himself be led before Rāvaṇa, whom he urged to return Sītā. Rāvaṇa ordered his death, but his brother Vibhīṣaṇa reminded him that envoys may not be slain; so Rāvaṇa had oiled rags wrapped round Hanumān's tail and set alight, and paraded him through the streets. Sītā prayed to the fire god to be cool to him, and Hanumān felt no heat. Breaking his bonds, he leapt from palace roof to palace roof until Laṅkā was a sea of flame — then, in sudden fear for Sītā, went back and found her unharmed. He leapt back across the sea and gave Rāma the crest-jewel, which Rāma pressed to his breast weeping.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第五卷·火烧楞伽。

beats.textZh: 猴军浩浩荡荡向南进发，来到大海边。楞伽城里，维毗沙那劝哥哥把悉多还回去，免得国破家亡，罗波那却骂他是叛徒。维毗沙那带着四个随从飞过大海来投奔罗摩。须羯哩婆怀疑他是奸细，罗摩说：凡是来向我求庇护的，我都要保护，哪怕是罗波那本人。他接纳了维毗沙那，当场为他举行了楞伽王的灌顶。罗摩向大海祈求让路，在海边躺了三天三夜，大海毫无回应。罗摩发怒，搭箭要把大海射干，海神这才从水中升起，告诉他：猴军中的那罗是工巧天的儿子，让他来造桥，我会托住桥身。猴子们拔来大树、搬来山石，扔进海里，五天之内，一座一百由旬长的石桥横跨了大海。猴军踏着石桥渡海，把楞伽城团团围住。
beats.textEn: The army marched south to the sea. In Laṅkā Vibhīṣaṇa urged his brother to return Sītā before ruin came, and Rāvaṇa called him a traitor; so Vibhīṣaṇa flew across the sea with four companions to Rāma. Sugrīva suspected a spy, but Rāma said he would protect anyone who sought his refuge, even Rāvaṇa himself, and consecrated Vibhīṣaṇa then and there as king of Laṅkā. Rāma lay three days by the shore begging the ocean to give way; when it did not answer, he angrily drew an arrow to dry it up, and the Ocean rose from the waters and told him that Nala, son of the divine architect Viśvakarman, could build a bridge that the sea would bear. The monkeys hurled trees and rocks into the sea, and in five days a bridge a hundred leagues long spanned it. The army crossed and laid siege to Laṅkā.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·维毗沙那投奔与那罗造桥。

beats.textZh: 大战开始了。罗波那的儿子因陀罗耆能隐身作战，他躲在云中放出蛇箭，把罗摩和罗什曼那捆得动弹不得，猴军以为两位王子已死。危急之时，金翅鸟从天而降，群蛇见了天敌纷纷逃散，兄弟俩才得以解脱。罗波那的弟弟鸠槃羯叻拿身躯如山，一睡就是几个月，罗刹们敲锣打鼓、赶着大象从他身上踩过才把他叫醒。他冲进战场大口吞吃猴子，连须羯哩婆也被他夹走。罗摩用箭射断了他的双臂和双腿，最后射下了他的头。因陀罗耆又用梵天的神兵射倒了几乎整支猴军，哈奴曼奉命飞到喜马拉雅山采药，认不出是哪几种草药，就把整座山峰连根拔起托了回来，药草的香气让倒下的猴子全都复活了。最后，罗什曼那与因陀罗耆展开激战，射下了他的头。
beats.textEn: The war began. Rāvaṇa's son Indrajit, who could fight unseen, shot serpent-arrows from the clouds that bound Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa so fast the monkeys thought them dead — until Garuḍa swooped down and the serpents fled from their enemy. Rāvaṇa's giant brother Kumbhakarṇa, who slept for months at a time, was woken with drums and with elephants driven over his body; he strode into battle devouring monkeys and carried off Sugrīva, until Rāma's arrows severed his arms and legs and at last his head. Indrajit then felled almost the whole army with the weapon of Brahmā; Hanumān flew to the Himalaya for healing herbs and, unable to tell which they were, tore up the whole peak and brought it back, and the herbs' fragrance revived the fallen. At last Lakṣmaṇa fought Indrajit and shot off his head.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·因陀罗耆、鸠槃羯叻拿与药山。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 哈奴曼取药山的情节在通行本里出现过两次（一次救全军，一次救罗什曼那），各本次序不尽相同；本节只概述其中一次。

beats.textZh: 儿子和兄弟都死了，罗波那终于亲自出战。他用一支神矛击中罗什曼那，哈奴曼再一次取来草药救活了他。因陀罗派自己的车夫摩多梨驾着天车来帮助罗摩。两人的决战持续了很久，天地为之震动。罗摩一箭射下罗波那的一个头，立刻又长出一个新的头来；他一连射下了一百个头，罗波那仍然不死。这时摩多梨提醒他：用梵天的神兵吧。罗摩搭上仙人投山传给他的那支梵天之箭，箭上燃着火焰，带着风的速度，一箭射穿了罗波那的心脏。十首魔王从车上倒下，众神从天上撒下花雨。维毗沙那为哥哥痛哭，犹豫要不要为这个恶人举行葬礼，罗摩对他说：仇恨到死亡为止，他现在也是我的兄弟，为他举行葬礼吧。随后，维毗沙那在楞伽登上了王位。
beats.textEn: With his sons and brother dead, Rāvaṇa came out to fight himself. He struck down Lakṣmaṇa with a dart, and Hanumān again brought herbs to revive him. Indra sent his charioteer Mātali with his celestial chariot to carry Rāma. Their duel lasted long and shook heaven and earth. Each time Rāma's arrow struck off one of Rāvaṇa's heads, another grew in its place, until a hundred had fallen and he still lived. Then Mātali reminded Rāma of the weapon of Brahmā. Rāma loosed the arrow Agastya had given him, flaming and swift as the wind, and it pierced Rāvaṇa's heart; the ten-headed king fell from his chariot, and the gods rained flowers. When Vibhīṣaṇa wept and hesitated to give his wicked brother funeral rites, Rāma told him that enmity ends with death: Rāvaṇa was his brother too, and the rites should be done. Vibhīṣaṇa was then crowned king of Laṅkā.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·罗波那之死。

beats.headingEn: The ordeal of fire and the return home
beats.textZh: 悉多沐浴更衣后被带到罗摩面前。当着众人的面，罗摩却说出冷酷的话：我打这一仗，是为了洗雪家族的耻辱，不是为了你；你在别人家里住了这么久，现在你想去哪里就去哪里吧。悉多泪流满面，却镇定而有尊严地回答：我的心从来只属于你，被抓走不是我的过错。她请罗什曼那堆起柴堆，向火神祈祷后走进了火焰。火神从火中升起，把毫发无损的悉多交还给罗摩，宣布她清白无瑕。梵天和众神也现身，告诉罗摩他就是那罗延（毗湿奴）本身，十车王也乘着天车出现，祝福儿子。罗摩说：我早知道悉多是清白的，只是要让天下人都看到。他们乘着飞车布湿波迦飞回阿逾陀。在南迪村，婆罗多捧着那双鞋子出城迎接，把王国交还给哥哥。罗摩加冕为王，史诗说，在他统治的年代里，没有寡妇哀哭，没有疾病和盗贼，人们长寿而安乐。
beats.textEn: Sītā, bathed and adorned, was brought before Rāma. Before everyone he spoke harshly: he had fought to wipe out the insult to his line, not for her; she had lived long in another's house and might now go where she pleased. Weeping, but with calm dignity, Sītā answered that her heart had always been his and her capture was not her fault. She asked Lakṣmaṇa to build a pyre, prayed to the fire god and entered the flames. Agni rose from the fire, gave her back to Rāma unharmed and declared her pure. Brahmā and the gods appeared and told Rāma he was Nārāyaṇa himself, and Daśaratha came in a celestial car to bless his son. Rāma said he had known Sītā was pure but the world had to see it. In the flying chariot Puṣpaka they returned to Ayodhyā; at Nandigrāma Bharata met them with the sandals and restored the kingdom. Rāma was crowned, and in his reign, says the epic, no widow wept, there was no sickness or theft, and people lived long and happily.
beats.sourceTitle: The Rámáyan of Válmíki, translated into English verse (R. T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874)
beats.evidenceNote: 格里菲斯译本第六卷·悉多的火之考验、回国与加冕。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 火的考验是今天印度内外讨论最多的情节之一；第七卷（后篇）里还有悉多被第二次放逐的故事，不在本篇范围。

facts.textZh: 梵天出现在“乳海搅拌（文本叙事）”之中。
facts.textEn: In Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.5 the distressed gods go to Brahmā, who leads them to the Lord Ajita (Viṣṇu) and praises him; the churning follows in 8.6–8.9.

deityStoryCards.name: Dhanvantari
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Divine figure who emerges from the churned ocean carrying the amṛta in both registered textual witnesses.

beats.textZh: 精校本《初篇》1.15 中，诸神聚集在须弥山上商议如何得到甘露；那罗延（毗湿奴）建议诸神与阿修罗一起搅动大海。
beats.textEn: In the critical edition at Ādiparvan 1.15, the gods gather on Mount Meru to deliberate how to obtain the amṛta; Nārāyaṇa (Viṣṇu) advises that gods and asuras churn the ocean together.
beats.uncertaintyNote: “那罗延”在此按既有毗湿奴实体连接，不扩展神学解释。

beats.headingZh: 曼陀罗山、婆苏吉与龟王
beats.headingEn: Mandara, Vāsuki and the tortoise king
beats.textZh: 巨蛇阿难陀拔起曼陀罗山作为搅棒，龙王婆苏吉充当搅绳；山的底部由龟王阿库帕拉承托。这一见证没有说龟王是毗湿奴的化身。
beats.textEn: The serpent Ananta uproots Mount Mandara to serve as the churning rod and the nāga Vāsuki serves as the rope; the tortoise king Akūpāra bears the base of the mountain. This witness does not say that the tortoise king is a form of Viṣṇu.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 阿难陀拔山一项为中等置信度，待逐颂校对；阿难陀尚未单独建实体。

beats.headingZh: 檀文陀利捧着甘露出现
beats.textZh: 搅拌中先后涌现多种存在与宝物，最后檀文陀利捧着盛满甘露的水罐出现。
beats.textEn: As the churning goes on, a series of beings and treasures emerges, and finally Dhanvantari appears holding a vessel filled with the amṛta.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 此前出现之物的逐项清单尚未建模，不从其他版本补齐。

beats.headingEn: The deluding female form and Rāhu
beats.textZh: 阿修罗夺走甘露后，那罗延化作迷惑人的女子形象，把甘露取回交给诸神。罗睺假扮天神偷饮甘露，被日月揭发后，那罗延以神盘斩下其头；随后天神与阿修罗爆发大战。
beats.textEn: After the Dānavas seize the amṛta, Nārāyaṇa takes on a deluding female form and recovers it for the gods. Rāhu, disguised as a god, drinks some of it; when the Sun and Moon expose him, Nārāyaṇa cuts off his head with the discus, and a great battle between gods and Dānavas follows.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 专名实体“摩希尼”只连接《薄伽梵往世书》见证；此处保留“迷惑的女身”描述。

beats.headingEn: Scope of the constituted critical text
beats.textZh: 在精校本 1.15–1.17 的正文里，没有湿婆吞下毒药的情节。这只说明本定位“未陈述”，不代表所有写本或地方传统都没有；校勘记录与附录尚待逐项核对。
beats.textEn: The constituted critical text at 1.15–1.17 does not include Śiva swallowing the poison. This records only that the locator does not state it; it does not mean that every manuscript or regional tradition lacks it, and the apparatus and appendices still have to be checked.
beats.evidenceNote: 精校本初篇 1.15–1.17 正文范围与 BORI 精校本说明。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 写本校勘与附录已作为独立研究队列排队。
