deityStoryCards.name: Athena
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 赫西俄德与颂歌传统中从宙斯而生、具武装与城邦守护层面的女神；埃癸斯证据另接《伊利亚特》。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Armed daughter of Zeus and city guardian in registered witnesses.

beats.textZh: 诗人赫西俄德说，他从赫利孔山的缪斯们开始歌唱。缪斯是宙斯与记忆女神谟涅摩叙涅的九个女儿，她们在赫利孔山上的泉边跳舞，在夜里裹着雾气走下山来，赞美众神。有一天，赫西俄德正在神圣的赫利孔山下放羊，缪斯们对他说：“荒野里的牧人啊，可耻的家伙，只知道填饱肚子！我们会说许多像真话的假话，也懂得在愿意的时候说出真话。”说完，她们折下一根茂盛的月桂枝，作为权杖交给他，又把神圣的歌声吹进他的胸中，叫他歌唱将来和过去的事，赞美永生的神族，并且总要在开头和结尾歌唱她们。于是赫西俄德请求缪斯：请从头告诉我，众神、大地、河流、无边的大海、闪耀的星辰和广阔的天空，最初是怎样出现的。
beats.textEn: Hesiod begins with the Muses of Helicon, the nine daughters of Zeus and Memory, who dance by the springs of the mountain and walk down at night veiled in mist, praising the gods. Once, as he shepherded lambs beneath Helicon, they mocked him — 'shepherds of the wilderness, mere bellies' — and said they could tell many lies that seem true, and truth when they wish. They gave him a staff of laurel, breathed a divine voice into him to sing of things to come and things past, and bade him sing of the gods. So he asks them to tell from the beginning how gods, earth, rivers, sea, stars and heaven first came to be.

beats.textZh: 最先出现的是卡俄斯——一片张开的空隙。接着出现的是胸怀宽广的大地盖亚，她是住在白雪覆盖的奥林波斯山顶的众神永远稳固的座基；还有大地深处幽暗的塔耳塔罗斯；以及众神之中最俊美的爱若斯，他让所有的神和人四肢酥软，制服他们胸中的理智。从卡俄斯又生出黑暗厄瑞玻斯和黑夜纽克斯；黑夜与厄瑞玻斯相爱，生下了明亮的以太和白昼。大地首先生出与自己一样大的、布满星辰的天空乌拉诺斯，让他把自己四面覆盖，并做众神永久的居所；她又生出高大的群山，那是山林仙女们喜爱的地方；她还不经爱情，生出了波涛汹涌、荒凉无际的大海蓬托斯。
beats.textEn: Verily at the first Chaos came to be — a gaping void — and then broad-breasted Earth, the ever-sure foundation of the gods of Olympus; dim Tartarus in the depth of the earth; and Eros, fairest of the gods, who loosens the limbs and overcomes the mind. From Chaos came Erebus and black Night, and from Night, joined with Erebus, came bright Aether and Day. Earth first bore starry Heaven, Ouranos, equal to herself, to cover her on every side; she bore the long hills, haunts of the nymphs, and, without love, the fruitless deep, Pontus.

beats.textZh: 后来大地与天空相爱，生下了深深漩涡的大洋神俄刻阿诺斯，还有科俄斯、克利俄斯、许珀里翁、伊阿佩托斯，以及忒亚、瑞亚、忒弥斯、谟涅摩叙涅、头戴金冠的福柏和可爱的忒堤斯——这些就是十二位提坦。在他们之后，最小的孩子出世了，他就是心思弯曲的克洛诺斯，他是所有孩子中最可怕的一个，并且憎恨自己精力旺盛的父亲。大地还生下了三个狂傲的独眼巨人：布戎忒斯、斯忒罗珀斯和阿耳革斯，他们后来为宙斯打造了雷霆和闪电，每人额头正中只有一只圆眼睛。此外，大地与天空又生下三个强大得不可名状的儿子：科托斯、布里阿瑞俄斯和古革斯。他们每人肩上长着一百只手臂，五十个头，力大无穷。
beats.textEn: Then Earth lay with Heaven and bore deep-swirling Oceanus, Coeus and Crius, Hyperion and Iapetus, Theia and Rhea, Themis and Mnemosyne, gold-crowned Phoebe and lovely Tethys — the Titans — and after them the youngest, wily Cronus, most terrible of her children, who hated his lusty father. She bore the overbearing Cyclopes, Brontes, Steropes and Arges, each with one round eye in his forehead, who would later give Zeus thunder and lightning; and three more sons, great and strong beyond telling — Cottus, Briareos and Gyes — each with a hundred arms and fifty heads.

beats.textZh: 天空乌拉诺斯憎恨自己的孩子们，每当一个孩子出生，他就把他们藏进大地的深处，不让他们见到光明，并以这种恶行为乐。广大的大地在里面痛苦地呻吟。她想出一条狡猾的计谋：她造出灰色的坚硬金属，用它打成一把巨大的镰刀，然后对孩子们说：我的孩子们，你们的父亲作恶多端，谁愿意听我的话，为我们报这可耻的冤仇？孩子们都吓得说不出话来，只有克洛诺斯鼓起勇气回答：母亲，我愿意做这件事。大地非常高兴，把他藏在埋伏之处，把锯齿状的镰刀交到他手里。天空乌拉诺斯带着黑夜降临，渴望着爱情，展开身体覆盖大地；这时克洛诺斯从埋伏中伸出左手，右手挥起长长的镰刀，割下了父亲的生殖器，把它向身后远远地抛去。溅落的血滴被大地接住，随着岁月流转，大地生出了强大的复仇女神厄里倪厄斯、身披闪亮铠甲的巨人族，以及梣木仙女。
beats.textEn: Heaven hated his children and hid each of them, as soon as it was born, in the depths of Earth, rejoicing in his wickedness while vast Earth groaned within. She made grey adamant, shaped a great sickle, and asked her sons who would punish their father's outrage. Fear seized them all except great Cronus, who answered that he would. Earth hid him in ambush and gave him the jagged sickle. When Heaven came at nightfall, longing for love, and spread himself over Earth, Cronus stretched out his left hand from his hiding place and with the sickle in his right cut off his father's members and threw them behind him. From the drops of blood Earth later bore the Erinyes, the armoured Giants and the ash-tree nymphs.

beats.textZh: 克洛诺斯割下的部分从陆地被抛进波涛汹涌的大海，随着海浪漂流了很久，四周泛起白色的泡沫，泡沫中生长出一位少女。她先漂向神圣的库忒拉岛，又从那里来到四面环海的塞浦路斯。她走上岸来，成为一位庄严美丽的女神，她纤细的脚下长出了青草。众神和人类称她为阿佛洛狄忒——“泡沫所生的女神”，又称她为头戴华冠的库忒瑞亚，因为她到过库忒拉；也称她为塞浦路斯女神，因为她生在波涛环绕的塞浦路斯。她一出生，爱若斯就陪伴着她，美丽的欲望也追随着她。从一开始，她在神与人之中掌管的，就是少女的私语、微笑、欺骗、甜蜜的欢愉、爱情与温柔。
beats.textEn: The members, cast from the land into the surging sea, drifted a long time, and white foam spread around them; in it grew a maiden. She drifted first to holy Cythera and then to sea-girt Cyprus, and came forth an awful and lovely goddess, grass growing beneath her slender feet. Gods and men call her Aphrodite, the foam-born, and Cytherea and Cyprogenes. Eros and fair Desire went with her from her birth, and her portion among gods and men is the whispers of maidens, smiles, deceits, sweet delight, love and graciousness.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 荷马史诗说阿佛洛狄忒是宙斯与狄俄涅之女；本站把两种出身作为不同见证分开保存。

beats.headingZh: 黑夜的子女与海中的怪物
beats.headingEn: The children of Night and the monsters of the sea
beats.textZh: 乌拉诺斯称他的孩子们为“提坦”，意思是“伸手的人”，因为他们胆敢伸手犯下大罪，日后必遭报应。黑夜纽克斯没有和任何神结合，独自生下了可憎的厄运、黑色的死亡之灵和死神，还生下睡眠与梦的一族；又生下嘲讽、悲哀、守护金苹果的赫斯珀里得斯姐妹、命运三女神，以及惩罚不义的复仇女神涅墨西斯、欺骗、友爱、衰老和顽固的争吵。大海蓬托斯则生出诚实温和的海中老人涅柔斯，涅柔斯又有五十个海中女儿。海的另一支后代生出各种奇异的生物：灰衣的格赖埃、住在大洋彼岸的戈耳工姐妹——其中美杜莎是凡人，珀耳修斯砍下她的头时，从她身上跳出了飞马珀伽索斯；还有半女半蛇的厄喀德娜，她生下地狱犬刻耳柏洛斯和勒耳那的九头水蛇；喷火的客迈拉也出自这一支。
beats.textEn: Heaven called his sons Titans, 'strainers', for they had strained to do a fearful deed. Night, lying with none, bore hateful Doom and black Fate and Death, Sleep and the tribe of Dreams, Blame and Woe, the Hesperides who guard the golden apples, the Fates, Nemesis, Deceit, Friendship, Old Age and Strife. Sea begot truthful Nereus, father of fifty sea-daughters, and through his other children came wonders: the grey Graiae, the Gorgons beyond Ocean — among them mortal Medusa, from whose severed neck, when Perseus beheaded her, sprang the horse Pegasus — and half-nymph, half-snake Echidna, mother of Cerberus and the Hydra of Lerna, from whose line came the fire-breathing Chimaera too.

beats.textZh: 提坦们也有了后代：许珀里翁和忒亚生下了伟大的太阳赫利俄斯、明亮的月亮塞勒涅和照耀大地的黎明厄俄斯；大洋神的女儿斯堤克斯生下了热望、胜利、强力和暴力。后来宙斯召集众神说：谁和我一起与提坦作战，我就不剥夺他的权利。斯堤克斯第一个带着孩子们来到宙斯身边，宙斯就让她成为众神起誓时所凭的大誓，让她的孩子永远住在自己身边。福柏和科俄斯的孙女赫卡忒，更是被宙斯尊重胜过一切：宙斯给了她在大地、大海和星空中各一份荣耀。凡人献祭祈求恩惠时，都要呼唤赫卡忒；她愿意眷顾谁，谁就能在集会中出众、在战场上得胜、在比赛中获奖、在海上满载而归、在牧场上牛羊繁衍。虽然她是她母亲唯一的孩子，却在众神中享有一切荣耀。
beats.textEn: The Titans had children too: Hyperion and Theia bore great Helios, bright Selene and Eos who shines on all. Styx, daughter of Ocean, bore Zelus, Nike, Kratos and Bia. When Zeus promised that whoever fought with him against the Titans would keep their rights, Styx came first with her children, and Zeus made her the great oath of the gods and kept her children ever beside him. Hecate, granddaughter of Phoebe and Coeus, Zeus honoured above all, giving her a share of earth, sea and starry heaven. Whoever sacrifices calls upon her, and whom she favours prospers in the assembly, in battle, in contests, at sea and among the herds.

beats.textZh: 瑞亚被克洛诺斯征服，为他生下了出色的孩子们：赫斯提亚、得墨忒耳、脚穿金鞋的赫拉、住在地下、心肠无情的哈得斯、撼动大地的波塞冬，还有众神与人类之父、睿智的宙斯。可是，每当一个孩子从母亲的腹中来到她的膝上，伟大的克洛诺斯就把他吞下去。他这样做，是怕其他尊贵的天神之子取代他在众神中的王位，因为大地和星空曾经告诉他：他注定要被自己的儿子推翻，尽管他很强大——这是伟大的宙斯的计划。所以克洛诺斯时刻警惕，等待着、吞下了自己的孩子，瑞亚陷入了无法排解的悲伤。
beats.textEn: Rhea, subdued by Cronus, bore splendid children: Hestia, Demeter, gold-shod Hera, pitiless Hades who dwells under the earth, the loud-crashing Earth-Shaker, and wise Zeus, father of gods and men. But great Cronus swallowed each as it came from the womb to its mother's knees, lest another of the proud sons of Heaven hold the kingly office, for Earth and starry Heaven had told him he was destined to be overcome by his own son. So he kept watch and swallowed his children, and unceasing grief seized Rhea.

beats.headingEn: The baby in the Cretan cave
beats.textZh: 当瑞亚就要生下宙斯的时候，她恳求自己的父母——大地和星空——帮她想个办法，悄悄生下这个孩子，好为她的父亲和被吞下的孩子们向克洛诺斯复仇。父母听从了她，把她送到克里特岛富饶的吕克托斯。广大的大地从她手中接过婴儿，在克里特把他抚养长大，把他藏在神圣大地的深处、浓密森林覆盖的埃该昂山的一个山洞里。瑞亚则用襁褓包起一块大石头，交给天空的儿子、众神之王克洛诺斯。他接过石头就吞进了肚子里，这个可怜的人，并不知道在石头的后面，他的儿子安然无恙地活了下来，将来要用暴力推翻他、夺去他的尊位。岁月流转，宙斯的力量和四肢迅速成长；狡猾的克洛诺斯被大地的计谋所骗，先吐出了最后吞下的那块石头，又吐出了自己的孩子们。宙斯把那块石头立在神圣的皮托，作为后世凡人的一个标记。他还解放了被父亲捆在地下的兄弟——独眼巨人们，他们感激他的恩惠，把雷霆和闪电送给了他。
beats.textEn: When Rhea was about to bear Zeus, she begged Earth and Heaven to help her bear him secretly and avenge her father and her swallowed children. They sent her to Lyctus in Crete, and Earth took the baby and hid him in a cave beneath the wooded Aegean mount. Rhea wrapped a great stone in swaddling clothes and gave it to Cronus, who swallowed it, not knowing that his son lived on unconquered. Zeus grew swiftly; beguiled by Earth, Cronus vomited up first the stone and then his children. Zeus set the stone at Pytho as a sign to mortals, and freed the Cyclopes, who in gratitude gave him thunder and lightning.

beats.headingEn: The division at Mecone and the theft of fire
beats.textZh: 提坦伊阿佩托斯的儿子中，有扛着天穹的阿特拉斯、狂傲的墨诺提俄斯、聪明多计的普罗米修斯和糊涂的厄庇米修斯。当神与人在墨科涅商定献祭的份额时，普罗米修斯分开一头大牛：他把肉和肥美的内脏藏在牛胃里，把白骨用闪亮的脂肪包起来，请宙斯挑选。宙斯识破了诡计，却故意伸手选了白骨，从此凡人在祭坛上焚烧白骨献给众神。宙斯因此发怒，不再把不熄的火赐给世上的人。普罗米修斯又欺骗了他：用一根空心的茴香秆偷来了远处可见的火光。宙斯更加愤怒，用无法挣脱的锁链把普罗米修斯绑在一根柱子上，派一只长翅膀的鹰去啄食他不死的肝脏——白天被吃掉多少，夜里就长回多少，直到宙斯的儿子赫拉克勒斯杀死那只鹰，才把他从痛苦中解救出来。
beats.textEn: Among the sons of Iapetus were Atlas, who holds up the sky, proud Menoetius, clever Prometheus and witless Epimetheus. When gods and men were settling their portions at Mecone, Prometheus divided a great ox: he hid the meat and rich entrails in the stomach and wrapped the white bones in glistening fat, and bade Zeus choose. Zeus saw the trick but chose the bones, and ever since men burn white bones to the gods. In anger Zeus withheld fire, but Prometheus stole its far-seen gleam in a hollow fennel stalk. Zeus bound him with chains to a pillar and sent an eagle to eat his immortal liver, which grew back each night, until Heracles killed the eagle and set him free from torment.

beats.textZh: 为了补偿火的代价，宙斯给人类送去了一样祸害。按照宙斯的意志，著名的跛足神赫淮斯托斯用泥土造出一个羞怯少女的模样；明眸女神雅典娜给她系上腰带，穿上银白色的衣裳，从她头上垂下一块精工刺绣的面纱，又给她戴上用新鲜花朵编成的美丽花环，和一顶赫淮斯托斯亲手制作的、雕满海陆奇兽的金冠。当这个美丽的祸害被带到神和人的面前时，惊叹攫住了永生的神和会死的人。赫西俄德说，女人的族类就是从她而来；她们像蜂房里只享用别人劳动的雄蜂，给凡人带来负担。宙斯还设下另一个祸害：谁若逃避婚姻，晚年就无人奉养；谁若娶了妻子，也难免与烦恼相伴。所以，谁也欺骗不了宙斯，就连伊阿佩托斯之子普罗米修斯也逃不过他的愤怒。
beats.textEn: In return for fire Zeus made an evil for men. At his will the famous lame god Hephaestus moulded from earth the likeness of a shy maiden; bright-eyed Athena girded and clothed her in silvery raiment, draped an embroidered veil from her head, crowned her with fresh flowers and with a golden crown Hephaestus had made, chased with wonders of land and sea. Gods and men marvelled when she was brought forth. From her, says Hesiod, comes the race of women; and Zeus set a second evil, that whoever shuns marriage has no one to tend him in old age. So it is not possible to deceive the mind of Zeus; not even Prometheus escaped his wrath.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 《神谱》中的第一个女人没有名字；“潘多拉”与她打开罐子的故事见于赫西俄德《工作与时日》，本篇不合并。

beats.textZh: 当初乌拉诺斯嫉妒科托斯、布里阿瑞俄斯和古革斯的力量与身形，用强大的锁链把他们捆住，囚禁在宽广大地的尽头，他们在那里长久地忍受痛苦与悲伤。克洛诺斯和瑞亚的孩子们在奥林波斯山上，与在俄特律斯山上的提坦们已经交战了整整十年，双方不分胜负。这时，宙斯听从大地的劝告，把百臂巨人们带回光明之中，给他们吃神食、喝琼浆，振奋他们的精神。宙斯对他们说：大地与天空的孩子们啊，请听我说。为了胜利与力量，我们已经与提坦们苦战了很久；请记起我们的友谊，是我们的计划把你们从残酷的锁链和黑暗中解救出来，现在请在这场可怕的战斗中展现你们不可抵挡的力量吧！科托斯回答说：我们知道你的智慧超群，是你把我们从冰冷的锁链中救出，我们一定会用坚定的心与提坦作战，守护你的统治。
beats.textEn: Ouranos, jealous of the strength and shape of Cottus, Briareos and Gyes, had bound them in cruel chains at the ends of the earth. For ten full years the children of Cronus on Olympus and the Titans on Othrys had fought without decision. Then, on Earth's counsel, Zeus brought the Hundred-Handers up to the light, revived them with nectar and ambrosia, and reminded them that the Olympians had freed them from their bonds. Cottus answered that they knew Zeus's wisdom, and would fight the Titans with unwavering hearts to defend his rule.

beats.textZh: 那一天，男神和女神都投入了可怕的战斗。百臂巨人每人肩上长着一百只手，从坚实的手中掷出巨大的岩石；提坦们也加强了阵线，双方同时展现出双手的力量。无边的大海可怕地轰鸣，大地发出巨响，广阔的天空颤抖呻吟，高高的奥林波斯山从根基上摇撼，震动一直传到幽暗的塔耳塔罗斯。这时宙斯不再克制自己的力量，他从天空和奥林波斯山上一路冲下，不停地投掷闪电，雷霆和闪光从他强壮的手中密集地飞出，旋转着神圣的火焰。生命之源的大地在燃烧中轰响，无边的森林在大火中噼啪作响，整个大地、大洋的水流和荒凉的大海都在沸腾，炽热的气浪包围了提坦们，耀眼的电光刺瞎了他们的眼睛，那景象仿佛天空与大地相撞。科托斯、布里阿瑞俄斯和古革斯冲在最前面，每次掷出三百块岩石，用飞石遮住了提坦们，把他们打入宽广大地之下的深处，用痛苦的锁链捆绑起来。
beats.textEn: That day gods and goddesses joined in fearful strife. The Hundred-Handers hurled huge rocks from their strong hands, and the Titans strengthened their ranks; the boundless sea rang terribly, the earth crashed, wide heaven groaned and high Olympus shook to its foundations, and the tremor reached dim Tartarus. Then Zeus no longer held back his might: he came from heaven and Olympus hurling lightning, the bolts flying thick from his strong hand. The life-giving earth crashed in flames, the forests crackled, the earth, Ocean and the sea seethed, hot vapour lapped the Titans and the flash blinded them; it seemed as if earth and heaven had met. The Hundred-Handers, foremost in the fight, hurled three hundred rocks at a time, overshadowed the Titans with missiles, and sent them down beneath the earth in bitter chains.

beats.textZh: 提坦们被关进的地方，离大地之下的距离，就像天空离大地那么远：一块青铜的铁砧从天上落下，要九天九夜，第十天才到地面；再从地面落下，又要九天九夜，第十天才到塔耳塔罗斯。四周围着青铜的墙，黑夜在它的颈部围了三层，上面是大地和荒凉大海的根。波塞冬在那里装上了青铜的大门，百臂巨人们住在那里，作为宙斯忠实的看守。那里也是黑夜的可怕居所：黑夜与白昼在那里相遇，在巨大的青铜门槛上互相问候，一个进去，另一个就出来，从不同时在家。睡眠和死亡这两个黑夜的孩子也住在那里；冥府之王哈得斯和可怕的珀耳塞福涅的宫殿也在那里，一条凶猛的狗守在门前，对进来的人摇尾巴，却不让任何人出去。那里还住着大洋神的长女斯堤克斯，众神若在她的水上发假誓，就要像死去一样躺一整年，不能吃神食、喝琼浆，接下来九年被逐出众神的集会和宴席。
beats.textEn: The Titans lie as far beneath the earth as heaven is above it: a bronze anvil falling from heaven would fall nine nights and days and reach the earth on the tenth, and as long again to reach Tartarus. A bronze fence runs around it, Night is poured round its neck in three rows, and above it grow the roots of earth and sea; Poseidon fixed bronze gates there, and the Hundred-Handers dwell there as Zeus's faithful guards. There too stands the house of Night, where Night and Day greet each other at the bronze threshold, never both at home; there live Sleep and Death; there stands the house of Hades and Persephone, guarded by a hound that fawns on those who enter but lets none leave; and there lives Styx, by whose water any god who swears falsely lies breathless a year and is barred from the gods' feasts for nine more.

beats.textZh: 宙斯把提坦们赶出天界之后，广大的大地与塔耳塔罗斯结合，生下了她最小的孩子提丰。他双手有力，双脚不知疲倦，肩上长出一百个蛇头，可怕的蛇头吐着黑色的舌头，眼睛在眉毛下闪着火光；那些头还能发出各种不可思议的声音：有时说众神能听懂的话，有时像公牛怒吼，有时像狮子咆哮，有时像小狗吠叫，有时发出尖锐的嘶声，在高山间回响。那一天，若不是众神与人类之父及时察觉，提丰就要统治神和人了。宙斯猛烈地打起雷来，大地、天空、大海和塔耳塔罗斯都发出巨响，奥林波斯山在不朽的脚下颤抖。宙斯从奥林波斯山跳下，用雷霆和闪电击打提丰，烧焦了他所有的头，用鞭打把他制服。提丰成了残废倒下，大地在大火中熔化，就像锡在熔炉中熔化一样。宙斯把他扔进宽广的塔耳塔罗斯。从提丰身上生出了狂暴的湿风，它们给航海的人和田里的庄稼带来灾难。
beats.textEn: When Zeus had driven the Titans from heaven, Earth lay with Tartarus and bore her youngest child, Typhoeus, with tireless feet and a hundred snake heads flickering dark tongues and flashing fire from their eyes. His heads spoke in every voice: now words the gods understood, now the bellow of a bull, the roar of a lion, the yelp of whelps, a hissing that echoed among the hills. He would have ruled gods and men had Zeus not seen it. Zeus thundered until earth, heaven, sea and Tartarus resounded, leapt from Olympus, struck Typhoeus with lightning, burned all his heads and lashed him down; the earth melted like tin in a crucible. Zeus hurled him into Tartarus, and from him come the wild, damp winds that wreck ships and spoil crops.

beats.textZh: 当有福的众神结束了苦战，以武力决定了与提坦们的荣誉之争，他们听从大地的建议，敦促目光远大的奥林波斯之神宙斯来统治和主宰他们，宙斯便在众神中公平地分配了各自的荣誉。众神之王宙斯的第一个妻子是比任何神和人都更有智慧的墨提斯。可是当她就要生下明眸女神雅典娜的时候，宙斯听从了大地和天空的劝告，用甜言蜜语骗过她，把她吞进了自己的肚子里——因为大地和天空告诉他，墨提斯注定会生下非常聪明的孩子：先是一个女儿，然后是一个将成为众神与人类之王的儿子。宙斯先下手为强，让墨提斯在他体内为他出谋划策、分辨善恶。后来，宙斯从自己的头里生出了明眸的雅典娜。他又先后娶了忒弥斯，生下时序女神与命运女神；娶了欧律诺墨，生下美惠三女神；与得墨忒耳生下珀耳塞福涅；与谟涅摩叙涅生下九位缪斯；与勒托生下阿波罗和阿耳忒弥斯；最后娶赫拉为妻，生下青春女神赫柏、战神阿瑞斯和助产女神厄勒提亚。
beats.textEn: When the gods had finished their toil and settled their honours with the Titans by force, they urged Zeus, on Earth's advice, to reign over them, and he divided their honours. His first wife was Metis, wisest of gods and men; but when she was about to bear Athena, Zeus, told by Earth and Heaven that she was destined to bear a son who would be king of gods and men, beguiled her with words and put her in his own belly, so that she might advise him of good and evil. He himself gave birth to bright-eyed Athena from his head. Then he married Themis, mother of the Seasons and Fates; Eurynome, mother of the Graces; Demeter, who bore Persephone; Mnemosyne, mother of the Muses; Leto, mother of Apollo and Artemis; and last Hera, who bore Hebe, Ares and Eileithyia.

facts.textZh: 雅典娜是宙斯的孩子。
facts.textEn: Theogony 924-926 describes Athena as produced from Zeus’s head.

facts.textZh: 墨提斯是雅典娜的父母。
facts.textEn: Theogony says Metis was about to give birth to Athena.

facts.textZh: 雅典娜使用埃癸斯神盾。
facts.textEn: Iliad 5 depicts Athena putting on the tasselled aegis while arming for battle.

facts.textZh: 《荷马颂歌·致雅典娜》（第28首）提到雅典娜。
facts.textEn: Homeric Hymn 28 is addressed to Athena and narrates her armed birth.
facts.sourceTitle: Homeric Hymn 28 to Athena, Evelyn-White English text

deityStoryCards.name: Indra
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《梨俱吠陀》中的因陀罗：金刚杵持有者，并在 1.32 与 2.12 的具体见证中与蛇敌、受阻水流、大气和战斗相连。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Indra in registered Rigvedic witnesses, wielder of the vajra and linked to serpent combat, released waters, atmosphere and battle.

beats.textZh: 《梨俱吠陀》1.32把因陀罗列为主要行动者，把弗栗多列为他的对手。
beats.textEn: Rigveda 1.32 identifies Indra as the principal agent and Vrtra as his opponent.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 本页只代表此颂歌见证。

beats.textZh: 同一颂歌的登记Claims把金刚杵连接到因陀罗，并把其制造连接到陀湿多。
beats.textEn: Claims registered from the same hymn connect the vajra to Indra and its making to Tvastr.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 不把后期佛教或图像版本反投到吠陀颂歌。

beats.textZh: 事件档案以对手被击杀、水得以流出作为颂歌叙事结果；它不是现代自然科学陈述。
beats.textEn: The event profile records the opponent struck down and the waters flowing out as the narrative result of the hymn; it is not a modern scientific statement.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 知识层保持为神话叙事／文本见证。

facts.textZh: 因陀罗使用金刚杵／雷霆。
facts.textEn: In RV 1.32, Indra is associated with wielding the vajra against Vṛtra.
facts.sourceLocation: Registered text passage or museum catalogue

facts.textZh: 《梨俱吠陀》1.32见证提到因陀罗。
facts.textEn: RV 1.32 names Indra as the hymn’s deity and actor.
facts.sourceLocation: Registered text passage or museum catalogue

facts.textZh: 因陀罗杀死了弗栗多。
facts.textEn: Rigveda 1.32 narrates Indra killing Vrtra, also designated as a serpent in the hymn.

facts.textZh: 因陀罗与雷相关。
facts.textEn: Rigveda 1.32 places Indra’s combat amid lightning, thunder and rain imagery while preserving its own Vedic vocabulary and narrative.

deityStoryCards.name: Tvastr
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《梨俱吠陀》1.32 见证中为因陀罗制作金刚杵者。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Maker of Indra’s vajra in the registered Rigveda 1.32 witness.

beats.textZh: 《梨俱吠陀》1.32把因陀罗列为主要行动者，把弗栗多列为他的对手。
beats.textEn: Rigveda 1.32 identifies Indra as the principal agent and Vrtra as his opponent.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 本页只代表此颂歌见证。

beats.textZh: 同一颂歌的登记Claims把金刚杵连接到因陀罗，并把其制造连接到陀湿多。
beats.textEn: Claims registered from the same hymn connect the vajra to Indra and its making to Tvastr.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 不把后期佛教或图像版本反投到吠陀颂歌。

beats.textZh: 事件档案以对手被击杀、水得以流出作为颂歌叙事结果；它不是现代自然科学陈述。
beats.textEn: The event profile records the opponent struck down and the waters flowing out as the narrative result of the hymn; it is not a modern scientific statement.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 知识层保持为神话叙事／文本见证。

facts.textZh: 陀湿多创造了金刚杵／雷霆。
facts.textEn: Rigveda 1.32.2 says Tvastr fashioned the vajra for Indra.

deityStoryCards.name: Tlaloc
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 与农业相关的雨神；大神庙北侧是他的神庙（墨西哥国家人类学与历史研究所）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Rain god linked to agriculture whose temple occupied the north side of the Templo Mayor (INAH).

beats.headingEn: The war god on the south
beats.textZh: 大神庙南侧的神殿属于维齐洛波奇特利——墨西加人的太阳战神，也是他们的守护神。
beats.textEn: The southern chapel of the Templo Mayor belongs to Huitzilopochtli, the Mexica's solar god of war and their patron.
beats.sourceTitle: Museo de Sitio del Templo Mayor
beats.evidenceNote: INAH 大神庙遗址博物馆说明。

beats.headingEn: The rain god on the north
beats.textZh: 北侧的神殿属于特拉洛克——掌管雨水、与农业紧密相连的神。战争与农业，两位神并立在同一座金字塔的顶端。
beats.textEn: The northern temple belongs to Tlaloc, god of rain and closely tied to agriculture. War and farming stand side by side at the top of one pyramid.
beats.sourceTitle: Museo de Sitio del Templo Mayor
beats.evidenceNote: INAH 大神庙遗址博物馆说明。

beats.headingEn: A temple that grew in layers
beats.textZh: 据 INAH 介绍，墨西加人在1325年建立特诺奇蒂特兰时修了一座小神庙，此后经过多次重建和扩建，越修越高。
beats.textEn: According to INAH, the Mexica built a small temple when they founded Tenochtitlan in 1325, and it was rebuilt and enlarged many times over.
beats.sourceTitle: Museo de Sitio del Templo Mayor
beats.evidenceNote: INAH 大神庙遗址博物馆说明。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 各建造阶段的具体年代仍有不确定之处。

facts.textZh: 特拉洛克——职掌：rain and agriculture
facts.textEn: INAH calls Tlaloc the god of rain, directly linked to agriculture.
facts.sourceTitle: Museo de Sitio del Templo Mayor

deityStoryCards.name: Tezcatlipoca
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 又称蒂特拉卡瓦；《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷中令羽蛇神在图拉衰落的巫师之一。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Also called Titlacauan; among the sorcerers who bring Quetzalcoatl's glory at Tollan to an end (Florentine Codex Book 3).

beats.headingZh: 被当作神的蒂特拉卡瓦
beats.headingEn: Titlacauan, held to be a god
beats.textZh: 第三卷第2章讲人们怎样把一位叫蒂特拉卡瓦、也叫特斯卡特利波卡的人物当作神来敬奉。
beats.textEn: Chapter 2 of Book 3 tells how one called Titlacauan, or Tezcatlipoca, came to be regarded as a god.
beats.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第2章。

beats.textZh: 第3章讲羽蛇神——图拉的一位大法师。第4章说，当巫师们来到他身边，他的荣光便走到了尽头；第5章又记下蒂特拉卡瓦带来的另一个异兆。
beats.textEn: Chapter 3 tells of Quetzalcoatl, a great wizard at Tollan. Chapter 4 relates how his glory came to an end when the sorcerers came to him, and chapter 5 records another portent brought about by Titlacauan.
beats.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第3–5章。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 本段依据章节标题与概要，具体情节尚未逐句核对。

beats.textZh: 第14章记载，羽蛇神离去时，追随他的人经过伊斯塔克特佩特尔与波波卡特佩特尔两座雪山之间，被冻死在冰雪里。
beats.textEn: Chapter 14 records that as Quetzalcoatl departs, his vassals freeze to death in the ice as they pass between Iztactepetl and Popocatepetl.
beats.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第14章。

facts.textZh: 特斯卡特利波卡出现在“羽蛇神在图拉的衰落”之中。
facts.textEn: Titlacauan is among the sorcerers whose portents bring Quetzalcoatl's glory to an end (Book 3, chapters 4–5).

deityStoryCards.name: Coyolxauhqui
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Daughter of Coatlicue who leads her brothers against their mother and is killed by Huitzilopochtli at Coatepec.

beats.textZh: 科阿特利库埃住在蛇山上。一天她打扫时，一团羽毛从天上飘下来。她把羽毛捡起来，塞在腰间——就这样怀孕了。
beats.textEn: Coatlicue lives on Coatepec. One day as she sweeps, a ball of feathers drifts down. She picks it up and tucks it at her waist — and so she becomes pregnant.
beats.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。

beats.textZh: 她的女儿科约尔沙乌基对兄弟们——四百个南方人——说：母亲让我们蒙羞，我们必须杀了她。于是他们全副武装，朝蛇山进发。
beats.textEn: Her daughter Coyolxauhqui tells her brothers, the four hundred Centzon Huitznahua, that their mother has shamed them and must be killed. Armed, they set out for Coatepec.
beats.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。

beats.textZh: 腹中的维齐洛波奇特利安慰母亲：不要怕，我知道该怎么做。敌人冲上山顶的那一刻，他出生了，手持盾牌、投枪和投枪器。
beats.textEn: From the womb Huitzilopochtli comforts his mother: do not be afraid, I know what to do. The moment the attackers reach the summit he is born, carrying shield, darts and dart-thrower.
beats.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。

beats.textZh: 维齐洛波奇特利砍下科约尔沙乌基的头，她的身体沿着蛇山滚落下去。四百个兄弟也被他从山顶追得四散奔逃。
beats.textEn: Huitzilopochtli cuts off Coyolxauhqui's head, and her body tumbles down the side of Coatepec. He drives the four hundred brothers from the summit, scattering them in every direction.
beats.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 学者认为这段叙事与大神庙的布局相呼应，属于解释，不写成事实。

facts.textZh: 科约尔沙乌基是科阿特利库埃的孩子。
facts.textEn: Coyolxauhqui is a daughter of Coatlicue who urges her brothers, the Centzon Huitznahua, to kill their mother.

facts.textEn: INAH calls Huitzilopochtli the solar god of war and patron of the Mexica.
facts.sourceTitle: Museo de Sitio del Templo Mayor

facts.textZh: 维齐洛波奇特利是科阿特利库埃的孩子。
facts.textEn: Huitzilopochtli is the child Coatlicue conceives at Coatepec.

facts.textZh: 维齐洛波奇特利在特诺奇蒂特兰大神庙受到崇拜。
facts.textEn: INAH describes Huitzilopochtli's chapel on the south side of the Templo Mayor.
facts.sourceTitle: Museo de Sitio del Templo Mayor

facts.textZh: 维齐洛波奇特利——击败：the Centzon Huitznahua, scattered from Coatepec
facts.textEn: He scatters the Centzon Huitznahua from the top of Coatepec.

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Great wizard of Tollan whose glory ends when sorcerers come to him in Florentine Codex Book 3.
