beats.textZh: 须佐之男说：我没有坏心。父亲问我为什么哭，我说想去母亲的国家，父亲就把我赶走了。我只是来向你告别的。天照大神问：怎么证明你的心是清白的？须佐之男说：我们各自立誓生孩子吧。两人隔着天安河站定。天照大神先拿过须佐之男佩带的十拳剑，把它折成三段，在天之真名井里涮得叮当作响，放进嘴里嚼碎，吹出的气雾中生出了三位女神。接着须佐之男拿过天照大神缠在头发和手臂上的勾玉串，同样在井里涮洗、嚼碎、吹气，从雾气中生出了五位男神。
beats.textEn: Susanoo replied that he had no evil intent: his father had expelled him and he had only come to say farewell. Asked how he could prove the purity of his heart, he proposed that each should swear and produce children. Standing on either side of the Tranquil River of Heaven, Amaterasu first took his ten-grasp sabre, broke it into three, rinsed the pieces jingling in the True-Pool-Well of Heaven, crunched them and blew out a misty breath, from which three goddesses were born. Then Susanoo took the strings of curved jewels from her hair and arms, rinsed, crunched and blew in the same way, and five male deities were born.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十三节。

beats.textZh: 天照大神宣布：后来生的五位男神，是从我的东西里生出来的，所以是我的孩子；先生的三位女神，是从你的东西里生出来的，所以是你的孩子。须佐之男却说：因为我的心是清白的，所以我生出了温柔的女孩子。这样说来，当然是我赢了。他自以为得胜，得意忘形起来。（这五位男神中的长子，后来成了天皇家的祖先；三位女神则成为宗像大社供奉的神。）
beats.textEn: Amaterasu declared that the five male deities, born from her jewels, were her children, and the three goddesses, born from his sabre, were his. But Susanoo said that because his heart was pure he had begotten gentle maidens, and so of course he had won. Puffed up with his victory, he grew reckless. (The eldest of the five male deities becomes, later in the Kojiki, the ancestor of the imperial line; the three goddesses are those worshipped at Munakata.)
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十四节。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 括号里关于皇室祖先与宗像三女神的说明见于《古事记》的同一段落及后文，属于文本自身的谱系说明。

beats.headingEn: Riot in the Plain of High Heaven
beats.textZh: 仗着这场“胜利”，须佐之男在高天原胡作非为。他踏坏天照大神水田的田埂，填平灌溉的水沟，又在她品尝新谷的神殿里撒下粪便。天照大神却替他辩解：那像粪便的东西，是我弟弟喝醉了吐出来的；他填平水沟、踏坏田埂，是舍不得那些土地白白空着。可须佐之男的恶行不但没有停止，反而更加厉害。有一天，天照大神正坐在神圣的织殿里，让织女们为众神织造衣裳。须佐之男在织殿的屋顶上捅开一个洞，把一匹从尾巴倒着剥了皮的天之斑马扔了进去。织女吓得跳起来，被梭子刺中下身，就这样死了。
beats.textEn: On the strength of his victory Susanoo ran riot. He broke down the divisions of Amaterasu's rice fields, filled in the ditches, and strewed excrement in the palace where she tasted the first fruits. Amaterasu excused him: what looked like excrement was what her brother had vomited when drunk, and he had filled the ditches and broken the ridges only because he grudged the land lying idle. But his wickedness grew worse. While Amaterasu sat in her sacred weaving hall seeing to the weaving of the deities' garments, he broke a hole in the roof and flung down a heavenly piebald horse flayed backwards; a heavenly weaving maiden, startled, struck herself with her shuttle and died.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十五节。

beats.textZh: 天照大神看见这一切，感到害怕，就打开天之岩户——天上的岩石屋子的门——走了进去，把门牢牢关上，隐居起来。于是整个高天原一片黑暗，下面的苇原中国也一片黑暗，永远的黑夜笼罩了一切。在这片黑暗里，无数恶神的声音像五月的苍蝇一样到处嗡嗡作响，各种各样的灾祸接连发生。《古事记》对这场灾难只写了寥寥几句，却是神代故事的一个大转折：天照大神是照耀天地的女神，她一躲起来，天上和人间就没有了白天，众神的世界也失去了秩序。接下来的一整段，讲的都是众神如何同心协力，想办法把她请出来。
beats.textEn: Terrified at the sight, Amaterasu opened the door of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling, went in, made it fast and hid herself. Then the whole Plain of High Heaven was dark, and the Central Land of Reed-Plains below was dark too: eternal night prevailed. In that darkness the voices of the myriad deities swarmed like summer flies, and every kind of calamity arose.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

beats.textZh: 八百万位神聚集在天安河的河滩上开会商议，请高御产巢日神的儿子思金神想办法。依照他的计划，众神先把常世的长鸣鸟聚在一起，让它们一齐啼叫。又从天安河上游取来坚硬的岩石，从天上的金山取来铁，请来锻冶师天津麻罗，命伊斯许理度卖命造一面镜子，命玉祖命做一串长长的、有五百颗勾玉的玉串。他们又请天儿屋命和布刀玉命，从天香山上取来一头雄鹿完整的肩胛骨，用天香山上的桦树皮烧它，进行占卜。
beats.textEn: The eight hundred myriad deities assembled in a divine assembly in the bed of the Tranquil River of Heaven and bade Omoikane, child of Takami-musubi, think of a plan. They gathered the long-singing birds of eternal night and made them sing. They took hard rocks from the river-bed and iron from the Heavenly Metal-Mountains, called the smith Amatsumara, and charged Ishikoridome to make a mirror and Tamanoya to make a long string of five hundred curved jewels. They summoned Ame-no-Koyane and Futotama to pull out the whole shoulder-blade of a true stag of Mount Kagu and perform divination with cherry-bark from the same mountain.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

beats.headingEn: The sakaki tree hung with treasures
beats.textZh: 众神把天香山上一棵长满枝叶的真杨桐树连根拔起，在上面的枝条上挂起那串五百颗勾玉，在中间的枝条上挂起那面八咫镜，在下面的枝条上挂起白色和青色的布帛。布刀玉命双手捧着这棵树，作为隆重的供品；天儿屋命念诵庄严的祝词。天手力男神则悄悄藏在岩户门边，等待时机。这些东西在后世都有了特别的意义：镜子和勾玉与后来从大蛇尾中得到的草薙剑，被看作代代相传的三件神圣宝物；注连绳、杨桐枝和祝词，至今仍是神社祭祀中常见的东西。不过在这个故事里，它们只有一个用处——把躲起来的女神请出来。
beats.textEn: They uprooted a five-hundred-branched true sakaki tree from Mount Kagu of Heaven. On its upper branches they hung the long string of five hundred curved jewels; on its middle branches the large mirror; on its lower branches pendant offerings of white and blue cloth. Futotama held these as grand offerings, Ame-no-Koyane recited a solemn liturgy, and Ame-no-Tajikarao stood hidden beside the door.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

beats.textZh: 天宇受卖命用天香山的日影蔓束起衣袖，用真拆葛做成头饰，手里握着一束天香山的竹叶，在天之岩户前倒扣一只木桶，在上面用力踏脚，踏得咚咚作响。她跳着跳着，神灵附了体，露出了胸脯，把裙带一直推到了下身。整个高天原都震动起来，八百万位神一齐哈哈大笑。这是整个神话里最热闹、也最奇特的一幕：漆黑一片的天上，众神围着紧闭的岩户，看着一位女神在倒扣的木桶上又踏又跳，笑声震动了天地。后世把天宇受卖命尊为舞蹈与艺能之神，神乐的起源也常被追溯到这一段。
beats.textEn: Ame-no-Uzume bound up her sleeves with heavenly clubmoss from Mount Kagu, made a head-dress of spindle-tree, took in her hand a bundle of bamboo grass from Mount Kagu, and laid an upturned tub before the door of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling, stamping on it until it resounded. Becoming divinely possessed, she bared her breasts and pushed her skirt-string down to her private parts. The Plain of High Heaven shook, and the eight hundred myriad deities laughed together.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

beats.textZh: 天照大神觉得奇怪，把岩户的门稍稍打开一条缝，在里面问：我藏了起来，以为高天原会一片黑暗，苇原中国也会一片黑暗，为什么天宇受卖命还在跳舞，八百万位神都在大笑？天宇受卖命回答：因为这里来了一位比您更尊贵的神，所以我们高兴地跳舞欢笑。就在她说话的时候，天儿屋命和布刀玉命把镜子推到天照大神面前。天照大神看到镜中的光，越发惊奇，一点一点地走出门来想看个究竟。藏在门边的天手力男神一把握住她的手，把她拉了出来。布刀玉命立刻在她身后拉起一根注连绳，说：您不能再回到里面去了！天照大神一出来，高天原和苇原中国自然又恢复了光明。
beats.textEn: Amaterasu, wondering, opened the door a crack and asked why, when she had thought Heaven and the Central Land would be dark, Ame-no-Uzume danced and all the deities laughed. Uzume answered that they rejoiced because there was a deity more illustrious than she. While she spoke, Ame-no-Koyane and Futotama pushed the mirror forward to show it to Amaterasu, who, more and more astonished, came gradually out to gaze. Tajikarao, hidden beside the door, took her hand and drew her out, and Futotama stretched a bottom-tied rope behind her, saying she must not go back further in than this. As she came forth, Heaven and the Central Land were lit again.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

beats.headingEn: Expulsion and the origin of grain
beats.textZh: 八百万位神一起商议，罚须佐之男交出一千桌赎罪的供品，剪掉他的胡子，拔掉他手指和脚趾的指甲，把他赶出了高天原。在路上，须佐之男向大宜都比卖讨要食物。大宜都比卖从鼻子、嘴巴和臀部取出各种美味，做成佳肴献给他。须佐之男偷偷看见了，以为她拿污秽的东西给他吃，就把她杀了。从被杀的女神身上长出了各种东西：头上生出蚕，两只眼睛里生出稻种，两只耳朵里生出粟，鼻子里生出小豆，阴部生出麦，臀部生出大豆。神产巢日神让人把这些收起来，当作种子。
beats.textEn: The eight hundred myriad deities took counsel together, fined Susanoo a thousand tables of offerings, cut off his beard and pulled out his finger- and toe-nails, and drove him out with a divine expulsion. Then he asked food of Ōgetsuhime, who took dainties from her nose, mouth and hindquarters and offered them to him. Watching, he thought she was offering him filth, and killed her. From her body things were born: silkworms from her head, rice-seeds from her eyes, millet from her ears, small beans from her nose, barley from her genitals and soy beans from her hindquarters. Kami-musubi had them taken and used as seeds.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十七节。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 《日本书纪》里杀死食物女神的是月读，对象叫保食神；本篇只讲《古事记》的版本。

beats.textZh: 须佐之男被赶出天界，降落到出云国肥河上游一个叫鸟发的地方。这时他看见河上漂下来一双筷子，心想上游一定有人住，就沿着河往上走。果然遇见一位老人和一位老妇人，两人中间夹着一位少女，正在哭泣。老人说：我是这里的国神大山津见神的儿子，名叫足名椎，妻子叫手名椎，女儿叫栉名田比卖。我们原本有八个女儿，可是高志的八岐大蛇每年都来，吃掉一个。现在又到了它来的时候，所以我们在哭。须佐之男问那条蛇长什么样。老人说：它的眼睛像红色的酸浆果，一个身子上长着八个头、八条尾巴，身上长满了苔藓、桧树和杉树，身长横跨八道山谷、八座山峰，看它的肚子，总是血淋淋地溃烂着。
beats.textEn: Expelled, Susanoo descended to Torikami at the head of the river Hi in Izumo. Seeing chopsticks floating down, he knew people lived upstream and went up the river, where he found an old man and an old woman weeping with a maiden between them. The old man said he was Ashinazuchi, son of the great mountain deity, his wife was Tenazuchi and their daughter Kushinadahime. They had had eight daughters, but the eight-forked serpent of Koshi came every year and devoured one, and now it was time for it to come again. Its eyes, he said, were like red winter-cherries; it had one body with eight heads and eight tails; moss, cypress and cryptomeria grew on its body; its length spanned eight valleys and eight hills; and its belly was always bloody and inflamed.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十八节。

beats.headingEn: Eight vats of liquor and the Kusanagi sword
beats.textZh: 须佐之男说：我是天照大神的弟弟，刚从天上下来。你们愿意把女儿嫁给我吗？老夫妇恭恭敬敬地答应了。须佐之男把少女变成一把密齿的梳子，插在自己的发髻上，然后吩咐老夫妇：酿造八次反复酿成的烈酒，再围一道篱笆，篱笆上开八个门，每个门口搭一个台子，每个台子上放一只酒槽，槽里都盛满烈酒。一切准备好后，八岐大蛇果然来了，它把八个头分别伸进八只酒槽里，大口喝酒，喝醉了就趴下睡着了。须佐之男拔出佩带的十拳剑，把大蛇砍成碎块，肥河里流的全成了血。他砍到大蛇中间的那条尾巴时，剑刃崩了个缺口。他觉得奇怪，用剑尖剖开尾巴一看，里面有一把锋利的大刀。他认为这是不同寻常的宝物，就把它献给了天照大神——这就是草薙剑。
beats.textEn: Susanoo revealed that he was the elder brother of Amaterasu, just descended from Heaven, and asked for the maiden; the old couple respectfully agreed. He turned her into a close-toothed comb and stuck it in his hair. Then he told them to brew eightfold-refined liquor, build a fence with eight gates, and at each gate set a platform with a vat full of the liquor. The serpent came as foretold, dipped a head into each vat and drank, then lay down drunk and slept. Susanoo drew his ten-grasp sabre and cut the serpent to pieces, so that the river Hi ran with blood. When he cut its middle tail, the edge of his sabre broke; wondering, he split the tail open with its point and found a great sword. Thinking it a strange thing, he presented it to Amaterasu — the Herb-Quelling sword, Kusanagi.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十八节。
beats.uncertaintyNote: “草薙”这个名字在《古事记》的这一段只作注明；名称由来的故事（日本武尊割草）在后文另有讲述。

beats.headingZh: 须贺的宫殿与八云之歌
beats.headingEn: The palace of Suga and the song of eight clouds
beats.textZh: 之后，须佐之男在出云国寻找建造宫殿的地方。他来到须贺这个地方，说：我来到这里，心里清清爽爽的。就在那里建起了宫殿，所以那地方至今叫做须贺。他在那里建宫时，有云从地上升起，他便作了一首歌：八云立，出云八重垣，为了让妻子住进来，我筑起八重垣——啊，那八重垣！这被认为是日本最早的和歌。他把栉名田比卖的父亲足名椎叫来，任命他做宫殿的长官，并赐给他一个名字：稻田宫主须贺之八耳神。
beats.textEn: Then Susanoo looked for a place in Izumo to build a palace. Arriving at Suga he said that his heart was refreshed, and he built his palace there — which is why the place is still called Suga. As he built it, clouds rose up, and he made a song: Eight clouds arise. The eightfold fence of Izumo makes an eightfold fence for the spouses to retire within. Oh, that eightfold fence! He called Ashinazuchi and made him master of the palace, giving him the name Inada-no-Miyanushi-Suga-no-Yatsumimi.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十九节。
beats.uncertaintyNote: “日本最早的和歌”是后世（如《古今和歌集》序）的说法，不是《古事记》本文的断言。

deityStoryCards.name: Kagutsuchi (Deity of Fire)
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Fire deity whose birth burns Izanami in the Kojiki; Chamberlain calls him the Deity-of-Fire and names him Kagu-tsu-chi in his notes.

beats.headingEn: A spear from the Floating Bridge
beats.textZh: 天上的众神命令伊邪那岐和伊邪那美去巩固还在漂浮的大地，并交给他们一支镶玉的天沼矛。两神站在天浮桥上，把矛伸进海里搅动；提起矛时，矛尖滴下的盐水层层堆积，成了淤能碁吕岛。
beats.textEn: The heavenly deities command Izanagi and Izanami to make firm the drifting land and give them a jewelled spear. Standing on the Floating Bridge of Heaven, they stir the brine; when they lift the spear, the drops from its tip pile up into Onogoro Island.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.uncertaintyNote: 《日本书纪》说两神是自己决定动手，本版不合并。

beats.headingEn: The birth of the fire deity
beats.textZh: 两神结合，生出许多岛屿和神灵。可是伊邪那美生下火神时被烧伤，病倒在床，最终“神去”——也就是死去。
beats.textEn: Joined together, the pair bring forth islands and deities. But when Izanami gives birth to the Deity-of-Fire she is burned, falls sick, and at length 'divinely retires' — she dies.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)

beats.textZh: 伊邪那岐想再见到妻子，便追到黄泉，请她回去：“我们造的国土还没有完成。”伊邪那美回答：你来得太晚了，我已经吃了黄泉灶火煮的东西——不过她答应去和黄泉的神商量。
beats.textEn: Longing to see her, Izanagi follows Izanami to Yomi and asks her to come back, for the lands they made are not yet finished. She answers that he has come too late: she has already eaten from the hearth of Yomi — yet she agrees to consult the deities there.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.uncertaintyNote: 之后的逃离情节可参看本库“黄泉中的八雷神”故事。

beats.textZh: 伊邪那岐回来后在水中洗净自己，身上不断化生出神。最后，他洗左眼时生出天照大神，洗右眼时生出月读，洗鼻子时生出须佐之男。
beats.textEn: Back from Yomi, Izanagi bathes to purify himself, and deities are born as he washes. Last of all, washing his left eye brings forth Amaterasu, his right eye Tsukuyomi, and his nose Susanoo.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 张伯伦译本第十节（kj017）及译注。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 三神的通行名称来自译者注释。

facts.textZh: 火之迦具土神是伊邪那美的孩子。
facts.textEn: Izanami gives birth to the Deity-of-Fire.
facts.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)

deityStoryCards.name: Honoikazuchi
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》黄泉段八雷神之一。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: One of the eight thunder kami in the Kojiki Yomi episode.

beats.textZh: 学术神名索引把八位雷神定位到《古事记》上卷的黄泉段落，并说他们出现在伊邪那美身上。
beats.textEn: The scholarly divine-name index locates the eight thunder kami in the Yomi episode of the upper Kojiki scroll and places them on Izanami.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 只采用公开学术索引范围。

beats.textZh: 数据库为大雷、火雷、黑雷、拆雷、若雷、土雷、鸣雷与伏雷分别建档，不把八名压成一个泛称。
beats.textEn: The database keeps Ooikazuchi, Honoikazuchi, Kuroikazuchi, Sakuikazuchi, Wakaikazuchi, Tsuchiikazuchi, Naruikazuchi, and Fusuikazuchi as separate records rather than one generic name.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 部分名称的精细语义仍待校勘。

beats.textZh: 鸣雷、若雷等相近名称在后世神社或地方传统中可能出现，但系统不会仅凭名字相似就认定为《古事记》中的同一神。
beats.textEn: Similar names such as Naruikazuchi or Wakaikazuchi may occur in later shrine or local traditions, but name similarity alone does not establish identity with the Kojiki figures.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 身份关系保留为争议或未知。

facts.textZh: 火雷属于《古事记》八雷神。
facts.textEn: Honoikazuchi is indexed as one of the Kojiki eight thunder kami.

deityStoryCards.name: Honoikazuchi (Otokuni tradition)
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 学术条目所述乙训郡火雷神／红箭谱系人物；不与《古事记》黄泉八雷中的火雷自动合并。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Honoikazuchi of the Otokuni red-arrow genealogy; not automatically merged with the Kojiki Yomi thunder kami.

beats.headingEn: A fragment, not the complete work
beats.textZh: 资料来自《山城国风土记》逸文的学术说明；原书没有完整保存，因此系统不重建一部想象中的完整《风土记》。

beats.textEn: Similar names such as Naruikazuchi or Wakaikazuchi may occur in later shrine or local traditions, but name similarity alone does not establish identity with the Kojiki figures.

facts.textZh: 若雷属于《古事记》八雷神。

beats.textZh: 伊邪那岐从黄泉回来，在河里洗去污秽。他洗左眼时，生出了天照大神；洗右眼时，生出了月读；洗鼻子时，生出了建速须佐之男。伊邪那岐非常欢喜，说：我生了许多孩子，最后得到了三个尊贵的孩子。他摘下颈上的玉串，摇得叮当作响，交给天照大神，命她统治高天原；又命月读统治夜之国；命须佐之男统治大海。三位神各自领受了父亲的命令，去治理分给自己的地方——只有一位没有去。
beats.textEn: Returning from Yomi, Izanagi washed away its pollution in a river. As he washed his left eye, Amaterasu was born; as he washed his right eye, Tsukuyomi; as he washed his nose, Takehaya-Susanoo. Rejoicing that at the end of his begetting he had gained three illustrious children, Izanagi took off his necklace of jewels, shook it so that it jingled, and gave it to Amaterasu, charging her to rule the Plain of High Heaven. He charged Tsukuyomi with the dominion of the night, and Susanoo with the plain of the sea. Each went to rule as charged — all but one.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十一节。

beats.headingEn: The god who wept the mountains dry
beats.textZh: 须佐之男不肯去治理大海。他一直哭，哭到胡子长了八拳那么长垂到胸前，还在哭。他哭得青山枯萎，河流和大海全都干涸。于是恶神的声音像五月的苍蝇一样到处嗡嗡作响，各种灾祸一齐发生。伊邪那岐问他：你为什么不治理我交给你的地方，却在这里哭个不停？须佐之男回答：我哭，是因为想去母亲所在的根之坚洲国。伊邪那岐大怒，说：既然如此，你就不许再住在这个国家！就把他赶走了。
beats.textEn: Susanoo would not rule the sea. He wept and howled until his beard, eight hands long, reached down over his breast. His weeping withered the green mountains and dried up all the rivers and seas, so that the voices of evil deities swarmed like summer flies and every kind of calamity arose. Izanagi asked why he wept instead of ruling the land entrusted to him. Susanoo answered that he wept because he wished to go to his mother's land, the Nether Distant Land. In great anger Izanagi said that he should not dwell in this land, and expelled him.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十二节。

beats.textZh: 须佐之男说：那么我先去向姐姐天照大神告别，然后再走。他向天上走去，山川都震动起来，大地都摇晃了。天照大神听到动静，大吃一惊，说：我弟弟上来，一定没安好心，他是想夺走我的国家。她立刻解开头发，绾成男子的发髻，在发髻上、发鬘上和左右手腕上都缠上长长的勾玉串，背上装着一千支箭的箭囊，胸前挂着装着五百支箭的箭囊，手臂上戴着护腕，挥舞着弓。她用力踏地，双腿陷到大腿那么深，把泥土像雪花一样踢散，威风凛凛地站着等他，大声问：你上来做什么？
beats.textEn: Susanoo said he would first take leave of his elder sister Amaterasu. As he went up to Heaven the mountains and rivers shook and every land quaked. Amaterasu, alarmed, said her brother could only be coming to take her land. She undid her hair and bound it up in the manner of a man, wound strings of curved jewels on her bunches of hair, her head-dress and both arms, slung on her back a quiver of a thousand arrows and at her side a quiver of five hundred, put on an elbow-pad and brandished her bow. She stamped till her legs sank into the hard earth to the thighs, kicked the soil about like rotten snow, and stood waiting to demand why he had come.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十三节。

beats.headingEn: The oath by the Tranquil River
beats.textZh: 须佐之男说：我没有坏心。父亲问我为什么哭，我说想去母亲的国家，父亲就把我赶走了。我只是来向你告别的。天照大神问：怎么证明你的心是清白的？须佐之男说：我们各自立誓生孩子吧。两人隔着天安河站定。天照大神先拿过须佐之男佩带的十拳剑，把它折成三段，在天之真名井里涮得叮当作响，放进嘴里嚼碎，吹出的气雾中生出了三位女神。接着须佐之男拿过天照大神缠在头发和手臂上的勾玉串，同样在井里涮洗、嚼碎、吹气，从雾气中生出了五位男神。
beats.textEn: Susanoo replied that he had no evil intent: his father had expelled him and he had only come to say farewell. Asked how he could prove the purity of his heart, he proposed that each should swear and produce children. Standing on either side of the Tranquil River of Heaven, Amaterasu first took his ten-grasp sabre, broke it into three, rinsed the pieces jingling in the True-Pool-Well of Heaven, crunched them and blew out a misty breath, from which three goddesses were born. Then Susanoo took the strings of curved jewels from her hair and arms, rinsed, crunched and blew in the same way, and five male deities were born.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十三节。

beats.textZh: 天照大神宣布：后来生的五位男神，是从我的东西里生出来的，所以是我的孩子；先生的三位女神，是从你的东西里生出来的，所以是你的孩子。须佐之男却说：因为我的心是清白的，所以我生出了温柔的女孩子。这样说来，当然是我赢了。他自以为得胜，得意忘形起来。（这五位男神中的长子，后来成了天皇家的祖先；三位女神则成为宗像大社供奉的神。）
beats.textEn: Amaterasu declared that the five male deities, born from her jewels, were her children, and the three goddesses, born from his sabre, were his. But Susanoo said that because his heart was pure he had begotten gentle maidens, and so of course he had won. Puffed up with his victory, he grew reckless. (The eldest of the five male deities becomes, later in the Kojiki, the ancestor of the imperial line; the three goddesses are those worshipped at Munakata.)
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十四节。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 括号里关于皇室祖先与宗像三女神的说明见于《古事记》的同一段落及后文，属于文本自身的谱系说明。

beats.headingEn: Riot in the Plain of High Heaven
beats.textZh: 仗着这场“胜利”，须佐之男在高天原胡作非为。他踏坏天照大神水田的田埂，填平灌溉的水沟，又在她品尝新谷的神殿里撒下粪便。天照大神却替他辩解：那像粪便的东西，是我弟弟喝醉了吐出来的；他填平水沟、踏坏田埂，是舍不得那些土地白白空着。可须佐之男的恶行不但没有停止，反而更加厉害。有一天，天照大神正坐在神圣的织殿里，让织女们为众神织造衣裳。须佐之男在织殿的屋顶上捅开一个洞，把一匹从尾巴倒着剥了皮的天之斑马扔了进去。织女吓得跳起来，被梭子刺中下身，就这样死了。
beats.textEn: On the strength of his victory Susanoo ran riot. He broke down the divisions of Amaterasu's rice fields, filled in the ditches, and strewed excrement in the palace where she tasted the first fruits. Amaterasu excused him: what looked like excrement was what her brother had vomited when drunk, and he had filled the ditches and broken the ridges only because he grudged the land lying idle. But his wickedness grew worse. While Amaterasu sat in her sacred weaving hall seeing to the weaving of the deities' garments, he broke a hole in the roof and flung down a heavenly piebald horse flayed backwards; a heavenly weaving maiden, startled, struck herself with her shuttle and died.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十五节。

beats.textZh: 天照大神看见这一切，感到害怕，就打开天之岩户——天上的岩石屋子的门——走了进去，把门牢牢关上，隐居起来。于是整个高天原一片黑暗，下面的苇原中国也一片黑暗，永远的黑夜笼罩了一切。在这片黑暗里，无数恶神的声音像五月的苍蝇一样到处嗡嗡作响，各种各样的灾祸接连发生。《古事记》对这场灾难只写了寥寥几句，却是神代故事的一个大转折：天照大神是照耀天地的女神，她一躲起来，天上和人间就没有了白天，众神的世界也失去了秩序。接下来的一整段，讲的都是众神如何同心协力，想办法把她请出来。
beats.textEn: Terrified at the sight, Amaterasu opened the door of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling, went in, made it fast and hid herself. Then the whole Plain of High Heaven was dark, and the Central Land of Reed-Plains below was dark too: eternal night prevailed. In that darkness the voices of the myriad deities swarmed like summer flies, and every kind of calamity arose.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

beats.textZh: 八百万位神聚集在天安河的河滩上开会商议，请高御产巢日神的儿子思金神想办法。依照他的计划，众神先把常世的长鸣鸟聚在一起，让它们一齐啼叫。又从天安河上游取来坚硬的岩石，从天上的金山取来铁，请来锻冶师天津麻罗，命伊斯许理度卖命造一面镜子，命玉祖命做一串长长的、有五百颗勾玉的玉串。他们又请天儿屋命和布刀玉命，从天香山上取来一头雄鹿完整的肩胛骨，用天香山上的桦树皮烧它，进行占卜。
beats.textEn: The eight hundred myriad deities assembled in a divine assembly in the bed of the Tranquil River of Heaven and bade Omoikane, child of Takami-musubi, think of a plan. They gathered the long-singing birds of eternal night and made them sing. They took hard rocks from the river-bed and iron from the Heavenly Metal-Mountains, called the smith Amatsumara, and charged Ishikoridome to make a mirror and Tamanoya to make a long string of five hundred curved jewels. They summoned Ame-no-Koyane and Futotama to pull out the whole shoulder-blade of a true stag of Mount Kagu and perform divination with cherry-bark from the same mountain.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

beats.headingEn: The sakaki tree hung with treasures
beats.textZh: 众神把天香山上一棵长满枝叶的真杨桐树连根拔起，在上面的枝条上挂起那串五百颗勾玉，在中间的枝条上挂起那面八咫镜，在下面的枝条上挂起白色和青色的布帛。布刀玉命双手捧着这棵树，作为隆重的供品；天儿屋命念诵庄严的祝词。天手力男神则悄悄藏在岩户门边，等待时机。这些东西在后世都有了特别的意义：镜子和勾玉与后来从大蛇尾中得到的草薙剑，被看作代代相传的三件神圣宝物；注连绳、杨桐枝和祝词，至今仍是神社祭祀中常见的东西。不过在这个故事里，它们只有一个用处——把躲起来的女神请出来。
beats.textEn: They uprooted a five-hundred-branched true sakaki tree from Mount Kagu of Heaven. On its upper branches they hung the long string of five hundred curved jewels; on its middle branches the large mirror; on its lower branches pendant offerings of white and blue cloth. Futotama held these as grand offerings, Ame-no-Koyane recited a solemn liturgy, and Ame-no-Tajikarao stood hidden beside the door.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

beats.textZh: 天宇受卖命用天香山的日影蔓束起衣袖，用真拆葛做成头饰，手里握着一束天香山的竹叶，在天之岩户前倒扣一只木桶，在上面用力踏脚，踏得咚咚作响。她跳着跳着，神灵附了体，露出了胸脯，把裙带一直推到了下身。整个高天原都震动起来，八百万位神一齐哈哈大笑。这是整个神话里最热闹、也最奇特的一幕：漆黑一片的天上，众神围着紧闭的岩户，看着一位女神在倒扣的木桶上又踏又跳，笑声震动了天地。后世把天宇受卖命尊为舞蹈与艺能之神，神乐的起源也常被追溯到这一段。
beats.textEn: Ame-no-Uzume bound up her sleeves with heavenly clubmoss from Mount Kagu, made a head-dress of spindle-tree, took in her hand a bundle of bamboo grass from Mount Kagu, and laid an upturned tub before the door of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling, stamping on it until it resounded. Becoming divinely possessed, she bared her breasts and pushed her skirt-string down to her private parts. The Plain of High Heaven shook, and the eight hundred myriad deities laughed together.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

beats.textZh: 天照大神觉得奇怪，把岩户的门稍稍打开一条缝，在里面问：我藏了起来，以为高天原会一片黑暗，苇原中国也会一片黑暗，为什么天宇受卖命还在跳舞，八百万位神都在大笑？天宇受卖命回答：因为这里来了一位比您更尊贵的神，所以我们高兴地跳舞欢笑。就在她说话的时候，天儿屋命和布刀玉命把镜子推到天照大神面前。天照大神看到镜中的光，越发惊奇，一点一点地走出门来想看个究竟。藏在门边的天手力男神一把握住她的手，把她拉了出来。布刀玉命立刻在她身后拉起一根注连绳，说：您不能再回到里面去了！天照大神一出来，高天原和苇原中国自然又恢复了光明。
beats.textEn: Amaterasu, wondering, opened the door a crack and asked why, when she had thought Heaven and the Central Land would be dark, Ame-no-Uzume danced and all the deities laughed. Uzume answered that they rejoiced because there was a deity more illustrious than she. While she spoke, Ame-no-Koyane and Futotama pushed the mirror forward to show it to Amaterasu, who, more and more astonished, came gradually out to gaze. Tajikarao, hidden beside the door, took her hand and drew her out, and Futotama stretched a bottom-tied rope behind her, saying she must not go back further in than this. As she came forth, Heaven and the Central Land were lit again.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十六节。

beats.headingEn: Expulsion and the origin of grain
beats.textZh: 八百万位神一起商议，罚须佐之男交出一千桌赎罪的供品，剪掉他的胡子，拔掉他手指和脚趾的指甲，把他赶出了高天原。在路上，须佐之男向大宜都比卖讨要食物。大宜都比卖从鼻子、嘴巴和臀部取出各种美味，做成佳肴献给他。须佐之男偷偷看见了，以为她拿污秽的东西给他吃，就把她杀了。从被杀的女神身上长出了各种东西：头上生出蚕，两只眼睛里生出稻种，两只耳朵里生出粟，鼻子里生出小豆，阴部生出麦，臀部生出大豆。神产巢日神让人把这些收起来，当作种子。
beats.textEn: The eight hundred myriad deities took counsel together, fined Susanoo a thousand tables of offerings, cut off his beard and pulled out his finger- and toe-nails, and drove him out with a divine expulsion. Then he asked food of Ōgetsuhime, who took dainties from her nose, mouth and hindquarters and offered them to him. Watching, he thought she was offering him filth, and killed her. From her body things were born: silkworms from her head, rice-seeds from her eyes, millet from her ears, small beans from her nose, barley from her genitals and soy beans from her hindquarters. Kami-musubi had them taken and used as seeds.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十七节。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 《日本书纪》里杀死食物女神的是月读，对象叫保食神；本篇只讲《古事记》的版本。

beats.textZh: 须佐之男被赶出天界，降落到出云国肥河上游一个叫鸟发的地方。这时他看见河上漂下来一双筷子，心想上游一定有人住，就沿着河往上走。果然遇见一位老人和一位老妇人，两人中间夹着一位少女，正在哭泣。老人说：我是这里的国神大山津见神的儿子，名叫足名椎，妻子叫手名椎，女儿叫栉名田比卖。我们原本有八个女儿，可是高志的八岐大蛇每年都来，吃掉一个。现在又到了它来的时候，所以我们在哭。须佐之男问那条蛇长什么样。老人说：它的眼睛像红色的酸浆果，一个身子上长着八个头、八条尾巴，身上长满了苔藓、桧树和杉树，身长横跨八道山谷、八座山峰，看它的肚子，总是血淋淋地溃烂着。
beats.textEn: Expelled, Susanoo descended to Torikami at the head of the river Hi in Izumo. Seeing chopsticks floating down, he knew people lived upstream and went up the river, where he found an old man and an old woman weeping with a maiden between them. The old man said he was Ashinazuchi, son of the great mountain deity, his wife was Tenazuchi and their daughter Kushinadahime. They had had eight daughters, but the eight-forked serpent of Koshi came every year and devoured one, and now it was time for it to come again. Its eyes, he said, were like red winter-cherries; it had one body with eight heads and eight tails; moss, cypress and cryptomeria grew on its body; its length spanned eight valleys and eight hills; and its belly was always bloody and inflamed.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十八节。

beats.headingEn: Eight vats of liquor and the Kusanagi sword
beats.textZh: 须佐之男说：我是天照大神的弟弟，刚从天上下来。你们愿意把女儿嫁给我吗？老夫妇恭恭敬敬地答应了。须佐之男把少女变成一把密齿的梳子，插在自己的发髻上，然后吩咐老夫妇：酿造八次反复酿成的烈酒，再围一道篱笆，篱笆上开八个门，每个门口搭一个台子，每个台子上放一只酒槽，槽里都盛满烈酒。一切准备好后，八岐大蛇果然来了，它把八个头分别伸进八只酒槽里，大口喝酒，喝醉了就趴下睡着了。须佐之男拔出佩带的十拳剑，把大蛇砍成碎块，肥河里流的全成了血。他砍到大蛇中间的那条尾巴时，剑刃崩了个缺口。他觉得奇怪，用剑尖剖开尾巴一看，里面有一把锋利的大刀。他认为这是不同寻常的宝物，就把它献给了天照大神——这就是草薙剑。
beats.textEn: Susanoo revealed that he was the elder brother of Amaterasu, just descended from Heaven, and asked for the maiden; the old couple respectfully agreed. He turned her into a close-toothed comb and stuck it in his hair. Then he told them to brew eightfold-refined liquor, build a fence with eight gates, and at each gate set a platform with a vat full of the liquor. The serpent came as foretold, dipped a head into each vat and drank, then lay down drunk and slept. Susanoo drew his ten-grasp sabre and cut the serpent to pieces, so that the river Hi ran with blood. When he cut its middle tail, the edge of his sabre broke; wondering, he split the tail open with its point and found a great sword. Thinking it a strange thing, he presented it to Amaterasu — the Herb-Quelling sword, Kusanagi.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十八节。
beats.uncertaintyNote: “草薙”这个名字在《古事记》的这一段只作注明；名称由来的故事（日本武尊割草）在后文另有讲述。

beats.headingZh: 须贺的宫殿与八云之歌
beats.headingEn: The palace of Suga and the song of eight clouds
beats.textZh: 之后，须佐之男在出云国寻找建造宫殿的地方。他来到须贺这个地方，说：我来到这里，心里清清爽爽的。就在那里建起了宫殿，所以那地方至今叫做须贺。他在那里建宫时，有云从地上升起，他便作了一首歌：八云立，出云八重垣，为了让妻子住进来，我筑起八重垣——啊，那八重垣！这被认为是日本最早的和歌。他把栉名田比卖的父亲足名椎叫来，任命他做宫殿的长官，并赐给他一个名字：稻田宫主须贺之八耳神。
beats.textEn: Then Susanoo looked for a place in Izumo to build a palace. Arriving at Suga he said that his heart was refreshed, and he built his palace there — which is why the place is still called Suga. As he built it, clouds rose up, and he made a song: Eight clouds arise. The eightfold fence of Izumo makes an eightfold fence for the spouses to retire within. Oh, that eightfold fence! He called Ashinazuchi and made him master of the palace, giving him the name Inada-no-Miyanushi-Suga-no-Yatsumimi.
beats.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
beats.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十九节。
beats.uncertaintyNote: “日本最早的和歌”是后世（如《古今和歌集》序）的说法，不是《古事记》本文的断言。

facts.textZh: 须佐之男是伊邪那岐的孩子。
facts.textEn: The deity born when Izanagi washes his nose is rendered by Chamberlain as His Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness.
facts.sourceTitle: The Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters (tr. Basil Hall Chamberlain)
facts.sourceLocation: Sect. X, Purification of the August Person (kj017)

facts.textZh: 须佐之男击败了八岐大蛇。
facts.textEn: The Kokugakuin academic entry summarizes Susanoo defeating Yamata no Orochi.

facts.textZh: 须佐之男出现在“从八岐大蛇体内发现草薙剑”之中。
facts.textEn: Susanoo is the actor who defeats the serpent and finds the sword in the academic summary.

deityStoryCards.name: Fujin
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 日本风神入口；本批仅登记宗达屏风中的后世图像见证。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Japanese wind-deity entry currently limited to the later Sotatsu screen witness.

beats.textZh: 俵屋宗达《风神雷神图屏风》描绘了风神。
beats.textEn: Kyoto National Museum identifies the paired composition as Wind God and Thunder God, providing a seventeenth-century Fujin visual witness.
beats.sourceTitle: Wind God and Thunder God screens
beats.sourceLocation: Official catalogue or public institutional description

beats.textZh: 尾形光琳《风神雷神图屏风》A-11189-1描绘了风神。
beats.textEn: The Kōrin screens depict the Wind God.
beats.sourceTitle: Wind God and Thunder God by Ogata Kōrin

deityStoryCards.name: Naruikazuchi
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》黄泉段八雷神之一；与后世同名神社传统的关系未知。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: One of the Kojiki eight thunder kami; identity with later similarly named shrine traditions is unknown.

beats.textZh: 学术神名索引把八位雷神定位到《古事记》上卷的黄泉段落，并说他们出现在伊邪那美身上。
beats.textEn: The scholarly divine-name index locates the eight thunder kami in the Yomi episode of the upper Kojiki scroll and places them on Izanami.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 只采用公开学术索引范围。

beats.textZh: 数据库为大雷、火雷、黑雷、拆雷、若雷、土雷、鸣雷与伏雷分别建档，不把八名压成一个泛称。
beats.textEn: The database keeps Ooikazuchi, Honoikazuchi, Kuroikazuchi, Sakuikazuchi, Wakaikazuchi, Tsuchiikazuchi, Naruikazuchi, and Fusuikazuchi as separate records rather than one generic name.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 部分名称的精细语义仍待校勘。

beats.textZh: 鸣雷、若雷等相近名称在后世神社或地方传统中可能出现，但系统不会仅凭名字相似就认定为《古事记》中的同一神。
beats.textEn: Similar names such as Naruikazuchi or Wakaikazuchi may occur in later shrine or local traditions, but name similarity alone does not establish identity with the Kojiki figures.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 身份关系保留为争议或未知。

deityStoryCards.name: Kuroikazuchi
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》黄泉段八雷神之一。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: One of the eight thunder kami in the Kojiki Yomi episode.

beats.textZh: 学术神名索引把八位雷神定位到《古事记》上卷的黄泉段落，并说他们出现在伊邪那美身上。
beats.textEn: The scholarly divine-name index locates the eight thunder kami in the Yomi episode of the upper Kojiki scroll and places them on Izanami.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 只采用公开学术索引范围。

beats.textZh: 数据库为大雷、火雷、黑雷、拆雷、若雷、土雷、鸣雷与伏雷分别建档，不把八名压成一个泛称。
beats.textEn: The database keeps Ooikazuchi, Honoikazuchi, Kuroikazuchi, Sakuikazuchi, Wakaikazuchi, Tsuchiikazuchi, Naruikazuchi, and Fusuikazuchi as separate records rather than one generic name.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 部分名称的精细语义仍待校勘。

beats.textZh: 鸣雷、若雷等相近名称在后世神社或地方传统中可能出现，但系统不会仅凭名字相似就认定为《古事记》中的同一神。
beats.textEn: Similar names such as Naruikazuchi or Wakaikazuchi may occur in later shrine or local traditions, but name similarity alone does not establish identity with the Kojiki figures.

facts.textZh: 黑雷属于《古事记》八雷神。
facts.textEn: Kuroikazuchi is indexed as one of the Kojiki eight thunder kami.

deityStoryCards.name: Ranginui
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 天父；与帕帕图阿努库从黑暗中出现，孩子们把他们分开，光明由此进入世界（Te Ara）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Sky father who, with Papatūānuku, emerges from darkness; their children separate them and let in the light (Te Ara).

beats.textZh: Te Ara 写道：在毛利传统中，创世的核心行动是天与地的分离。故事从黑暗与虚无开始，天父兰吉努伊与地母帕帕图阿努库从中出现。起初天地紧紧相连，他们的孩子就出生在两者之间。
beats.textEn: Te Ara writes that in Māori tradition the central act of creation is the separation of earth and sky. The story begins in darkness and nothingness, from which Ranginui the sky father and Papatūānuku the earth mother emerge. At first earth and sky are joined, and their children are born between them.
beats.sourceLocation: Page 1 — Common threads in creation stories
beats.evidenceNote: Te Ara“毛利创世传统”第1页。

beats.textZh: 孩子们决定把父母分开。天与地一旦分离，光就照进了世界——从黑暗走向光明，正是由孩子们的这一行动完成的。
beats.textEn: The children decide to separate their parents. Once earth and sky are apart, light enters the world: the move from darkness to light is achieved by the children's act.
beats.sourceLocation: Page 1 — Common threads in creation stories
beats.uncertaintyNote: Te Ara 说明：在部分部族版本中，塔内在分开天地时起重要作用；本站不选定某一部族的说法。

beats.textZh: 分离之后，孩子们成为自然各部分的神（atua）：塔内是森林之神，塔加罗阿是海洋之神，还有地震之神鲁奥莫科、风与天气之神塔维里马特阿。把这些神编进同一个谱系，是毛利人解释自然世界的传统方式。
beats.textEn: After the separation the children become atua of different parts of nature: Tāne of the forests, Tangaroa of the sea, Rūaumoko of earthquakes, Tāwhirimātea of winds and weather. Weaving these atua into one genealogy is the traditional Māori way of explaining the natural world.
beats.sourceLocation: Page 1 — Common threads in creation stories
beats.uncertaintyNote: 鲁奥莫科与塔维里马特阿尚未建立独立实体。

beats.textZh: Te Ara 也提醒，各部族的创世故事差异很大，特别是关于至高存在的角色。这里只讲公开页面所总结的共同线索，具名部族的版本须经相应权威授权。
beats.textEn: Te Ara also cautions that tribal versions vary considerably, especially on the role of a supreme being. This retelling covers only the common threads the public page summarizes; named iwi versions require permission from the appropriate authority.
beats.sourceLocation: Page 1 — Common threads in creation stories

deityStoryCards.name: Papatūānuku
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 地母；与兰吉努伊相连，直到孩子们把他们分开（Te Ara 对共同线索的概述）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Earth mother joined to Ranginui until their children part them (Te Ara's summary of common threads).

beats.textZh: Te Ara 写道：在毛利传统中，创世的核心行动是天与地的分离。故事从黑暗与虚无开始，天父兰吉努伊与地母帕帕图阿努库从中出现。起初天地紧紧相连，他们的孩子就出生在两者之间。
beats.textEn: Te Ara writes that in Māori tradition the central act of creation is the separation of earth and sky. The story begins in darkness and nothingness, from which Ranginui the sky father and Papatūānuku the earth mother emerge. At first earth and sky are joined, and their children are born between them.
beats.sourceLocation: Page 1 — Common threads in creation stories
beats.evidenceNote: Te Ara“毛利创世传统”第1页。

beats.textZh: 孩子们决定把父母分开。天与地一旦分离，光就照进了世界——从黑暗走向光明，正是由孩子们的这一行动完成的。
beats.textEn: The children decide to separate their parents. Once earth and sky are apart, light enters the world: the move from darkness to light is achieved by the children's act.
beats.sourceLocation: Page 1 — Common threads in creation stories
beats.uncertaintyNote: Te Ara 说明：在部分部族版本中，塔内在分开天地时起重要作用；本站不选定某一部族的说法。

beats.textZh: 分离之后，孩子们成为自然各部分的神（atua）：塔内是森林之神，塔加罗阿是海洋之神，还有地震之神鲁奥莫科、风与天气之神塔维里马特阿。把这些神编进同一个谱系，是毛利人解释自然世界的传统方式。
beats.textEn: After the separation the children become atua of different parts of nature: Tāne of the forests, Tangaroa of the sea, Rūaumoko of earthquakes, Tāwhirimātea of winds and weather. Weaving these atua into one genealogy is the traditional Māori way of explaining the natural world.
beats.sourceLocation: Page 1 — Common threads in creation stories
beats.uncertaintyNote: 鲁奥莫科与塔维里马特阿尚未建立独立实体。

beats.textZh: Te Ara 也提醒，各部族的创世故事差异很大，特别是关于至高存在的角色。这里只讲公开页面所总结的共同线索，具名部族的版本须经相应权威授权。

deityStoryCards.name: Brigid
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《第二次马格图雷德之战》中达格达之女布里格，为儿子鲁阿丹哀哭，是爱尔兰第一次听到的哀歌。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Bríg, daughter of the Dagda in Cath Maige Tuired, whose keening for her son Rúadán is the first heard in Ireland.

beats.textZh: 达努神族带来了四件宝物，其中一件是从穆里亚斯城带来的达格达的大锅：凡是围着它吃饭的人，从没有一个是不饱足地离开的。
beats.textEn: The Túatha Dé Danann brought four treasures. One was the Dagda's cauldron from the city of Murias: no company that ate from it ever went away unsatisfied.
beats.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)

beats.headingEn: The master of all arts at Tara
beats.textZh: 鲁格来到塔拉的大门前，守门人问他会什么手艺。他报出一门又一门，而宫里每门手艺都已有人；最后他问：有没有一个人能同时精通所有这些？于是他以“百艺之主”的身份被请了进去。
beats.textEn: Lug comes to the door of Tara, and the doorkeeper asks what art he brings. He names one after another, and each already has a master within — until he asks whether anyone there has all of them at once. So he is admitted as the Samildánach, master of all arts.
beats.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)

beats.textZh: 萨温节前后，达格达在乌恩辛河边遇见一个女人正在洗东西，一只脚踩在南岸，一只脚踩在北岸。她就是莫莉甘。两人结合之后，她告诉达格达弗魔族将在哪里登陆，并许诺要取弗魔王因德赫的心血。
beats.textEn: Around Samain the Dagda meets a woman washing at the river Unshin, one foot on the southern bank and one on the northern. She is the Morrígan. After they unite she tells him where the Fomoire will land and promises to take the heart's blood of their king Indech.
beats.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)

beats.textZh: 布里格是达格达的女儿，她和布雷斯的儿子鲁阿丹被派去刺杀铁匠戈伊布纽，却被戈伊布纽杀死。布里格赶来为儿子哀哭，先是尖声恸哭，最后低声啜泣——这是爱尔兰第一次听到哀歌与哭泣。
beats.textEn: Rúadán, son of Bres and of Bríg the Dagda's daughter, is sent to kill the smith Goibniu and is killed instead. Bríg comes and keens for her son, shrieking first and weeping at the end — the first time keening and weeping were heard in Ireland.
beats.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)
beats.uncertaintyNote: 文本写作 Bríg；与数据库中“布里吉德”实体的对应依学界通行用法。

beats.textZh: 弗魔族勇士巴洛尔有一只毒眼，只在战场上睁开，要四个人用把手才能抬起眼皮。鲁格用投石一击，石头把那只眼睛从巴洛尔脑后打了出去，结果看见它的反而是他自己的军队。
beats.textEn: The Fomorian champion Balor has a deadly eye, opened only on the battlefield, its lid lifted by four men with a handle. Lug casts a sling stone that drives the eye out through the back of Balor's head, so that it is his own host that looks upon it.
beats.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)

beats.textZh: 战斗结束后，恩玛斯的女儿莫莉甘把这场大胜宣告给爱尔兰的王者高地、神丘里的众灵、各条大河与河口，然后又说出关于未来的预言。
beats.textEn: When the battle is won, the Morrígan, daughter of Ernmas, proclaims the great victory to the royal heights of Ireland, its síd-hosts, its chief waters and river-mouths — and then speaks prophecy.
beats.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)
beats.uncertaintyNote: 预言诗的内容未逐句建模。

facts.textZh: 布里吉德是达格达的孩子。
facts.textEn: Rúadán is the son of Bres and of Bríg, the Dagda's daughter.
facts.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)
facts.sourceLocation: §123 (Rúadán mac Bresi & Bríghi ingene in Dagdai)

beats.textZh: 布里格是达格达的女儿，她和布雷斯的儿子鲁阿丹被派去刺杀铁匠戈伊布纽，却被戈伊布纽杀死。布里格赶来为儿子哀哭，先是尖声恸哭，最后低声啜泣——这是爱尔兰第一次听到哀歌与哭泣。
beats.textEn: Rúadán, son of Bres and of Bríg the Dagda's daughter, is sent to kill the smith Goibniu and is killed instead. Bríg comes and keens for her son, shrieking first and weeping at the end — the first time keening and weeping were heard in Ireland.
beats.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)
beats.uncertaintyNote: 文本写作 Bríg；与数据库中“布里吉德”实体的对应依学界通行用法。

beats.textZh: 弗魔族勇士巴洛尔有一只毒眼，只在战场上睁开，要四个人用把手才能抬起眼皮。鲁格用投石一击，石头把那只眼睛从巴洛尔脑后打了出去，结果看见它的反而是他自己的军队。
beats.textEn: The Fomorian champion Balor has a deadly eye, opened only on the battlefield, its lid lifted by four men with a handle. Lug casts a sling stone that drives the eye out through the back of Balor's head, so that it is his own host that looks upon it.
beats.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)

beats.textZh: 战斗结束后，恩玛斯的女儿莫莉甘把这场大胜宣告给爱尔兰的王者高地、神丘里的众灵、各条大河与河口，然后又说出关于未来的预言。
beats.textEn: When the battle is won, the Morrígan, daughter of Ernmas, proclaims the great victory to the royal heights of Ireland, its síd-hosts, its chief waters and river-mouths — and then speaks prophecy.
beats.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)
beats.uncertaintyNote: 预言诗的内容未逐句建模。

facts.textZh: 布里吉德是达格达的孩子。
facts.textEn: Rúadán is the son of Bres and of Bríg, the Dagda's daughter.
facts.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)
facts.sourceLocation: §123 (Rúadán mac Bresi & Bríghi ingene in Dagdai)

facts.textZh: 达格达出现在“第二次马格图雷德之战”之中。
facts.textEn: The Dagda takes part in the preparations and the battle.
facts.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)

deityStoryCards.name: Lugh
deityStoryCards.hookZh: “百艺之主”，在《第二次马格图雷德之战》中用投石击杀巴洛尔。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: The Samildánach, master of all arts, who in Cath Maige Tuired kills Balor with a sling stone.

beats.textZh: 达努神族带来了四件宝物，其中一件是从穆里亚斯城带来的达格达的大锅：凡是围着它吃饭的人，从没有一个是不饱足地离开的。
beats.textEn: The Túatha Dé Danann brought four treasures. One was the Dagda's cauldron from the city of Murias: no company that ate from it ever went away unsatisfied.
beats.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)

beats.headingEn: The master of all arts at Tara
beats.textZh: 鲁格来到塔拉的大门前，守门人问他会什么手艺。他报出一门又一门，而宫里每门手艺都已有人；最后他问：有没有一个人能同时精通所有这些？于是他以“百艺之主”的身份被请了进去。
beats.textEn: Lug comes to the door of Tara, and the doorkeeper asks what art he brings. He names one after another, and each already has a master within — until he asks whether anyone there has all of them at once. So he is admitted as the Samildánach, master of all arts.
beats.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)

beats.textZh: 萨温节前后，达格达在乌恩辛河边遇见一个女人正在洗东西，一只脚踩在南岸，一只脚踩在北岸。她就是莫莉甘。两人结合之后，她告诉达格达弗魔族将在哪里登陆，并许诺要取弗魔王因德赫的心血。
beats.textEn: Around Samain the Dagda meets a woman washing at the river Unshin, one foot on the southern bank and one on the northern. She is the Morrígan. After they unite she tells him where the Fomoire will land and promises to take the heart's blood of their king Indech.
beats.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)

facts.textZh: 鲁格出现在“第二次马格图雷德之战”之中。
facts.textEn: Lug fights in the battle and faces Balor.
facts.sourceTitle: Cath Maige Tuired: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired (English translation)

deityStoryCards.name: Itzamna
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 年老的天神伊察姆纳（Itzamnaaj），有一个鸟形化身，在玛雅太初神话中地位重要（大都会博物馆，2022）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Aged celestial god Itzamnaaj with an avian avatar, important in Maya primordial myths (Met, 2022).

beats.textZh: 2022 年的展览按“众神的一生”展开：从婴儿、壮年到老年。其中的老年之神叫伊察姆纳（Itzamnaaj），他还有一个鸟形化身，两者在太初神话中都很重要。
beats.textEn: The 2022 exhibition followed the gods through life — infancy, prime and old age. The aged god is Itzamnaaj, who has a bird avatar; both play important roles in primordial myths.
beats.sourceTitle: Lives of the Gods: Divinity in Maya Art — exhibition announcement
beats.evidenceNote: 大都会艺术博物馆 2022 年展览说明。

beats.textZh: “Itzamnaaj”是殖民时期尤卡坦一位重要神祇的名字。博物馆提醒，古典期这位老神的名字符号该怎样读，学界还没有定论。
beats.textEn: 'Itzamnaaj' is the name of a major deity in colonial Yucatán. The museum notes that how to read the Classic-period name glyph of this elderly god is still uncertain.
beats.sourceTitle: Lives of the Gods: Divinity in Maya Art — exhibition announcement
beats.evidenceNote: 大都会艺术博物馆展览说明。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 名字读法未定，本站同时保留“伊察姆纳”与“Itzamnaaj”。

beats.textZh: 这里依据的是一份现代展览介绍，而不是古代文本。展览说伊察姆纳在太初神话中很重要，但没有在说明里讲出那些神话；本站因此不替它补写情节。
beats.textEn: This version rests on a modern exhibition text, not an ancient one. The exhibition says Itzamnaaj mattered in primordial myths but does not retell them, so the site does not fill in a plot.
beats.sourceTitle: Lives of the Gods: Divinity in Maya Art — exhibition announcement
beats.evidenceNote: 大都会艺术博物馆展览说明。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 待找到可定位的古代或殖民时期文本见证后再扩充。

deityStoryCards.name: Kukulkan
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 与奇琴伊察“库库尔坎神庙”相连的羽蛇之名；联合国教科文组织称其为图拉统治者“羽蛇”名号的玛雅译名（通行说法）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Feathered-serpent name linked to El Castillo, the 'Temple of Kukulkan' at Chichen-Itza; UNESCO reports it as the Maya rendering of a Tula ruler's Quetzalcoatl name.

beats.textZh: 奇琴伊察是尤卡坦半岛上的前西班牙时期古城，已列入世界遗产名录。联合国教科文组织的记录把卡斯蒂略金字塔列为城市北部建筑群中的主要建筑。
beats.textEn: Chichen-Itza is a pre-Hispanic city on the Yucatán peninsula, inscribed on the World Heritage List. UNESCO's record names El Castillo among the chief buildings of the city's northern group.
beats.evidenceNote: 联合国教科文组织世界遗产 483 号记录。

beats.textZh: 奇琴伊察北区最重要的建筑是卡斯蒂略金字塔，联合国教科文组织的记录说，它又被称为“库库尔坎神庙”。
beats.textEn: The chief monument of Chichen-Itza's northern group is El Castillo, which UNESCO's record says is also known as the Temple of Kukulkan.
beats.evidenceNote: 联合国教科文组织世界遗产 483 号记录。

beats.textZh: 同一记录提到一种最常见的说法：图拉之王“一芦苇·托皮尔钦·羽蛇”占领了这座城市，而“库库尔坎”正是玛雅人对“羽蛇”这个名字的翻译。
beats.textEn: The same record cites the most common version: the King of Tula, Ce Acatl Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl, took the city — and 'Kukulkan' is how the Maya translated his name.
beats.evidenceNote: 联合国教科文组织世界遗产 483 号记录。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 这是关于统治者名号的传统说法，不把玛雅与墨西加的神合并为同一实体。

deityStoryCards.name: Chaac
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 玛雅雨神，古典期象形文字写作 Chahk；大都会博物馆的陶盘上他半身浸在水中。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Maya rain god, written Chahk in Classic hieroglyphs; shown waist-deep in water on a Met plate.

beats.headingEn: The rain god in the water
beats.textZh: 这只古典期的玛雅陶盘上，雨神恰克半身浸在水波纹里，四周写着表示“海”的象形文字。
beats.textEn: On this Classic Maya plate the rain god Chahk stands waist-deep in watery motifs, surrounded by hieroglyphs for 'sea'.
beats.evidenceNote: 大都会艺术博物馆 2021.320 号。

beats.textZh: 在古典期的玛雅象形文字里，这位雨神的名字写作 Chahk；人们常写的“恰克”就是这个名字。
beats.textEn: In Classic-period Maya hieroglyphs the rain god's name is written Chahk — the familiar 'Chaac'.
beats.evidenceNote: 大都会艺术博物馆藏品说明。

beats.textZh: 这只陶盘在 2021 年由 Mol 收藏捐赠给大都会艺术博物馆。博物馆的说明只描述画面本身，并没有讲述一个完整的雨神故事。
beats.textEn: The plate entered The Metropolitan Museum of Art in 2021 as a gift of the Mol Collection. The museum's entry describes the image itself; it does not narrate a full rain-god myth.
beats.evidenceNote: 大都会艺术博物馆藏品出处说明。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 这是物质见证，本站不补写神话情节。

facts.textZh: 恰克——职掌：rain
facts.textEn: The Met identifies Chahk as the Maya rain god.

deityStoryCards.name: Angra Mainyu
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《万迪达德》第一章中“全然是死亡”的存在，对阿胡拉·马兹达创造的每一片良地施以反创造的灾祸。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: In Videvdad 1, 'all death', who answers each good land made by Ahura Mazda with a counter-created plague.

beats.textZh: 阿胡拉·马兹达说：我所创造的良地中，第一片是雅利安瓦伊贾，在善河岱提亚旁边。
beats.textEn: Ahura Mazda says: the first of the good lands I created was Airyana Vaejah, by the good river Daitya.
beats.sourceTitle: Vendidad, Fargard 1, translated by James Darmesteter
beats.uncertaintyNote: 雅利安瓦伊贾不映射为现代坐标。

beats.headingEn: The one who is all death
beats.textZh: 随后，“全然是死亡”的安格拉·曼纽来了，他针对这片良地造出了河中之蛇和寒冬，那是恶魔们的作品。
beats.textEn: Then came Angra Mainyu, who is all death, and against it he counter-created the serpent in the river and winter, a work of the daevas.
beats.sourceTitle: Vendidad, Fargard 1, translated by James Darmesteter

beats.textZh: 名单一片接一片地继续：第二片是粟特人居住的平原，安格拉·曼纽就造出蝗虫。如此一共列出十六片良地，每一片都对应一种反创造的灾祸。
beats.textEn: The list goes on land by land: the second is the plain where the Sughdhas dwell, and Angra Mainyu makes the locust. In all, sixteen good lands are named, each answered by a counter-created plague.
beats.sourceTitle: Vendidad, Fargard 1, translated by James Darmesteter
beats.evidenceNote: 第一章第二片良地及以下。
beats.uncertaintyNote: 译者认为这是宗教地理，混合了神话之地与真实国家；只有部分地名可以确认。

facts.textZh: 安格拉·曼纽与阿胡拉·马兹达为敌。
facts.textEn: Throughout Videvdad 1 every good land made by Ahura Mazda is answered by a plague from Angra Mainyu.
facts.sourceTitle: Vendidad, Fargard 1, translated by James Darmesteter

facts.textZh: 安格拉·曼纽出现在“十六地的创造与反创造”之中。
facts.textEn: Angra Mainyu sets a counter-creation against each land.
facts.sourceTitle: Vendidad, Fargard 1, translated by James Darmesteter

deityStoryCards.name: Mithra
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《密赫尔颂》中的“广阔牧场之主”：阿胡拉·马兹达所造、与其同受崇拜，守护契约，有千耳万眼。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Lord of wide pastures in the Mihr Yasht: created by Ahura Mazda as worthy of worship as himself, guardian of the contract, with a thousand ears and ten thousand eyes.

beats.textZh: 颂歌一开头，阿胡拉·马兹达对查拉图斯特拉说：我创造广阔牧场之主密特拉时，使他与我自己一样，值得献祭、值得祈祷。
beats.textEn: The hymn opens with Ahura Mazda telling Zarathustra: when I created Mithra, lord of wide pastures, I made him as worthy of sacrifice and as worthy of prayer as myself.
beats.sourceTitle: Mihr Yasht (Yasht 10), translated by James Darmesteter

beats.textZh: 对密特拉说谎、背弃契约的恶人，会给整个国家带来死亡。所以契约绝不可背弃——不论是与信徒订立的，还是与不信者订立的。
beats.textEn: The wretch who lies to Mithra, breaking the contract, brings death upon the whole land. So the contract must never be broken, whether made with one of the faithful or with an unbeliever.
beats.sourceTitle: Mihr Yasht (Yasht 10), translated by James Darmesteter
beats.uncertaintyNote: “契约”是译者对 miθra 一词的理解，学界另有讨论。

beats.headingEn: A thousand ears, ten thousand eyes
beats.textZh: 颂歌赞美密特拉说真话，是集会中的首领；他有一千只耳朵，一万只眼睛，什么都瞒不过他。
beats.textEn: The hymn praises Mithra as truth-speaking, a chief in assemblies, with a thousand ears and ten thousand eyes — nothing escapes him.
beats.sourceTitle: Mihr Yasht (Yasht 10), translated by James Darmesteter

beats.textZh: 每天清晨，他是天上诸神中第一个越过哈拉山的，比不朽的、驾着快马的太阳还要早。
beats.textEn: Each morning he is the first of the heavenly gods to reach over Mount Hara, ahead of the undying, swift-horsed sun.
beats.sourceTitle: Mihr Yasht (Yasht 10), translated by James Darmesteter

facts.textZh: 密特拉——称号：lord of wide pastures
facts.textEn: The hymn repeatedly calls Mithra 'lord of wide pastures'.
facts.sourceTitle: Mihr Yasht (Yasht 10), translated by James Darmesteter

facts.textZh: 安格拉·曼纽与阿胡拉·马兹达为敌。
facts.textEn: Throughout Videvdad 1 every good land made by Ahura Mazda is answered by a plague from Angra Mainyu.
facts.sourceTitle: Vendidad, Fargard 1, translated by James Darmesteter

facts.textZh: DSab 三语楔形文字铭文提到阿胡拉·马兹达。
facts.textEn: DSab invokes Ahuramazda and asks for protection of Darius and his work.
facts.sourceTitle: Susa: Central Part of the Statue
facts.sourceLocation: Achemenet central part, DSab presentation and attributed translation

facts.textZh: 阿胡拉·马兹达出现在“十六地的创造与反创造”之中。
facts.textEn: Ahura Mazda makes the sixteen good lands.
facts.sourceTitle: Vendidad, Fargard 1, translated by James Darmesteter

facts.textZh: 阿胡拉·马兹达创造了雅利安瓦伊贾。
facts.textEn: Ahura Mazda says the first of the good lands he created was Airyana Vaejah, by the good river Daitya.
facts.sourceTitle: Vendidad, Fargard 1, translated by James Darmesteter

deityStoryCards.name: Olodumare
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 活态约鲁巴传统中的至高存在；在具名社区权威授权之前，本站不发布故事。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Supreme being in living Yorùbá tradition; no public story is published here until a named community authority grants scope.

boundary.textZh: 这位神祇属于活态传统。在具名社区权威授权并写明可用范围之前，本站不发布故事，也不替社区讲述。
boundary.textEn: Living tradition. Permitted: Name, civilization link and a note that no public story has been published here. Not collected: Oríkì, Ifá verses, ritual and lineage narratives without named community authorization.
boundary.authorityName: Relevant Yorùbá and diaspora custodial communities

deityStoryCards.name: Oshun
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 约鲁巴女神；联合国教科文组织记录把她与奥孙-奥索博神树林相连；活态信仰中的叙事需社区许可。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Yoruba goddess whom UNESCO's record links to the Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove; living-practice narratives require community permission.

beats.textZh: 奥舒恩——职掌：fertility
beats.textEn: UNESCO's description calls Osun a goddess of fertility.

beats.textZh: 奥舒恩在奥孙-奥索博神树林受到崇拜。
beats.textEn: UNESCO describes the Osun Sacred Grove as the abode of Osun, a Yoruba goddess of fertility, its landscape and river dotted with sanctuaries, shrines, sculptures and artworks in her honour.

boundary.textZh: 此处只使用公开记录；活态传统中的叙事、祷词与仪式须经社区授权。
boundary.textEn: Not collected without permission: Narratives, praise poetry, ritual and festival detail drawn from living practice.

deityStoryCards.name: Ogun
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 活态约鲁巴神灵；在具名社区权威授权之前，本站不发布故事。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Living Yorùbá orisha; no public story is published here until a named community authority grants scope.

boundary.textZh: 这位神祇属于活态传统。在具名社区权威授权并写明可用范围之前，本站不发布故事，也不替社区讲述。
boundary.textEn: Living tradition. Permitted: Name, civilization link and a note that no public story has been published here. Not collected: Oríkì, Ifá verses, ritual and lineage narratives without named community authorization.
boundary.authorityName: Relevant Yorùbá and diaspora custodial communities

deityStoryCards.name: Shango
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 奥约约鲁巴活态传统中的 Ṣàngó：雷、闪电、正义、王权与祖先记忆公共层；受限知识只登记访问边界，不收集秘密内容。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Sango in the living Oyo Yoruba tradition, with public thunder, justice, kingship and ancestor-memory layers; restricted knowledge is represented only by access metadata.

beats.textZh: 尚戈与奥约尚戈节相关。
beats.textEn: The annual Oyo Sango Festival is a public living-tradition expression centered on Sango.

beats.textZh: 尚戈与尚戈双斧祭仪杖相关。
beats.textEn: Museum records identify Ose Sango as a double-axe-topped sacred or devotional staff associated with Sango.

beats.textZh: 尚戈与雷相关。
beats.textEn: The community-backed UNESCO Sango Festival dossier publicly identifies Sango with thunder, lightning, justice and Oyo kingship/ancestor memory.

deityStoryCards.name: Utu
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 太阳神；吉尔伽美什向他求助，他赐下勇士为远征胡瓦瓦引路（ETCSL 1.8.1.5）。
deityStoryCards.hookEn: Sun god whom Gilgameš asks for help; he grants warriors to guide the expedition against Ḫuwawa (ETCSL 1.8.1.5).

beats.textZh: 吉尔伽美什决定动身进山。
beats.textEn: Gilgameš resolves to set off for the mountains.

beats.textZh: 恩奇都说：山是乌图管的，这件事应该先让乌图知道。
beats.textEn: Enkidu says the mountains are Utu's concern, so Utu should be told of the plan.

beats.textZh: 吉尔伽美什向乌图祈求。乌图接受他的眼泪作为礼物，赐给他七位勇士为他引路，一同去面对胡瓦瓦。
beats.textEn: Gilgameš prays to Utu, who accepts his tears as a gift and grants him seven warriors to guide him toward Ḫuwawa.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 七位勇士的具体身份描述尚未逐句建模。

beats.headingEn: From the great above to the great below
beats.textZh: 从伟大的天上，她把心思转向了伟大的地下。女神从伟大的天上，把心思转向了伟大的地下。伊南娜从伟大的天上，把心思转向了伟大的地下。我的女主人舍弃了天空，舍弃了大地，走向冥界。她舍弃了“恩”的祭司之职，舍弃了“拉加尔”的祭司之职，走向冥界。她舍弃了乌鲁克的伊安那神庙，舍弃了巴德提比拉的神庙、扎巴拉姆的吉古那神庙、阿达布的神庙、尼普尔的神庙、基什的神庙，还有阿卡德的伊乌尔马什神庙——一共七座城市的七座神庙，独自走向冥界。
beats.textEn: From the great heaven she set her mind on the great below. From the great heaven the goddess set her mind on the great below; Inana set her mind on the great below. My mistress abandoned heaven, abandoned earth, and descended to the netherworld. She abandoned the office of en and of lagar. She abandoned the E-ana in Unug, and her temples in Bad-tibira, Zabalam, Adab, Nibru and Kiš, and the E-ulmaš in Agade — seven temples in seven cities — and went down to the netherworld.

beats.textZh: 伊南娜取下七种神力，把它们收集在手中，放在手边。她头上戴着平原上的“舒古拉”王冠，额前垂着假发，脖子上挂着小粒的青金石项链，胸前佩着一对蛋形的珠子，身上裹着象征女主人身份的“帕拉”长袍，眼睛涂上一种叫作“让男人来吧，让他来吧”的眼影，胸前系着一块叫作“男人啊，来吧”的胸饰，手上戴着金指环，手里拿着青金石的量杆和测绳。就这样，她穿戴整齐，向冥界走去。
beats.textEn: Inana gathered the seven divine powers and held them in her hand. She put the šugura, the turban of the open country, on her head, a wig on her brow, small lapis lazuli beads around her neck and twin egg-shaped beads on her breast. She wrapped her body in the pala dress, the garment of ladyship, painted her eyes with the ointment called 'Let a man come, let him come', bound on the pectoral called 'Come, man, come', slipped a gold ring on her hand and held the lapis lazuli measuring rod and line.

beats.textZh: 伊南娜一边走，一边对她的大臣宁舒布尔说：我忠实的大臣，说话可靠的使者，我现在要下到冥界去。我到了冥界以后，你要在废墟中为我敲起鼓，在议会的厅堂里为我哭泣，在众神的家中为我奔走哀告；你要抓伤你的眼睛、你的嘴、你的大腿，像穷人一样只穿一件衣服。然后你独自一人，先到尼普尔的埃库尔神庙去，在恩利尔面前哭诉：父亲恩利尔，不要让你的女儿死在冥界！如果恩利尔不帮你，你就去乌尔，到南纳那里去哭诉；如果南纳也不帮你，你就去埃利都，到恩基那里去哭诉。父亲恩基，那位深知一切的神，知道生命之草、生命之水，他一定不会让我死去。
beats.textEn: As Inana went, she told her minister Ninšubur: my faithful minister, I am going down to the netherworld. When I have arrived there, make a lament for me in the ruins, beat the drum for me in the assembly, go round the houses of the gods; lacerate your eyes, mouth and thighs, dress in a single garment like a pauper. Then go alone to Enlil in the E-kur at Nibru and weep: Father Enlil, don't let your daughter be put to death in the netherworld. If Enlil does not help, go to Nanna in Urim; if Nanna does not help, go to Enki in Eridug. Father Enki, who knows the plant of life and the water of life, will surely not let me die.

beats.headingEn: At the gate of the netherworld
beats.textZh: 伊南娜来到冥界的宫殿“甘泽尔”前，用力推门，在门口大声喊道：守门人，开门！守门人，开门！内提，开门，我独自一人要进去！冥界的首席守门人内提问她：你是谁？伊南娜说：我是天上的伊南娜，要到太阳升起的地方去。内提说：你若是天上的伊南娜，要到太阳升起的地方去，为什么到这条有去无回的路上来？伊南娜说：因为我的姐姐埃列什基伽勒的丈夫、天牛古伽拉纳死了，我来参加他的葬礼宴会。内提让她等着，去向冥后埃列什基伽勒报告。埃列什基伽勒听了，拍着大腿，咬着嘴唇，把这件事放在心上，然后吩咐内提：把冥界的七道门都闩上，把冥界宫殿的门一扇一扇地打开一条缝；让她弯下腰进来，进门时脱去她的王者服饰。
beats.textEn: At the palace Ganzer Inana pushed aggressively on the door and shouted: open up, doorman! Neti, open up, I shall enter alone! Neti, chief doorman of the netherworld, asked who she was. She was Inana going to the east, she said. Why then, asked Neti, had she come to the land of no return? Because, she said, Gud-gal-ana, the husband of her elder sister Ereškigala, had died, and she had come to his funeral rites. Neti went to report. Ereškigala slapped her thigh, bit her lip and took the matter to heart; she ordered the seven gates bolted and each door of the palace opened only a crack, so that Inana would enter crouching and be stripped as she came.

beats.textZh: 内提照吩咐闩上了七道门，又把宫殿的门打开一条缝，对伊南娜说：来吧，伊南娜，进来吧。她走进第一道门时，头上的王冠被取走了。她问：这是怎么回事？内提回答：满足吧，伊南娜，冥界的神力已经实现了。伊南娜，在冥界的仪式中你不能开口。走进第二道门时，脖子上的青金石项链被取走了；第三道门，胸前的蛋形珠子被取走了；第四道门，胸饰被取走了；第五道门，手上的金指环被取走了；第六道门，青金石的量杆和测绳被取走了；第七道门，她身上那件象征女主人身份的帕拉长袍也被取走了。每一次她发问，得到的都是同样的回答：满足吧，伊南娜，冥界的神力已经实现了。
beats.textEn: Neti bolted the seven gates and opened the palace door a crack: come, Inana, enter. At the first gate the turban was removed from her head. 'What is this?' 'Be satisfied, Inana, a divine power of the netherworld has been fulfilled. Inana, you must not open your mouth against the rites of the netherworld.' At the second gate the lapis beads were removed from her neck; at the third the egg-shaped beads; at the fourth the pectoral; at the fifth the gold ring; at the sixth the measuring rod and line; and at the seventh the pala dress, the garment of ladyship. Each time she asked, and each time the same answer came.

beats.textZh: 伊南娜弯着腰、赤身裸体地走了进去。她的姐姐埃列什基伽勒从王座上站了起来，伊南娜就在王座上坐下了。冥界的七位审判官——阿努纳众神，对她作出了判决。埃列什基伽勒用死亡的目光盯着她，对她说出愤怒的话语，对她喊出罪恶的叫声。伊南娜被打倒了，变成了一具尸体，那具尸体被挂在了钩子上。这是整首诗中最冷酷的一刻：天上的女王、带着七件神力走下冥界的伊南娜，转眼之间就成了钩子上的一具尸体。冥界的门已经关上，在那里没有人能替她求情。可是她临行前早有安排——在地上，还有一个人在等着她。
beats.textEn: After she had crouched down and her clothes had been removed, they were carried away. Then her sister Ereškigala rose from her throne, and Inana sat on the throne instead. The Anuna, the seven judges, rendered their decision against her. Ereškigala looked at her with the look of death, spoke to her with the speech of anger, shouted at her with the shout of heavy guilt. The afflicted woman was turned into a corpse, and the corpse was hung on a hook.

beats.textZh: 三天三夜过去了，伊南娜没有回来，她的大臣宁舒布尔照女主人的吩咐，在废墟中为她哀哭，在议会厅里为她敲鼓，在众神的家中奔走，抓伤自己的眼睛、嘴和大腿，像穷人一样只穿一件衣服。她独自来到尼普尔的埃库尔神庙，在恩利尔面前哭诉：父亲恩利尔，不要让你的女儿死在冥界！不要让你宝贵的金属在冥界的尘土里被弄脏，不要让你宝贵的青金石被石匠的石头劈碎，不要让少女伊南娜死在冥界！可是恩利尔大怒说：我的女儿渴望伟大的天上，又渴望伟大的地下。冥界的神力是不能贪求的，谁去了那里，谁就得留在那里！恩利尔不肯帮忙。宁舒布尔又去了乌尔的南纳那里，南纳也同样拒绝了她。
beats.textEn: After three days and three nights had passed, Ninšubur did as her mistress had ordered: she lamented in the ruins, beat the drum in the assembly, went round the gods' houses, lacerated her eyes, mouth and thighs and dressed like a pauper. Alone she went to the E-kur and wept before Enlil: don't let your precious metal be alloyed with the dust of the netherworld, don't let your lapis be split by the stone-cutter, don't let young lady Inana be put to death. Father Enlil angrily replied that his daughter craved the great heaven and the great below; whoever obtains the divine powers of the netherworld remains there. Enlil would not help, and Nanna in Urim likewise refused.

beats.textZh: 宁舒布尔来到埃利都，在恩基面前哭诉。父亲恩基回答说：我的女儿做了什么？她让我心焦！伊南娜做了什么？她让我心焦！所有土地的女主人做了什么？天上的圣女做了什么？她让我心焦！恩基从一只手指甲的尖上取下一点泥垢，造出了“库尔加拉”；又从另一只手指甲的尖上取下一点泥垢，造出了“加拉图拉”。他把生命之草交给库尔加拉，把生命之水交给加拉图拉，嘱咐它们：像苍蝇一样绕着门飞，像蛇一样从门轴下溜进去。那位生育者的母亲埃列什基伽勒正因为孩子的缘故躺在那里，没有衣服遮盖她圣洁的肩膀，没有亚麻布遮盖她的胸膛，她会喊“哎呀，我的里面！”，你们就跟着说“哎呀，你的里面！”；她喊“哎呀，我的外面！”，你们就说“哎呀，你的外面！”她会因此高兴，送给你们河水和田里的谷物，你们都不要接受，只要求她把挂在钩子上的那具尸体交给你们。
beats.textEn: Ninšubur went to Eridug and wept before Enki. Father Enki answered: what has my daughter done? She has me worried! What has Inana done? She has me worried! He removed some dirt from the tip of one fingernail and created the kur-ĝara; from the other he created the gala-tura. To one he gave the life-giving plant, to the other the life-giving water. Flit past the door like flies, he told them; slip through the door pivots like phantoms. The mother who gave birth, Ereškigala, lies there in pain because of her children, her shoulders and breast uncovered. When she cries 'Oh my heart!', say 'You are troubled, our mistress, oh your heart!' She will offer you the river and the fields; refuse them, and ask for the corpse hanging on the hook.

beats.textZh: 两个小人照恩基的吩咐，像苍蝇一样绕着门飞，像幽灵一样从门轴下溜了进去。冥后正痛苦地躺着，她喊“哎呀，我的里面”，它们就说“你很痛苦，我们的女主人，哎呀，你的里面”；她喊“哎呀，我的外面”，它们就说“哎呀，你的外面”。埃列什基伽勒问：你们是谁？我要祝福你们，你们是神，我要和你们说话；你们是人，我要给你们定下命运。她让它们以天地的名义发誓，送给它们满河的水，它们不要；送给它们满田的谷物，它们也不要。它们说：请把挂在钩子上的那具尸体给我们吧。冥后说：那是你们女主人的尸体。它们说：不论是我们国王的还是我们女主人的，都请给我们吧。尸体被交给了它们。一个把生命之草撒在尸体上，另一个把生命之水洒在尸体上。于是，伊南娜站了起来。
beats.textEn: They did as Enki said, slipping in like flies and phantoms. When the queen cried 'Oh my heart!', they answered 'You are troubled, our mistress, oh your heart!', and so with 'oh my liver'. Who are you? she asked; if gods, I will speak with you, if mortals, I will decree a destiny for you. She made them swear and offered the river with its water and the field with its grain, and they refused. Give us the corpse hanging on the hook, they said. That is the corpse of your queen. Whether it is our king's or our queen's, give it to us. The corpse was handed over; one sprinkled the life-giving plant on it, the other the life-giving water, and so Inana arose.

beats.textZh: 伊南娜正要从冥界上去，阿努纳众神抓住了她，说：有谁从冥界上去，能够安然无恙？如果伊南娜要从冥界上去，就让她提供一个替身来代替她！于是一群“加拉”恶魔跟着她一起上去。走在她前面的那个，手里拿着权杖，却不是大臣；走在她身边的那个，腰间佩着武器，却不是战士。这些恶魔不知道食物，不知道饮水，不吃撒下的面粉，不喝倒出的清水，不收礼物；它们从不享受夫妻的欢乐，不亲吻可爱的孩子；它们从男人膝上夺走妻子，从母亲胸前夺走孩子。
beats.textEn: As Inana was about to ascend, the Anuna seized her: who has ever ascended from the netherworld unscathed? If Inana is to ascend, let her provide a substitute. So the galla demons went up with her — the one in front holding a sceptre though not a minister, the one beside her bearing a weapon though not a warrior. These are demons who know no food, know no drink, eat no flour offering and drink no libation, accept no gifts, enjoy no lovemaking and kiss no children; they tear the wife from a man's embrace and the child from its mother's breast.

beats.textZh: 伊南娜走出冥界，宁舒布尔扑倒在她脚下，身上满是灰尘，穿着肮脏的衣服。恶魔们说：走吧，伊南娜，我们要把她带走。伊南娜说：她是我说话可靠的大臣，是忠实的使者，她没有忘记我的吩咐，在废墟中为我哀哭，在议会厅里为我敲鼓，在众神的家中为我奔走。是她让我活了过来，我怎么能把她交给你们？她们来到乌玛，沙拉神穿着肮脏的衣服，在自己的神庙里扑倒在伊南娜脚下；来到巴德提比拉，卢拉尔神也穿着肮脏的衣服扑倒在她脚下。恶魔们每次都说要把他们带走，伊南娜都说：他是我的歌者、我的侍从，他为我哀悼，不能给你们。于是这几位都得到了赦免。
beats.textEn: As Inana came out, Ninšubur threw herself at her feet, covered in dust and dressed in a filthy garment. The demons said: we will take her. Inana refused: she is my minister of fair words, who did not forget my instructions, who lamented in the ruins, beat the drum and went round the gods' houses — she brought me back to life; how could I give her to you? At Umma, Šara threw himself at her feet in a filthy garment; at Bad-tibira, Lulal did the same. Each time the demons asked to take them, and each time Inana refused, because they had mourned for her.

beats.textZh: 她们来到库拉巴的大苹果树下，看见伊南娜的丈夫杜木兹穿着华丽的衣服，坐在高高的王座上，没有为她哀悼。恶魔们扑上去，抓住他的大腿，打翻他的七只奶桶，不让牧人再吹奏他的芦笛。伊南娜用死亡的目光盯着他，对他说出愤怒的话语，喊出罪恶的叫声：就是他，把他带走！杜木兹吓得脸色苍白，痛哭起来，他向天上举起双手，向太阳神乌图祈祷：乌图啊，你是我的朋友，我是你的妹夫；我把奶油带到你母亲的家，把牛奶带到宁加尔的家。请把我的手变成蛇的手，把我的脚变成蛇的脚，让我从恶魔手里逃走，不让它们抓住我。乌图接受了他的眼泪，把他的手变成蛇的手，把他的脚变成蛇的脚，杜木兹便从恶魔手中逃脱了。故事的结尾残缺不全，可以读出的部分说：杜木兹在冥界待半年，他的姐姐盖什提南娜待另外半年。
beats.textEn: Beneath the great apple tree of Kul-aba they found Dumuzid, Inana's husband, clothed in a magnificent garment and seated on a magnificent throne, not mourning. The demons seized him by the thighs, spilled his seven churns and silenced the shepherd's pipe. Inana looked at him with the look of death, spoke the speech of anger: take him away! Dumuzid turned pale and wept, raised his hands to Utu: you are my brother-in-law and I your sister's husband; I carried cream to your mother's house. Change my hands into snake's hands and my feet into snake's feet, so I may escape my demons. Utu accepted his tears and changed his hands and feet, and Dumuzid escaped. The broken ending says Dumuzid will spend half the year below and his sister Geštin-ana the other half.
beats.uncertaintyNote: 结尾诗行残缺；杜木兹与盖什提南娜各在冥界半年的安排依据可读出的部分，其他苏美尔作品另有不同讲法。
